source.title: Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique
source.authors: Laurent Fargues and Jean-Marc Fontaine, with a Préface by Pierre Colmez
source.read: The authors' copy courbe.pdf dated 16 avril 2017 (Colmez's Préface, pp. 1–50; Chapters 1–11 and the bibliography, pp. 51–389), SHA-256 cc159f38a3801c736b71ecea363496abe7706550bfb416600718ee9933922ca3, fetched 29 September 2026 from the link in papers.json and read in full by nine readers in parallel (the Préface; Chapter 1; Chapters 2–3; Chapter 4; Chapter 5; Chapters 6–7; Chapters 8–9; Chapter 10; Chapter 11 and the bibliography). Their drafts were merged, deduplicated and checked. Locators are the statement numbers and printed pages of that copy. The Astérisque edition was not compared with it; its numbering may differ.
readSections: Préface (P. Colmez): La courbe de Fargues et Fontaine
Ch. 1 Fonctions holomorphes de la variable π et anneaux de périodes (§§1.1–1.10)
Ch. 2 Zéros des fonctions holomorphes : le cas F algébriquement clos (§§2.1–2.7)
Ch. 3 Zéros des fonctions holomorphes : le cas F parfait quelconque (§§3.1–3.6)
Ch. 4 Q_p-espaces vectoriels formels et périodes des groupes p-divisibles (§§4.1–4.6)
Ch. 6 La courbe fondamentale lorsque F est algébriquement clos (§§6.1–6.7)
Ch. 7 La courbe fondamentale pour F parfait quelconque (§§7.1–7.9)
Ch. 8 Classification des fibrés vectoriels : le cas F algébriquement clos (§§8.1–8.6)
Ch. 9 Classification des fibrés : le cas F parfait (§§9.1–9.5)
Ch. 10 Faiblement admissible implique admissible et le théorème de la monodromie p-adique (§§10.1–10.6)

summary: Fargues and Fontaine construct the fundamental curve of p-adic Hodge theory and classify its vector bundles. For a local field E and a perfectoid field F of characteristic p they develop the theory of holomorphic functions of the variable π — the rings B^b, B_I, B and B^+ with their Gauss norms, Newton polygons, Weierstrass factorisation, principality of the B_I and divisors, first for F algebraically closed and then by Galois descent for F perfect (Chapters 1–3); describe the Banach spaces B^{φ^h=π^d} as periods of π-divisible O-modules and their universal covers (Chapter 4); set up an abstract theory of curves, Harder–Narasimhan filtrations and generalised Riemann spheres with a classification criterion by degree-one modifications (Chapter 5); prove that P = ⊕_d B^{φ=π^d} is graded-factorial when F is algebraically closed, so that X_{F,E} = Proj(P) is a complete curve with B_e a principal ideal domain, and for F perfect a complete curve with B_{F,e} Dedekind of class group Hom(G_F, E^×) (Chapters 6–7); classify the vector bundles on X_{F,E} by slopes for F algebraically closed, by two proofs (Gross–Hopkins and Drinfeld period maps, and Colmez's Banach spaces), and show that X_Ē is simply connected (Chapter 8); classify bundles over any perfect F by Galois descent and compute π_1(X_{F,Ē}) = Gal(F̄|F) (Chapter 9); prove 'weakly admissible implies admissible' and the p-adic monodromy theorem through G_K-equivariant bundles (Chapter 10); and relate bundles to φ-modules over B^+, B and the Robba ring, with GAGA and Berger's theorem (Chapter 11). Colmez's Préface tells the history and surveys the Banach-space, almost C-representation and (φ,Γ)-module methods the curve replaced. The atlas plans the curve by the Fargues–Scholze route (RelativeFarguesFontaine, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, FarguesFontaineDiamonds), and 181 of the 1109 items are planned there or in PerfectoidSpaces, PadicHodgeTheory, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology and PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology; 15 are in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. What the atlas lacks is the book's own method: the function theory of the variable π and the schematic curve over a perfect field, the abstract bundle theory with the classification over non-algebraically-closed F and the φ-module descriptions, the periods of p-divisible groups, and p-adic Hodge theory read on equivariant bundles. These are routed as four Part II proposals (of RelativeFarguesFontaine, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory and PadicHodgeTheory), with smaller items going as sources to existing layers. The independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18) corrected 66 statuses (65 planned items became missing because the cited layer plans only a special case), joined the VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals Part II to the accepted proposal of that id with its exact title, replaced the FarguesFontaineDiamonds source route by a VB3 source route for Colmez's Dimension, and found 34 further mistakes in the book, among them false statements in Proposition 11.2.24, Lemme 11.2.25, Théorème 6.4.4 (a missing orbit hypothesis), Lemme 1.6.8 and Théorème 2.5.1(2).

items.name: Préface note 8: the degree on B_e; a Bézout B_e is principal
items.statement: Let B_e = B_cris^{φ=1} ⊂ B_dR. For x ∈ B_e let deg x be the least integer d such that x ∈ t^{−d}B_dR^+. Then deg(xy) = deg x + deg y, and x is invertible in B_e if and only if deg x = 0. Consequently, if B_e is a Bézout ring then it is a principal ideal ring: if I is an ideal and a ∈ I has minimal degree, then a generates the principal ideal (a, b) for every b ∈ I, hence a generates I.
items.locator: Préface §1.1–1.2, note 8, p. 3, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Préface-only argument (the chapters prove principality of B_e differently: 'anneau presque euclidien', Déf. 5.2.1–Prop. 5.2.5, and Théorème 6.5.2). Mathlib has the class mathlib:IsBezout but no statement 'Bézout + additive degree with units of degree 0 ⇒ principal', and no B_e. The conclusion (the complement of a classical point of the curve is the spectrum of a PID) is planned at VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point, FS II.2.9) and VB2:classification (node .../classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains), but neither the degree function on B_e nor this lemma is stated there.

items.name: Préface note 11 (Kedlaya–Temkin [40]): negative answer to Fontaine's Question 1
items.statement: (Black box, [40].) Fontaine's Question 1 — if I is an ideal of degree 1 of B_e, is the field B_e/I isomorphic to C? — has a negative answer: there are ideals I of degree 1 of B_e for which B_e/I is not isomorphic to C.
items.locator: Préface §1.3, note 11, pp. 4–5 (cf. Remarque 4.4(i), p. 40), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External result used as a black box (Kedlaya–Temkin, arXiv:1506.00742). As abstract fields B_e/I and C are both algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and of the same cardinality, hence isomorphic; the 'non' has to be read for topological (valued) fields, as in Remarque 4.4(i) ('B_dR^+(K_y) dépend de y (en tant qu'anneau topologique [40])'). Nothing in the atlas states it (searched: Kedlaya–Temkin, residue fields of the curve).

items.name: Remarque 3.14(iii) and note 11: quotients of O(X_E − {x_0}) by nonzero ideals (modified Question 3)
items.statement: Let x_0, x_1, …, x_d be pairwise distinct closed points of X_E, with generators t_{x_0}, …, t_{x_d} ∈ (B_E^+)^{φ_E=π} of the corresponding homogeneous ideals, and let m_1, …, m_d ≥ 1. Then, by the Chinese remainder theorem and Théorème 3.13(ii)(b), the quotient of O(X_E − {x_0}) = (B_E^+[1/t_{x_0}])^{φ_E=1} by the ideal generated by ∏_{i=1}^d (t_{x_i}/t_{x_0})^{m_i} is isomorphic to ∏_{i=1}^d B_dR^+(K_{x_i})/(t_{x_i}^{m_i}). For E = Q_p and x_0 = ∞ this is the positive answer to the modified form of Fontaine's Question 3 on the quotients B_e/I (every nonzero ideal of the principal ring B_e is of this form).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.14(iii), p. 37 (with note 11, pp. 4–5), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Préface-only formulation; the chapters only use the analogous fact inside the proof of Prop. 7.2.1 (p. 264: 'A/(a) est isomorphe à un produit d'anneaux de valuation discrète quotientés par une puissance de leur idéal maximal') and Prop. 7.2.3. The atlas plans the PID property and the completions B_dR^+ at a degree-one divisor (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration) but not this product decomposition. The statement as written by Colmez is a sketch (x_0, …, x_d and 'la réponse … est oui'); the formulation above is the precise content.

items.name: Préface §1.4 (end): Aut(C^♭) is transitive when C^♭ is maximally complete
items.statement: If C^♭ is maximally complete, the group Aut(C^♭) of automorphisms of C^♭ acts transitively on m_{C^♭} (i.e. on its nonzero elements), and hence transitively on the nonzero elements of (B_cris^+)^{φ=p}, every such element being of the form log[1 + x] with x ∈ m_{C^♭}.
items.locator: Préface §1.4, p. 9, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Literally 'transitivement sur m_{C^♭}' must be read on m_{C^♭} − {0}. The description (B_cris^+)^{φ=p} − {0} = {log[1+x] : x ∈ m_{C^♭} − {0}} is the case E = Q_p of Théorème 3.11(ii) (chapters: Prop. 2.3.9, Prop. 4.4.6). Nothing in the atlas (searched: maximally/spherically complete, Aut(C^♭)).

items.name: Préface §1.4 (end): |X| ≅ Aut(C^♭)/(Aut(C) × φ^Z) for maximally complete C
items.statement: If C is replaced by a maximally complete closure (so that C^♭ is also maximally complete), then the action of Aut(C^♭) on the points of X induces a bijection |X| ≅ Aut(C^♭)/(Aut(C) × φ^Z).
items.locator: Préface §1.4, p. 9, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof, as a consequence of the previous item; 'Aut(C)' has to mean continuous automorphisms of C (they are the automorphisms of C^♭ fixing the untilt ∞), and φ is the absolute Frobenius of C^♭. Not stated in the chapters; nothing in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.1.3: D_st, D_pst, D_dR; semistable, potentially semistable, de Rham representations; Hodge–Tate weights
items.statement: Let V be a (finite-dimensional, continuous, Q_p-linear) representation of G_K. Put D_st(V) = (B̃^+_log[1/t] ⊗ V)^{G_K}, D_pst(V) = lim_{→, [L:K]<∞} (B̃^+_log[1/t] ⊗ V)^{G_L}, D_dR(V) = (B_dR ⊗ V)^{G_K}. D_st(V) is a (φ, N)-module over K_0 of dimension ≤ dim V, and V is called semistable (or log-crystalline) if equality holds; D_pst(V) is a (φ, N)-module over Q_p^nr with a smooth action of G_K (inertia acting through a finite quotient), of dimension ≤ dim V, and V is potentially semistable (potentially log-crystalline) if equality holds; D_dR(V) is a filtered K-module of dimension ≤ dim V, and V is de Rham if equality holds. If V is de Rham and i ∈ Z, dim_K(D_dR^{−i}(V)/D_dR^{1−i}(V)) is the multiplicity of i as a (Hodge–Tate) weight of V, and i is a weight of V if this multiplicity is nonzero.
items.locator: Préface §2.1.3, p. 11, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors, R06.2/admissible-representations, R06.3/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module; weight convention R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention (the Préface's convention gives Q_p(1) the weight 1, matching HT(χ_p) = +1). The Préface uses B̃^+_log[1/t] instead of B_st = B_cris[u] (§2.1.1 explains that all relevant periods lie in finite-dimensional φ-stable subspaces); the atlas uses B_st, so a comparison is needed. The chapters work with G_K-equivariant bundles instead (Déf. 10.4.5, 10.6.5) and do not define these functors on representations.

items.name: Préface §2.1.3: K ⊗ D_st(V) ⊂ (Q̄_p ⊗ D_pst(V))^{G_K} ⊂ D_dR(V); semistable ⇒ pst ⇒ de Rham
items.statement: For every representation V of G_K there are natural injections K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) ⊂ (Q̄_p ⊗_{Q_p^nr} D_pst(V))^{G_K} ⊂ D_dR(V); hence semistable ⇒ potentially semistable ⇒ de Rham.
items.locator: Préface §2.1.3, p. 11, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/crystalline-semistable-de-rham-implications (K ⊗ D_st(V) → D_dR(V), semistable ⇒ de Rham), R06.2/admissibility-dimension-bound, R06.3/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module and R06.3/p-adic-monodromy-theorem ('Conversely every potentially semistable representation is de Rham').

items.name: Préface §2.1.2: V_st(D) and admissible filtered (φ, N)-modules
items.statement: For a filtered (φ, N)-module D over K, V_st(D) = Ker((B̃^+_log[1/t] ⊗_{K_0} D)^{N=0, φ=1} → (B_dR ⊗_K D_K)/Fil^0), a representation of G_K; D is called admissible if dim_{Q_p} V_st(D) = rg(D).
items.locator: Préface §2.1.2, p. 10, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful (V_st(D) := Fil^0(B_st ⊗ D)^{φ=1,N=0}) and R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion (admissible iff dim V_st(D) = dim D). The chapters define V_cris and admissibility only for filtered φ-modules (p. 340, before Théorème 10.5.7).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.3: D_st and V_st are mutually inverse on semistable / admissible objects
items.statement: If V is semistable, then D_st(V) is filtered over K via K ⊗_{K_0} D_st(V) = D_dR(V), the resulting filtered (φ, N)-module is admissible, and V is naturally isomorphic to V_st(D_st(V)). If D is an admissible filtered (φ, N)-module, then V_st(D) is semistable and D is naturally isomorphic to D_st(V_st(D)). Hence the conjectures 'fa ⇒ a' and 'dR ⇒ pst' give a complete description of de Rham representations in terms of semilinear algebra.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.3, p. 11, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine's theorem, quoted. Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful, R06.2/admissible-implies-weakly-admissible, R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion. The printed text has 'D_st(V_st(V))' (source issue E3).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.4 (Sen [51]): de Rham with all Hodge–Tate weights 0 ⇔ inertia acts through a finite quotient
items.statement: Let V be a representation of G_K. The following are equivalent: (i) V is de Rham with all Hodge–Tate weights 0 (i.e. B_dR^+ ⊗ V ≅ (B_dR^+)^{dim V}); (ii) the inertia subgroup acts on V through a finite quotient. These conditions imply that V is potentially unramified (and potentially semistable).
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.4, pp. 11–12, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External black box (translation of Sen 1973). Not planned as such: the atlas has only Sen's module and operator (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/sen-module) and the easy direction (ii) ⇒ (i) (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/potentially-unramified-and-characters (1), R06.2/hodge-tate-characters-are-de-rham (3)); the monodromy theorem is planned via Berger–Kedlaya (R06.3), not via Sen. The chapters use Sen's theorem in §10.6.4 (p. 344, 'D'après Sen ([58] 3.2)') without stating it.

items.name: Préface §2.2.1: the ring C{T}~ and Colmez's skew field 𝒞 of finite-rank analytic Q_p-linear correspondences
items.statement: Let O_C{T}~ be the p-adic completion of the integral closure of O_C{T} in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and C{T}~ = O_C{T}~[1/p], a Banach algebra for the spectral norm; Spm(C{T}~) is a profinite covering of the closed unit ball, and elements of C{T}~ are viewed as multivalued functions on the unit ball. Fix a point 0̃ ∈ Spm(C{T}~) above 0. A finite-rank additive analytic correspondence is an f ∈ C{T}~ with f(0̃) = 0 such that {f(x+y)} − {f(x)} − {f(y)} is contained in a finite-rank Z_p-module independent of x, y. Its graph Γ_f^0 = {(x, y) ∈ C² : y ∈ {f(x)}} is a Z_p-submodule of C²; the Q_p-linear correspondence (still denoted f) has graph Γ_f = the Q_p-span of Γ_f^0. 𝒞 is the set of these finite-rank analytic Q_p-linear correspondences on C; the rank of f is dim_{Q_p} U_f with U_f = {f(0)}, and V_f = {x ∈ C : 0 ∈ {f(x)}}. The correspondences of rank 0 are the f_c = cT, c ∈ C.
items.locator: Préface §2.2.1, p. 12, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From Colmez [12, chap. 5, 9]. Not in the chapters (FF §8.4 uses Banach–Colmez spaces but not 𝒞) and not in the atlas (searched: fundamental lemma, analytic correspondence, Banach–Colmez).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.5 (the 'lemme fondamental', Colmez [12]): nonzero correspondences are surjective with finite-dimensional kernel
items.statement: If f ∈ 𝒞 − {0}, then f is surjective (every y ∈ C lies in {f(x)} for some x ∈ C) and V_f = {x ∈ C : 0 ∈ {f(x)}} is a Q_p-vector space of dimension equal to the rank of f.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.5, p. 12, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12, §§5.5–5.7, th. 9.5]. The Préface explains (Remarque 2.7) that Fontaine's 'lemme fondamental' is this theorem applied to the f_A. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.6(i): 𝒞 is a skew field with centre Q_p
items.statement: For f, g ∈ 𝒞 there are unique f + g ∈ 𝒞 and f·g ∈ 𝒞 with {(f+g)(x)} ⊂ {f(x)} + {g(x)} and {(f·g)(x)} ⊂ f({g(x)}) for all x ∈ C; with these laws 𝒞 is a (skew) field with centre Q_p.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.6(i), pp. 12–13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.6(ii): C is a maximal commutative subfield of 𝒞
items.statement: The map c ↦ f_c = cT identifies C with a maximal commutative subfield of 𝒞.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.6(ii), p. 12, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.6(iii): inverse of a correspondence
items.statement: If g is the inverse of f in 𝒞, then Γ_g is the transpose of Γ_f (Γ_g = {(y, x) : (x, y) ∈ Γ_f}) and f and g have the same rank.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.6(iii), p. 13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.7: the correspondences f_A attached to trace-zero tensors
items.statement: There is a surjection θ : (B̃^+_rig(C{T}~))^{φ=p} → C{T}~. For c ∈ C, cT has a unique lift ĉT in (B̃^+_rig(C{T}~))^{φ=p} with ĉT(0̃) = 0; choose also lifts ĉ of c. Let Tr : C ⊗_{Q_p} C → C, α ⊗ β ↦ αβ. If A = Σ_i α_i ⊗ β_i satisfies Tr(A) = 0, then Σ_i β̂_i α̂_iT ∈ (B̃^+_rig(C{T}~))^{φ=p²} is divisible by t and f_A = θ(t^{−1} Σ_i β̂_i α̂_iT) ∈ 𝒞. Fontaine's 'lemme fondamental' is Théorème 2.5 applied to an element of the form f_A.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.7, p. 13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the chapters or the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.8: structure of 𝒞 (exact sequence 0 → C → 𝒞 → C ⊗ C → C → 0)
items.statement: Every f ∈ 𝒞 can be written f = f_c + f_A (c ∈ C, A ∈ C ⊗_{Q_p} C with Tr(A) = 0); setting δ(f) = A, δ(f) does not depend on the writing, and 0 → C → 𝒞 →^{δ} C ⊗_{Q_p} C →^{Tr} C → 0 is exact.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.8, p. 13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.9(i): neighbouring representations — the non-degenerate case
items.statement: Let V_1 be a finite-dimensional representation of G_K with basis e_1, …, e_d, M_1 = B_dR^+ ⊗ V_1, and M_2 a G_K-stable B_dR^+-submodule of B_dR ⊗ V_1 such that (M_1+M_2)/M_1 and (M_1+M_2)/M_2 are 1-dimensional over C; write (M_1+M_2)/M_1 = C t^{−1}(α_1e_1 + ⋯ + α_de_d) and (M_1 ∩ M_2)/tM_1 = {Σ x_ie_i ∈ C ⊗ V_1 : Σ β_ix_i = 0} (so Σ β_iα_i = 0). Let X = (B_e ⊗ V_1) ∩ (M_1+M_2) and u_i : X → (M_1+M_2)/M_i the natural maps, so that 0 → V_1 → X → (M_2+M_1)/M_1 → 0 is exact. If β_1 ⊗ α_1 + ⋯ + β_d ⊗ α_d ≠ 0 in C ⊗_{Q_p} C, then u_2 is surjective and Ker u_2 is a representation V_2 of G_K of dimension d.
items.locator: Préface §2.2.2, Proposition 2.9(i), p. 13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from the fundamental exact sequence and Théorèmes 2.5, 2.8. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.9(ii): neighbouring representations — the degenerate case
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.9, if β_1 ⊗ α_1 + ⋯ + β_d ⊗ α_d = 0 in C ⊗_{Q_p} C, then dim_{Q_p}(Im u_2) ≤ d and Ker u_2 is infinite-dimensional over Q_p.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.9(ii), p. 13, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.10(i): neighbouring representations share B_e, B_dR and de Rham-ness
items.statement: In case (i) of Proposition 2.9 (automatic if V_1 is irreducible, by note 17): B_e ⊗ V_2 = B_e ⊗ V_1, B_dR ⊗ V_2 = B_dR ⊗ V_1 and B_dR^+ ⊗ V_i = M_i (i = 1, 2); in particular V_2 is de Rham if and only if V_1 is de Rham.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.10(i) and note 17, p. 14, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.10(ii) and note 18: neighbouring filtrations preserve admissibility
items.statement: Two filtrations Fil_1, Fil_2 on D_K are neighbours if Σ_{j∈Z} dim_K (Fil_1^j + Fil_2^j)/(Fil_1^j ∩ Fil_2^j) = 2; Fil_2 ↦ M_2 = Fil_2^0(B_dR ⊗_K D_K) is a bijection from the filtrations neighbouring Fil_1 onto the G_K-stable B_dR^+-lattices M_2 of B_dR ⊗ V_1 = B_dR ⊗_K D_K with (M_1+M_2)/M_i of C-dimension 1. If V_1 = V_st(D, Fil_1) (in case (i) of Proposition 2.9), then M_i = Fil_i^0(B_dR ⊗_K D_K); hence for neighbouring filtrations Fil_1, Fil_2 on D_K, (D, Fil_1) is admissible iff (D, Fil_2) is admissible.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.10(ii) and note 18, p. 14, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.2.3: criterion for equality of subcategories (by neighbouring chains)
items.statement: Let 𝒯 be a category in which dimension and exact sequences make sense, with a symmetric neighbour relation, and subcategories 𝒯′ ⊃ 𝒯″ such that: (0) objects of 𝒯′ are finite-dimensional; (1) a 1-dimensional T ∈ 𝒯 in 𝒯′ lies in 𝒯″; (2) if T_1, T_2 are neighbours then (a) if both are finite-dimensional, T_1 ∈ 𝒯″ ⇔ T_2 ∈ 𝒯″, and (b) T_1 irreducible in 𝒯′ ⇒ T_2 ∈ 𝒯′; (3) if 0 → T_1 → T → T_2 → 0 is exact in 𝒯′ and T_1, T_2 ∈ 𝒯″ then T ∈ 𝒯″; (4) every T ∈ 𝒯′ is joined by a chain T = T_0, …, T_r of successive neighbours in 𝒯 with T_r ∈ 𝒯″. Then 𝒯″ = 𝒯′ (proof by induction on the dimension).
items.locator: Préface §2.2.3, p. 14, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Abstract device implicit in [14, 30]; the proof is only indicated ('ne pose pas de problème'; it also uses tacitly that neighbours have the same dimension). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.2.4 (Fontaine–Laffaille [31]): filtrations with two consecutive weights defined over K_0 are admissible
items.statement: (Black box, [31], as invoked in the sketch of 'fa ⇒ a'.) Starting from a filtered (φ, N)-module, neighbour moves (raising one weight by 1 and lowering another by 1) lead in finitely many steps to a filtration all of whose weights are k or k+1 (k ∈ Z), which can moreover be arranged to be defined over K_0; such a filtration is admissible by the results of Fontaine–Laffaille [31].
items.locator: Préface §2.2.4, p. 15, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/small-weight-admissibility (weakly admissible filtered φ-modules over K = K_0 of filtration length < p are admissible); stage R07.3 names the rational admissibility theorem (FL Thm 8.4). Fontaine–Laffaille needs the final filtered module to be weakly admissible and crystalline (N = 0); the Préface's sketch does not say how this is arranged (it refers to [14] for the details), and uses that V_st over K of D ⊗ K equals V_st over K_0 of D.

items.name: Préface §2.2.5: H^1_g = H^1_st — a de Rham extension of semistable representations is semistable
items.statement: (Black box: [36], [46, prop. 1.24] if k_K is finite; [2, th. VI.2] in general.) If 0 → V_1 → V → V_2 → 0 is an extension of representations of G_K with V_1, V_2 semistable and V de Rham, then V is semistable (i.e. H^1_g = H^1_st).
items.locator: Préface §2.2.5, p. 15 (and item 3 of the introduction to §2, p. 9), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4/ordinary-implies-semistable (a) (for K/Q_p finite). The general residue field case [2, th. VI.2] is not planned. The chapters do not state it (FF §10.6 argues with bundles; cf. §10.6.5.4 'd'après Hyodo').

items.name: Préface §2.3: algèbres sympathiques, Espaces de Banach, Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie, presentations
items.statement: A sympathetic algebra Λ is a p-adic Banach algebra, with the spectral norm, such that x ↦ x^p is surjective on {x : |x − 1| < 1} (such an algebra is perfectoid). An Espace de Banach W is a functor Λ ↦ W(Λ) from sympathetic algebras to p-adic Banach spaces; examples: finite-dimensional Q_p-spaces V (constant functor) and V^d (Λ ↦ Λ^d). A sequence 0 → W_1 → W → W_2 → 0 is exact if it is exact on Λ-points for every sympathetic Λ. W is of finite Dimension if there are d ∈ N, finite-dimensional Q_p-spaces V_1, V_2 and exact sequences 0 → V_1 → Y → V^d → 0 and 0 → V_2 → Y → W → 0 (a presentation of W).
items.locator: Préface §2.3, p. 16, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez's original definition [12]. The atlas plans Banach–Colmez spaces only in the Fargues–Scholze form (v-sheaves T ↦ H^0(X_T, E)): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3 (node VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition), which is a different formalism; Remarque 2.11 records that the effective objects are analytic groups and general ones quotients by Q_p-spaces (diamonds [54, 22]).

items.name: Préface §2.3: the Graph 𝒢_f of f ∈ 𝒞 and its two exact sequences
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒞 the Graph 𝒢_f ⊂ V² is the Espace de Banach with 𝒢_f(Λ) = {(λ_1, λ_2) ∈ Λ² : (s(λ_1), s(λ_2)) ∈ Γ_f for all s : Λ → C}. The two projections V² → V^1 induce exact sequences 0 → U_f → 𝒢_f → V^1 → 0 and 0 → V_f → 𝒢_f → V^1 → 0 ([12, cor. 6.9]), where U_f, V_f are the Q_p-spaces of dimension rank(f) of Théorème 2.5.
items.locator: Préface §2.3, p. 16, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.12(i): the Dimension (dim, ht) of an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie is well defined
items.statement: If W is an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie with presentation as above, then Dim W = (dim W, ht W) with dim W = d and ht W = dim_{Q_p} V_1 − dim_{Q_p} V_2 depends only on W and not on the presentation.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.12(i), p. 16, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas (FS-style BC spaces in VB3 have a dimension as diamonds but no height invariant).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.12(ii): kernels, images, cokernels and additivity of Dim
items.statement: If f : W_1 → W_2 is a morphism of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie, then Ker f, Im f and Coker f are Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie, and Dim W_1 = Dim Ker f + Dim Im f, Dim W_2 = Dim Coker f + Dim Im f.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.12(ii), p. 16, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.12(iii): dim W = 0 ⇒ ht W ≥ 0
items.statement: If W is an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie with dim W = 0, then ht W ≥ 0.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.12(iii), p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.12(iv): sub-Spaces of successive extensions of V^1 have nonnegative height
items.statement: If W is a successive extension of copies of V^1 and W_0 is a sub-Espace de Banach de Dimension finie of W, then ht W_0 ≥ 0.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.12(iv), p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.13: an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie is determined by its C-points
items.statement: For an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie W, W = 0 iff W(C) = 0; consequently (using kernels and cokernels) a morphism f : W_1 → W_2 is an isomorphism iff f_C : W_1(C) → W_2(C) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.13, p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.14: 𝒞 as an endomorphism ring
items.statement: The skew field 𝒞 is the ring of endomorphisms of the projective limit of the V^1/V, V running over the finite-dimensional Q_p-subspaces of C = V^1(C); that 𝒞 is a field expresses that this object is simple.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.14, p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Heuristic remark (stated, not proved). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.3.1: Dimensions of X^r_st(D) and X^r_dR(D) ([12, prop. 10.1, 10.7])
items.statement: Let D be a filtered (φ, N)-module over K of rank h and r ∈ N; put X^r_st(D) = (t^{−r}B̃^+_log ⊗_{K_0} D)^{N=0, φ=1} and X^r_dR(D) = (t^{−r}B_dR^+ ⊗_K D_K)/Fil^0. These are the C-points of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie 𝕏^r_st(D), 𝕏^r_dR(D), with Dim 𝕏^r_st(D) = Σ_{r_i ≤ r} (r − r_i, 1) (r_i the slopes of φ with multiplicity) and, if r ≥ r(D) (the least r with D_K^{r+1} = 0 and all r_i ≤ r), Dim 𝕏^r_st(D) = (rh − t_N(D), h) and Dim 𝕏^r_dR(D) = (rh − t_H(D), 0).
items.locator: Préface §2.3.1, p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [12]. The Préface also prints Dim 𝕏^r_dR(D) = (r dim D_K − Σ_{i=1}^r dim D_K^i, 0), which needs D_K^0 = D_K (source issue E4); the formula (rh − t_H(D), 0) for r ≥ r(D) is correct in general. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.3.1: V_st(D) is the kernel of 𝕏^r_st(D) → 𝕏^r_dR(D)
items.statement: The natural map X^r_st(D) → X^r_dR(D) (induced by B̃^+_log → B_dR^+) extends to a morphism of Espaces de Banach 𝕏^r_st(D) → 𝕏^r_dR(D), and for r ≥ r(D), V_st(D) is its kernel.
items.locator: Préface §2.3.1, p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion uses the untruncated map (B_st ⊗ D)^{N=0,φ=1} → (B_dR ⊗ D_K)/Fil^0).

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.15: surjectivity criterion when t_H(D) = t_N(D)
items.statement: Let D be a filtered (φ, N)-module over K with t_H(D) = t_N(D). The following are equivalent: (i) V_st(D) is finite-dimensional over Q_p; (ii) X^r_st(D) → X^r_dR(D) is surjective for r = r(D); (ii′) X^r_st(D) → X^r_dR(D) is surjective for every r ≥ r(D). Moreover these imply (iii) D is weakly admissible and (iv) dim_{Q_p} V_st(D) = rg D.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.15, p. 17, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Théorème 2.12. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.3.1: for weakly admissible D, V_st(D) = V_st(D′) with D′ the largest admissible subobject
items.statement: (Black box: [14, prop. 4.5], [12, prop. 11.11].) If D is weakly admissible, then V_st(D) is finite-dimensional over Q_p, with dim V_st(D) = rg D iff D is admissible; in fact V_st(D) = V_st(D′) where D′ is the largest admissible subobject of D. With Proposition 2.15 this gives 'weakly admissible ⇒ admissible'.
items.locator: Préface §2.3.1, p. 18, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion (V_st(D) finite-dimensional and semistable for weakly admissible D, D′ = D_st(V_st(D)) a weakly admissible subobject, admissible iff equality).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.16 (Colmez [13, prop. 0.3]): φ-stable lattices in (B̃^+_rig)^d attached to a B_dR^+-lattice
items.statement: Let M be a B_dR^+-lattice contained in (B_dR^+)^d and let M̃^+_rig = {x ∈ (B̃^+_rig)^d : φ^n(x) ∈ M for all n ∈ Z}. Then M̃^+_rig is a free B̃^+_rig-module of rank d with a basis e_1, …, e_d such that: there are h ∈ N and a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_d ∈ N with φ^h(e_i) = p^{a_i}e_i for all i; and φ^n(e_1), …, φ^n(e_d) is a basis of M over B_dR^+ for every n ∈ Z.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.16, p. 18, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [13]; the Préface notes its proof is too combinatorial to sketch. Close in content to the chapters' equivalence of B-pairs, φ-modules over B^+ and bundles plus the classification (Th. 11.1.9, Th. 8.2.10; Préface note 30), but not stated there. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.17 (Colmez [13, prop. 0.4]): cocycles in (B̃^+_log)^{φ^h=p^a} trivial in B_dR^+ are coboundaries
items.statement: Let σ ↦ c_σ be a continuous 1-cocycle on G_K with values in (B̃^+_log)^{φ^h=p^a} such that σ ↦ N^k(φ^{−n}(c_σ)) is a coboundary in B_dR^+ for all k ∈ N and n ∈ Z. Then there is c ∈ (B̃^+_log)^{φ^h=p^a} with c_σ = (σ − 1)·c for all σ ∈ G_K.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.17, p. 19, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez [13]; used in the Préface's proofs of 'dR ⇒ pst' (§2.3.2, §5.3). The chapters use a different result of [13] (Prop. 10.6.17 = [13, prop. 10.11]). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.18: height bound for sub-Spaces of (B_dR^+)^d; B_dR^+ contains no V^1
items.statement: If W is a sub-Espace de Banach de Dimension finie of (B_dR^+)^d and B_dR^+·W(C) is the B_dR^+-submodule of (B_dR^+)^d generated by W(C), then ht(W) ≥ rg_{B_dR^+}(B_dR^+·W(C)). In particular B_dR^+ does not contain V^1.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.18, p. 19, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.3.3: U_m and B_m as Espaces de Banach of Dimensions (m, 1) and (m, 0)
items.statement: For m ∈ N let U_m = (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p^m} and B_m = B_dR^+/t^m. They are the C-points of Espaces de Banach 𝕌_m, 𝔹_m of Dimensions (m, 1) and (m, 0), and the natural map U_m → B_m is surjective with kernel Q_p t^m.
items.locator: Préface §2.3.3, p. 19, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The exact sequence 0 → Q_p t^m → U_m → B_m → 0 is the fundamental exact sequence, restated in the chapters (Th. 6.4.1, §8.2.1.3) and planned for m = 1 at VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3 (node VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence); the Dimension statement in Colmez's formalism is not planned.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.19: the maps (x, y) ↦ ax + by between the spaces P_d = t^{−d}U_d
items.statement: Let P_d = t^{−d}U_d be the set of elements of B_e of degree ≤ d. Let a, b ∈ B_e be coprime of degrees n and m, and g_{a,b}(x, y) = ax + by. Then g_{a,b} : P_m ⊕ P_n → P_{n+m} is surjective with kernel Q_p·(−b, a), but g_{a,b} : P_{m−1} ⊕ P_{n−1} → P_{n+m−1} is not surjective (it is injective); P_d is the C-points of an Espace de Banach of Dimension (d, 1).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.19, p. 20, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof by comparing Dimensions. Not in the chapters or the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.20 ([28, prop. 6.2], [34]): Galois-equivariant continuous Q_p-linear maps C → C are K-scalars
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p and C = C_p. If λ : C → C is Q_p-linear, continuous and commutes with the action of G_K, then there is c ∈ K with λ(x) = cx for all x ∈ C.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.20, p. 20, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [28], Fourquaux [34]. Note 19: false with Q̄_p in place of C. Not in the atlas (R06.1 plans Ax–Sen–Tate and Tate–Sen, not this).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.21 ([28, th. 6.1]): continuous Q_p-linear G_K-maps between C-representations are C-linear
items.statement: If W_1, W_2 are C-representations of G_K (K/Q_p finite), every continuous Q_p-linear G_K-equivariant map W_1 → W_2 is C-linear.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.21, p. 20, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [28], via Théorème 2.20 and Sen's classification of C-representations [52]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.4: almost C-representations (presque C-représentations) and presentations
items.statement: An almost C-representation W is a Q_p-Banach space with a continuous action of G_K such that there are a C-representation W′ of G_K (a finite-dimensional C-space with a semilinear G_K-action) and finite-dimensional G_K-stable Q_p-subspaces V′ ⊂ W′, V ⊂ W with W/V ≅ W′/V′ as representations of G_K; the exact sequences 0 → V′ → W′ → W′/V′ → 0 and 0 → V → W → W′/V′ → 0 form a presentation of W.
items.locator: Préface §2.4, p. 20, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29]. Not in the chapters or the atlas (searched: almost C, presque). An accepted Part II route (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) plans 'Fontaine's almost C-representations, their dimension and height, the reduction of Ext-groups in C(G_K) to the categories of Q_p- and B^+_dR-representations, the finiteness, Euler-characteristic and duality theorem'; it has no stages yet, so the status stays missing, and this item should go to that roadmap.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.22(i) ([29, th. 5.1]): Dim of an almost C-representation is well defined
items.statement: If W is an almost C-representation with a presentation as above, Dim W = (dim W, ht W) with dim W = dim_C W′ and ht W = dim_{Q_p} V − dim_{Q_p} V′ depends only on W.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.22(i), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29]. Not in the atlas. An accepted Part II route (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) plans 'Fontaine's almost C-representations, their dimension and height, the reduction of Ext-groups in C(G_K) to the categories of Q_p- and B^+_dR-representations, the finiteness, Euler-characteristic and duality theorem'; it has no stages yet, so the status stays missing, and this item should go to that roadmap.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.22(ii) ([29, th. 5.1]): the category of almost C-representations is abelian with additive Dim
items.statement: If f : W_1 → W_2 is a morphism of almost C-representations, then Ker f, Im f and Coker f are almost C-representations, and Dim W_1 = Dim Ker f + Dim Im f, Dim W_2 = Dim Coker f + Dim Im f.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.22(ii), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29]. Not in the atlas. An accepted Part II route (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) plans 'Fontaine's almost C-representations, their dimension and height, the reduction of Ext-groups in C(G_K) to the categories of Q_p- and B^+_dR-representations, the finiteness, Euler-characteristic and duality theorem'; it has no stages yet, so the status stays missing, and this item should go to that roadmap.

items.name: Préface Exemple 2.23(i): U = (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p} is an almost C-representation of Dimension (1, 1)
items.statement: U = (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p} is an almost C-representation of Dimension (1, 1), since U/Q_p t = C.
items.locator: Préface Exemple 2.23(i), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Exemple 2.23(ii): B_2 = B_dR^+/t² is an almost C-representation of Dimension (2, 0)
items.statement: B_2 = B_dR^+/t² is an almost C-representation of Dimension (2, 0): for a suitable 2-dimensional G_K-stable Q_p-subspace V = Q_p t ⊕ Q_p a of U, the map U ⊗ V → B_2, u ⊗ v ↦ uv (mod t²), realises B_2 as the quotient of the almost C-representation U ⊗ V (of Dimension (2, 2)) by the 2-dimensional Q_p-representation spanned by t ⊗ t and t ⊗ a − a ⊗ t.
items.locator: Préface Exemple 2.23(ii), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed choice a = log[1 + p^♭] does not give a G_K-stable V (source issue E6); a = log[(1+p)^♭] (p-power roots of the unit 1+p) works. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.24(i): Galois cohomology of almost C-representations (Tate)
items.statement: For an almost C-representation W of G_K, the groups H^i(G_K, W) are finite-dimensional over Q_p, vanish for i ≥ 3, and dim H^0(G_K, W) − dim H^1(G_K, W) + dim H^2(G_K, W) = −[K : Q_p]·ht(W); this gives the independence of ht(W) from the presentation (the independence of dim W is much harder).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.24(i), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed text says 'nuls si i ≥ 2' (source issue E7; H^2(G_K, Q_p(1)) = Q_p). Special cases planned: H^i(G_K, C(n)) at PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem; the local Euler characteristic for finite-dimensional Q_p-representations was not found in the atlas (ArithmeticGaloisDuality plans the global formula R02.4/global-euler-characteristic and local duality D7).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.24(ii) ([29], corollary of th. 5.13): W′ can be taken to be C^d
items.statement: In the definition of an almost C-representation one may require W′ to be the trivial representation C^d.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.24(ii), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29, p. 355]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.25 ([29, th. 4.1]): maps from an extension of C by a representation onto C
items.statement: Let V be a Q_p-representation of G_K of dimension h, E an extension of C by V, and f : E → C continuous and G_K-equivariant with f(E) ≠ f(V). Then f is surjective and Ker f is a Q_p-representation of G_K of dimension h.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.25 with its proof sketch, pp. 21–22, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29]; the sketch shows every extension of C by V is of the form E_α ⊂ U(−1) ⊗ V and reduces to Proposition 2.9. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.26(i): almost C-representations are C-points of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie
items.statement: Every extension of C by a finite-dimensional representation is of the form E_α, which is the C-points of an Espace de Banach de Dimension finie; hence every almost C-representation can be 'analytified': the category of almost C-representations embeds into that of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.26(i), p. 22, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (see also Berger [6], not cited in the text).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.26(ii) and notes 20–21: the skew field D_K
items.statement: Let D_K be the ring of endomorphisms of the projective limit of the C/V, V running over finite-dimensional G_K-stable Q_p-subspaces of C. Then D_K is a (skew) field and there is an exact sequence 0 → K → D_K → (C ⊗ C)^{G_K} → K → 0, obtained by taking G_K-invariants of the sequence of Théorème 2.8 (for the G_K-action f^σ = f^{σ̃} − f^{σ̃}(0) on 𝒞); moreover (C ⊗ C_f)^{G_K} = (C ⊗ C)^{G_K}, C_f being the union of the finite-dimensional subrepresentations of C.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.26(ii), notes 20 and 21, p. 22, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Fontaine [29]; note 20 proves the equality (C ⊗ C_f)^{G_K} = (C ⊗ C)^{G_K}. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.27: B_dR^+-representations and X^r_st(D), X_dR(D) are almost C-representations
items.statement: The category of almost C-representations contains the B_dR^+-representations (B_dR^+-modules of finite length with a continuous semilinear G_K-action, [29, th. 5.13]) and the almost B_dR^+-representations; in particular for a filtered (φ, N)-module D, X^r_st(D) and X_dR(D) are almost C-representations whose Dimension equals that of the corresponding Espace de Banach, so 'fa ⇒ a' can be proved in the same way via almost C-representations.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.27, pp. 22–23, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.28(i) (Fontaine): Ext groups of almost C-representations and their Euler characteristic
items.statement: Let X, Y be almost C-representations of G_K. The groups Ext^i(X, Y) are finite-dimensional Q_p-spaces, zero for i > 2, and Σ_{i=0}^2 (−1)^i dim_{Q_p} Ext^i(X, Y) = −[K : Q_p]·ht(X)·ht(Y).
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.28(i), p. 23, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The sign (−1)^i is missing in the print (source issue E8). Not in the atlas. An accepted Part II route (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) plans 'Fontaine's almost C-representations, their dimension and height, the reduction of Ext-groups in C(G_K) to the categories of Q_p- and B^+_dR-representations, the finiteness, Euler-characteristic and duality theorem'; it has no stages yet, so the status stays missing, and this item should go to that roadmap.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.28(ii) (Fontaine): duality for Ext of almost C-representations
items.statement: For almost C-representations X, Y of G_K, Ext^i(X, Y) and Ext^{2−i}(Y, X(1)) are in duality.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.28(ii), p. 23, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. An accepted Part II route (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) plans 'Fontaine's almost C-representations, their dimension and height, the reduction of Ext-groups in C(G_K) to the categories of Q_p- and B^+_dR-representations, the finiteness, Euler-characteristic and duality theorem'; it has no stages yet, so the status stays missing, and this item should go to that roadmap.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.29 ([15, 47]): syntomic cohomology groups are Banach–Colmez spaces
items.statement: If X is a proper smooth algebraic variety over K̄ (i.e. over the algebraic closure), the syntomic cohomology groups H^i_Syn(X, r) are the C-points of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie; if X is defined over K they are moreover almost C-representations.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.29, p. 23, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez–Nizioł [15], Nizioł [47]; black box, not used later. The printed 'sur K' vs 'définie sur K' distinguishes K̄ and K (the bar is lost in the text file). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface §2.5.1: the rings E^I of analytic functions on annuli, the valuations v_r, v_J, and divisors
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ ]0, +∞], E^I is the ring of analytic functions defined over Q_p on the annulus C(I) = {v_p(T) ∈ I}. For r ∈ ]0, +∞] and f = Σ_k a_kT^k ∈ Q_p[T, T^{−1}], v_r(f) = inf_k (v_p(a_k) + kr), a multiplicative valuation; for a compact interval J, v_J = inf_{r∈J} v_r (an algebra valuation, v_J(fg) ≥ v_J(f) + v_J(g), not multiplicative unless J is a point), and v_J(f) = inf_{z∈C(J)} v_p(f(z)). E^I is the completion of Q_p[T, T^{−1}] for the family v_J, J ⊂ I compact; it is a Fréchet algebra (Banach if I is compact). A divisor on C(I) is a formal sum D = Σ n_x(x) with n_x ∈ N; it is locally finite if Σ_{x∈C(J)} n_x < ∞ for all compact J ⊂ I, and G_{Q_p}-invariant if n_{σ(x)} = n_x.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.1, p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/annulus-laurent-ring, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-multiplicative, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-maximum-principle, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/frechet-topology (stage P7:annulus-foundations); divisors of analytic functions on annuli are not planned. The print has 'v_J(f) = Σ_{z∈C(J)} v_p(f(z))' (source issue E9).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.30(i) (Lazard [43]): E^I is Bézout, principal for compact I; closed ideals are principal
items.statement: Let I be an interval of ]0, +∞]. E^I is a Bézout ring (principal if I is compact), and an ideal of E^I is closed if and only if it is principal.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.30(i), p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid (Lazard), RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout (closed ⇔ finitely generated ⇔ principal, Bézout), RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free. The RD.0 nodes treat Kedlaya's Γ_I, Γ_an,r (annuli near the boundary and closed annuli); discs and general intervals I ⊂ ]0, +∞] are covered only implicitly. Review: only compact I (RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid: 'for every closed interval I ⊆ [0, r_0), Γ_I is a principal ideal domain') and the boundary half-open annuli I = ]0, r] (RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout: Γ_an,r Bézout, closed ⇔ principal) are planned; open annuli ]a, b[ away from the boundary and the disc cases (+∞ ∈ I, e.g. the open unit disc ring E^{]0,+∞]}) are not stated anywhere, so the theorem as stated is missing. The general interval case of Lazard's theorem fits the source route to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0 with items 60, 61 and 64.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.30(ii) (Lazard [43]): closed ideals of E^I ↔ Galois-invariant locally finite divisors
items.statement: Let I be an interval of ]0, +∞]. Sending a closed ideal to the divisor of one of its generators is a bijection from the set of closed ideals of E^I onto the set of locally finite, G_{Q_p}-invariant divisors on C(I).
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.30(ii), p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Lazard's theorem; proof via Newton polygons (Remarque 2.31(i)). Nearest atlas nodes: PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/weierstrass-preparation-on-circles, PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/annulus-factor-theorem (zeros and factorisation on annuli), which do not state the divisor bijection. The analogous statement for the FF rings B_E(I) is restated in the chapters (Th. 2.7.4, Th. 3.5.5).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.31(ii): Lazard's theorem over a general complete valued field
items.statement: If Q_p is replaced by an arbitrary complete valued field L in the definition of the rings E^I, Théorème 2.30 remains true for compact I; for non-compact I it holds only if L is spherically complete.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.31(ii), p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Lazard [43]. Nearest: RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (mentions a statement 'for spherically complete K'). Not planned as stated.

items.name: Préface §2.5.1: the Robba ring R
items.statement: The Robba ring is R = lim_{→, r>0} E^{]0,r]}, the ring of analytic functions on the overconvergent annulus C(]0,0])^† = lim_{←, r>0} C(]0, r]).
items.locator: Préface §2.5.1, p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/robba-ring (stage P7:annulus-foundations), PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-ring.

items.name: Préface §2.5.1: the Robba ring is Bézout
items.statement: The Robba ring R is a Bézout ring.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.1, p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout ('for ℓ = k((t)) the Robba ring R is a Bézout domain'). The chapters prove Bézout for their Robba ring R_F (Cor. 3.5.8) in the perfect setting.

items.name: Préface §2.5.1: the only closed ideals of the Robba ring are 0 and R
items.statement: The only closed ideals of the Robba ring R (for its inductive limit topology) are {0} and R.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.1, p. 24, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas (RD.0 treats closed ideals of Γ_an,r, not of the inductive limit).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.32(iii): no Teichmüller expansions in B̃_rig; (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p²} is a genuine diamond
items.statement: It is false that every element z of B̃_rig can be written uniquely as Σ_{k∈Z} p^k[x_k] with x_k ∈ C^♭ subject to growth conditions; e.g. not every element of (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p²} has a unique expression Σ_{k∈Z} (p^{2k}[x^{p^{−k}}] + p^{2k+1}[y^{p^{−k}}]); the Espace de Banach (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p²} is 'really a diamond, and not an analytic space'.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.32(iii) and note 22, p. 25, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Warning remark without proof. Nearest atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iv): BC(O(λ)) is a perfectoid open ball for 0 < λ ≤ [E:Q_p], which excludes λ = 2 over Q_p) and the stage text of VB3:general-BC ('not every Banach–Colmez space is representable by a perfectoid space'); no node proves non-representability of BC(O(2)).

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.33 (Berger [3, prop. 3.2]): Frobenius-finite elements of B̃_rig lie in B̃^+_rig
items.statement: If x ∈ B̃_rig and the φ^n(x), n ∈ N, span a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space, then x ∈ B̃^+_rig.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.33, p. 25, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:P7/frobenius-regularisation ((b): a matrix A over B̃†_log with A = Pφ^{−1}(A), P ∈ GL_u(F), has entries in B̃^+_log), which implies this statement. Print: 'pour x ∈ N' (source issue E11).

items.name: Préface §2.5.2: the cyclotomic rings B_rig,Q_p, B^I_K, B_rig,K and B̃_rig,K
items.statement: Let π = [ε] − 1. B_rig,Q_p (resp. B^I_{Q_p}) is the closure of Q_p[π, π^{−1}] in B̃_rig (resp. B̃^I), and f ↦ f(π) is an isomorphism of topological rings R ≅ B_rig,Q_p (resp. E^I ≅ B^{I′}_{Q_p} with I′ = ((p−1)/p)I, for I ⊂ ]0, 1]). For K/Q_p finite, K_n = K(ζ_{p^n}), K_∞ = ∪K_n, χ the cyclotomic character, H_K = Ker χ|_{G_K}, Γ_K = G_K/H_K; B̃_rig,K = (B̃_rig)^{H_K}, B̃^I_K = (B̃^I)^{H_K}. There is r(K) > 0 such that for I ⊂ ]0, r(K)], B̃^I_K contains a unique étale extension B^I_K of B^I_{Q_p} with B̃^I_{Q_p} ⊗_{B^I_{Q_p}} B^I_K ≅ B̃^I_K; B_rig,K = lim_{→, r≤r(K)} B^{]0,r]}_K, and B̃_rig,Q_p ⊗_{B_rig,Q_p} B_rig,K ≅ B̃_rig,K.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.2, p. 25, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings, P7/robba-ring-of-p-adic-field, P7/robba-ring-tensor-identity, P7/berger-robba-identification; stage PG.0 (field-of-norms rings). The atlas records (PadicHodgeTheory/E1) that the coefficient field of B^†_rig,K is F′ = K_∞ ∩ K_0^nr, which the Préface's 'même type que pour K = Q_p' glosses over. The print says 'extension finie de F' with F undefined (source issue E12); it also prints I′ = (p/(p−1))I, which inverts the normalisation (with the Préface's w_r, w_r(π) = rp/(p−1) for r ≤ (p−1)/p, so the correct interval is ((p−1)/p)I).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.34(i) (Kedlaya): compact-interval rings are principal
items.statement: If 0 < r ≤ s, the rings B̃^{[r,s]} and B̃^{[r,s]}_K are principal ideal rings; if 0 < r < s ≤ r(K), B^{[r,s]}_K is a principal ideal ring.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.34(i), p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: B^{[r,s]}_K via Lazard (RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid, with P7/berger-robba-identification); B̃^{[r,s]} via RD.0/extended-robba-ring (Γ^alg_I is a PID) — the perfect cases are also restated in the chapters (Th. 2.5.1, Th. 3.5.1). Print: '[s,r]' (source issue E13). Review: RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid assumes 'ℓ discretely valued or trivially valued' and RD.0/extended-robba-ring ('for every closed interval I the ring Γ^alg_I is a PID') is only for ℓ^alg, the completed algebraic closure of k((t)); B̃^{[r,s]}_K is Kedlaya's Γ^ℓ_I for ℓ = the tilt of the completion of K_∞, which is perfect, not discretely valued and not algebraically closed, so its principality is not planned (the VB2 PID node is also only at an algebraically closed point). Only B̃^{[r,s]} and B^{[r,s]}_K are planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.34(ii) (Kedlaya): half-open rings are Bézout, closed ideals = principal ideals
items.statement: B̃^{]0,r]}, B̃^{]0,r]}_K and, if r ≤ r(K), B^{]0,r]}_K are Bézout rings, and in each of them an ideal is closed if and only if it is principal.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.34(ii), p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout, RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free, RD.0/extended-robba-ring; perfect case also FF Th. 3.5.7 and Prop. 3.5.2 (chapters). Kedlaya [37, th. 3.20], [38, prop. 2.6.8, th. 2.9.6]. Review: RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout assumes 'v_ℓ discrete (Remark 2.9.7: the implication closed ⇒ principal would need spherical completeness of ℓ otherwise)', and RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free assumes 'discreteness of v_ℓ'; RD.0/extended-robba-ring states Bézout only for the union R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con, not for the fixed-radius ring Γ^alg_an,r = B̃^{]0,r]}, and says nothing about B̃^{]0,r]}_K. Only B^{]0,r]}_K is planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.34(iii) (Kedlaya): B_rig,K, B̃_rig,K and B̃_rig are Bézout
items.statement: The rings B_rig,K, B̃_rig,K and B̃_rig are Bézout rings.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.34(iii), p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout (Robba ring), RD.0/extended-robba-ring (R^alg is Bézout); FF Cor. 3.5.8 in the chapters for the perfect Robba ring R_F. Review: B_rig,K (RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout with P7/berger-robba-identification) and B̃_rig = R^alg (RD.0/extended-robba-ring: 'R^alg is a Bézout domain') are planned, but B̃_rig,K = (B̃_rig)^{H_K}, Kedlaya's Γ^ℓ_an,con for ℓ the tilt of the completion of K_∞ (perfect, not discretely valued, not algebraically closed), is not, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.35 (Forster [32], Kedlaya [38, §2.8]): closed submodules of free modules are free
items.statement: Let R be B^{]0,r]}_K, B̃^{]0,r]}_K or B̃^{]0,r]}, and M a free R-module of rank d. A submodule of M is free if and only if it is closed, and then its rank is ≤ d.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.35, p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/closed-submodules-of-free-robba-modules (Forster, for B^{†,s}_rig,K), PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (closed submodules of finite free Γ_an,r-modules are free, for discretely valued ℓ). The converse 'free ⇒ closed' is implicit. Review: RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free has the hypothesis 'Enough r_0-units; discreteness of v_ℓ', so it does not cover ℓ^alg or the tilt of the completion of K_∞; with R06.3/closed-submodules-of-free-robba-modules only the case R = B^{]0,r]}_K is planned, and the cases B̃^{]0,r]}_K and B̃^{]0,r]} are not, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface Proposition 2.36: the Dieudonné–Manin classification over Q̆_p
items.statement: Let Q̆_p = W(F̄_p)[1/p]. Every φ-module M over Q̆_p has a canonical decomposition M ≅ ⊕_{λ∈Q} Q̆_p(λ)^{m_λ}, where for λ = d/h (h ≥ 1, (d, h) = 1) Q̆_p(λ) is the φ-module with basis e_1, …, e_h, φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i ≤ h − 1 and φ(e_h) = p^d e_1.
items.locator: Préface Proposition 2.36, p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Classical; used without statement in the chapters (e.g. pp. 286–287, 315). Nodes VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/slope-decomposition. Mathlib has only the rank-one case (mathlib:WittVector.isocrystal_classification, read: one-dimensional isocrystals over an algebraically closed field are standard), so not 'library'. Print: 'φ(e_h) = π^d e_1' (source issue E14).

items.name: Préface §2.5.3: φ-modules over B̃_rig, B̃_rig(λ), Frobenius slopes, isocline and étale modules
items.statement: A φ-module over B̃_rig is a free B̃_rig-module of finite rank with a bijective semilinear Frobenius φ. For λ ∈ Q, B̃_rig(λ) = B̃_rig ⊗_{Q̆_p} Q̆_p(λ). In a decomposition M ≅ ⊕ B̃_rig(λ)^{m_λ} the λ with m_λ ≠ 0 are the Frobenius slopes of M, the multiplicity of λ = d/h being h·m_λ; M is isocline if it has only one slope, and étale if it is isocline of slope 0.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.3, p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes RD.1/frobenius-module, RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules, RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module, RD.1/frobenius-slopes (over R^alg = B̃_rig for ℓ^alg = C^♭, cf. PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.37 (Kedlaya [37, th. 4.16], [38, th. 4.5.7]): Dieudonné–Manin decomposition over B̃_rig
items.statement: Every φ-module M over B̃_rig admits a decomposition M ≅ ⊕_{λ∈Q} B̃_rig(λ)^{m_λ}.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.37, p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring, with PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action identifying B̃†_rig with Γ^alg_an,con for ℓ^alg = C^♭. In the chapters it is only implicit (Cor. 11.2.22 + Th. 11.3.1 + Th. 8.2.10; Rem. 11.3.4 alludes to 'le théorème de Kedlaya de classification des φ-modules sur R_F'). The VB0 decomposition cites this Préface statement as a signpost.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.38(i): the slope filtration over B̃_rig is canonical, the decomposition is not
items.statement: The decomposition of Théorème 2.37 is not canonical (unlike the classical case); what is canonical is the increasing filtration by the M_µ = ⊕_{λ≤µ} B̃_rig(λ)^{m_λ}.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.38(i), p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node RD.1/dieudonne-manin-slopes-are-hn-slopes (the sum of summands of slope ≤ s_i is the HN filtration; 'when v_ℓ is nontrivial only the filtration is [canonical]'). The print has ⊕_{λ≥µ} (source issue E15).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.38(ii): degree of φ-modules over B̃_rig and the Harder–Narasimhan structure
items.statement: Let B̃^† ⊂ B̃_rig be the subring of bounded elements (= B̃_rig ∩ W(C^♭)[1/p]), with the valuation v_p of W(C^♭)[1/p]; v_p(φ(x)) = v_p(x) and (B̃_rig)^* = (B̃^†)^*. If M is a φ-module of rank 1 over B̃_rig with basis e, then φ(e) = λe with λ ∈ B̃^† and deg M := v_p(λ) does not depend on e; for M of rank d, deg M = deg(∧^d M). With rank and degree the category of φ-modules over B̃_rig is a Harder–Narasimhan category whose HN filtration is the filtration of (i) [38, 39].
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.38(ii), pp. 26–27, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes RD.1/degree-and-slope, RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration (with semistability inequalities reversed relative to bundles, which is the convention needed here), RD.1/dieudonne-manin-slopes-are-hn-slopes; units of R^alg: RD.0/extended-robba-ring. See source issue E15 on the sign convention.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.39 (Kedlaya's slope filtration theorem over B_rig,K, [37, th. 6.10], [38, th. 6.4.1], [39, th. 1.7.1])
items.statement: Let ∆ be a φ-module over B_rig,K (its slopes being those of B̃_rig ⊗ ∆; B^†_K = B_rig,K ∩ B̃^†). Then ∆ has a unique filtration 0 = ∆_0 ⊂ ∆_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ ∆_r = ∆ by saturated sub-φ-modules such that each ∆_i/∆_{i−1} is isocline, of slope λ_i with λ_1 < λ_2 < ⋯ < λ_r. Moreover ∆_i/∆_{i−1} has a unique φ-stable sub-B^†_K-module D_i with B_rig,K ⊗_{B^†_K} D_i ≅ ∆_i/∆_{i−1}. (Remarque 2.40: if ∆ is a (φ, Γ)-module, all these objects are Γ-stable, by uniqueness.)
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.39 and Remarque 2.40, p. 27, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement, RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (over the Robba ring of k((t)) with a Frobenius lift; B_rig,K is of this form in the variable π_K over F′, P7/berger-robba-identification).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.41(i): the representation attached to an étale (φ, Γ)-module
items.statement: If ∆ is an étale (φ, Γ)-module over B_rig,K (resp. B̃_rig,K), then V(∆) = (B̃_rig ⊗_{B_rig,K} ∆)^{φ=1} (resp. (B̃_rig ⊗_{B̃_rig,K} ∆)^{φ=1}) is a representation of G_K of dimension the rank of ∆.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.41(i), p. 27, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stage texts PG.1 (Fontaine's étale equivalence) and PG.2 (Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence and Robba realisation, étale objects); node PadicHodgeTheory:P7/robba-realisation-comparison imports them. The B̃_rig,K version is not explicit in the atlas. The Préface's proof combines [25], [9] (or [8]) and Kedlaya's Th. 2.39. Review: only the B_rig,K case is planned (PG.2 'Separate equivalence for étale objects'); the case of étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B̃_rig,K, which needs Kedlaya's descent from B̃_rig,K, is stated nowhere, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.41(ii): ∆̃(V) and its descent ∆(V) to B_rig,K
items.statement: If V is a representation of G_K, then ∆̃(V) = (B̃_rig ⊗ V)^{H_K} is a (φ, Γ)-module over B̃_rig,K of rank dim V, and ∆̃(V) contains a unique sub-B_rig,K-module ∆(V), stable by φ and Γ, such that B̃_rig,K ⊗_{B_rig,K} ∆(V) → ∆̃(V) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.41(ii), p. 27, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stage PG.2; node PadicHodgeTheory:P7/robba-realisation-comparison (D^†_rig(V)). The uniqueness of the descent inside ∆̃(V) is not explicitly stated in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.41(iii): étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B_rig,K and B̃_rig,K ≅ representations
items.statement: The functors V ↦ ∆(V), ∆ ↦ V(∆) (resp. V ↦ ∆̃(V), ∆ ↦ V(∆)) are mutually inverse and give equivalences {representations of G_K} ≅ {étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B_rig,K} ≅ {étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B̃_rig,K}.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.41(iii), p. 27, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stages PG.1–PG.2 plan the equivalence over B_K and its Robba realisation; the B̃_rig,K (perfect) form and Kedlaya's input (étale over B_rig,K ⇔ étale over B^†_K) are not explicit. Rem. 5.10(iv) of the Préface / FF §11.5 give the decompletion B̃_rig,K ↔ B_rig,K. Review: only the equivalence with étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B_rig,K is planned (PG.1–PG.2); the second equivalence, with étale (φ, Γ)-modules over B̃_rig,K, is not, so the item is missing.

items.name: Préface §2.5.5: localisation maps ι_n : B̃^{]0,r]} → B_dR^+, models ∆^{]0,r]} and ∆^+_dif,n
items.statement: Let ω = π/φ^{−1}(π) = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + ⋯ + [ε^{1/p}]^{p−1}; ω generates Ker θ in A_inf, A_inf/(φ^n(ω)) ≅ O_C and the completion of A_inf[1/p] localised at φ^n(ω) is B_dR^+ for every n ∈ N. For p^{−n} ≤ r the completed localisation of B̃^{]0,r]} at φ^n(ω) is B_dR^+ (φ^n(ω) is invertible if p^{−n} > r); ι_n : B̃^{]0,r]} → B_dR^+ commutes with G_K and ι_{n+1}(φ(x)) = ι_n(x); ι_n(π) = ζ_{p^n}e^{t/p^n} − 1, and ι_n(B^{]0,r]}_K) ⊂ K_n[[t]] for p^{−n} ≤ r ≤ r(K). A (φ, Γ)-module ∆ over B_rig,K is the inductive limit of sub-B^{]0,r]}_K-modules ∆^{]0,r]} (0 < r ≤ r(∆)) with B_rig,K ⊗ ∆^{]0,r]} ≅ ∆, ∆^{]0,r]} Γ-stable and B^{]0,r/p]}_K ⊗_{φ(B^{]0,r]}_K)} φ(∆^{]0,r]}) ≅ ∆^{]0,r/p]}; for r_n = v_p(ζ_{p^n} − 1) = 1/((p−1)p^{n−1}) ≤ r(∆), ∆^+_dif,n = K_n[[t]] ⊗_{B^{]0,r_n]}_K} ∆^{]0,r_n]} with localisation ι_n.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.5, p. 28, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7/localisation-maps-p-adic-field, P7/extended-localisation-maps, P7/fontaine-dif-module, R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta; models D^{†,r}: stage PG.2 and P7/robba-realisation-comparison. The atlas normalises radii as r_n = p^{n−1}(p−1) (reciprocal convention).

items.name: Préface §2.5.6: the ring B_log,K = B_rig,K[log π] with φ, Γ and N
items.statement: B_log,K = B_rig,K[log π] with ϕ(log π) = p log π + log(ϕ(π)/π^p), γ(log π) = log π + log(γ(π)/π), and the B_rig,K-linear derivation N with N(log π) = −p/(p−1); ι_n(log π) = log(ζ_{p^n}e^{t/p^n} − 1), so ι_n(B_log,K) ⊂ K_n[[t]]. B̃_log = B̃_rig ⊗_{B_rig,K} B_log,K = B̃_rig[log π] contains log[p^♭] and hence the ring B̃^+_log = B̃^+_rig[log[p^♭]] of §2.1.1, compatibly with φ, N and G_K.
items.locator: Préface §2.5.6, p. 28, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/cyclotomic-log-robba-ring, P7/log-extended-period-rings, P7/extended-localisation-maps (which records log[ε − 1] = (p/(p−1))u + (element of B̃^+_rig)). The printed expression of log[p^♭] in terms of log π has p/(p−1) and (p−1)/p interchanged (source issue E16).

items.name: Préface §2.5.6: Berger's (φ, Γ)-module ∆(D) attached to a filtered (φ, N)-module
items.statement: For a (φ, N)-module D of rank h over K_0 put ∆_0(D) = (B_log,K ⊗_{K_0} D)^{N=0}, a (φ, Γ)-module over B_rig,K. For D filtered over K and r ≤ r(K) put ∆_0^{]0,r]}(D) = (B^{]0,r]}_K[log π] ⊗_{K_0} D)^{N=0} and ∆^{]0,r]}(D) = {z ∈ ∆_0^{]0,r]}(D)[1/t] : ι_n(z) ∈ Fil^0(K_n((t)) ⊗_K D_K) for all n ≥ n(r)}; ∆(D) = B_rig,K ⊗_{B^{]0,r]}_K} ∆^{]0,r]}(D).
items.locator: Préface §2.5.6, p. 28, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berger [4]. Not in the atlas (P7 plans Berger's Robba realisation of representations and B^†_log,K, but not the modification ∆(D) of filtered (φ, N)-modules). The chapters' analogue is the bundle E(D) (Déf. 10.2.1, Prop. 10.6.2).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.42(i) (Berger [4, th. II.1.6]): ∆(D) is a (φ, Γ)-module of rank h independent of r
items.statement: For a filtered (φ, N)-module D of rank h over K, the B_rig,K-module ∆(D) = B_rig,K ⊗_{B^{]0,r]}_K} ∆^{]0,r]}(D) does not depend on the choice of r and is a (φ, Γ)-module of rank h over B_rig,K.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.42(i) with proof sketch, pp. 28–29, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof uses N nilpotent (∆_0^{]0,r]}(D) ≅ B^{]0,r]}_K ⊗ D), a Chinese remainder theorem for finitely generated B^{]0,r]}_K-modules and Th. 2.35. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.42(ii) (Berger [4, th. II.2.6, IV.2.1]): D ↦ ∆(D) is exact, tensor, and respects HN filtrations
items.statement: The functor D ↦ ∆(D) is an exact ⊗-functor which respects Harder–Narasimhan filtrations (every direct-factor sub-(φ, Γ)-module of ∆(D) is ∆(D′) for a sub-(φ, N)-module D′, and deg ∆(D) = deg D).
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.42(ii) with proof sketch, pp. 29, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. The degree comparison depends on the sign conventions discussed in source issues E2 and E15.

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.43(ii): D weakly admissible ⇔ ∆(D) étale; hence 'fa ⇒ a'
items.statement: A filtered (φ, N)-module D is weakly admissible if and only if ∆(D) is étale; since V_st(D) = (B̃_rig ⊗ ∆(D))^{φ=1}, Théorème 2.41 then gives 'weakly admissible ⇒ admissible'.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.43(ii), p. 29, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berger's proof of Colmez–Fontaine. The atlas plans Colmez–Fontaine (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem, 'proved in R06.3') but not this route.

items.name: Préface §2.5.7: the connection ∇ on ∆(V) and Berger's modification N(V) of a de Rham representation
items.statement: For V a representation of G_K and ∆(V) its (φ, Γ)-module over B_rig,K, (γ − 1)/(χ(γ) − 1) has a limit ∇ as γ → 1, a connection on ∆(V) acting on B_rig,K as ∇ = t∂ with ∂ = (1 + π)d/dπ. If V is de Rham of dimension d with Hodge–Tate weights ≤ 0, then K_n[[t]] ⊗_K D_dR(V) is a K_n[[t]]-lattice in ∆^+_dif,n (r_n ≤ r(∆)) and N^{]0,r]} = {z ∈ ∆^{]0,r]} : ι_n(z) ∈ K_n[[t]] ⊗_K D_dR(V) for all n ≥ n(r)} is a sub-B^{]0,r]}_K-module of rank d, stable by Γ and ∇, with ∇(N^{]0,r]}) ⊂ tN^{]0,r]} and N^{]0,r/p]} = B^{]0,r/p]}_K ⊗_{φ(B^{]0,r]}_K)} φ(N^{]0,r]}); hence N(V) = B_rig,K ⊗ N^{]0,r]} is a φ-module over B_rig,K with the connection ∂ (∂ ∘ φ = pφ ∘ ∂).
items.locator: Préface §2.5.7, p. 30, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:P7/nabla-operator-on-robba-ring, P7/connection-on-robba-realisation, R06.3/de-rham-lattice-Ns, R06.3/de-rham-differential-equation, R06.3/de-rham-differential-equation-has-frobenius-structure (Berger [3, §5]).

items.name: Préface Théorème 2.44 (Tsuzuki [55]): étale (φ, ∂)-modules over B^†_K have finite local monodromy
items.statement: If D is an étale (φ, ∂)-module over B^†_K, there is a finite extension L of K such that ∂ is trivial on B^†_L ⊗ D.
items.locator: Préface Théorème 2.44, p. 30, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy (unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over R^bd become horizontal after a finite separable extension of k((t))); translating 'finite separable extension of the residue field of B^†_K' into 'finite extension L of K' uses the field of norms (stage PG.0). Not used in the chapters (they prove dR ⇒ pst with bundles, §10.6).

items.name: Préface Remarque 2.45 (Berger [4, th. III.2.4]): the monodromy theorem for non-étale (φ, Γ)-modules
items.statement: The argument of §2.5.7 extends to (φ, Γ)-modules ∆ over B_rig,K that are not necessarily étale, the hypothesis 'V de Rham' being replaced by '(B_dR ⊗_{K_n[[t]]} ∆^+_dif,n)^{G_K} has dimension rg ∆ over K': such ∆ are potentially semistable (become log-crystalline after a finite extension).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 2.45, p. 30, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berger [4]. The atlas plans the monodromy theorem for Galois representations only (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/p-adic-monodromy-theorem). The chapters' bundle version (Th. 10.6.10) covers the corresponding statement via Th. 11.5.1.

items.name: Préface Exemple 2.46: the (G_K, B)-pairs M(V), M(D), M(∆); V ↦ M(V) is fully faithful
items.statement: To a Q_p-representation V of G_K, a filtered (φ, N)-module D over K, and a (φ, Γ)-module ∆ over B_rig,K one attaches the (G_K, B)-pairs M(V) = (B_cris^{φ=1} ⊗ V, B_dR^+ ⊗ V), M(D) = ((B̃^+_log[1/t] ⊗ D)^{N=0,φ=1}, Fil^0(B_dR ⊗_K D_K)), M(∆) = ((B̃_rig[1/t] ⊗_{B_rig,K} ∆)^{φ=1}, B_dR^+ ⊗_{K_n[[t]]} ι_n(∆^{]0,r_n]})). Since V = M_e(V) ∩ M_dR^+(V), V ↦ M(V) is an equivalence of the category of representations of G_K onto a subcategory of (G_K, B)-pairs.
items.locator: Préface Exemple 2.46, p. 31, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: B-pairs are not in the atlas (searched 'B-pair'). The chapters compute the B-pair of E(D, φ, N) (Cor. 10.3.17) and state bundles ≅ B-pairs (§10.1.2, p. 315).

items.name: Préface Corollaire 3.3: the closed prime ideals of A_E
items.statement: The closed prime ideals of A_E = O_E ⊗_{W(k_E)} A_inf (C^♭ algebraically closed) are: (0), with residue field Fr(A_E); the maximal ideal, with residue field k_{C^♭} = k_C; (π), with residue field C^♭; the ideals (π − [a]) for a ∈ m_{C^♭} − {0} (up to equivalence), with residue field C_a algebraically closed of characteristic 0, complete for v_p, with C_a^♭ ≅ C^♭; and W(m_{C^♭}) (denoted ([π^♭])), with residue field Ĕ. Everything follows from Théorème 3.1 except that C_a is algebraically closed ([FF, prop. 2.2.19], [53, prop. 3.8]). (Note 26: without closedness, Zorn's lemma produces exotic maximal ideals from elements whose Newton polygon has infinitely many slopes.)
items.locator: Préface Corollaire 3.3 and note 26, pp. 32–33, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Préface-only list (the chapters prove the ingredients: Th. 2.4.1–2.4.6, Prop. 2.2.19, Cor. 2.2.22). The atlas plans the untilt ↔ primitive degree-one ideal correspondence (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence) but not the classification of all closed primes of A_E.

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.10(ii) (Berger [5, rem. 1.1.3]): B_E^+ is not Bézout
items.statement: The ring B_E^+ (closure of A_E[1/π] in B_E) is not a Bézout ring. (Colmez adds, as a guess by analogy with equal characteristic, that B_E is probably not Bézout either, at least if C^♭ is not maximally complete.)
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.10(ii), p. 35, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box from Berger [5]; the second sentence is a heuristic, not a claim. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.17 and §3.3: Spa A_E, the function δ, Y_E^ad = δ^{−1}(]0, +∞[) and X_E^ad = Y_E^ad/φ^Z
items.statement: ([54, prop. 13.1.1].) Spec(A_E) can be analytified: let δ : Spa A_E → [0, +∞] be δ(x) = v_x(π)/v_x([π^♭]), v_x the real-valued valuation determined by x. Then Y_E^ad is the inverse image of ]0, +∞[ under δ. One has δ(φ(x)) = qδ(x), so φ acts properly discontinuously on Y_E^ad and one may form the quotient X_E^ad = Y_E^ad/φ^Z.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.17 and §3.3, p. 38, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Tau Ceti layer 6 defines 𝒴 = {v ∈ Spa(A_inf, A_inf) : v(p[ϖ]) ≠ 0} with the radius κ (κ(φ(v)) = pκ(v)), the wandering windows and the quotient 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^Z; FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0 reuses it; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y, RF0:annuli (node RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli) and RF1 (node RF1/frobenius-quotient-and-presentation) for general E. Colmez's δ is the reciprocal of the atlas's κ (up to normalisation). The chapters construct the curve via the rings B_I and the ind-scheme (Prop. 6.7.1, Rem. 11.2.8), not via Spa A_E.

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.19 (first bullet): diamond identities behind |Y_E| ≅ |D̃^×_C|/O_E^*
items.statement: Spd E ≅ Spd Ê_∞ / Gal(E_∞/E) with Gal(E_∞/E) ≅ O_E^* (E_∞ the Lubin–Tate tower), and the bijection |Y_E| ≅ |D̃^×_C|/O_E^* is a manifestation of the equality of diamonds Spd Ê_∞ × Spd C ≅ Spd(Ê_∞^♭) × Spd(C^♭) ≅ (D̃^×_{C^♭})^◇ = (D̃^×_C)^◇.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.19, p. 38, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Diamond-theoretic reinterpretation ([54, 22]); not proved in the Préface. The atlas plans the untilt product formula (next item) but not this Lubin–Tate/perfectoid-disc identification.

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.19 (second bullet): E^◇ × C^◇ ≅ Y_E (diamond form of Proposition 3.4)
items.statement: Proposition 3.4 (|Y_E| = E-untilts of C^♭) is a manifestation of the equality of diamonds Spd E × Spd C ≅ Y_E^◇.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.19, p. 38, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F1 (α_F : Y_F^◇ ≅ Spa(F) × Spd Q_p, E = Q_p), RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y (node RF0:integral-Y/untilt-functor-of-points, FS II.1.2: 𝒴_S^◇ ≅ Spd O_E × S) and RF1 (node RF1/diamond-formula-and-map-to-base).

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.19 (third bullet; Weinstein [56]): π_1((E^◇ × C^◇)/(1 × φ)) = G_E
items.statement: (Black box, [56], the version of Théorème 3.15 for X_E^ad.) π_1((Spd E × Spd C)/(1 × φ)) = G_E.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.19, p. 38, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Weinstein, 'The Galois group of Q_p as a geometric fundamental group'. The algebraic statement (X_E geometrically simply connected, Th. 3.15) is restated in the chapters (Th. 8.6.1); the diamond version is not in the atlas (FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 plans (X_F)_fét ≅ (X_F^◇)_fét, which is an ingredient).

items.name: Préface Remarque 3.19 (third bullet): π_1((E^◇ × E^◇)/(1 × φ)) = G_E × G_E (analogue of Drinfeld's lemma)
items.statement: Since Spd C/G_E ≅ Spd E, one also has π_1((Spd E × Spd E)/(1 × φ)) = G_E × G_E, an arithmetic analogue of Drinfeld's lemma.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 3.19, p. 38, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequence of [56]. The atlas plans Drinfeld's lemma for function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.4) and a version in FS IV.7 (VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 stage text), not this statement.

items.name: Préface Remarque 4.4(i): H^1(X_E, O(λ)) computed at any classical point
items.statement: If λ = d/h < 0, then for every y ∈ |Y_E|, H^1(X_E, O_{X_E}(λ)) ≅ B_dR^+(K_y)/(t_y^{−d}B_dR^+(K_y) + E_h) — somewhat disturbing since B_dR^+(K_y) depends on y as a topological ring ([40]).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 4.4(i), p. 40, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: stage VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 ('Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology with actual Frobenius maps and signs', integer n only) and node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5: H^1 as a Banach–Colmez space); neither states the explicit quotient at an arbitrary classical point y or for fractional λ. The chapters give the formula at ∞ (Prop. 8.2.3). The print has t_y^d (source issue E24).

items.name: Préface Remarque 4.4(ii): cohomology of O(λ) as Espaces de Banach and its Euler characteristic (d, h)
items.statement: The cohomology groups of O_{X_E}(λ), λ = d/h, are the C-points of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie ℍ^i(X_E, O_{X_E}(λ)), and Dim ℍ^0(X_E, O(λ)) − Dim ℍ^1(X_E, O(λ)) = (d, h).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 4.4(ii), p. 40, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
