items.note: Representability of H^0, H^1 as FS-style BC spaces is planned (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists), but the Dimension (dim, ht) calculus of Colmez is not.

items.name: Préface Remarque 4.6(iv): Euler–Poincaré characteristic of a bundle in Banach–Colmez Dimensions
items.statement: If ℰ is a vector bundle on X_E, its cohomology groups are the C-points of Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie ℍ^i(X_E, ℰ), and Dim ℍ^0(X_E, ℰ) − Dim ℍ^1(X_E, ℰ) = (deg ℰ, rg ℰ).
items.locator: Préface Remarque 4.6(iv), p. 40, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Remarque 4.4(ii) and the classification (Th. 4.5). Not in the atlas (see previous item).

items.name: Préface §5.4: infinitely ramified Galois extensions of Lie type are perfectoid
items.statement: Let K_∞ be an infinitely ramified Galois extension of K of Lie type (Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) a p-adic Lie group). Then K_∞ (i.e. its completion) is perfectoid; its tilt K_∞^♭ is a closed subfield of C^♭ with a continuous action of Γ, and Gal(C^♭/K_∞^♭) = Gal(C/K_∞).
items.locator: Préface §5.4, p. 46, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof (Sen; such extensions are arithmetically profinite). The Galois-group identification is the tilting equivalence, restated in the chapters (Th. 3.2.1, Th. 3.3.1) and planned at PerfectoidSpaces:P3 (node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger). The perfectoidness is planned only for the cyclotomic tower (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension).

items.name: Préface Remarque 5.10(ii): the descended diagram of categories over K_∞^♭; failure of essential surjectivity
items.statement: Adding a G_K-action to the diagram of Remarque 4.9 and descending to K_∞ by Théorème 5.9 gives a diagram {G_K-bundles on X} ≅ {(G_K, B)-pairs}, {Γ-bundles on X_{K_∞}} ← {(φ, Γ)-modules over B^+(K_∞^♭)} → {(φ, Γ)-modules over K_0}, GAGA to {Γ-bundles on X^an_{K_∞}} ← {(φ, Γ)-modules over B(K_∞^♭)} ≅ {(φ, Γ)-modules over R(K_∞^♭)}; the functor {(φ, Γ)-modules over B^+(K_∞^♭)} → {(φ, Γ)-modules over B(K_∞^♭)} is not essentially surjective, unlike the algebraically closed case.
items.locator: Préface Remarque 5.10(ii), p. 47, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The non-essential-surjectivity claim is stated without proof (compare FF Rem. 11.1.11 for F not algebraically closed). Not in the atlas.

items.name: §1.1: standing hypotheses and notation (E, π, q, Frob_q, F, v, |·|, ϖ_F)
items.statement: E is a complete field for a discrete valuation with residue field the finite field F_q, q = p^{f_E}; π is a chosen uniformizer of O_E (written π_E when the dependence on E matters). If E has characteristic p then E = F_q((π)); if E has characteristic 0 then E|Q_p (finite). Frob_q is the f_E-th power of the Frobenius of an O_E-algebra of characteristic p. F is a perfect field of characteristic p, an extension of F_q, complete for a nontrivial valuation v: F → ℝ ∪ {+∞}; |·| = q^{−v(·)}, m_F = {x ∈ O_F | v(x) > 0}, k_F is the residue field, and ϖ_F denotes any element of F with 0 < |ϖ_F| < 1.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 52, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The same data are fixed in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 (general local field E, perfectoid base over F_q) and in AdicSpaces Layer 6 (F complete rank-one perfect of characteristic p with pseudouniformizer ϖ, but only E = Q_p).

items.name: §1.2.1: ramified Witt polynomials W_{n,π}
items.statement: Assume E has characteristic 0. For n ≥ 0 put W_{n,π} = Σ_{i=0}^{n} π^i X_i^{q^{n−i}} ∈ O_E[X_0, …, X_n], and let 𝓕 be the functor O_E-algebras → Sets, A ↦ A^ℕ; an element of 𝓕(A) is written [x_i]_{i≥0}.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 53, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: Lemme 1.2.1: existence and uniqueness of the π-Witt vector functor W_{O_E,π}
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) There is a unique factorization of 𝓕: O_E-algebras → Sets through a functor W_{O_E,π}: O_E-algebras → O_E-algebras such that the natural transformation W_{π,A}: W_{O_E,π}(A) → A^ℕ, [a_i]_{i≥0} ↦ (W_{n,π}(a_0, …, a_n))_{n≥0}, is a morphism of O_E-algebras.
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.1, p. 53, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: Lemme 1.2.1 (proof): image of the π-ghost map (Dwork criterion)
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) If A is an O_E-algebra without p-torsion equipped with an endomorphism ϕ lifting Frob_q modulo π, then W_{π,A} is injective with image {(x_i)_{i≥0} ∈ A^ℕ | x_{i+1} ≡ ϕ(x_i) mod π^{i+1} for all i}.
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.1, démonstration, p. 53, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing for general π. The p-typical analogue is planned as KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5/ghost-image-criterion; Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: change of uniformizer u_{π,π′}
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) Since the image of W_{π,A} (A p-torsion free with Frobenius lift) depends only on the ideal (π), for another uniformizer π′ there is a unique isomorphism of functors on O_E-algebras u_{π,π′}: W_{O_E,π} ≅ W_{O_E,π′} with W_{π′} ∘ u_{π,π′} = W_π; moreover u_{π′,π″} ∘ u_{π,π′} = u_{π,π″}.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 53, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0's stage text plans 'uniformizer-change comparisons' only for W_{O_E}(R) with R a perfect F_q-algebra; the functor-level statement for all O_E-algebras is not planned. Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: Définition 1.2.2: the ramified Witt vector functor W_{O_E} and its ghost map
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) W_{O_E} = lim_{←, π} W_{O_E,π}: O_E-algebras → O_E-algebras, the projective limit over all uniformizers π of O_E along the u_{π,π′}; W: W_{O_E}(A) → A^ℕ is the composite W_{O_E}(A) ≅ W_{O_E,π}(A) → A^ℕ. Like W_{O_E}, the morphism W: W_{O_E}(−) → (−)^ℕ does not depend on the choice of uniformizer.
items.locator: Définition 1.2.2, p. 54, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: Teichmüller lift, Frobenius F and Verschiebung V_π on W_{O_E}
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) For a ∈ A put [a] = [a, 0, 0, …] ∈ W_{O_E,π}(A); since u_{π,π′}([a]) = [a] this defines a Teichmüller lift [−]: A → W_{O_E}(A) independent of π. There is a unique endomorphism F of W_{O_E}(−) such that W(Fa) = (x_{i+1})_{i≥0} whenever W(a) = (x_i)_{i≥0}; F does not depend on π. V_π: W_{O_E}(−) → W_{O_E}(−) is deduced from the shift [a_i]_{i≥0} ↦ [0, a_0, a_1, …] on W_{O_E,π} via W_{O_E} ≅ W_{O_E,π}; it depends on π.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 54, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: relations between F and V_π
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) F V_π = π; V_{π′} = (π′/π) V_π for another uniformizer π′; V_π(F(x)·y) = x·V_π(y). Consequently, for every n ≥ 1, V_π^n W_{O_E} is an ideal of W_{O_E} independent of the choice of π.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 54, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: V_π-adic completeness and V_π-expansions of ramified Witt vectors
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) For every O_E-algebra A, W_{O_E}(A) is V_π-adically separated and complete: with W_{O_E,n}(A) = W_{O_E}(A)/V_π^n W_{O_E}(A), the natural map W_{O_E}(A) → lim_{n≥1} W_{O_E,n}(A) is an isomorphism; every a ∈ W_{O_E}(A) can be written uniquely as Σ_{n≥0} V_π^n [a_n] with a_n ∈ A.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 54, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: V_π F = π and the Frobenius formula over F_q-algebras
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) If A is an F_q-algebra then V_π F = π and F(Σ_{n≥0} V_π^n [a_n]) = Σ_{n≥0} V_π^n [a_n^q].
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 54, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: W_{O_E}(A) for A perfect is the unique π-adic lift
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) If A is a perfect F_q-algebra, W_{O_E}(A) is π-adically complete and without π-torsion, every element can be written uniquely as Σ_{n≥0} [x_n] π^n with x_n ∈ A, and W_{O_E}(A) is, up to unique isomorphism, the unique π-adically complete π-torsion-free lift of the O_E-algebra A (i.e. with W_{O_E}(A)/π = A).
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 55, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property states exactly this (unique π-adically complete flat O_E-lift with unique multiplicative section, W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗̂_{W(F_q)} O_E). For E = Q_p Mathlib has W(R) p-adically complete (mathlib:WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP) and the existence (not uniqueness) of Teichmüller series (mathlib:WittVector.dvd_sub_sum_teichmuller_iterateFrobeniusEquiv_coeff).

items.name: Lemme 1.2.3: the comparison morphism u: W_{O_E}(A) → W_{O_{E′}}(A)
items.statement: Let E′|E be a finite extension (characteristic 0), f = f_{E′/E}, π′ a uniformizer of E′. There is a unique morphism of O_E-algebras u: W_{O_E}(A) → W_{O_{E′}}(A), natural in the O_{E′}-algebra A, such that the ghost map W = (W_n)_{n≥0} of W_{O_{E′}} satisfies W ∘ u = (W_{f n})_{n≥0}. One has u([a]) = [a], u(V_π x) = (π/π′) V_{π′}(u(F_E^{f−1} x)) (printed with F^{f−1} applied after u; corrected, see source issues) and u(F_E^{f} x) = F_{E′} u(x).
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.3, p. 55, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: the natural morphism Δ: W_{O_E} → W_{O_E}∘W_{O_E}
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0; recalled.) There is a unique natural morphism of O_E-algebras Δ: W_{O_E}(−) → W_{O_E}(W_{O_E}(−)) such that W(Δ(x)) = (F^n x)_{n≥0}.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 55, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: base change W_{O_E}(A) ⊗_{O_{E′_0}} O_{E′} → W_{O_{E′}}(A), an isomorphism for perfect A
items.statement: Let E′|E be finite (characteristic 0), F_{q′}|F_q the residue extension and E′_0 the maximal unramified extension of E in E′, so that W_{O_E}(F_{q′}) = O_{E′_0}. For an O_{E′}-algebra A, the composite O_{E′_0} = W_{O_E}(F_{q′}) →^Δ W_{O_E}(O_{E′_0}) → W_{O_E}(A) makes W_{O_E}(A) an O_{E′_0}-algebra, u is O_{E′_0}-linear, and one gets a natural morphism W_{O_E}(A) ⊗_{O_{E′_0}} O_{E′} → W_{O_{E′}}(A) under which F_E^{f_{E′/E}} ⊗ Id corresponds to F_{E′}. If A is a perfect F_{q′}-algebra this morphism is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §1.2.1, p. 55, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the case E = Q_p (next item) is planned, in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property. Missing at FF's generality (arbitrary O_E-algebras, E|Q_p ramified). Mathlib only has p-typical Witt vectors (the case O_E = Z_p, pi = p): mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:WittVector.ghostMap, mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller, mathlib:WittVector.frobenius, mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung. The atlas plans W_{O_E}(R) only for perfect F_q-algebras R (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); no node plans the pi-typical Witt functor of a general O_E-algebra.

items.name: §1.2.1: W(A) ⊗_{O_{E_0}} O_E ≅ W_{O_E}(A) for perfect A
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) Let E_0 be the maximal unramified extension of Q_p in E and W = W_{Q_p} the usual Witt vectors. For every perfect F_q-algebra A there is a canonical isomorphism W(A) ⊗_{O_{E_0}} O_E ≅ W_{O_E}(A), via which [a] ⊗ 1 ↦ [a] and F^{f_E} ⊗ Id ↔ F.
items.locator: §1.2.1, pp. 55–56, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property: 'W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗̂_{W(F_q)} O_E'. The Frobenius compatibility is part of the RF0 stage text (Teichmüller representatives, Frobenius).

items.name: Proposition 1.2.4 (1): the Q-twisted Witt functor W_{O_E,Q,π}
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) Let Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q ≡ X^q mod π, Q_0 = X and Q_n = Q ∘ ⋯ ∘ Q (n times) for n ≥ 1, and W_{n,Q,π} = Σ_{i=0}^{n} π^i Q_{n−i}(X_i) ∈ O_E[X_0, …, X_n]. There is a unique factorization of 𝓕: O_E-algebras → Sets, A ↦ A^ℕ, through a functor W_{O_E,Q,π}: O_E-algebras → O_E-algebras such that W_{Q,π,A}: W_{O_E,Q,π}(A) → A^ℕ, [a_i]_{i≥0} ↦ (W_{n,Q,π}(a_0, …, a_n))_{n≥0}, is a morphism of O_E-algebras.
items.locator: Proposition 1.2.4 (1), p. 56, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing. No atlas node plans Lubin-Tate-twisted Teichmueller lifts [x]_Q or [x]_LT; the nearest node is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2), which uses the untwisted series sum_i pi^i [X^{q^{-i}}]. Mathlib/Tau Ceti have no Lubin-Tate formal groups (only the formal group of a Weierstrass curve in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup).

items.name: Proposition 1.2.4 (2): W_{O_E,Q,π} ≅ W_{O_E,π}
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) There is a unique isomorphism u_{Q,π}: W_{O_E,Q,π} → W_{O_E,π} with W_π ∘ u_{Q,π} = W_{Q,π}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.2.4 (2), p. 57, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

Mathlib/Tau Ceti have no Lubin-Tate formal groups (only the formal group of a Weierstrass curve in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup).

items.name: Lemme 1.2.5: image of the Q-ghost map
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0, Q as in Prop. 1.2.4.) Let A be an O_E-algebra without π-torsion equipped with a lift ϕ of Frob_q mod π. Then W_{Q,π,A} is injective with image {(x_i)_{i∈ℕ} | x_{i+1} ≡ ϕ(x_i) mod π^{i+1} for all i}.
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.5, p. 57, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Lemme 1.2.6: Q raises congruences modulo powers of π
items.statement: (Q ∈ O_E[X], Q ≡ X^q mod π.) Let A be an O_E-algebra, i ≥ 1 and x, y ∈ A with x ≡ y mod π^i. Then Q(x) ≡ Q(y) mod π^{i+1}.
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.6, p. 57, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 1.2.7 (general A): the Q-Teichmüller lift [−]_Q
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0, Q as in Prop. 1.2.4.) There is a unique map [−]_Q: A → W_{O_E}(A), natural in the O_E-algebra A, such that W([a]_Q) = (Q_n(a))_{n≥0}. It satisfies Q([a]_Q) = [Q(a)]_Q, and every element of W_{O_E}(A) can be written uniquely as Σ_{n≥0} V_π^n [a_n]_Q.
items.locator: Proposition 1.2.7, p. 57, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 1.2.7 (perfect A): Q-Teichmüller expansions and the limit formula
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) If A is a perfect F_q-algebra, every element of W_{O_E}(A) can be written uniquely as Σ_{n≥0} [x_n]_Q π^n; x ↦ [x]_Q is the unique lift satisfying Q([x]_Q) = [x^q]_Q; and [x]_Q = lim_{n→+∞} Q_n([x^{q^{−n}}]). More generally, if x̂_n is any lift of x^{q^{−n}} to W_{O_E}(A), then [x]_Q = lim_{n→+∞} Q_n(x̂_n).
items.locator: Proposition 1.2.7, p. 57, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Exemple 1.2.8: the Q-Teichmüller lift for Q = X^q and for the cyclotomic Q
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) If Q(X) = X^q then [a]_Q = [a]. If E = Q_p and Q(X) = (1 + X)^p − 1 then [a]_Q = [1 + a] − 1.
items.locator: Exemple 1.2.8, pp. 57–58, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: §1.2.2: W_{O_E}(A) is ([x]_Q,[y]_Q)-adically complete
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) Assume moreover Q(X) ≡ πX mod X², and let LT_Q ∈ O_E[[X,Y]] be the Lubin–Tate formal group law with [π]_{LT_Q} = Q. Let A be a perfect F_q-algebra and x, y ∈ A such that A is separated and complete for the (x, y)-adic topology. Then W_{O_E}(A) is separated and complete for the ([x]_Q, [y]_Q)-adic topology (because it is so for the ([x], [y], π)-adic topology and ([x]_Q, [y]_Q, π) = ([x], [y], π)).
items.locator: §1.2.2, p. 58, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Lemme 1.2.9: the Q-Teichmüller lift commutes with the Lubin–Tate law
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses (E of characteristic 0, Q ≡ X^q mod π, Q ≡ πX mod X², A perfect and (x, y)-adically separated complete), LT_Q([x]_Q, [y]_Q) = [LT_Q(x, y)]_Q.
items.locator: Lemme 1.2.9, p. 58, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Corollaire 1.2.10: x ↦ [x]_Q is a morphism of O_E-modules for the Lubin–Tate laws
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0, Q as above.) The Q-Teichmüller lift defines a morphism of O_E-modules (m_F, +_{LT_Q}) → (W_{O_E}(m_F), +_{LT_Q}), x ↦ [x]_Q.

items.name: §1.2.2: the Lubin–Tate Teichmüller lift [x]_LT for a general Lubin–Tate law
items.statement: (E of characteristic 0.) If LT is any Lubin–Tate formal group law attached to E (with [π]_LT ∈ O_E[[X]] not necessarily a polynomial), then for x ∈ m_F the sequence [π^n]_LT([x^{q^{−n}}]) converges for the weak topology (§1.4.3) and its limit [x]_LT defines a morphism of O_E-modules (m_F, +_LT) → (W_{O_E}(m_F), +_LT), x ↦ [x]_LT.
items.locator: §1.2.2, p. 58, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: External (Lubin–Tate theory): the formal group law LT_Q
items.statement: Black box used in §1.2.2: for Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q ≡ πX mod X² and Q ≡ X^q mod π there is a (unique) formal group law LT_Q ∈ O_E[[X, Y]] (a formal O_E-module) with [π]_{LT_Q} = Q; in particular Q_n(LT_Q(X, Y)) = LT_Q(Q_n(X), Q_n(Y)) for all n. More generally Lubin–Tate laws LT with [π]_LT ∈ O_E[[X]] a power series are used.
items.locator: used in §1.2.2, p. 58 (Lemme 1.2.9 and its proof), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 1.3.1: the rings 𝒪_ℰ and ℰ
items.statement: Since F is perfect: 𝒪_ℰ is the unique π-adically complete O_E-algebra without π-torsion such that 𝒪_ℰ/π𝒪_ℰ = F, and ℰ = 𝒪_ℰ[1/π]; ℰ|E is the complete unramified extension inducing F|F_q on residue fields. There is a unique multiplicative lift [−]: F → 𝒪_ℰ, and every element of ℰ can be written uniquely as Σ_{n≫−∞} [x_n] π^n with x_n ∈ F (printed 'tout élément de 𝒪_ℰ'; the elements of 𝒪_ℰ are those with x_n = 0 for n < 0; see source issues).
items.locator: Définition 1.3.1, p. 59, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property with R = F (unique π-adically complete flat lift and unique multiplicative section).

items.name: Définition 1.3.2: the rings B^b, B^{b,+} and A (= A_inf)
items.statement: B^b = {Σ_{n≫−∞} [x_n] π^n ∈ ℰ | sup_n |x_n| < +∞}, B^{b,+} = {Σ_{n≫−∞} [x_n] π^n ∈ ℰ | x_n ∈ O_F}, A = {Σ_{n≥0} [x_n] π^n ∈ ℰ | x_n ∈ O_F} (A_inf in the classical literature). One has B^b = B^{b,+}[1/[ϖ_F]] and B^{b,+} = A[1/π].
items.locator: Définition 1.3.2, p. 59, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: A = W_{O_E}(O_F) is RF0's W_{O_E}(R^+) (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property); for E = Q_p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (f) plans W^b = W(R^+)[1/[ϖ]] ('Witt vectors with bounded Teichmüller coordinates'). The description of B^b as bounded Teichmüller expansions for general E is not stated separately.

items.name: §1.3: explicit form of 𝒪_ℰ, ℰ and A in both characteristics
items.statement: (1) If E = F_q((π)) has characteristic p, [−] is additive and embeds F in 𝒪_ℰ, 𝒪_ℰ = F ⊗̂_{F_q} O_E = lim_{n≥1} F ⊗_{F_q} O_E/π^n O_E = F[[π]] (F discrete, O_E π-adic), ℰ = F((π)) and A = O_F ⊗̂ O_E = O_F[[π]]. (2) If E|Q_p, 𝒪_ℰ = W_{O_E}(F) and A = W_{O_E}(O_F), and addition and multiplication of Teichmüller expansions are given by generalized polynomials: Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n + Σ_{n≥0}[y_n]π^n = Σ_{n≥0}[P_n(x_0, …, x_n, y_0, …, y_n)]π^n and (Σ[x_n]π^n)(Σ[y_n]π^n) = Σ_{n≥0}[Q_n(x_0, …, x_n, y_0, …, y_n)]π^n with P_n, Q_n ∈ F_q[X_i^{1/p^∞}, Y_j^{1/p^∞}]_{0≤i,j≤n}.
items.locator: §1.3, pp. 59–60, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property covers both descriptions (W_{O_E}(R), and R[[π]] in equal characteristic). The generalized-polynomial formulas are not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 1.3.3: the Frobenius ϕ
items.statement: ϕ is the unique automorphism of 𝒪_ℰ lifting Frob_q on F. It stabilizes ℰ, B^b, B^{b,+} and A, and ϕ(Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n) = Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n^q]π^n.
items.locator: Définition 1.3.3, p. 60, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The RF0 stage text plans the Frobenius of W_{O_E}(R) for perfect R.

items.name: Remarque 1.3.5 (i): Cohen rings and Frobenius lifts via the cotangent complex
items.statement: Let K|F_q be a field. Since F_q is perfect, K is a filtered colimit of smooth F_q-algebras and L_{K/F_q} ≅ Ω¹_{K/F_q}[0]. Since H^{−2}(L_{K/F_q}) = 0, K|F_q lifts to a flat π-adic O_E-algebra O_{ℰ_K} (a Cohen ring); since H^{−1}(L_{K/F_q}) = 0 two such lifts are isomorphic, and Frob_q lifts to O_{ℰ_K}. If K is not perfect, Ω¹_{K/F_q} may be nonzero, two lifts are not canonically isomorphic and several Frobenius lifts may exist (e.g. K = F_q((T)), O_{ℰ_K} = O_E[[X]][1/X]^∧ with X ↦ X^q or X ↦ (1 + X)^q − 1). For F perfect everything is defined up to unique isomorphism and the lift ϕ of Frobenius on 𝒪_{ℰ_F} is canonical.
items.locator: Remarque 1.3.5, p. 60, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing: no atlas node plans Cohen rings (RD.0/analytic-ring uses the Cohen ring C_ℓ as an input) or the cotangent-complex deformation argument; Mathlib has neither.

items.name: Remarque 1.3.5 (ii): Frobenius lifts ↔ embeddings into the perfection
items.statement: If ϕ is a lift of Frobenius on O_{ℰ_K}, there is a canonical isomorphism (lim_{→, ϕ} O_{ℰ_K})^∧ ≅ O_{ℰ_{K^{1/p^∞}}}. This gives a bijection between pairs (O_{ℰ_K}, ϕ), ϕ a Frobenius lift on a Cohen ring, and pairs (O_{ℰ_K}, ι) with ι: O_{ℰ_K} ↪ O_{ℰ_{K^{1/p^∞}}} an embedding inducing K ⊂ K^{1/p^∞} modulo π whose image is stable under the canonical Frobenius; for K = F_q((T)) the two lifts above correspond to X ↦ [T] and X ↦ [T + 1] − 1.
items.locator: Remarque 1.3.5, pp. 60–61, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/frobenius-equivariant-embedding ('the completed direct limit of O_E →σ O_E →σ ⋯ is identified with W(k((t))^perf, O^perf)', ι_σ(t) = [t] for σ(t) = t^q) and RD.0/analytic-ring (the same identification for general ℓ). The bijection of pairs is not stated.

items.name: Définition 1.4.1: Gauss norms |·|_ρ and Gauss valuations v_r on B^b
items.statement: For x = Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n ∈ B^b, ρ ∈ ]0, 1] and r ∈ [0, +∞[: |x|_ρ = sup_n |x_n| ρ^n and v_r(x) = inf_n (v(x_n) + n r); thus |·|_ρ = q^{−v_r(·)} for ρ = q^{−r}. For ρ < 1 (resp. r > 0) the supremum (resp. infimum) is attained; in general this fails for |·|_1 and v_0.
items.locator: Définition 1.4.1, p. 61, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines, on W(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}] = ℰ for E|Q_p, v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) and w_r(x) = min_n (r v_n(x) + n) = r·v_{1/r}(x) (Kedlaya's reciprocal normalization; the endpoint ρ = 1 is not covered). Equal characteristic: PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm (O_K(I), K = F).

items.name: §1.4.1: limit formulas for Gauss norms
items.statement: For x ∈ B^b: |x|_1 = lim_{ρ→1} |x|_ρ, v_0(x) = lim_{r→0} v_r(x), and lim_{r→+∞} v_r(x)/r = v_π(x).
items.locator: §1.4.1, p. 61, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in RD.0 (whose w_r are only for r > 0 and w_0 = v_π); P7:annulus-foundations/bounded-robba-ring has |f|_1 = lim_{ρ→1}|f|_ρ for classical bounded Robba elements (equal-characteristic analogue only).

items.name: §1.4.1: Gauss norms and Frobenius
items.statement: For x ∈ B^b and ρ ∈ ]0,1], r ≥ 0: |ϕ(x)|_ρ = |x|^q_{ρ^{1/q}} and v_r(ϕ(x)) = q v_{r/q}(x).
items.locator: §1.4.1, p. 61, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/partial-valuation-multiplicativity: 'w_r(x) = w_{r/q}(x^σ)', which is v_s(ϕx) = q v_{s/q}(x) after w_r = r·v_{1/r}.

items.name: Lemme 1.4.2 (1): the seminorms N_k on A
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 and x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A put N_k(x) = sup_{0≤n≤k} |x_n| (x, y ∈ A, ρ ∈ ]0,1]). For γ ∈ [0, 1] ∩ |F|, N_k(x) ≤ γ if and only if x ∈ A·[a] + Aπ^{k+1} for a ∈ O_F with |a| = γ.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.2 (1), p. 61, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines the same quantities (v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) = −log_q N_n(x)) and takes w_r = min_n(r v_n + n) as the definition of the Gauss valuation, but none of the five properties is stated as a node (in particular not the equality (5) between this and inf_n(v(x_n) + nr), nor the independence of π).

items.name: Lemme 1.4.2 (2): the seminorms N_k on A
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 and x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A put N_k(x) = sup_{0≤n≤k} |x_n| (x, y ∈ A, ρ ∈ ]0,1]). The function N_k does not depend on the choice of the uniformizer π.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.2 (2), p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines the same quantities (v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) = −log_q N_n(x)) and takes w_r = min_n(r v_n + n) as the definition of the Gauss valuation, but none of the five properties is stated as a node (in particular not the equality (5) between this and inf_n(v(x_n) + nr), nor the independence of π).

items.name: Lemme 1.4.2 (3): the seminorms N_k on A
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 and x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A put N_k(x) = sup_{0≤n≤k} |x_n| (x, y ∈ A, ρ ∈ ]0,1]). N_k(x + y) ≤ max{N_k(x), N_k(y)}.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.2 (3), p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines the same quantities (v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) = −log_q N_n(x)) and takes w_r = min_n(r v_n + n) as the definition of the Gauss valuation, but none of the five properties is stated as a node (in particular not the equality (5) between this and inf_n(v(x_n) + nr), nor the independence of π).

items.name: Lemme 1.4.2 (4): the seminorms N_k on A
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 and x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A put N_k(x) = sup_{0≤n≤k} |x_n| (x, y ∈ A, ρ ∈ ]0,1]). N_k(xy) ≤ sup_{i+j=k} N_i(x) N_j(y).
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.2 (4), p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines the same quantities (v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) = −log_q N_n(x)) and takes w_r = min_n(r v_n + n) as the definition of the Gauss valuation, but none of the five properties is stated as a node (in particular not the equality (5) between this and inf_n(v(x_n) + nr), nor the independence of π).

items.name: Lemme 1.4.2 (5): the seminorms N_k on A
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 and x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A put N_k(x) = sup_{0≤n≤k} |x_n| (x, y ∈ A, ρ ∈ ]0,1]). |x|_ρ = sup_{k≥0} N_k(x) ρ^k.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.2 (5), p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines the same quantities (v_n(x) = min_{i≤n} v(z_i) = −log_q N_n(x)) and takes w_r = min_n(r v_n + n) as the definition of the Gauss valuation, but none of the five properties is stated as a node (in particular not the equality (5) between this and inf_n(v(x_n) + nr), nor the independence of π).

items.name: Proposition 1.4.3 (a): Gauss norms do not depend on π
items.statement: The Gauss norms |·|_ρ (ρ ∈ ]0,1]) of Définition 1.4.1 do not depend on the choice of the uniformizer π.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.3, p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in RD.0 or P7 (P7's annulus rings have a fixed variable).

items.name: Proposition 1.4.3 (b): Gauss norms are algebra norms
items.statement: For ρ ∈ ]0,1] and x, y ∈ B^b: |x + y|_ρ ≤ max{|x|_ρ, |y|_ρ} and |xy|_ρ ≤ |x|_ρ |y|_ρ.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.3, p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Implied by RD.0/partial-valuation-multiplicativity (w_r is a valuation on W_r(ℓ,O)[π^{-1}] ⊇ B^b, r > 0) and P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm (equal characteristic).

items.name: Proposition 1.4.5: intrinsic characterization of |·|_ρ, ρ ∈ ]0,1[
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ ]0, 1[ and let |·|_ρ also denote the unique absolute value on E defining its topology with |π|_ρ = ρ. For x ∈ B^b, |x|_ρ = inf { sup_{n≥0} |x_n|·|λ_n|_ρ : x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]λ_n, x_n ∈ F, λ_n ∈ E, sup_n |x_n| < +∞, lim_{n→+∞} λ_n = 0 }.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.5, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.4.1: concavity of r ↦ v_r(x) and the maximum principle
items.statement: For x ∈ B^b the function [0, +∞[ → ℝ ∪ {+∞}, r ↦ v_r(x), is concave. Consequently, if 0 < ρ_1 ≤ ρ ≤ ρ_2 ≤ 1 then |x|_ρ ≤ max{|x|_{ρ_1}, |x|_{ρ_2}} (maximum principle on the annulus with radii in [ρ_1, ρ_2]).
items.locator: §1.4.1, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for the Witt-vector rings. Classical analogue: PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-maximum-principle (equal characteristic, K = F); AdicSpaces Layer 6.3 takes λ_I = max(λ_s, λ_r) as the definition of the interval norm (E = Q_p) without stating the maximum principle.

items.name: External (Hadamard three-circle theorem), Remarque 1.4.6
items.statement: If f is holomorphic on the punctured disc {z ∈ ℂ | 0 < |z| < 1} and M(R) = sup_{|z|=R} |f(z)| for 0 < R < 1, then R ↦ log M(R) is a convex function of log R (quoted as the archimedean analogue of the concavity of r ↦ v_r(x)).
items.locator: Remarque 1.4.6, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has the Hadamard three-lines theorem on vertical strips (mathlib:Complex.HadamardThreeLines.norm_le_interp_of_mem_verticalClosedStrip'), not the three-circle form. Used only as an analogy.

items.name: Définition 1.4.7: the norm |·|_0 = q^{−v_π}
items.locator: Définition 1.4.7, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations: 'w = w_0 is the π-adic valuation normalised by w(π) = 1'.

items.name: Lemme 1.4.8: monotonicity of |x|_ρ when |x|_0 ≤ 1
items.statement: Let x ∈ B^b with |x|_0 ≤ 1. Then for 0 < ρ′ ≤ ρ ≤ 1, |x|_{ρ′} ≤ |x|_ρ.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.8, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Equal-characteristic analogue: P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-maximum-principle (d) (no negative coefficients ⇒ ρ ↦ |f|_ρ nondecreasing). Not stated for general E.

items.name: §1.4.1: the topology of (|·|_{ρ′})_{0≤ρ′≤ρ} is that of max{|·|_0, |·|_ρ}
items.statement: For ρ ∈ [0, 1] the topology on B^b defined by the family of norms (|·|_{ρ′})_{0≤ρ′≤ρ} coincides with the topology defined by the single norm max{|·|_0, |·|_ρ}.
items.locator: §1.4.1, p. 63, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.9: multiplicativity of the Gauss norms
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], |·|_ρ is multiplicative on B^b: |xy|_ρ = |x|_ρ |y|_ρ. Equivalently, every v_r, r ≥ 0, is a valuation.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.9, p. 64, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mixed characteristic, ρ ∈ ]0,1[: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/partial-valuation-multiplicativity ('w_r is a valuation on W_r(ℓ, O)[π^{-1}]', with additivity of extreme dominant indices), in Kedlaya's normalization w_r = r·v_{1/r}. Equal characteristic: PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-multiplicative (ρ < 1) and P7:annulus-foundations/amice-ring (|·|_1 multiplicative on E_K). The endpoint ρ = 1 in mixed characteristic is not stated. Mathlib has multiplicativity of Gauss norms only for power series over a normed field (mathlib:MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm_mul_eq_mul, mathlib:Polynomial.gaussNorm_mul), not for Witt-vector expansions.

items.name: Définition 1.4.10: the weak topology on A
items.statement: The weak topology on A is the topology of convergence of the coefficients of Teichmüller expansions, i.e. the product topology transported by the bijection O_F^ℕ ≅ A, (x_n)_{n≥0} ↦ Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n.
items.locator: Définition 1.4.10, p. 64, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y/curly-Y-affinoid-definition equips W_{O_E}(R^+) with the (π,[ϖ])-adic topology directly; the product-topology description is not stated.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.11 (1): the weak topology of A
items.statement: The weak topology of A coincides with the ([ϖ_F], π)-adic topology.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.11 (1), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E. RF0:integral-Y takes the (π,[ϖ])-adic topology as the definition; the comparison with the product topology is not stated.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.11 (2): the weak topology of A
items.statement: The weak topology of A is defined by the family of seminorms (N_k)_{k≥0} of Lemme 1.4.2.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.11 (2), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.11 (3): the weak topology of A
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ ]0, 1[, the topology induced by |·|_ρ on A is the weak topology.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.11 (3), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.11 (4): the weak topology of A
items.statement: A is separated and complete for the weak topology.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.11 (4), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E. For E = Q_p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (c) and AdicSpaces Layer 6.1 plan the (p,[ϖ])-adic completeness and separatedness of W(O_F).

items.name: Remarque 1.4.12: |[ε] − 1|_1 = 1 and discontinuity of the Teichmüller map for |·|_1
items.statement: Assume E|Q_p. For every ε ∈ 1 + m_F ∖ {1}, |[ε] − 1|_1 = 1. Hence lim_{α→0, α≠0} |[1 + α] − 1|_1 ≠ |[1] − 1|_1 = 0, and the Teichmüller map x ↦ [x] is not continuous for the topology defined by |·|_1 (whereas for E = F_q((π)) the topology of |·|_1 on A is that of uniform convergence of Teichmüller coefficients).
items.locator: Remarque 1.4.12, p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.4.13: A is complete for |·|_1
items.statement: The ring A is separated and complete for the topology defined by |·|_1, which is the [ϖ_F]-adic topology.
items.locator: Proposition 1.4.13, p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For E = Q_p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (c) plans that W(R^+) is [ϖ]-adically complete and separated; not stated for general E, nor the identification with the |·|_1-topology.

items.name: Lemme 1.4.14: completeness for a smaller finitely generated ideal
items.statement: Let R be a ring that is separated and complete for the I-adic topology. Then for every finitely generated ideal J ⊂ I, R is separated and complete for the J-adic topology.
items.locator: Lemme 1.4.14, p. 65 (stated without proof), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib at the pinned commit (mathlib:IsAdicComplete has no lemma passing to a smaller finitely generated ideal); this is Stacks Project Lemma 090T. No atlas node states it.

items.name: Corollaire 1.4.15 (1): completeness of A for |·|_ρ
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], A is complete for |·|_ρ. A is complete for |·|_0, and the topology it induces on A is the π-adic topology.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.4.15 (1), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E (E = Q_p analogues: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (a), (c)).

items.name: Corollaire 1.4.15 (2): completeness of A for |·|_ρ
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], A is complete for |·|_ρ. For ρ ∈ ]0, 1[, A is complete for |·|_ρ, and the induced topology is the ([ϖ_F], π)-adic topology.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.4.15 (2), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E (E = Q_p analogues: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (a), (c)).

items.name: Corollaire 1.4.15 (3): completeness of A for |·|_ρ
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], A is complete for |·|_ρ. A is complete for |·|_1, and the induced topology is the [ϖ_F]-adic topology.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.4.15 (3), p. 65, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E (E = Q_p analogues: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (a), (c)).

items.name: §1.5.1: Legendre transform, slopes and inf-convolution
items.statement: For ϕ: ℝ → ℝ ∪ {+∞} not identically +∞, its Legendre transform is L(ϕ): ℝ → ℝ ∪ {−∞}, λ ↦ inf{ϕ(x) + λx | x ∈ ℝ}, a concave function. The slope of a polygon is the opposite of the derivative of the associated piecewise affine function (so that slopes of Newton polygons are valuations of roots). For ϕ_1, ϕ_2 put (ϕ_1 ∗ ϕ_2)(x) = inf{ϕ_1(a) + ϕ_2(b) | a + b = x}.
items.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No Legendre transform or inf-convolution in Mathlib, Tau Ceti or the atlas.

items.name: §1.5.1: inverse Legendre transform
items.statement: If ϕ is convex and lower semicontinuous (and not identically +∞), ϕ can be recovered from L(ϕ): ϕ(x) = sup{L(ϕ)(λ) − λx | λ ∈ ℝ}. (The book assumes only ϕ convex; lower semicontinuity is needed, see source issues. It holds for the Newton polygons to which the formula is applied.)
items.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No Legendre/Fenchel duality in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: §1.5.1: Legendre duality between slopes and break abscissae
items.statement: A convex function ϕ: ℝ → ℝ ∪ {+∞}, not identically +∞, is a polygon with integer break abscissae if and only if L(ϕ) is locally affine with slopes in ℤ on the open segment where L(ϕ) ≠ −∞. The slopes of L(ϕ) are then the abscissae of the break points of ϕ, and the abscissae of the break points of L(ϕ) are the slopes of ϕ (printed: 'of L(ϕ)'; see source issues).
items.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: §1.5.1: Legendre transform of an inf-convolution
items.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: §1.5.1: inf-convolution of polygons concatenates slopes
items.statement: If ϕ_1 and ϕ_2 are decreasing convex polygons with integer break abscissae, bounded below, then ϕ_1 ∗ ϕ_2 is also one, and its finite strictly positive slopes are obtained by concatenating those of ϕ_1 and ϕ_2.
items.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: Définition 1.5.2: the Newton polygon Newt(x) of x ∈ B^b
items.statement: For x = Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n ∈ B^b, Newt(x) is the largest decreasing convex polygon of ℝ² lying below the set of points (n, v(x_n))_{n∈ℤ}. It is determined by v_π(x) and its slopes (λ_i)_{i∈ℤ}, λ_i the slope on [i, i+1], with λ_i = +∞ for i < v_π(x) and λ_i ≥ λ_{i+1} for all i.
items.locator: Définition 1.5.2, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring: 'The Newton polygon of x ∈ Γ_I is the lower convex hull of the points (v_n(x), n) with the segments of slope −s, s ∉ I, removed' (Kedlaya's convention: transposed axes and partial valuations), which for x ∈ B^b and I = [0, r_0) carries the same information. Equal characteristic: P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks.

items.name: §1.5.2: Newt(x) and the Gauss valuations are Legendre dual
items.statement: For x ∈ B^b: v_0(x) = lim_{t→+∞} Newt(x)(t) and ]−∞, v_π(x)[ = Newt(x)^{−1}({+∞}). For x ≠ 0 the Legendre transform of (the piecewise affine function) Newt(x) is L(Newt(x))(λ) = v_λ(x) for λ ≥ 0 and −∞ for λ < 0. In particular Newt(x) does not depend on the choice of π.
items.locator: §1.5.2, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The duality is implicit in RD.0/analytic-ring's definition of the Newton polygon but is not stated; independence of π is not stated.

items.name: §1.5.2: Newt(xy) = Newt(x) ∗ Newt(y)
items.statement: For nonzero x, y ∈ B^b, Newt(xy) = Newt(x) ∗ Newt(y) (because v_r(xy) = v_r(x) + v_r(y) for all r ≥ 0); the finite strictly positive slopes of Newt(xy) are obtained by concatenating, with multiplicity, those of Newt(x) and of Newt(y).
items.locator: §1.5.2, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/partial-valuation-multiplicativity ('Newton-polygon additivity') and RD.0/analytic-ring-slope-additivity; equal characteristic P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-multiplicative (additivity of n(f,ρ), N(f,ρ)).

items.name: Exemple 1.5.3: Newton polygon of Π(π − [a_i])
items.statement: Let a_1, …, a_d ∈ m_F ∖ {0} and Π_{i=1}^{d}(π − [a_i]) = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n. Then x_d ∈ O_F^× and the nonzero slopes of the convex hull of the points (i, v(x_i))_{0≤i≤d} are the (v(a_i))_{1≤i≤d}. (Printed with a_0, …, a_d, Π_{i=0}^{n} and (v(a_i))_{0≤i≤d}; see source issues.)
items.locator: Exemple 1.5.3, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.5.4: non-archimedean Jensen formula
items.statement: Let x ∈ A nonzero and r > 0; let (λ_i)_{i≥0} be the finite slopes of Newt(x), λ_i the slope on [i, i+1], and n the integer with λ_{n−1} ≥ r and λ_n < r (n = 0 if λ_0 < r). Then v(x_0) = Σ_{i=0}^{n−1} λ_i − n r + v_r(x).
items.locator: Remarque 1.5.4, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: External (Jensen's formula), Remarque 1.5.4
items.statement: Let f be holomorphic on {z ∈ ℂ | |z| < 1} and 0 < R < 1; assume f has no zero on |z| = R and f(0) ≠ 0, and let a_1, …, a_n be the zeros of f in |z| ≤ R counted with multiplicity. Then log|f(0)| = Σ_{i=1}^{n} log|a_i| − n log R + (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} log|f(Re^{iθ})| dθ.
items.locator: Remarque 1.5.4, p. 67, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib's Jensen formula (Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/JensenFormula.lean): for f analytic on the closed ball of radius R about c with f(c) ≠ 0, circleAverage (log‖f‖) c R = Σᶠ_u divisor(u)·log(R·‖c − u‖⁻¹) + log‖f c‖, which is FF's identity after rearranging (and does not need the no-zero-on-the-circle hypothesis). Used only as an analogy.

items.name: Définition 1.6.1: K-Fréchet and K-Banach algebras
items.statement: Let K be a topological field whose topology is defined by a nonarchimedean absolute value (intervals in [0,1] are nonempty by convention). A K-Fréchet algebra is a complete topological K-algebra A whose topology can be defined by a family (‖·‖_n)_{n∈ℕ}, ‖·‖_n: A → ℝ_+, satisfying ‖x‖_n = 0 ⇔ x = 0, ‖x + y‖_n ≤ max{‖x‖_n, ‖y‖_n}, ‖1‖_n = 1, ‖xy‖_n ≤ ‖x‖_n‖y‖_n, and such that the topology induced by (‖·‖_n)_n on K is its original topology. A K-Banach algebra is a K-Fréchet algebra whose topology can be defined by a single such norm.
items.locator: Définition 1.6.1, pp. 68–69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has no notion of (nonarchimedean) Fréchet algebra; P7:annulus-foundations/frechet-topology treats the Fréchet topology of O_K(I) only.

items.name: Définition 1.6.2: the Fréchet algebras B_I and B
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ [0, 1], B_I is the completion of B^b with respect to the family of norms (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈I}, and ‖·‖_I = sup_{ρ∈I} |·|_ρ: B_I → [0, +∞]. B := B_{]0,1[}.
items.locator: Définition 1.6.2, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mixed characteristic, I ⊂ [0,1[: RD.0/analytic-ring (Kedlaya's Γ_I = Fréchet completion of Γ_{r_0}[π^{-1}] for the valuations w_s, s ∈ I; for ℓ = F perfect, Γ = 𝒪_ℰ; radii reparametrized s ↔ ρ = q^{−1/s}). Compact I ⊂ ]0,1[: RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli (B_{S,I} as rational localizations of W_{O_E}(R^+)) and AdicSpaces Layer 6.3 (Kedlaya's interval rings B^I, E = Q_p). Intervals containing 1 are not covered. Equal characteristic: for E = F_q((π)), B_I is the classical ring O_F(I) of PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/annulus-laurent-ring (K = F, variable π), but that identification (Exemple 1.6.5) is not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.6.1: B_I is a Fréchet (Banach if I compact) algebra over E or E^disc
items.statement: B_I is an E-Fréchet algebra, E carrying the topology induced by ‖·‖_I: if 1 ∉ I, E has its usual topology; if 1 ∈ I, E carries the discrete topology E^disc (trivial valuation). If I is compact: if 1 ∉ I, B_I is an E-Banach algebra, its topology being defined by ‖·‖_I = max{|·|_{ρ_1}, |·|_{ρ_2}} when 0 ∉ I = [ρ_1, ρ_2], and by max{|·|_0, |·|_ρ} when I = [0, ρ] (Lemme 1.4.8); if 1 ∈ I, B_I is an E^disc-Banach algebra.
items.locator: §1.6.1, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring (Γ_I Fréchet); AdicSpaces Layer 6.3 ('B^I is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring' with λ_I = max(λ_s, λ_r), E = Q_p, compact I ⊂ ]0,1[). The E^disc cases (1 ∈ I) and I = [0, ρ] with max{|·|_0,|·|_ρ} are not stated.

items.name: §1.6.1: Frobenius ϕ: B_I ≅ B_{ϕ(I)}
items.statement: With ϕ: [0,1] → [0,1], ϕ(ρ) = ρ^q, the automorphism ϕ of B^b extends to an isomorphism ϕ: B_I ≅ B_{ϕ(I)}; in particular it induces an automorphism of B.
items.locator: §1.6.1, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring: 'σ induces Γ_I → Γ_{q^{-1}I}' (mixed characteristic, I ⊂ [0,1[).

items.name: §1.6.1: B_I as a projective limit of Banach algebras
items.statement: If J ⊂ I there is a continuous morphism B_I → B_J, and B_I ≅ lim_{←J} B_J, J running over the compact intervals contained in I.
items.locator: §1.6.1, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E; equal-characteristic analogue P7:annulus-foundations/annulus-limit-comparison (a).

items.name: §1.6.1: A is closed in B_I
items.statement: By Corollaire 1.4.15, A ⊂ B_I is closed.
items.locator: §1.6.1, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 1.6.3: B_I for I = [ρ_1, ρ_2] with ρ_i ∈ |F|
items.statement: Let I = [ρ_1, ρ_2] ⊂ ]0, 1] with ρ_1, ρ_2 ∈ |F| and a, b ∈ F with |a| = ρ_1, |b| = ρ_2. The unit ball of ‖·‖_I in B^b is A[[a]/π, π/[b]], and hence B_I = (A[[a]/π, π/[b]])^∧[1/π], the completion being for the π-adic topology.
items.locator: Exemple 1.6.3, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli constructs the rational localizations Y_{S,I} = Spa(B_{S,I}, B^+_{S,I}) whose rings are of this shape, and AdicSpaces Layer 6.3 plans 'the unit ball B^{I,+} equals the power-bounded subring' (E = Q_p); neither states the identification with the Gauss-norm completion B_I.

items.name: Exemple 1.6.4: B_{{0}} = ℰ
items.locator: Exemple 1.6.4, p. 69, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas (trivial: completion of B^b for |·|_0 = q^{−v_π}).

items.name: Exemple 1.6.5: B_I in equal characteristic
items.statement: Assume E = F_q((π)). If 0, 1 ∉ I, B_I is the ring of holomorphic functions of the variable π with coefficients in F on the annulus with radii in I: B_I = {Σ_{n∈ℤ} x_n π^n | x_n ∈ F, ∀ρ ∈ I, lim_{|n|→+∞} |x_n|ρ^n = 0}. If I ≠ {0} and I ≠ {1}, B_I consists of such functions on I ∖ {0, 1} which are moreover meromorphic at 0 if 0 ∈ I and bounded outside the annulus if 1 ∈ I. The ring B_{{1}} = {Σ_{n∈ℤ} x_n π^n | x_n ∈ F, lim_{n→−∞} x_n = 0, sup_n |x_n| < +∞} has no geometric interpretation.
items.locator: Exemple 1.6.5, p. 70, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The rings on the right are planned in PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations (annulus-laurent-ring O_F(I) with K = F; amice-ring E_F for B_{{1}}), but their identification with the Gauss-norm completions B_I is not stated.

items.name: Remarque 1.6.6: bounded series with coefficients tending to 0 are not closed under addition
items.statement: If E|Q_p, the set {Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ B^b | lim_{n→+∞} |x_n| = 0} is not stable under addition (there is no good notion of holomorphic function of π with coefficients in F on annuli of outer radius ≥ 1).
items.locator: Remarque 1.6.6, p. 70, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas (compare the related failure of continuity in Remarque 1.4.12).

items.name: Remarque 1.6.7: convergence of Teichmüller series in B
items.statement: Let (x_n)_{n∈ℤ} be a sequence in F with lim_{|n|→+∞} |x_n|ρ^n = 0 for all ρ ∈ ]0, 1[. Then Σ_{n∈ℤ}[x_n]π^n converges in B. If E = F_q((π)) every element of B is uniquely of this form; if E|Q_p it is not known whether every element of B is of this form, whether such an expression is unique, or whether sums and products of such elements are of this form (likewise for all B_I with 0 ∉ I).
items.locator: Remarque 1.6.7, p. 70, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated. RD.0/semiunit-presentation plans presentations x = Σ u_i π^i by semiunits (not Teichmüller expansions) for Kedlaya's Γ_I.

items.name: §1.6.2: change of E for A and B^b
items.statement: Let E′|E be a finite extension whose residue field F_{q′} embeds in F (so F|F_{q′}|F_q), and E′_0 the maximal unramified extension of E in E′ (E′_0 = W_{O_E}(F_{q′})_ℚ if E|Q_p, E ⊗_{F_q} F_{q′} if E has characteristic p). Then A_{E′} = A_E ⊗_{O_{E′_0}} O_{E′} and B^b_{E′} = B^b_E ⊗_{E′_0} E′.
items.locator: §1.6.2, pp. 70–71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the base case over Q_p (W(R) ⊗̂ O_E = W_{O_E}(R)) is planned, in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property.

items.name: Lemme 1.6.8: Gauss norms under change of E
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ [0, 1] and e = e_{E′/E}. Via the identification B^b_{E′} = B^b_E ⊗_{E′_0} E′, |·|_{E′, ρ^{1/e}} = |·|_{E,ρ} ⊗ |·|_{E′, ρ^{1/e}}.
items.locator: Lemme 1.6.8, p. 71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas. Normalization caveat: at ρ = 0 the equality holds only up to the power [E′:E] = e·f (|x|_{E′,0} = q′^{−e v_{π_E}(x)} = |x|_{E,0}^{ef} for x ∈ B^b_E), and for ρ ∈ ]0,1[ it requires the same absolute value |·| on F for E and E′ (§1.1 normalizes |·| = q^{−v} with q = q_E, which changes to |·|^f for E′); only the topologies are used in Prop. 1.6.9.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.9 (i): B_{E,I} ⊗̂_{E′_0} E′ ≅ B_{E′, I^{1/e}}
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ [0, 1] there is an isomorphism B_{E,I} ⊗̂_{E′_0} E′ ≅ B_{E′, I^{1/e_{E′|E}}}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.9, p. 71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; P7:annulus-foundations/coefficient-extension is the classical analogue for extending the coefficient field of O_K(I), not the field E of the variable.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.9 (ii): uncompleted tensor product for compact I
items.statement: When I is compact, B_{E,I} ⊗_{E′_0} E′ ≅ B_{E′, I^{1/e_{E′|E}}}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.9, p. 71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.6.2: Frobenius under change of E
items.statement: Via the isomorphisms of Prop. 1.6.9, ϕ_E^{f_{E′/E}} ⊗ Id = ϕ_{E′}. In particular, if E′|E is unramified then B_{E,I} = B_{E′,I} but ϕ_{E′} = ϕ_E^{[E′:E]}: changing E changes the Frobenius, not the algebra.
items.locator: §1.6.2, p. 71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 1.6.10: stabilization of the one-sided derivatives of v_r along Cauchy sequences
items.statement: (For x ∈ B^b nonzero, ∂_g v_r(x) and ∂_d v_r(x) are the left and right derivatives at r of the continuous piecewise affine function r′ ↦ v_{r′}(x), and ∂_d v_0(x) ∈ ℤ ∪ {+∞}.) Let r ∈ ]0, +∞[ and (x_n)_{n∈ℕ} a Cauchy sequence in B^b for v_r not tending to 0. Then the sequences (∂_g v_r(x_n))_n and (∂_d v_r(x_n))_n are constant for n ≫ 0. Moreover, if (y_n)_n tends to 0 for v_r, then for n ≫ 0, ∂_g v_r(x_n + y_n) = ∂_g v_r(x_n) and ∂_d v_r(x_n + y_n) = ∂_d v_r(x_n). The same holds for ∂_d v_0.
items.locator: Lemme 1.6.10, pp. 71–72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 1.6.11: ∂_g v_r and ∂_d v_r on B_I
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1] be an interval, x ∈ B_I nonzero and ρ = q^{−r} ∈ I ∩ ]0, 1[. Define ∂_g v_r(x) = lim_n ∂_g v_r(x_n) and ∂_d v_r(x) = lim_n ∂_d v_r(x_n) for any sequence x_n ∈ B^b with x_n → x (well defined by Lemme 1.6.10); similarly ∂_d v_0(x) when 1 ∈ I.
items.locator: Définition 1.6.11, p. 72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.12: rank-two valuations (v_r, ∂_d v_r) and (v_r, −∂_g v_r)
items.statement: Give ℝ ⊕ ℤ the lexicographic order. If q^{−r} ∈ I ∖ {0, 1}, the maps B_I ∖ {0} → ℝ ⊕ ℤ, x ↦ (v_r(x), ∂_d v_r(x)) and x ↦ (v_r(x), −∂_g v_r(x)), are valuations on B_I.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.12, p. 72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/partial-valuation-multiplicativity states the additivity of the smallest and largest dominant indices for products (the multiplicative half, on W_r(ℓ,O)[π^{-1}]); the ultrametric inequality and the extension to B_I are not stated.

items.name: Remarque 1.6.13: the rank-two valuations lie in Spa(B_I, O_E + B_I°°) ∖ Spa(B_I, B_I°)
items.statement: The rank-two valuations of Prop. 1.6.12 on B^b are continuous for |·|_{q^{−r}} (they are specializations of v_r), hence extend to B_I as soon as q^{−r} ∈ I; they belong to Spa(B_I, O_E + B_I°°) ∖ Spa(B_I, B_I°).
items.locator: Remarque 1.6.13, p. 72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 1.6.14: one-sided derivatives in equal characteristic
items.statement: If E = F_q((π)) (printed 'F = F_q((π))') and f = Σ_{n∈ℤ} x_n π^n ∈ B_I is nonzero, then ∂_g v_r(f) = sup{n ∈ ℤ | v(x_n) + nr = v_r(f)} and ∂_d v_r(f) = inf{n ∈ ℤ | v(x_n) + nr = v_r(f)}; moreover, when 1 ∈ I, ∂_d v_0(f) = +∞ if v(x_n) > v_0(f) for all n, and ∂_d v_0(f) = inf{n | v(x_n) = v_0(f)} otherwise.
items.locator: Exemple 1.6.14, p. 72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks (e): 'log|f|_ρ is a piecewise affine function of log ρ whose right (left) derivative at ρ is N(f,ρ) (n(f,ρ))', with n, N the least/greatest dominant indices (for K = F; the ρ = 1 clause is not covered).

items.name: Proposition 1.6.15: the restriction maps B_I → B_J are injective
items.statement: If J ⊂ I, the map B_I → B_J is injective.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.15, p. 72, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring: 'for I ⊆ J the restriction Γ_J → Γ_I is injective with dense image' (mixed characteristic, radii bounded away from 1); P7:annulus-foundations/restriction-maps (equal characteristic). Intervals containing 1 are not covered. Review: the case 1 ∈ I (E^disc-Banach rings such as B_{[ρ,1]}) in mixed characteristic is part of the statement and is not planned (Kedlaya's Γ_I needs I bounded away from r_0), so the item is missing.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.16: Gauss norms of approximating sequences stabilize on compacts
items.statement: Let I be an interval of ]0, 1] and (x_n)_{n≥0} a sequence of B^b converging to a nonzero x ∈ B_I. Then for every compact K ⊂ I there is N such that |x_n|_ρ = |x|_ρ for all n ≥ N and all ρ ∈ K.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.16, p. 73, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 1.6.17: r ↦ v_r(x) is a concave polygon with finitely many integer slopes
items.statement: If I = q^{−J} is a compact interval of ]0, 1[ and x ∈ B_I is nonzero, then J ∋ r ↦ v_r(x) is a concave polygon with finitely many slopes, all integers.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.6.17, p. 73, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring-slope-additivity: 'for a closed interval [r′, r] the total multiplicity of x ∈ Γ_{[r′,r]} is finite and equals i − j' (integer dominant indices); P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks (a), (e) in equal characteristic.

items.name: Définition 1.6.18: the Newton polygons Newt⁰_I(x) and Newt_I(x) for I compact
items.statement: Let I = [q^{−r_1}, q^{−r_2}] be a compact interval of ]0, 1] and x ∈ B_I nonzero. Newt⁰_I(x) is the decreasing convex function whose Legendre transform at λ ∈ [0, +∞[ is v_λ(x) if q^{−λ} ∈ I, v_{r_2}(x) + (λ − r_2)∂_g v_{r_2}(x) if λ < r_2, and v_{r_1}(x) + (λ − r_1)∂_d v_{r_1}(x) if λ ≥ r_1 (printed with r in place of λ in the last two formulas), and −∞ on ]−∞, 0[. Newt_I(x) is the polygon obtained from Newt⁰_I(x) by keeping only the slopes λ with q^{−λ} ∈ I; Newt_I(x) = ∅ if there is no such slope, and Newt_I(0) ≡ +∞. Newt⁰_I(x) is +∞ on ]−∞, ∂_d v_{r_1}(x)[ and of slope 0 on [∂_g v_{r_2}(x), +∞[; up to vertical translation Newt_I(x) is the polygon on [∂_d v_{r_1}(x), ∂_g v_{r_2}(x)] with slopes in [r_2, r_1], the slope λ having multiplicity ∂_g v_λ(x) − ∂_d v_λ(x).
items.locator: Définition 1.6.18, p. 74, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring: 'The Newton polygon of x ∈ Γ_I is the lower convex hull of the points (v_n(x), n) with the segments of slope −s, s ∉ I, removed; its slopes (with multiplicities) are the slopes of x' (Kedlaya's convention; intervals containing 1 not covered).

items.name: Corollaire 1.6.19: Newt_I(x) is realized by an element of B^b
items.statement: If I is a compact interval of ]0, 1] and x ∈ B_I, there exists y ∈ B^b with Newt_I(x) = Newt_I(y). In particular, if I ⊂ ]0, 1[, Newt_I(x) is a polygon with finitely many slopes and integer break abscissae.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.6.19, p. 75, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The finiteness part is covered by RD.0/analytic-ring-slope-additivity; the approximation by y ∈ B^b is not stated.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.20: Newton polygons of products
items.statement: For a compact interval I of ]0, 1] and x, y ∈ B_I, Newt⁰_I(xy) = Newt⁰_I(x) ∗ Newt⁰_I(y); hence the slopes of Newt_I(xy) are obtained by concatenating, with multiplicities, those of Newt_I(x) and of Newt_I(y).
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.20, p. 75, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring-slope-additivity: 'the multiplicity of s as a slope of xy is the sum of its multiplicities as a slope of x and of y'; P7:annulus-foundations/gauss-norm-multiplicative (equal characteristic). Intervals containing 1 not covered. Review: the case 1 ∈ I in mixed characteristic is part of the statement (I compact in ]0, 1]) and is not planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Définition 1.6.21 and Exemple 1.6.22: Newt_I(x) for an arbitrary interval I
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0, 1] and x ∈ B_I. For compact J′ ⊂ J ⊂ I ∖ {0}, Newt_{J′}(x) is obtained from Newt_J(x) by keeping the slopes λ with q^{−λ} ∈ J′; put Newt_I(x) = ⋃_J Newt_J(x), J running over the compact intervals of I ∖ {0}. When I is open in ℝ, Newt_I(x) is the inverse Legendre transform of λ ↦ v_λ(x) on −log_q(I ∖ {0}) restricted to slopes in −log_q(I ∖ {0}); for x ∈ B^b it is Newt(x) = Newt_{[0,1]}(x) restricted to slopes in −log_q(I ∖ {0}); for x ∈ B, Newt_{]0,1[}(x) is the inverse Legendre transform of λ ↦ v_λ(x) on ]0, +∞[ with the slope 0 removed if it occurs.
items.locator: Définition 1.6.21 and Exemple 1.6.22, p. 75, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/analytic-ring defines the Newton polygon of x ∈ Γ_I for arbitrary I ⊆ [0, r_0) bounded away from r_0 (Kedlaya's convention); the Legendre-transform description is not stated.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.23: B_I as Laurent-type series when 0 ∈ I, 1 ∉ I
items.statement: Suppose 0 ∈ I and 1 ∉ I. Then, inside B_{{0}} = ℰ (Prop. 1.6.15), B_I = {Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n ∈ ℰ | ∀ρ ∈ I ∖ {0}, lim_{n→+∞} |x_n|ρ^n = 0}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.23, p. 75, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines Kedlaya's W_r(ℓ, O) directly as the set {x | v_{n,r}(x) → ∞}, which is this right-hand side (after π-inversion and reparametrization), but the equality with the Gauss-norm completion is not stated (RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections (a) is the closest statement).

items.name: Proposition 1.6.24: B_{[0,1]} = B^b and B°_{[0,1]} = A
items.statement: B_{[0,1]} = B^b and B°_{[0,1]} = A (power-bounded elements).
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.24, p. 76, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.25: units of B_I for I ⊂ [0,1[ are the elements without slopes
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ [0, 1[, B_I^× = {x ∈ B_I ∖ {0} | Newt_I(x) = ∅}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.25, p. 76, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring: 'A nonzero x ∈ Γ_I is a unit of Γ_I iff it has no slopes (in I)' (mixed characteristic); P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks (c) for compact J in equal characteristic.

items.name: Proposition 1.6.26: units of B_I when 1 ∈ I
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0, 1] with 1 ∈ I. Then B_I^× is the set of nonzero x ∈ B_I such that Newt_I(x) ≠ ∅ and has 0 as its only slope; equivalently Newt_{I∖{1}}(x) = ∅ and ∂_d v_0(x) < +∞. (Proof left to the reader; not used later.)
items.locator: Proposition 1.6.26, p. 78, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 1.6.27: units of B_{{1}}
items.locator: Corollaire 1.6.27, p. 78, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.7.1: the field F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞}))^∧
items.statement: Let k|F_q be a perfect field and F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞})) the completion of the perfection of k((π_F)), with |π_F| = q^{−1}. Then F = {Σ_{α∈ℤ[1/p]} a_α π_F^α | a_α ∈ k, lim_α |a_α| q^{−α} = 0}, k carrying the trivial absolute value and the limit being along the filter of complements of finite subsets of ℤ[1/p]; i.e. for every C ≥ 0 the set {α | α ≤ C and a_α ≠ 0} is finite (printed '|α| ≤ C'; see source issues).
items.locator: §1.7.1, p. 79, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra describes the unit ball of perfected Tate algebras R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, a different (T-restricted) ring.

items.name: §1.7.1: explicit descriptions of A_F for F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞}))
items.statement: Put W_{O_E}(k) = O_E ⊗̂_{F_q} k when E has characteristic p (printed 'E ⊗̂_{F_q} k') and T = [π_F]. For every E: A_F = {Σ_{α∈ℕ[1/p]} a_α T^α | a_α ∈ W_{O_E}(k), lim_α |a_α| q^{−α} = 0} = {Σ_{α∈ℕ[1/p]} a_α T^α | ∀k ∈ ℕ, {α | v_π(a_α) = k} ⊂ ℝ_+ is discrete}, where |·| is any absolute value defining the π-adic topology of W_{O_E}(k) and the limit is along the cofinite filter of ℕ[1/p]; this is W_{O_E}(k)⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ understood as the (π, T)-adic completion of W_{O_E}(k)[T^{1/p^∞}] (equivalently its completion for the weak topology); the text says 'the π-adic completion', which is incorrect (see source issues).
items.locator: §1.7.1, p. 79, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 1.7.1: Gauss norms on A_F in the T-expansion
items.statement: For f = Σ_α a_α T^α ∈ A (F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞}))) and ρ ∈ [0, 1]: |f|_ρ = sup_α |a_α|_ρ q^{−α} if ρ ≠ 0 and |f|_0 = sup_α |a_α|_0, where for ρ ≠ 0, 1, |·|_ρ is the unique absolute value on W_{O_E}(k)_ℚ defining its topology with |π_E|_ρ = ρ, |·|_0 = |·|_{q^{−1}}, and |·|_1 is the trivial absolute value.
items.locator: Lemme 1.7.1, p. 79, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.7.1: B_I for F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞}))
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ [0, 1], I ≠ {0}, {1}: if 0, 1 ∉ I, B_I = {Σ_{α∈ℤ[1/p]} a_α T^α | a_α ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_ℚ, ∀ρ ∈ I, lim_α |a_α|_ρ q^{−α} = 0} (limit along the cofinite filter of ℤ[1/p]); otherwise B_I consists of the f = Σ_α a_α T^α ∈ B_{I∖{0,1}} satisfying in addition sup_α |a_α|_0 < +∞ if 0 ∈ I (i.e. inf_α v_π(a_α) > −∞) and sup_α |a_α|_1 q^{−α} < +∞ if 1 ∈ I (i.e. inf_{a_α≠0} α > −∞).
items.locator: §1.7.1, p. 80, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.7.2: B_{F,I} as completed colimit of perfected annulus rings (ϕ(X) = X^q)
items.statement: Let K = k((π_F)), A_K = W_{O_E}(k)[[X]] ⊂ O_{ℰ_K} = W_{O_E}(k)[[X]][1/X]^∧ with the Frobenius ϕ(X) = X^q. Then (lim_{→ϕ} A_K)^∧ ≅ A_{K^{1/p^∞}} ⊂ A_F (π-adic completion), via X ↦ T = [π_F]. For an interval I ⊂ [0,1], I ≠ {0}, {1}, A_F is the completion of lim_{→ϕ} A_K for the Gauss norms (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈I}; with B^b_K = A_K[1/π, 1/X] (printed 'A_K[1/X]') (Gauss norms via ι: B^b_K ↪ B^b_F) and B_{K,I} its completion as an E-Fréchet algebra, (lim_{→ n, ϕ} B_{K,ϕ^n(I)})^∧ ≅ B_{F,I}.
items.locator: §1.7.2, pp. 80–81, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; RD.0/frobenius-equivariant-embedding plans the analogous statement for O_ℰ (completed colimit along σ is W(k((t))^perf, O^perf)) and the embedding R ↪ R^alg.

items.name: Lemme 1.7.2: Gauss norms under X ↦ [π_F] (ρ ↦ ρ̌)
items.statement: Put ρ̌ = q^{−1/r} if ρ = q^{−r} ≠ 0, 1, 0̌ = 1, 1̌ = 0, Ǐ = {ρ̌ | ρ ∈ I}, and for f = Σ_{k≥0} a_k X^k ∈ A_K, ‖f‖_ρ = sup_k |a_k|ρ^k if ρ ≠ 0 and ‖f‖_0 = q^{−v_X(f)}, with |π_E| = q^{−1} on W_{O_E}(k) (the Gauss norm of radius ρ on the open unit disc over W_{O_E}(k)_ℚ). Then via ι: B^b_K ↪ B^b_F, |ι(f)|_ρ = ‖f‖_{ρ̌}^r for ρ = q^{−r} ∈ ]0, 1[, and |ι(f)|_ρ = ‖f‖_{ρ̌} for ρ ∈ {0, 1} (printed '|ι(f)|_ρ = ‖f‖_{ρ̌}' for all ρ ∈ [0, 1]; see source issues).
items.locator: Lemme 1.7.2, p. 81, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.7.2: B_I as functions on the perfected tower of annuli
items.statement: If 0, 1 ∉ Ǐ, let O_Ǐ = {Σ_{n∈ℤ} a_n T^n | a_n ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_ℚ, ∀ρ ∈ Ǐ, lim_{|n|→+∞} |a_n|ρ^n = 0}; in general O_Ǐ is the set of f ∈ O_{Ǐ∖{0,1}} meromorphic at 0 if 0 ∈ Ǐ and bounded outside the annulus Ǐ ∖ {1} (lim_{ρ→1} ‖f‖_ρ < +∞). The finite étale surjective map ϕ(X) = X^q of the punctured unit disc gives a tower D_Ǐ ← D_{ϕ(I)ˇ} ← ⋯ ← D_{ϕ^n(I)ˇ} ← ⋯ inducing isometric embeddings (O_Ǐ, ‖·‖_ρ) ↪ (O_{ϕ(I)ˇ}, ‖·‖_{ρ^{1/q}}) ↪ ⋯ for ρ ∈ Ǐ, and B_I is the completion of lim_{→n≥0} O_{ϕ^n(I)ˇ} for these norms as ρ runs through I; e.g. B is the algebra of holomorphic functions on 'lim_{←n} D*', D* = {0 < |X| < 1}, the transition maps being finite étale of degree q.
items.locator: §1.7.2, pp. 81–82, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.7.3: the cyclotomic embedding X ↦ [1 + π_F] − 1 is isometric for ρ > q^{−q/(q−1)}
items.statement: Let A_K = W_{O_E}(k)[[X]] with the Frobenius ϕ(X) = (1 + X)^q − 1 and ι: A_K ↪ A_F, X ↦ [1 + π_F] − 1. If ρ ∈ [0, 1] satisfies ρ > q^{−q/(q−1)}, then for f ∈ A_K, ‖f‖_ρ = |ι(f)|_{ρ̌}^r where ρ = q^{−r} (and ‖f‖_1 = |ι(f)|_0) (printed '‖f‖_ρ = |ι(f)|_{ρ̌}'; see source issues).
items.locator: Proposition 1.7.3, p. 82, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/overconvergent-cyclotomic-rings and P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (d) plan the embedding of Berger's cyclotomic rings into B̃^† (E = Q_p, F = C_p^♭) with Berger's radius convention, not this norm identity.

items.name: §1.7.3: B_I as functions on the cyclotomic perfected tower
items.statement: If I ⊂ [0, q^{−(q−1)/q}[ (printed 'I ⊂ [0, q^{−1/(q−1)}]', which is too large for q ≥ 3; see source issues), then (with ϕ(X) = (1+X)^q − 1) B_I is the algebra of holomorphic functions on lim_{←n,ϕ} D_{ϕ^n(I)ˇ}, with a boundedness condition near the radius |X| = 1 if 0 ∈ I (i.e. 1 ∈ Ǐ). (The range should be the one of Prop. 1.7.3; see source issues.)
items.locator: §1.7.3, p. 83, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.7.4: symmetry between E and F in equal characteristic
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field, E = k((π_E)) and F = k((π_F)) with |π_E| = |π_F| = q^{−1}, and D*_E (resp. D*_F) the punctured rigid-analytic disc over E (resp. F) in the variable π_F (resp. π_E). There is an isomorphism of Fréchet algebras O(D*_E) ≅ O(D*_F), Σ_n (Σ_k a_{n,k} π_E^k) π_F^n ↦ Σ_n (Σ_k a_{n,k} π_F^k) π_E^n, under which the Gauss norm of radius q^{−r} corresponds to the Gauss norm of radius q^{−1/r} (they agree up to the power 1/r: ‖f‖_{D*_F, q^{−1/r}} = ‖f‖_{D*_E, q^{−r}}^{1/r}, e.g. f = π_F has norms q^{−r} and q^{−1}). (Proof left to the reader.)
items.locator: Proposition 1.7.4, p. 83, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.7.5: adic interpretation of the E–F symmetry
items.statement: With R = O_E ⊗̂_k O_F = k[[π_E, π_F]], 𝔛 = Spf(R) and 𝔛^ad = Spa(R, R), both algebras of Prop. 1.7.4 are the Fréchet algebra of functions on the open 𝔛^ad ∖ V(π_E π_F); the two morphisms to Spa(F, O_F) and Spa(E, O_E) identify 𝔛^ad ∖ V(π_E π_F) with D*_E and with D*_F, which are therefore isomorphic as adic spaces over k (discrete topology).
items.locator: Remarque 1.7.5, pp. 83–84, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; compare RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli (Y_S = Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) ∖ V(π[ϖ]), for perfectoid S).

items.name: §1.7.5: A and B_I for a maximally complete F = k((π_F^Γ))
items.statement: Let k|F_q be perfect and Γ ⊂ ℝ a nonzero subgroup with pΓ = Γ; F = k((π_F^Γ)) = {Σ_{α∈Γ} a_α π_F^α | a_α ∈ k, {α | a_α ≠ 0} well ordered} with |Σ_α a_α π_F^α| = sup_{a_α≠0} q^{−α}. Then A = {Σ_{α∈Γ_+} a_α T^α | a_α ∈ W_{O_E}(k), lim_𝓕 a_α = 0}, where 𝓕 is the filter of complements of well-ordered subsets of Γ, and for I ⊂ ]0, 1[ (the printed extra clause 'différent de {0} et {1}' is vacuous) B_I = {Σ_{α∈Γ} a_α T^α | a_α ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_ℚ (printed W_{O_E}(k); see source issues), ∀ρ ∈ I, lim_𝓕 |a_α|_ρ q^{−α} = 0}.
items.locator: §1.7.5, p. 84, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas (Mathlib has Hahn series, mathlib:HahnSeries, but not these descriptions).

items.name: Définition 1.8.1: the Henselian field E† and the Robba ring R
items.locator: Définition 1.8.1, p. 85, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mixed characteristic: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations (W_con(ℓ, O) = ∪_r W_r(ℓ,O), so E† = W_con[π^{-1}]) and RD.0/analytic-ring (Γ_an,con = ∪_r Γ_{(0,r]}, the Robba ring over ℓ); RD.0/extended-robba-ring for ℓ the completed algebraic closure of k((t)); PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (B̃^†_rig, E = Q_p, F = C_p^♭). The identification of Kedlaya's rings with FF's direct limits is not stated separately.

items.name: §1.8: explicit description of E†
items.locator: §1.8, p. 85, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/witt-partial-valuations defines W_con(ℓ, O) by exactly this growth condition (v_{n,r}(x) → ∞ for some r > 0).

items.name: Proposition 1.8.2: E† is a Henselian valued field with completion ℰ
items.statement: ([11] II.4.1 and II.4.2.) The ring E† with the valuation v_π is a Henselian valued field whose completion is ℰ.
items.locator: Proposition 1.8.2, p. 85, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian: 'W_con(ℓ, O) is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal (π) and residue field ℓ; it is henselian, and it is not π-adically complete when v_ℓ is nontrivial' (mixed characteristic). Equal-characteristic analogue: RD.0/bounded-robba-ring (for R^bd over k((t))). Review: only E of characteristic 0 is planned; for E = F_q((π)) the ring E†_F of overconvergent Laurent series in π over the perfect field F is not the RD.0/bounded-robba-ring (whose hypothesis is 'K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0'), so the equal-characteristic case of FF's statement is not planned and the item is missing.

items.name: Corollaire 1.8.3: E†_L|E†_F for L|F finite
items.statement: If L|F is a finite extension, then E†_L|E†_F is finite of degree [L : F]. If moreover L|F is Galois, then E†_L|E†_F is Galois and Gal(L|F) ≅ Gal(E†_L|E†_F).
items.locator: Corollaire 1.8.3, p. 86, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings: for L/ℓ finite separable Γ^L_con is finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con of the same degree, with Galois action when L/ℓ is Galois (mixed characteristic). Review: RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings covers only E of characteristic 0 (O finite over a Cohen ring); the equal-characteristic case E = F_q((π)) is not planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Remarque 1.8.5: E† and R for F = F_q((π_F^{1/p^∞})) as completed perfections of classical rings
items.statement: Let E†_{F_q((π_F))} be the classical bounded Robba ring of germs of bounded holomorphic functions of X with coefficients in E on annuli of radii [ρ, 1[ as ρ → 1. Then E†_{F_q((π_F^{1/p^∞}))} = lim_{→ρ→1} (lim_{→n→+∞} O_{[ρ^{1/q^n}, 1]})^∧, where O_{[ρ_0,1]} is the ring of bounded functions on the annulus D_{[ρ_0,1[} = {ρ_0 ≤ |X| < 1} with the sup norm, the transition maps being induced by the finite étale map D_{[ρ_0^{1/q^n},1[} → D_{[ρ_0,1[}, X ↦ X^q (and similarly for the Frobenius lift X ↦ (1+X)^q − 1). Likewise R_{F_q((π_F^{1/p^∞}))} = lim_{→ρ→1} (lim_{→n→+∞} O_{[ρ^{1/q^n}, 1[})^∧.
items.locator: Remarque 1.8.5, p. 86, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; the closest planned statements are RD.0/frobenius-equivariant-embedding (R ↪ R^alg) and PadicHodgeTheory:P7/berger-robba-identification (B^†_rig,K ⊂ B̃^†_rig).

items.name: Proposition 1.8.6: R^× = (E†)^×
items.statement: R^× = (E†)^× (a consequence of Prop. 1.9.1).
items.locator: Proposition 1.8.6, p. 86, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RD.0/units-of-robba-ring: 'for any complete valued ℓ of characteristic p with Γ^ℓ having enough units, (Γ^ℓ_an,con)^× = (Γ^ℓ_con[π^{-1}])^×' (mixed characteristic; for ℓ = F perfect, Teichmüller lifts are units). Review: RD.0/units-of-robba-ring covers only E of characteristic 0 (it assumes 'K discretely valued' of characteristic 0 with O finite over a Cohen ring); the equal-characteristic case is not planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Proposition 1.9.1: extension of holomorphic functions to the boundary radius 0
items.statement: Let I ⊂ ]0, 1] be an interval with 0 ∈ Ī (0 in the closure of I). Then B_{I∪{0}} = {x ∈ B_I | ∃A, Newt⁰_I(x)|_{]−∞,A]} ≡ +∞} = {x ∈ B_I | ∃A, Newt_I(x) ⊂ {(t, u) ∈ ℝ² | t ≥ A}} = {x ∈ B_I | ∃N ∈ ℕ, π^N x is bounded near 0}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.9.1, p. 87, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring relates units of Γ_{(0,r]} to units of Γ_r[π^{-1}] (only the unit case).

items.name: Proposition 1.9.2: extension of holomorphic functions to the boundary radius 1
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0, 1] with 1 ∈ Ī. Then B_{I∪{1}} = {x ∈ B_I | Newt_I(x) is bounded below} = {x ∈ B_I | x is bounded on an annulus of radii [ρ, 1[ for some ρ ∈ I} = {x ∈ B_I | lim_{ρ→1} |x|_ρ < +∞}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.9.2, p. 88, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated for general E; equal-characteristic-style analogue for classical rings: P7:annulus-foundations/bounded-robba-ring (f ∈ R_K is in R^bd_K iff sup_{ρ∈(r,1)}|f|_ρ < ∞).

items.name: Remarque 1.9.3: existence of lim_{ρ→1} |x|_ρ
items.statement: For x ∈ B_I with 1 ∈ Ī, lim_{ρ→1} |x|_ρ always exists in [0, +∞], since r ↦ v_r(x) (q^{−r} ∈ I) is concave and so has a limit in ℝ ∪ {−∞} at 0.
