items.locator: Remarque 1.9.3, p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.9.4: B^b = B_{[0,1]} inside B
items.statement: B^b = B_{[0,1]} = {x ∈ B | ∃n ∈ ℤ, π^n x is bounded}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.9.4, p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 1.9.5 (1): units extend over radius 0
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0, 1]. If 0 ∈ Ī then B_I^× = B_{I∪{0}}^×.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.9.5 (1), p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For I = ]0, ρ]: RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring ('If I = (0, r], [x is a unit] iff x is a unit of Γ_r[π^{-1}]', Γ_r[π^{-1}] corresponding to B_{[0,ρ]}); other intervals with 0 ∈ Ī not stated. Review: only the special case I = ]0, ρ] (mixed characteristic) is planned, so the item is missing.

items.name: Corollaire 1.9.5 (2): units extend over radius 1
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0, 1]. If 1 ∈ Ī then B_I^× = B_{I∪{1}}^×.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.9.5 (2), p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 1.9.5 (3): units of B
items.locator: Corollaire 1.9.5 (3), p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.9.6: failure of extension for relatively compact intervals
items.statement: The extension results fail when I is relatively compact in ]0, 1[: for I = ]ρ_1, ρ_2[ with 0 < ρ_1 ≤ ρ_2 < 1 (as printed; ρ_1 < ρ_2 for I to be nonempty), B_Ī ⊂ B_I is smaller than the set of bounded functions in B_I (as one checks for E = F_q((π))).
items.locator: Remarque 1.9.6, p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 1.10.1: B^{b,+}
items.locator: Définition 1.10.1, p. 89, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: A[1/π] = W_{O_E}(O_F)[1/π] with W_{O_E}(O_F) from RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property; the localization is not a separate node.

items.name: Définition 1.10.2: B_I^+, B_ρ^+ and B^+
items.statement: For an interval I of [0, 1], B_I^+ is the completion of B^{b,+} for the Gauss norms (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈I}, i.e. the closure of B^{b,+} in B_I; B_ρ^+ := B^+_{{ρ}} and B^+ = B^+_{]0,1[}.
items.locator: Définition 1.10.2, pp. 89–90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned for general F; for E = Q_p and F = C_p^♭, PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (c) defines B̃^+_rig = ∩_n ϕ^n(B^+_cris) (a different definition).

items.name: §1.10.1: B_I^+ = B^{b,+} when 0 ∈ I
items.statement: B_0^+ = B^{b,+}, and in fact B_I^+ = B^{b,+} as soon as 0 ∈ I (Corollaire 1.4.15).
items.locator: §1.10.1, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 1.10.3: B_ρ^+ for ρ ∈ |F^×|
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ |F^×| and a ∈ F with ρ = |a|. The unit ball of |·|_ρ in B^{b,+} is A[[a]/π], and hence B_ρ^+ = (A[[a]/π])^∧[1/π], the completion being π-adic.
items.locator: Exemple 1.10.3, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For E = Q_p, F = C_p^♭ and ρ = |p^♭| this is B^+_max = A_inf[ξ/p]^∧[1/p] of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bmax-period-ring; the general statement is not planned.

items.name: Lemme 1.10.4: v_{r′} ≥ (r′/r) v_r on B^{b,+}
items.statement: For x ∈ B^{b,+} and 0 < r′ ≤ r, v_{r′}(x) ≥ (r′/r) v_r(x).
items.locator: Lemme 1.10.4, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas (compare RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections (d), which uses bounds of the form (s/c) w_c).

items.name: §1.10.1: B_I^+ = B_ρ^+ = B^+_{[ρ,1[} for ρ = min I > 0
items.statement: If I ⊂ ]0, 1[ is such that ρ = inf I belongs to I and ρ > 0, then B_I^+ = B_ρ^+ = B^+_{[ρ,1[}.
items.locator: §1.10.1, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.10.5: B_ρ^+ = B^+_{[ρ,1]}
items.locator: Proposition 1.10.5, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.10.6: B^+_{[ρ,1]} → B_ρ^+ is not a Banach isomorphism
items.statement: The restriction map B^+_{[ρ,1]} → B_ρ^+ is an isomorphism of algebras but not of Banach algebras; this does not contradict the open mapping theorem because B_ρ^+ is an E-Banach space whereas B^+_{[ρ,1]} is an E^disc-Banach space.
items.locator: Remarque 1.10.6, p. 90, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.1: B^+ as an intersection of the B_ρ^+
items.statement: For ρ ≤ ρ′, B_ρ^+ ⊂ B_{ρ′}^+; for every interval I, B_I^+ = ∩_{ρ∈I} B_ρ^+; in particular B^+ = ∩_{ρ>0} B_ρ^+.
items.locator: §1.10.1, p. 91, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.1: B^+ = ∩_n ϕ^n(B_ρ^+) is the largest ϕ-bijective subring of B_ρ^+
items.statement: Since ϕ: B_ρ^+ ≅ B_{ρ^q}^+ ⊂ B_ρ^+, ϕ is an endomorphism of B_ρ^+, and for 0 < ρ < 1, B^+ = ∩_{n≥0} ϕ^n(B_ρ^+). Thus B^+ is the largest subring of B_ρ^+ on which ϕ is bijective.
items.locator: §1.10.1, p. 91, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For E = Q_p, F = C_p^♭, ρ = |p^♭|: PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (c) remarks that ∩ϕ^n(B^+_max) = ∩ϕ^n(B^+_cris) = B̃^+_rig; the general statement is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 1.10.7: B_ρ^+ and B^+ via Newton polygons and |·|_1
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ [0, 1] (ρ < 1 for the first description to make sense): B_ρ^+ = {x ∈ B_{[ρ,1[} | Newt_{[ρ,1[}(x) ≥ 0} = {x ∈ B_{[ρ,1]} | |x|_1 ≤ 1}. Also B^+ = {x ∈ B | Newt(x) ≥ 0} = {x ∈ B | |x|_1 ≤ 1}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.10.7, p. 91, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.10.8: Teichmüller series in B_ρ^+
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ ]0, 1[ and (x_n)_{n∈ℤ} a sequence of O_F with lim_{n→−∞} |x_n|ρ^n = 0. Then Σ_{n∈ℤ}[x_n]π^n converges in B_ρ^+; but when E|Q_p it is not known whether every element of B_ρ^+ is of this form, whether such an expression is unique, or whether sums and products of such elements are of this form. The same applies to B^+.
items.locator: Remarque 1.10.8, p. 91, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 1.10.9: B^+ = B^+_rig
items.statement: The ring B^+ appears in the classical p-adic Hodge theory literature under the name B^+_rig.
items.locator: Remarque 1.10.9, p. 91, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (c) defines B̃^+_rig (E = Q_p, F = C_p^♭) as ∩_n ϕ^n(B^+_cris); its identification with FF's B^+ is not stated.

items.name: Remarque 1.10.10: B^+ for F = F_q((π_F^{1/p^∞})) as functions on a perfected disc
items.statement: By §1.7.2, B^+_{F_q((π_F^{1/p^∞}))} is the ring of rigid analytic functions on 'lim_{←ϕ} D_E', D_E the open unit disc over E and ϕ: X ↦ X^q; the inclusion B^+ ⊂ B is induced by lim_{←ϕ} D*_E ⊂ lim_{←ϕ} D_E, D*_E the punctured disc.
items.locator: Remarque 1.10.10, p. 92, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.2 and Définition 1.10.11: Witt covectors and bivectors BW_{O_E}(O_F)
items.statement: For an F_q-algebra R with the discrete topology: CW^u_{O_E}(R) = lim_{→n≥1} W_{O_E,n}(R) (transition maps V_π: W_{O_E,n}(R) → W_{O_E,n+1}(R)) = {[…, a_i, …, a_{−1}, a_0] | a_i ∈ R, a_i = 0 for i ≪ 0} (unipotent Witt covectors); it extends to the group of Witt covectors CW_{O_E}(R) = {[…, a_i, …, a_{−1}, a_0] | a_i ∈ R, ∃N ≤ 0 such that the ideal generated by (a_i)_{i≤N} is nilpotent} ([24] ch. II for E = Q_p), with Verschiebung V_π; BW_{O_E}(R) = lim_{←V_π} CW_{O_E}(R) = {Σ_{i∈ℤ} V_π^i[a_i] | a_i ∈ R, ∃N such that the ideal generated by (a_i)_{i≤N} is nilpotent}. Définition 1.10.11: BW_{O_E}(O_F) = lim_{←a} BW_{O_E}(O_F/a), a running over the nonzero ideals of O_F.
items.locator: §1.10.2 and Définition 1.10.11, p. 92, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No Witt covectors in Mathlib, Tau Ceti or the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.2: explicit description of BW_{O_E}(O_F) and its embedding in B^+
items.statement: BW_{O_E}(O_F) = {Σ_{n∈ℤ}[a_n]π^n | a_n ∈ O_F, liminf_{n→−∞} q^n v(a_n) > 0} = {Σ_{n∈ℤ}[a_n]π^n | a_n ∈ O_F, ∃s > 0, ∃C, ∀n, v(a_n) ≥ q^{−n}s + C}. These series converge in B^+, giving an embedding of O_E-modules BW_{O_E}(O_F) ↪ B^+_{F,E}.
items.locator: §1.10.2, p. 93, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.2: addition of bivectors via limits of Witt addition polynomials
items.statement: Let S_n ∈ O_E[X_0, …, X_n, Y_0, …, Y_n] be the universal polynomials giving addition of truncated Witt vectors of length n + 1: [X_0, …, X_n] + [Y_0, …, Y_n] = [S_0, …, S_n]. For a = Σ_{i∈ℤ}[a_i]π^i and b = Σ_{i∈ℤ}[b_i]π^i in BW_{O_E}(O_F), a + b = Σ_{i∈ℤ}[c_i]π^i with c_i = lim_{n→+∞} S_n(a_{i−n}^{q^{−n}}, a_{i−n+1}^{q^{−n+1}}, …, a_{i−1}^{q^{−1}}, a_i, b_{i−n}^{q^{−n}}, b_{i−n+1}^{q^{−n+1}}, …, b_{i−1}^{q^{−1}}, b_i), the limit existing thanks to the convergence conditions defining BW_{O_E}(O_F) (cf. [24] ch. II). If one only imposes lim_{n→−∞} v(a_n) + nr = +∞ and lim_{n→−∞} v(b_n) + nr = +∞ for all r > 0, the limit need not exist (partly explaining Remarque 1.6.7).
items.locator: §1.10.2, p. 93, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.3: the rings A_cris,ρ and B^+_cris,ρ
items.statement: Assume E = Q_p. For ρ ∈ |F| ∩ ]0, 1[ let a_ρ = {x ∈ O_F | |x| ≤ ρ}, consider the surjection W(O_F) → O_F → O_F/a_ρ (the first map Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]p^n ↦ x_0) and b_ρ = ker(W(O_F) → O_F/a_ρ). A_cris,ρ is the p-adic completion of the divided-power envelope of b_ρ, and B^+_cris,ρ = A_cris,ρ[1/p]. If ξ = Σ_{n≥0}[ξ_n]p^n satisfies |ξ_0| = ρ then A_cris,ρ = (W(O_F)[ξ^n/n!])^∧.
items.locator: §1.10.3, pp. 93–94, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/crystalline-period-ring plans A_cris, B^+_cris for O_C (C = C_p), i.e. the case F = C_p^♭, ρ = |p^♭| (b_ρ = ker(W(O_C^♭) → O_C/p)); general F and ρ are not planned.

items.name: §1.10.3: A_cris,ρ is the final object of the crystalline site (external, Fontaine)
items.statement: The p-adic thickening A_cris,ρ ↠ O_F/a_ρ defines a final pro-object of the crystalline site Cris(Spec(O_F/a_ρ)/Spec(Z_p)), and hence A_cris,ρ = H^0((Spec(O_F/a_ρ)/Spec(Z_p))_cris, O).
items.locator: §1.10.3, p. 94, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof or reference; not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.10.12: B^+_{ρ^p} ⊂ B^+_cris,ρ ⊂ B^+_ρ
items.statement: (E = Q_p, ρ ∈ |F| ∩ ]0,1[.) There are natural inclusions B^+_{ρ^p} ⊂ B^+_cris,ρ ⊂ B^+_ρ.
items.locator: Proposition 1.10.12, p. 94, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the second inclusion in the case F = C_p^♭, ρ = |p^♭| is planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bmax-period-ring (3) ('A_cris maps continuously into A_max').

items.name: §1.10.3: B^+ = ∩_n ϕ^n(B^+_cris,ρ)
items.statement: (E = Q_p.) B^+ = ∩_{n≥0} ϕ^n(B^+_cris,ρ); hence B^+ is the largest subring of B^+_cris,ρ on which the crystalline Frobenius ϕ is bijective.
items.locator: §1.10.3, p. 94, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For F = C_p^♭ and ρ = |p^♭|, PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action (c) takes ∩_n ϕ^n(B^+_cris) as the definition of B̃^+_rig; the identification with FF's B^+ is not stated.

items.name: Corollaire 1.10.13: ϕ-invariants over B^+[1/t] and B^+_cris,ρ[1/t] agree
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field with k ⊂ O_F and (D, ϕ) a k-isocrystal. If t ∈ B^+_cris,ρ satisfies ϕ(t) = pt, then (D ⊗_{W(k)_ℚ} B^+[1/t])^{ϕ=Id} = (D ⊗_{W(k)_ℚ} B^+_cris,ρ[1/t])^{ϕ=Id}.
items.locator: Corollaire 1.10.13, p. 94, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated; PadicHodgeTheory:P7/frobenius-regularisation is a related regularization-by-Frobenius statement (B̃^†_log, F = C_p^♭).

items.name: Définition 1.10.14: the ideals 𝔭, 𝔪 of B^{b,+} and the ring 𝓑
items.statement: 𝔭 = {x ∈ B^{b,+} | v_0(x) > 0} and 𝓑 = B^{b,+}/𝔭. The projection O_F ↠ k_F induces B^{b,+} → W_{O_E}(k_F)_ℚ, whose kernel 𝔪 is a maximal ideal of B^{b,+}; 𝔪 = {Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n | ∀n, v(x_n) > 0} while 𝔭 = {Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π^n | ∃C > 0, ∀n, v(x_n) ≥ C}.
items.locator: Définition 1.10.14, p. 95, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 1.10.15: 𝓑 is a local domain
items.statement: The ring 𝓑 is a local integral domain with maximal ideal 𝔪/𝔭 and residue field W_{O_E}(k_F)_ℚ.
items.locator: Lemme 1.10.15, p. 95, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: §1.10.4: factorization B^+ → 𝓑 and bijectivity of ϕ on 𝓑
items.statement: There are factorizations B^+ ⊂ B_ρ^+ = B^+_{[ρ,1]} → B_1^+ → B_1^+/{v_0 > 0} = 𝓑, compatible with ϕ, and ϕ acts bijectively on 𝓑 (since v_0 ∘ ϕ = q v_0; printed 'v_0 ∘ ϕ = ϕ').
items.locator: §1.10.4, p. 95, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas.

items.name: External (Hensel/Newton iteration in complete rings), proof of Prop. 1.8.2
items.statement: Black box: in the complete ring B°_{[0,ρ_1]}, if P is monic and P(x)/P′(x) is topologically nilpotent (with P′(x) a unit), Newton's method converges to a root y ≡ x mod π with P(y) = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 1.8.2, démonstration, p. 86, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has Hensel's lemma in the I-adic form (mathlib:IsAdicComplete.henselianRing: an I-adically complete ring is Henselian at I) but not the normed-ring Newton iteration in this form; the Henselian property itself is planned in RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian.

items.name: Définition 2.1.1: the functor (−)^{♭,Q} on π-adic O_E-algebras
items.statement: Let Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q ≡ X^q mod π and Q(0) = 0; put Q_0 = X and Q_n = Q∘⋯∘Q (n times). A π-adic O_E-algebra is an O_E-algebra that is π-adically separated and complete. The functor (−)^{♭,Q}: {π-adic O_E-algebras} → Sets sends A to A^{♭,Q} = {(x^{(n)})_{n≥0} : x^{(n)} ∈ A, Q(x^{(n+1)}) = x^{(n)} for all n}. One writes A^♭ := A^{♭,X^q}.
items.locator: Définition 2.1.1, p. 98, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For E = Q_p, Q = X^p the underlying monoid A^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} A is Mathlib's Perfection A p (mathlib:Perfection, a monoid for A not of characteristic p); the Lubin–Tate-type Q and ramified E are absent. Nearest planned node: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring (perfectoid Tate rings, Q = X^p only).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.2: reduction modulo a closed ideal is bijective on A^{♭,Q}
items.statement: Let A be a π-adic O_E-algebra and I a closed ideal of A such that A is separated and complete for the (I + (π))-adic topology. Then reduction modulo I induces a bijection A^{♭,Q} ⥲ (A/I)^{♭,Q}. Its inverse sends (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} ∈ (A/I)^{♭,Q} to (y^{(n)})_{n≥0} with y^{(n)} = lim_{k→+∞} Q_k(x̃^{(n+k)}), where x̃^{(m)} ∈ A is any lift of x^{(m)} and the limit is taken for the (I+(π))-adic topology.
items.locator: Proposition 2.1.2, p. 99, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has the case E = Q_p, Q = X^p with p ∈ I as a monoid isomorphism: mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv (R I-adically complete, R/I of characteristic p); the general-I case for E = Q_p follows by composing two instances but is not stated. Planned only for perfectoid Tate rings: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius.

items.name: Lemme 2.1.3: Q preserves congruences with a gain
items.statement: Let A be an O_E-algebra and J an ideal of A (Q as in Déf. 2.1.1). If x, y ∈ A satisfy x ≡ y mod J, then Q(x) ≡ Q(y) mod πJ + J².
items.locator: Lemme 2.1.3, p. 99, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Elementary; no library statement for general Q. (Stated without proof.)

items.name: Corollaire 2.1.4: A^{♭,Q} is a perfect F_q-algebra isomorphic to lim_{Frob_q} A/πA
items.statement: The functor (−)^{♭,Q} factors canonically as a functor from π-adic O_E-algebras to perfect F_q-algebras, isomorphic to A ↦ lim_{←,N} A/πA with transition maps Frob_q. The ring laws on A^{♭,Q} are (x^{(n)})_n + (y^{(n)})_n = (lim_{k→+∞} Q_k(x^{(n+k)} + y^{(n+k)}))_n and (x^{(n)})_n · (y^{(n)})_n = (lim_{k→+∞} Q_k(x^{(n+k)} y^{(n+k)}))_n.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.1.4, pp. 99–100, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For E = Q_p, Q = X^p: the ring lim_{Frob} A/pA is Mathlib's mathlib:Perfection (Perfection (A ⧸ p) p; for integers of a valued field it is mathlib:PreTilt), and the multiplicative identification is mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv; the transported addition formula and the general-E, general-Q version are not in the library.

items.name: Remarque 2.1.5: Teichmüller description of W_{O_E}(R)^{♭,Q} and independence of Q
items.statement: (a) If Q = X^q then (x^{(n)})_n·(y^{(n)})_n = (x^{(n)}y^{(n)})_n. (b) For R a perfect F_q-algebra, x ↦ ([x^{1/q^n}]_Q)_{n≥0} is a bijection R ⥲ W_{O_E}(R)^{♭,Q}, [−]_Q being the Q-Teichmüller lift of Prop. 1.2.7. (c) If I is a closed ideal of W_{O_E}(R) such that W_{O_E}(R) is separated and complete for the (I+(π))-adic topology, A = W_{O_E}(R)/I and θ: W_{O_E}(R) → A the projection, then x ↦ (θ([x^{1/q^n}]_Q))_{n≥0} is a bijection R ⥲ A^{♭,Q}. (d) For two polynomials Q_1, Q_2 as in Déf. 2.1.1 there is a canonical isomorphism A^{♭,Q_1} ⥲ A^{♭,Q_2}, (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} ↦ (lim_{k→+∞} Q_{2,k}(x^{(n+k)}))_{n≥0}, the composite A^{♭,Q_1} ⥲ (A/πA)^{♭,Q_1} = (A/πA)^{♭,X^q} = (A/πA)^{♭,Q_2} ⥲ A^{♭,Q_2}.
items.locator: Remarque 2.1.5, p. 100, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Part (c) is quoted as following from 'lemme 2.1.2' (a misprint for Proposition 2.1.2; see source issues). The E = Q_p analogue of (c) for untilts is planned as PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-tilt-identification.

items.name: §2.1.2: the morphisms W_n, θ_n and Fontaine's θ: W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}) → A
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 let W_n: W_{O_E,n} → G_a, Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V_π^k[a_k]_Q ↦ Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} π^k Q_{n−1−k}(a_k). If A is an O_E-algebra with an ideal I such that π^k x^{q^{n−1−k}} = 0 for all x ∈ I and 0 ≤ k ≤ n−1 (e.g. π^{n−1}A = 0 and I has π-divided powers, or π^nA = 0 and I = (π)), then W_n induces an O_E-algebra morphism W_{O_E,n}(A/I) → A, x ↦ W_{n,Q}(x̂) for any lift x̂ ∈ W_{O_E,n}(A). Taking A/π^nA and I = (π) gives θ_n: W_{O_E,n}(A/πA) → A/π^nA, Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} V_π^k[a_k]_Q ↦ Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} π^k Q_{n−1−k}(â_k) (â_k ∈ A/π^nA lifts), with θ_1 = Id and proj∘θ_{n+1} = θ_n∘F. For A a π-adic O_E-algebra the limit is θ: W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}) → A, Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]_Q π^n ↦ Σ_{n≥0} x_n^{(0)} π^n, a morphism of functors θ: W_{O_E}∘(−)^{♭,Q} → Id on π-adic O_E-algebras.
items.locator: §2.1.2, pp. 100–101, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Library covers exactly the case E = Q_p, Q = X^p (θ: W(R♭) → R for any p-adically complete R, θ([x]) = x♯). The ramified O_E-version (Lubin–Tate Q) is not in the library; it is planned for untilts in RF2:untilts (node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence) and for perfectoid pairs over Z_p in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib. Review: the planned nodes construct θ only for perfectoid rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib, E = Q_p; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence, untilts of perfectoid pairs); the maps W_n, θ_n and θ: W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}) → A for an arbitrary π-adic O_E-algebra A and a Lubin–Tate-type Q are not planned (the source (−)^{♭,Q} is itself missing, item 260), so the item is missing.

items.name: Lemme 2.1.6: Q_n(X) lies in the ideal (π^{n−k}X^{q^k})_{0≤k≤n}
items.statement: For every n ≥ 0, Q_n(X) ∈ (π^{n−k} X^{q^k})_{0≤k≤n} (ideal of O_E[X]). Consequently, under the hypothesis of §2.1.2, π^k Q_{n−1−k}(x) = 0 for all x ∈ I and 0 ≤ k ≤ n−1.
items.locator: Lemme 2.1.6, p. 101, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Elementary polynomial lemma; no library counterpart.

items.name: Proposition 2.1.7: W_{O_E} is left adjoint to (−)^{♭,Q}
items.statement: The functors W_{O_E}: {perfect F_q-algebras} → {π-adic O_E-algebras} and (−)^{♭,Q} in the other direction are adjoint, with adjunction maps θ: W_{O_E}∘(−)^{♭,Q} → Id and the canonical isomorphism Id ⥲ (−)^{♭,Q}∘W_{O_E}, x ↦ ([x^{1/q^n}]_Q)_{n≥0}. If Q_1, Q_2 are two such polynomials, the canonical isomorphism can: (−)^{♭,Q_1} ⥲ (−)^{♭,Q_2} satisfies θ∘W_{O_E}(can) = θ.
items.locator: Proposition 2.1.7, p. 102, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned in the equivalent form of the universal property of Witt vectors of a perfect ring: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (g) (E = Q_p) and the RF0 stage text 'the pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property' (node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property). Mathlib's mathlib:Perfection.lift is only the perfection adjunction in characteristic p.

items.name: Lemme 2.1.9 (1): an element of ker θ with x_0^{(0)} ∈ πA^× generates ker θ
items.statement: Let A be a π-adic O_E-algebra without π-torsion and x = Σ_{i≥0}[x_i]_Q π^i ∈ ker(θ: W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}) → A). If x_0^{(0)} ∈ πA^×, then ker θ = (x).
items.locator: Lemme 2.1.9 (1), p. 102, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof ('bien connu lorsque E = Q_p et Q = X^p'). Planned only for perfectoid rings and E = Q_p: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c) ('an element of ker θ generates ker θ iff it is primitive'); for C = C_p see PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta.

items.name: Lemme 2.1.9 (2): ker θ = ([ϖ] − π) when π has a compatible system of Q-roots
items.statement: Let A be a π-adic O_E-algebra without π-torsion. If there is ϖ ∈ A^{♭,Q} with ϖ^{(0)} = π, then ker θ = ([ϖ] − π) (Teichmüller lift in W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}); the book writes ϖ as an underlined π, π̲); moreover, for x = Σ[x_i]_Q π^i ∈ ker θ, ker θ = (x) if and only if x_0^{(0)} ∈ πA^×.
items.locator: Lemme 2.1.9 (2), p. 102, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof in the text. Nearest planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (perfectoid, E = Q_p), PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta (ξ = [p♭] − p for C_p).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.10: θ is surjective when Frobenius of A/πA is surjective
items.statement: Let A be a π-adic O_E-algebra such that the Frobenius of A/πA is surjective. Then θ: W_{O_E}(A^{♭,Q}) → A is surjective.
items.locator: Proposition 2.1.10, pp. 102–103, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta is exactly the case E = Q_p, Q = X^p (R p-adically complete, p not a unit, Frobenius surjective on R/p). The ramified version for general E is not in the library. Review: planned only for perfectoid untilts (RF2:untilts) and in the library only for E = Q_p, Q = X^p; the statement for a general π-adic O_E-algebra is not planned (compare item 268), so the item is missing.

items.name: §2.1.3: the valuation x ↦ v(x^{(0)}) on O_K^♭
items.statement: Let K|E be a complete valued field, |·| = q^{−v(·)}. For ρ ∈ R with |π| ≤ ρ < 1 and b_ρ = {x ∈ O_K : |x| ≤ ρ}, O_K^♭ ≅ (O_K/b_ρ)^♭ (by Prop. 2.1.2). The map v: O_K^♭ → R ∪ {+∞}, x ↦ v(x^{(0)}), is a valuation on O_K^♭.
items.locator: §2.1.3, p. 103, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib defines O_K^♭ as PreTilt O p = Perfection (O/p) p (canonically the same as FF's lim_{Frob_q} O_K/π) with the valuation PreTilt.val f = v(f^♯) (multiplicative, values in ℝ≥0), for O the integers of any valued field K with v(p) ≠ 1. The identification O_K^♭ ≅ (O_K/b_ρ)^♭ is Mathlib's quotientMulEquiv only for b_ρ ∋ p.

items.name: §2.1.3: dichotomy for the tilt valuation; K^♭ is a complete perfect valued field with valuation ring O_K^♭
items.statement: With K|E complete valued: either the valuation v of O_K^♭ is trivial, and then O_K^♭ ⥲ k_K^♭ = ∩_{n≥1} k_K^{q^n}; or it is non-trivial, and then K^♭ := Frac(O_K^♭) is a complete valued perfect field of characteristic p, identified with the sequences (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} of elements of K with (x^{(n+1)})^q = x^{(n)}, and its valuation ring is O_{K^♭} = O_K^♭.
items.locator: §2.1.3, p. 103, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has the fraction field mathlib:Tilt (FractionRing (PreTilt O p)) but not completeness, the valuation-ring identification or the trivial case. Planned only for perfectoid K: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field.

items.name: Proposition 2.1.11: K algebraically closed ⇒ K^♭ algebraically closed
items.statement: Let K|E be a complete valued field. If K is algebraically closed, then K^♭ is algebraically closed.
items.locator: Proposition 2.1.11, pp. 103–104, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii) ('K is algebraically closed iff K♭ is', K perfectoid; a complete algebraically closed K|E is perfectoid).

items.name: Définition 2.2.1: primitive elements, their degree, Prim_d and irreducible primitive elements
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. 2): E|Q_p finite with residue field F_q and uniformizer π; F a complete valued perfect field of characteristic p containing F_q, with valuation v (|x| = q^{−v(x)}), O_F, m_F, residue field k_F; A = W_{O_E}(O_F), every element uniquely Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n; B^{b,+} = A[1/π], B^b = A[1/π, 1/[ϖ_F]]; B_I (I ⊂ [0,1]) the completion of B^b for the norms |·|_ρ, ρ ∈ I; Newt the Newton polygon of Ch. 1. (1) x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n ∈ A is primitive if x_0 ≠ 0 and there is d ∈ N with x_d ∈ O_F^×; its degree is the least such d. (2) Prim is the set of primitive elements and Prim_d those of degree d. (3) A primitive element is irreducible if it has degree > 0 and is not a product of two primitive elements of degree > 0.
items.locator: Définition 2.2.1, p. 104, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only degree 1 is planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals (E = Q_p; that node also allows ξ_0 = 0, e.g. ξ = p, which FF exclude) and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence (ramified). Degree-d products appear in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-divisors/product-equation-and-affineness but no general notion of primitive element of degree d.

items.name: §2.2.1: characterisations of primitive elements; Prim is a graded monoid with Prim_0 = A^×
items.statement: Let x ↦ x̄ be the reduction A → W_{O_E}(k_F). For x ∈ A the following are equivalent: x is primitive of degree d; x ∉ πA and v_π(x̄) = d; the Newton polygon of x is +∞ on ]−∞,0[, takes values in R_{>0} on [0,d[ and is 0 on [d,+∞[. Prim is a submonoid of (A,×), graded by the degree (Prim = ⨿_{d≥0} Prim_d, Prim_d·Prim_{d'} ⊂ Prim_{d+d'}), and Prim_0 = A^×.
items.locator: §2.2.1, p. 104, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node; see Définition 2.2.1.

items.name: §2.2.2: description of Prim_1 (F algebraically closed)
items.statement: Assume F algebraically closed. Then Prim_1 = {[a] − πu : a ≠ 0, v(a) > 0, u ∈ A^×}.
items.locator: §2.2.2, p. 105, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals: 'equivalently ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u with u ∈ W(R+)^×' (E = Q_p, any perfectoid pair); FF additionally require a ≠ 0.

items.name: Lemme 2.2.3: completeness of A and D = A/(a) for a ∈ Prim_1
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, a = Σ_{i≥0}[a_i]π^i ∈ Prim_1, I = (a), D = A/I. Then A is separated and complete for the (I+(π))-adic topology, hence for the I-adic topology; D is π-adically separated and complete and has no π-torsion.
items.locator: Lemme 2.2.3, p. 105, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Pieces planned for E = Q_p: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (c) ((p,[ϖ])-adic completeness of W(R+)), PerfectoidSpaces:P1/quotient-by-primitive-element (d) (W(R+)/ξ p-adically complete); π-torsion-freeness of D and I-adic completeness of A are not stated.

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.4: the tilt of D = A/(a) is O_F
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, the map O_F → D^♭, x ↦ (θ([x^{1/q^n}]))_{n≥0}, is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.4, p. 105, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-tilt-identification ('The tilt of W(R+)/J is R+', E = Q_p); ramified version via RF2:untilts.

items.name: Lemme 2.2.5: series expansion of elements of D in powers of θ([a_0])
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a = Σ[a_i]π^i ∈ Prim_1, every element of D is of the form Σ_{n≥0} θ([x_n a_0^n]) with x_n ∈ O_F and, for each n, x_n = 0 or v(x_n) < v(a_0).
items.locator: Lemme 2.2.5, pp. 105–106, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.6: every element of D has n-th roots
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, for every integer n ≥ 1 every element of D = A/(a) has an n-th root in D.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.6, pp. 106–108, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Would follow from the planned algebraic closedness of the untilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field with PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair), but is not stated. The case p = 2 of the proof is left to the reader (see source issues).

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.8: every element of D is a Teichmüller value θ([y])
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1: for every x ∈ D there is y ∈ O_F with x = θ([y]).
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.8, p. 108, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c) (approximation by sharps only).

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.9: every degree-one primitive ideal is generated by [ϖ] − π
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, I = (a): via the identification O_F = D^♭ there is ϖ ∈ O_F with ϖ^{(0)} = π, and [ϖ] − π generates I; i.e. there is x ∈ A^× with xa = [ϖ] − π.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.9, p. 108, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Follows from Lemme 2.1.9. Nearest planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c) (E = Q_p) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta (C = C_p only).

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.10 (1): Weierstrass factorisation x = u[b]([c] − π)
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and x = Σ_{i≥0}[x_i]π^i ∈ A with v(x_1) = inf{v(x_i) : i ∈ N} and v(x_0) > v(x_1). Then there are b, c ∈ O_F and u ∈ A^× with x = u[b]([c] − π).
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.10 (1), p. 108, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.10 (2): Weierstrass division y = wx + [d]
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and x = Σ[x_i]π^i ∈ A with v(x_1) = inf_i v(x_i) = 0 and v(x_0) > 0. For every y ∈ A there are d ∈ O_F and w ∈ A with y = wx + [d] (not unique, Remarque 2.2.11).
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.10 (2) and Remarque 2.2.11, pp. 108–109, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (a) (Euclidean division by a primitive element, E = Q_p, approximate form).

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.12: a-adic expansions
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1 (e.g. a = [a_0] − π with a_0 ∈ m_F∖{0}). Every x ∈ A can be written, non-uniquely, as x = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]a^n with x_n ∈ O_F.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.12, p. 109, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 2.2.13: θ([x]) = 0 ⇒ x = 0
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, θ: A → D = A/(a). If x ∈ O_F satisfies θ([x]) = 0, then x = 0.
items.locator: Lemme 2.2.13, p. 109, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via multiplicativity of Newton polygons (Ch. 1). No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 2.2.14: D is a domain, (a) is prime
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, D = A/(a) is an integral domain; hence the ideal (a) is prime.
items.locator: Lemme 2.2.14, p. 109, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Implied by the planned statement that the untilt is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair with PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field), not stated separately.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.15: X^n − 1 splits in D
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, the integral closure of O_E in D contains ∪_{n≥1} Z_p[ζ_n]; i.e. for every n ≥ 1 the polynomial X^n − 1 splits in D.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.15, pp. 109–111, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Two proofs: via norm fields [61], and via the Lubin–Tate logarithm (the latter has a gap when q = 2; see source issues). No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.16: θ([x]) = θ([y]) ⇒ v(x) = v(y)
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1: if x, y ∈ O_F satisfy θ([x]) = θ([y]), then v(x) = v(y).
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.16, p. 111, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Equivalent to |x♯| = |x| once the untilt's absolute value is known; planned only in that form: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field (E = Q_p).

items.name: §2.2.2: the valuation v on D defined by v(θ([y])) = v(y)
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, define v: D → R ∪ {+∞} by v(x) = v(y) if x = θ([y]) (well defined by Cor. 2.2.8 and Prop. 2.2.16).
items.locator: §2.2.2, p. 111, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The atlas normalises the untilt's absolute value by |x♯| = |x| (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field) rather than constructing it this way.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.17: v is a valuation and D is its valuation ring
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a = Σ[a_i]π^i ∈ Prim_1, the function v on D is a valuation extending v(a_0)·(π-adic valuation of E), with v(π) = v(a_0), and D is the valuation ring of v in Frac(D). Thus (D, v) is a complete valuation ring extending O_E, with residue field k_F. Moreover (Remarque 2.2.18), via the identification O_F = D^♭ of Cor. 2.2.4, the valuation (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} ↦ v(x^{(0)}) induced on F coincides with the given valuation of F.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.17 and Remarque 2.2.18, pp. 111–112, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Via PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field (E = Q_p: the untilt of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field with |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|); ramified version RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.19: Frac(W_{O_E}(O_F)/(a)) is algebraically closed
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and a ∈ Prim_1, the complete valued field Frac(D), D = A/(a), is algebraically closed.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.19, p. 112, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: By composition of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair (untilt along a primitive ideal is perfectoid with tilt F) and PerfectoidSpaces:P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field (K♭ algebraically closed ⇒ K algebraically closed). FF's proof uses Prop. 2.2.6, 2.2.15, 2.2.20 and Kummer theory.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.20: trivial residue extension ⇒ solvable Galois group
items.statement: Let L|K be a finite Galois extension of complete valued fields for valuations with values in R. If the associated extension of residue fields is trivial, then Gal(L|K) is solvable.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.20, pp. 112–114, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Discretely valued case from ramification groups ([59] ch. IV). No atlas node or library result found.

items.name: Lemme 2.2.21: G acts trivially on p_λ/p_{λ+}
items.statement: In the proof of Prop. 2.2.20 (L|K finite Galois, trivial residue extension, G = Gal(L|K) with no non-trivial abelian quotient): for λ ∈ R_+, with p_λ = {x ∈ O_L : v(x) ≥ λ} and p_{λ+} = {x ∈ O_L : v(x) > λ}, G acts trivially on p_λ/p_{λ+}.
items.locator: Lemme 2.2.21, pp. 112–113, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The hypothesis that G has no non-trivial abelian quotient is used in the proof though not repeated in the statement.

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.22: degree-one primitive ideals ↔ untilts (C, ι) of F
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed. Consider the pairs (C, ι) with C|E a complete algebraically closed non-archimedean field and ι: F ⥲ C^♭ an isometry (C^♭ with |(x^{(n)})_n| = |x^{(0)}|). There is a bijection Prim_{F,1}/A_F^× ⥲ {(C, ι)}/∼ sending a primitive a of degree 1 to the complete valued field A[1/π]/(a) with ι(x) = ([x^{q^{−n}}] mod (a))_{n≥0}; the inverse sends (C, ι) to the class of a generator of the kernel of A_F ⥲ A_{C^♭} →θ O_C, the first arrow induced by ι.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.22, p. 114, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/marked-untilt (E = Q_p, any perfectoid pair); RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence (ramified).

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.23 (first part): equivalence (F, a) ↔ (C, p^♭)
items.statement: The functors (F, a) ↦ W(O_F)[1/p]/([a] − p) and (C, p^♭) ↦ (C^♭, p^♭) are mutually inverse equivalences between the category of pairs (F, a) with F a complete algebraically closed valued field of characteristic p and a ∈ F^× with v(a) > 0, and the category of pairs (C, p^♭) with C a complete algebraically closed valued field extension of Q_p and p^♭ ∈ O_{C^♭} with p^{♭(0)} = p.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.23, p. 114, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Variant (with a chosen generator [a] − p) of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals.

items.name: Corollaire 2.2.23 (second part): maximally complete F gives maximally complete C
items.statement: If F is a maximally complete field of positive characteristic, then C = W(O_F)[1/p]/([a] − p) is maximally complete (recovering the construction of [53] of maximally complete fields of characteristic 0).
items.locator: Corollaire 2.2.23, p. 114, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Asserted without proof. No atlas node.

items.name: Définition 2.3.1: the set |Y|, the points' residue fields C_y, θ_y and v_y
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. 2): E|Q_p finite with residue field F_q and uniformizer π; F a complete valued perfect field of characteristic p containing F_q, with valuation v (|x| = q^{−v(x)}), O_F, m_F, residue field k_F; A = W_{O_E}(O_F), every element uniquely Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]π^n; B^{b,+} = A[1/π], B^b = A[1/π, 1/[ϖ_F]]; B_I (I ⊂ [0,1]) the completion of B^b for the norms |·|_ρ, ρ ∈ I; Newt the Newton polygon of Ch. 1. F algebraically closed. (1) |Y| = Prim^{irred}/A^×, the set of ideals of A generated by a primitive irreducible element. (2) For y ∈ |Y|_{deg=1}: p_y the associated prime ideal of A, m_y^+ = p_y[1/π] the associated maximal ideal of A[1/π] = B^{b,+}, m_y = p_y[1/π, 1/[ϖ_F]] the associated ideal of B^b; O_{C_y} = A/p_y with fraction field C_y = B^b/m_y, and θ_y: A → O_{C_y} the projection. (3) For f ∈ B^b, f(y) := θ_y(f). (4) v_y is the valuation of C_y with v_y(θ_y([x])) = v(x), |·|_y = q^{−v_y}; v(f(y)) := v_y(f(y)), |f(y)| := |f(y)|_y. (If y = (a), a = Σ[a_i]π^i ∈ Prim_1, then v_y(π) = v(a_0).)
items.locator: Définition 2.3.1, pp. 114–115, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Classical points of Y_C and their residue fields: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12: classical points ↔ Div^1(C)); untilt/primitive-ideal dictionary RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.2 (1): d(y_1, y_2) = v_{y_1}(θ_{y_1}(p_{y_2})) is an ultrametric distance
items.statement: For y_1, y_2 ∈ |Y|_{deg=1} put d(y_1, y_2) = v_{y_1}(θ_{y_1}(p_{y_2})), i.e. d(y_1, y_2) = v_{y_1}(θ_{y_1}(a_2)) if p_{y_2} = (a_2). Then d is an ultrametric distance on |Y|_{deg=1} (in valuative form: symmetric, d(y,y) = +∞, d(y_1,y_3) ≥ min(d(y_1,y_2), d(y_2,y_3))).
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.2 (1), p. 115, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.2 (2): p_{y_1} + a_d = p_{y_2} + a_d and the induced isomorphism of truncations
items.statement: With a_r = {x ∈ A : v_0(x) ≥ r} and a_{y,r} = {x ∈ O_{C_y} : v_y(x) ≥ r} = θ_y(a_r): p_{y_1} + a_{d(y_1,y_2)} = p_{y_2} + a_{d(y_1,y_2)}, whence a canonical isomorphism O_{C_{y_1}}/a_{y_1,d(y_1,y_2)} ≅ O_{C_{y_2}}/a_{y_2,d(y_1,y_2)} compatible with θ_{y_1}, θ_{y_2}. Moreover d(y_1,y_2) is the largest r ≥ 0 with p_{y_1} + a_r = p_{y_2} + a_r.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.2 (2), p. 115, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: §2.3.1: distance to the origin and the crowns |Y_r|
items.statement: The 'distance to the origin' |Y|_{deg=1} → ]0,+∞[, y ↦ v(π(y)), is continuous. For r > 0, |Y_r|_{deg=1} = {y : v(π(y)) ≤ r}; |Y_r| ⊂ |Y_{r'}| for r ≤ r' and |Y|_{deg=1} = ∪_{r>0}|Y_r|_{deg=1}.
items.locator: §2.3.1, p. 116, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Corresponds (after reparametrisation v(π(y)) = v(ϖ)/rad(y)) to the radius function of RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli (FS Prop. II.1.16).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.4: completeness of (|Y_r|_{deg=1}, d)
items.statement: For every r > 0, the ultrametric space (|Y_r|_{deg=1}, d) is complete.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.4, p. 116, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 2.3.5: [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/q}]_Q is primitive of degree 1
items.statement: Let Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q ≡ X^q mod π and Q(X) ≡ πX mod X². If ε ∈ m_F∖{0}, then [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/q}]_Q is a primitive element of degree 1 of W_{O_E}(O_F).
items.locator: Lemme 2.3.5, p. 117, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3–II.2.4), which uses the Lubin–Tate universal cover.

items.name: Définition 2.3.6: u_ε and the point y_ε
items.statement: For ε ∈ m_F∖{0}, u_ε = [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/q}]_Q and y_ε ∈ |Y|_{deg=1} is the corresponding point; this defines m_F∖{0} → |Y|_{deg=1}, ε ↦ y_ε.
items.locator: Définition 2.3.6, p. 117, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: §2.3.2: residue field of y_ε and Tate-module description of ε
items.statement: For ε ∈ m_F∖{0}: C_{y_ε} is algebraically closed and complete for v_{y_ε}, with residue field k_F, and O_{C_y}/πO_{C_y} = O_F/ū O_F with ū = ε^{1−q^{−1}}. If LT_Q is the Lubin–Tate formal group law over O_E with [π]_{LT} = Q and G = Spf(O_E[[X]]), then via O_F ⥲ O_{C_{y_ε}}^{♭,Q}, x ↦ (θ_y([x^{q^{−n}}]_Q))_{n≥0}, ε is a generator of the rank-one O_E-module T_π(G) ⊂ O_{C_{y_ε}}^{♭,Q}. LT_Q makes m_F = G(O_F) an O_E-module, in fact an E-Banach space, π acting by Frob_q.
items.locator: §2.3.2 (after Exemple 2.3.7), p. 117, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.8: y_{ε_1} = y_{ε_2} iff ε_2 ∈ O_E^×·ε_1
items.statement: For ε_1, ε_2 ∈ m_F∖{0} the following are equivalent: (1) y_{ε_1} = y_{ε_2}; (2) v_{y_{ε_1}}∘θ_{y_{ε_1}} = v_{y_{ε_2}}∘θ_{y_{ε_2}} as valuations on W_{O_E}(O_F); (3) there is a ∈ O_E^× with ε_2 = a·ε_1 (Lubin–Tate action).
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.8, pp. 117–118, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.9: Lubin–Tate parametrisation (m_F∖{0})/O_E^× ≅ |Y|_{deg=1}
items.statement: The map (G(O_F)∖{0})/O_E^× = (m_F∖{0})/O_E^× → |Y|_{deg=1}, O_E^×·ε ↦ y_ε, is a bijection.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.9, p. 118, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence plans only the φ^Z-quotient form (BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× = Div^1 (see Corollaire 2.3.13).

items.name: §2.3.2: Frobenius action on |Y| and on the parametrisation
items.statement: φ^Z acts on |Y|; for k ∈ Z and an ideal I of A, φ^k: A/I ⥲ A/φ^k(I). Via Prop. 2.3.9 this corresponds to the action of φ^Z = E^×/O_E^× on (m_F∖{0})/O_E^×. If ε_2 = π^k·ε_1 then φ^k induces an isomorphism of valued fields (C_{y_1}, v_{y_1}) ⥲ (C_{y_2}, v_{y_2}) (printed 'isométrie'; in fact v_{y_2}∘φ^k = q^k v_{y_1}).
items.locator: §2.3.2, p. 118, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Freeness of φ on Y_S is planned in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1/frobenius-quotient-and-presentation, not the compatibility with the Lubin–Tate parametrisation. See source issues for 'isométrie'.

items.name: Définition 2.3.11: the quotient distance on (m_F∖{0})/O_E^×
items.statement: m_F∖{0} carries the ultrametric distance (ε_1, ε_2) ↦ v(ε_1 − ε_2), and (m_F∖{0})/O_E^× the quotient distance d(x, y) = sup{v(ε_1 − ε_2) : x = O_E^×·ε_1, y = O_E^×·ε_2}.
items.locator: Définition 2.3.11, p. 118, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.12 (1): comparison of distances
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.12 (1), pp. 118–119, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.12 (2): the parametrisation is a homeomorphism
items.statement: The parametrisation ε ↦ y_ε induces a homeomorphism (m_F∖{0})/O_E^× ⥲ |Y|_{deg=1} (quotient topology on the left, d-topology on the right).
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.12 (2), p. 119, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Corollaire 2.3.13: P(V) ≅ |Y|_{deg=1}/φ^Z
items.statement: If V = G(O_F) viewed as an E-Banach space, there is a homeomorphism P(V) = (V∖{0})/E^× ⥲ |Y|_{deg=1}/φ^Z.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.3.13, p. 120, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the bijection is planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS Cor. II.2.4, (BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× = Div^1 as v-sheaves) gives (V∖{0})/E^× ≅ |Y|_{deg=1}/φ^Z on C-points. The homeomorphism for FF's topology on |Y|_{deg=1} (Prop. 2.3.12, Prop. 2.3.16) is not planned; the v-sheaf isomorphism does not topologise the set of C-points.

items.name: §2.3.3: the Berkovich space M(B^b)
items.statement: M(B^b) is the set of valuations of B^b extending the π-adic valuation of E and continuous for the topology defined by (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈]0,1[}, with the topology induced by the weak (pointwise) topology on maps B^b → R ∪ {+∞}; it coincides with M(B), the continuous valuations of the Fréchet algebra B.
items.locator: §2.3.3, p. 120, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berkovich spectra of Banach rings are planned in TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0 (node TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/spectrum), not for B^b or Fréchet B.

items.name: Lemme 2.3.14: v_y∘θ_y is continuous on B^b
items.statement: For every y ∈ |Y|_{deg=1}, v_y∘θ_y: B^b → R ∪ {+∞} is continuous; more precisely, with r = v_y(π), v_y(θ_y(x)) ≥ v_r(x) for x ∈ B^b.
items.locator: Lemme 2.3.14, p. 120, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Remarque 2.3.15: |Y|_{deg=1} ↪ M(B^b)
items.statement: y ↦ v_y/v_y(π) is an injection |Y|_{deg=1} ↪ M(B^b), and v_r/r ∈ M(B^b) for every r > 0.
items.locator: Remarque 2.3.15, p. 120, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.16: the Berkovich topology on |Y|_{deg=1} is the metric topology
items.statement: The topology induced on |Y|_{deg=1} by that of M(B^b) is the topology defined by the distance d.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.16, p. 120, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The proof's displayed inequality is misprinted (see source issues). No atlas node.

items.name: §2.3.4 and Lemme 2.3.18: change of E — the norm N_{E'/E} and norms of degree-one primitive elements
items.statement: Let E'|E be finite with residue field F_{q'} ⊂ F and E'_0 the maximal unramified subextension; A_{E'} = A_E ⊗_{O_{E'_0}} O_{E'}. If E'|E is totally ramified, A_{E'} = A_E ⊗_{O_E} O_{E'} is finite free of rank [E':E] over A_E, giving the norm N_{E'/E}: A_{E'} → A_E (= ∏_τ (Id⊗τ)(x) over τ ∈ Hom_E(E', Ẽ')). Lemme 2.3.18: the norm of a primitive element of degree 1 is primitive of degree 1.
items.locator: §2.3.4, Lemme 2.3.18, p. 121, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.19 (1): p_y ∩ A_E = (N_{E'/E}(a)) defines p_{E',E}
items.statement: E'|E totally ramified. If y ∈ |Y_{E'}|_{deg=1} then p_y ∩ A_E ∈ |Y_E|_{deg=1}, and if p_y = (a) then p_y ∩ A_E = (N_{E'/E}(a)). Thus Spec(A_{E'}) → Spec(A_E) induces p_{E',E}: |Y_{E'}|_{deg=1} → |Y_E|_{deg=1}.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.19 (1), p. 121, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Left as an exercise in the text (see source issues). Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (change of coefficient field on the curve).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.19 (2): O_{C_y} ≅ O_{C_{y'}}
items.statement: If y = p_{E',E}(y'), the canonical morphism O_{C_y} → O_{C_{y'}} is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.19 (2), p. 121, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Left as an exercise in the text.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.19 (3): fibres of p_{E',E}
items.statement: p_{E',E} is surjective with fibres of cardinality [E':E]; if E'|E is Galois, Gal(E'|E) acts on |Y_{E'}|_{deg=1} over |Y_E|_{deg=1} and the fibres of p_{E',E} are principal homogeneous under this action.
items.locator: Proposition 2.3.19 (3), p. 121, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Left as an exercise in the text.

items.name: Théorème 2.4.1: primitive elements of degree d are products of d primitive elements of degree 1
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and f ∈ A primitive of degree d ≥ 1. Then there are a_1, …, a_d ∈ A primitive of degree 1 with f = ∏_{i=1}^d a_i.
items.locator: Théorème 2.4.1, pp. 122–123, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-divisors/product-equation-and-affineness and /relative-degree-criterion (FS VI.1.2–VI.1.3: products of primitive equations; degree-d divisors characterised on geometric fibres), which do not state the factorisation of a degree-d primitive element.

items.name: Corollaire 2.4.2: irreducible primitive = primitive of degree 1
items.statement: For F algebraically closed, the primitive irreducible elements are exactly the primitive elements of degree 1.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.4.2, p. 124, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Corollaire 2.4.3: Weierstrass decomposition f = u([x_1] − π)⋯([x_d] − π)
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and f ∈ A primitive of degree d ≥ 1 there are x_1, …, x_d ∈ m_F and u ∈ A^× with f = u·([x_1] − π)⋯([x_d] − π).
items.locator: Corollaire 2.4.3, p. 124, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 2.4.4: v(f(y)) = v_λ(f) when λ = v_y(π) is not a slope
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, f ∈ B^b and y ∈ |Y|_{deg=1} such that λ = v_y(π) is not a slope of Newt(f). Then v(f(y)) = v_λ(f).
items.locator: Lemme 2.4.4, p. 124, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Reduces to the classical fact for Laurent series over a complete valued field (planned for classical annuli in PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks).

items.name: Théorème 2.4.5: division by [z] − π for any positive slope
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and f ∈ A such that Newt(f) has a strictly positive slope. Then there are a ∈ A primitive of degree 1 and g ∈ A with f = ag; moreover a can be chosen of the form [z] − π with v(z) any strictly positive slope of Newt(f).
items.locator: Théorème 2.4.5, pp. 124–125, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 2.4.6: factoring out finitely many slopes in B^b
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, f ∈ B^b and λ_1, …, λ_d a finite set of strictly positive slopes of Newt(f), counted with multiplicities. Then f = ∏_{i=1}^d([z_i] − π)·g with g ∈ B^b and (v(z_1), …, v(z_d)) = (λ_1, …, λ_d).
items.locator: Théorème 2.4.6, p. 125, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: §2.4.1.1: the radius ‖y‖ = |π(y)| and the annuli |Y_I|
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y|, ‖y‖ = |π(y)| ∈ ]0,1[; for an interval I of ]0,1[ (or [0,1]), |Y_I| = {y ∈ |Y| : ‖y‖ ∈ I}.
items.locator: §2.4.1.1, p. 126, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Radius function and annuli Y_{S,I}: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli (different normalisation).

items.name: Lemme 2.4.7: θ_y extends continuously to B_I
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and I an interval of [0,1]. For y ∈ |Y_I|, θ_y: B^b → C_y extends to a continuous morphism θ_y: B_I → C_y (Fréchet topology on B_I, valuation topology on C_y); indeed |f(y)| ≤ |f|_ρ for ρ = ‖y‖ and f ∈ B^b.
items.locator: Lemme 2.4.7, p. 126, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 2.4.8: ker(θ_y: B_I → C_y) = B_I·m_y is principal
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and y ∈ |Y_I|. Then ker(θ_y: B_I → C_y) = B_I·m_y, in particular principal; likewise ker(θ_y: B_I^+ → C_y) = B_I^+·m_y^+.
items.locator: Lemme 2.4.8, pp. 126–127, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate (FS II.1.4: 0 → A →ξ A → B → 0 exact on rational neighbourhoods of the untilt).

items.name: Théorème 2.4.10: zeros of f ∈ B_I at every positive slope
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, I an interval of [0,1], f ∈ B_I non-zero and λ a strictly positive slope of Newt_I(f). Then there are z ∈ O_F with v(z) = λ and g ∈ B_I with f = ([z] − π)·g.
items.locator: Théorème 2.4.10, p. 127, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11, maximal ideals of affinoid rings are classical points) — not the Newton-polygon statement.

items.name: Corollaire 2.4.11: slopes of Newt_I(f) are the valuations of the zeros of f
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and f ∈ B_I non-zero, the non-zero slopes of Newt_I(f) are {−log_q‖y‖ : y ∈ |Y_I|, f(y) = 0}.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.4.11, p. 127, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 2.5.1 (1): B_I is a complete valued field for I = {0} or {ρ}, ρ ∉ |F|
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and I ⊂ [0,1[ compact. If I = {0}, or I = {ρ} with ρ ∉ |F|, then B_I is a complete valued field (B_{{0}} = ℰ = W_{O_E}(F)[1/π], the discretely valued field of Ch. 1, not the base field E).
items.locator: Théorème 2.5.1 (1), p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses Prop. 1.6.25. No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 2.5.1 (2): B_I is a PID with maximal spectrum |Y_I|
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and I ⊂ [0,1[ compact, not of the form in (1). Then B_I is a principal ideal domain and |Y_{I∖{0}}| (= |Y_I|) ⥲ Spm(B_I) (printed '|Y_I| ⥲ Spm(B_{I∖{0}})', false when 0 ∈ I: Spm(B_{]0,ρ]}) has maximal ideals that are not of the form ker θ_y; see source issues).
items.locator: Théorème 2.5.1 (2), p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned only for compact I ⊂ ]0,1[: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (FS II.1.11–II.1.12: for a connected affinoid U = Spa(B,B+) ⊂ Y_C, B is a PID and Spm(B) ↔ classical points). The case 0 ∈ I (e.g. I = [0,ρ], FF Thm. 2.5.1(2) and Thm. 2.5.3) is not planned: the FS node is for affinoids of Y_C, which excludes the boundary V(π). RD.0 plans the PID property only for discretely valued ℓ (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) and for F the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring).

items.name: Lemme 2.5.2: a factorial-type criterion for principality
items.statement: Let A be an integral domain with a subset E ⊂ Spm(A) of principal ideals such that every non-zero x ∈ A factors as x = u∏_{i∈I} a_i with u ∈ A^× and (a_i) ∈ E for all i. Then A is principal.
items.locator: Lemme 2.5.2, p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof; follows quickly from mathlib:IsPrincipalIdealRing.of_prime (every prime ideal principal ⇒ PID), but not in the library as stated.

items.name: Théorème 2.5.3: {x ∈ B_{[0,ρ]} : v_π(x) ≥ 0} is a PID
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and ρ ∈ [0,1[. The ring {x ∈ B_{[0,ρ]} : v_π(x) ≥ 0} is principal, with maximal ideals given by {(π)} ∪ |Y_{]0,ρ]}|.
items.locator: Théorème 2.5.3, p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Corollaire 2.5.4: |Y| ↔ closed maximal ideals of B
items.statement: For F algebraically closed, y ↦ B·m_y is a bijection between |Y| and the closed maximal ideals of B; likewise for every I ⊂ ]0,1[, |Y_I| is identified with the closed maximal ideals of B_I.
items.locator: Corollaire 2.5.4, p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the affinoid case (compact I) is planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains.

items.name: §2.6: convergence of Weierstrass products ∏(1 − [z_i]/π) in B^+
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and (z_i)_{i≥1} a sequence of m_F tending to 0. Then the infinite product ∏_{i=1}^{+∞}(1 − [z_i]/π) converges in B^+.
items.locator: §2.6, p. 128, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 2.6.1: Weierstrass factorisation near 0
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, I an interval of ]0,1] whose closure contains 0 (printed '0 ∈ I'; the overline is lost in extraction), and ρ_0 ∈ I. For every f ∈ B_I there are a sequence (z_i)_{i≥1} of m_F tending to 0 and g ∈ B_{I∪{0}} with no zeros in |Y_{]0,ρ_0]}| such that f = g·∏_{i=1}^{+∞}(1 − [z_i]/π).
items.locator: Théorème 2.6.1, p. 129, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses Prop. 1.9.1. No atlas node.

items.name: Exemple 2.6.2: Weierstrass products on B_{]0,1]} and B^+
items.statement: For F algebraically closed, every f ∈ B_{]0,1]} (resp. B^+) can be written f = g·∏_{i=1}^{+∞}(1 − [z_i]/π) with g ∈ B^b (resp. g ∈ B^{b,+}) and z_i ∈ m_F, z_i → 0.
items.locator: Exemple 2.6.2, p. 129, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Définition 2.7.1: B^+_{dR,y} and ord_y
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y| (F algebraically closed), B^+_{dR,y} is the m_y-adic completion of B^b; ord_y: B^+_{dR,y} → N ∪ {+∞} is its discrete valuation, extended to B_I when y ∈ |Y_I| (ord_y(f) = order of vanishing of f at y).
items.locator: Définition 2.7.1, p. 130, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration. For E = Q_p Mathlib has mathlib:BDeRhamPlus (completion of W(O^♭)[1/p] along ker θ, for O = O_{C_y}), which agrees with FF's m_y-adic completion of B^b only after a comparison not in the library.

items.name: Définition 2.7.1 (claims): B^+_{dR,y} is a complete DVR, equal to the completions of B_I and B_I^+
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y_I|, B^+_{dR,y} coincides with the m_y-adic completion of B_I and the m_y^+-adic completion of B_I^+; it is a complete discrete valuation ring ('B^+_{dR,y} = Ô_{Y,y}').
items.locator: Définition 2.7.1, p. 130, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration ('at a geometric untilt B^+_dR is a complete DVR whose residue field is the untilt'); PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-complete-dvr for C = C_p. Mathlib's BDeRham file lists the DVR property as TODO.

items.name: Définition 2.7.2: positive divisors on Y_I and div(f)
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0,1]. (1) Div^+(Y_I) is the monoid of formal sums D = Σ_{y∈|Y_I|} a_y[y] ∈ N[|Y_I|] such that supp(D) ∩ |Y_J| is finite for every compact J ⊂ I. (2) For f ∈ B_I non-zero, div(f) = Σ_y ord_y(f)[y]; its support is {y ∈ |Y_I| : f(y) = 0}.
items.locator: Définition 2.7.2, p. 130, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node for divisors of functions on Y_I.

items.name: Proposition 2.7.3: div(f) and the Newton polygon
items.statement: For F algebraically closed and f ∈ B_I∖{0}, the numbers −log_q‖y‖ counted with multiplicities (ord_y(f))_{y∈|Y_I|} are the finite strictly positive slopes of Newt(f) counted with multiplicity; moreover div(f) determines Newt_I(f) up to translation by an element of Z × R. Consequently (Prop. 1.9.1) if 0 is in the closure of I, f ∈ B_{I∪{0}} iff supp(div f) ⊂ |Y_{[ρ,1]}| for some ρ > 0; and (Prop. 1.6.25) if 1 ∉ I, f ∈ B_I^× iff div(f) = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7.3, p. 130, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 2.7.4: divisibility is detected by divisors; div is injective
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed and I an interval of [0,1] different from {1}. (1) For f, g ∈ B_I non-zero, f ∈ B_I·g ⟺ div(f) ≥ div(g). (2) The monoid morphism div: (B_I∖{0})/B_I^× → Div(Y_I) is injective. The same holds with B_I replaced by B_I^+[1/[ϖ_F]].
items.locator: Théorème 2.7.4, p. 131, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Remarque 2.7.5: divisors supported near 0 are principal in B^+
items.statement: If D ∈ Div^+(Y) has supp(D) ⊂ |Y_{]0,ρ]}| for some ρ ∈ ]0,1[, there is f ∈ B^+ with div(f) = D (an infinite product ∏(1 − [z_i]/π), z_i ∈ m_F, z_i → 0). The image of div is not characterised (analogue of [49] §8).
items.locator: Remarque 2.7.5, p. 131, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Generalised in Proposition 3.4.6. No atlas node.

items.name: Ch. 3 introduction: A_{F̂̄}^{G_F} = A_F (from Ax's theorem)
items.statement: Let F be a perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure with completion F̂̄ and G_F = Gal(F̄|F). By Ax, F̂̄^{G_F} = F, and therefore A_{F̂̄}^{G_F} = A_F. One sets |Y_F| = Prim^{irred}_F/A_F^×.
items.locator: Chapitre 3, §3.1, p. 133, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned only in characteristic 0 for C_p: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants.

items.name: Lemme 3.1.1: m_F ⊂ tr_{L/F}(O_L) for finite L|F
items.statement: Let F be a perfect complete valued field of characteristic p and L|F a finite extension. Then m_F ⊂ tr_{L/F}(O_L).
items.locator: Lemme 3.1.1, p. 134, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (v): 'if S is faithfully flat over R, then Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°°'.

items.name: Corollaire 3.1.2: vanishing of continuous Galois cohomology
items.statement: (Continuous cohomology.) m_F·H^1(G_F, O_{F̂̄}) = 0, H^1(G_F, m_{F̂̄}) = 0 and H^1(G_F, 1 + m_{F̂̄}) = 0.
items.locator: Corollaire 3.1.2, p. 134, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Tate's method [60] + Lemme 3.1.1. Nearest planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-vanishing-on-hk (characteristic 0, cyclotomic).

items.name: Lemme 3.1.3: U = 1 + W_{O_E}(m_{F̂̄}) is a topological group
items.statement: Give A_{F̂̄} the weak topology and U := ker(A_{F̂̄}^× → W_{O_E}(k_{F̄})^×) = 1 + W_{O_E}(m_{F̂̄}) the induced topology. Then U is a topological group, and for fixed ρ ∈ ]0,1[ the subgroups {x ∈ U : |x − 1|_ρ ≤ ε}, ε > 0, form a basis of neighbourhoods of 1.
items.locator: Lemme 3.1.3, p. 134, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 3.1.4: filtration of U
items.statement: With U_k = 1 + π^k W_{O_E}(m_{F̂̄}) (k ≥ 1), there are isomorphisms of topological groups U ⥲ lim_k U/U_k, U/U_1 ⥲ 1 + m_{F̂̄} and U_k/U_{k+1} ⥲ m_{F̂̄}.
items.locator: Lemme 3.1.4, p. 135, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Left as an exercise in the text. No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.5: H^1(G_F, 1 + W_{O_E}(m_{F̂̄})) = 0
items.statement: H^1(G_F, 1 + W_{O_E}(m_{F̂̄})) = 0 (continuous cohomology).
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.5, p. 135, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.6: Galois-stable primitive ideals descend
items.statement: Let a ∈ A_{F̂̄} be primitive with (σ(a)) = (a) as ideals of A_{F̂̄} for every σ ∈ G_F. Then there is b ∈ A_F primitive with (a) = (b).
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.6, p. 135, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.7: divisor of an irreducible primitive element over F
items.statement: G_F acts isometrically (hence continuously) on |Y_{F̂̄}|, and (a) ↦ div(a) maps |Y_F| to Div^+_fin(Y_{F̂̄})^{G_F}. If a ∈ A_F is primitive irreducible, then div(a) = Σ_{σ} [y^σ] (σ over G_F/G_L; printed 'σ ∈ Gal(L|F)') with y ∈ |Y_{F̂̄}|, G_L = Stab_{G_F}(y) and [L:F] = deg(a).
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.7, p. 136, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.1.8: |Y_F| = |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F-fin}/G_F
items.statement: Let |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F−fin} be the points of |Y_{F̂̄}| with finite G_F-orbit. There is a surjective Galois-invariant map β: |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F−fin} → |Y_F| whose fibres are the G_F-orbits, |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F−fin}/G_F ⥲ |Y_F|, and deg(y) = |β^{−1}(y)| for y ∈ |Y_F|.
items.locator: Théorème 3.1.8, p. 136, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F4 explicitly does not assert a classification of all closed points for non-algebraically-closed F.

items.name: §3.1.3.1: perfectoid fields over E
items.statement: A complete valued field K|E is perfectoid if it is not discretely valued and the Frobenius of O_K/π_E O_K is surjective. K^♭ carries the absolute value |(x^{(n)})_{n≥0}| = |x^{(0)}|.
items.locator: §3.1.3.1, p. 137, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation (formulated with K°/p; equivalent).

items.name: Proposition 3.1.9 (a): K^♭ is a complete perfect valued field with |K| = |K^♭|
items.statement: Let K|E be perfectoid. Then K^♭ is a complete valued perfect field and |K| = |K^♭|.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.9, p. 137, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field ('|K♭^×| = |K^×|', valuation ring K♭° = lim K°).

items.name: Proposition 3.1.9 (b): θ surjective with kernel generated by a primitive element of degree 1
items.statement: Let K|E be perfectoid. Then θ: W_{O_E}(O_{K^♭}) → O_K is surjective and its kernel is generated by a primitive element of degree 1.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1.9, p. 137, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (E = Q_p); surjectivity for E = Q_p is mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta. Ramified version: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate (generator π − a[ϖ]).

items.name: Corollaire 3.1.10: K perfectoid is algebraically closed iff K^♭ is
items.statement: A perfectoid field K|E is algebraically closed if and only if K^♭ is.
items.locator: Corollaire 3.1.10, p. 137, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii); one direction also PerfectoidSpaces:P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field.

items.name: Théorème 3.1.11: residue fields of |Y_F| are perfectoid with tilt of degree d over F
items.statement: Let a ∈ A_F be primitive irreducible of degree d. Then K = B^b_{F,E}/(a) is a perfectoid field extension of E, and F → K^♭, x ↦ (x^{q^{−n}} mod a)_{n≥0}, makes K^♭ an extension of F of degree d.
items.locator: Théorème 3.1.11, pp. 138–139, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The case d = 1 is the planned untilt construction (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts); degree d > 1 is not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 3.1.12: every perfect F has a perfectoid untilt over E
items.statement: There is a perfectoid field K|E with K^♭ ≅ F; e.g. K = B^b_F/([a] − π) with 0 < |a| < 1.
items.locator: Corollaire 3.1.12, p. 139, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair with J = ([a] − p) (E = Q_p); ramified via RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence.

items.name: Définition 3.1.13: m_y, K_y, θ_y for y ∈ |Y_F|
items.statement: For y = (a) ∈ |Y_F| with a ∈ Prim^{irred}_F: m_y = B^b_F·a, m_y^+ = B^{b,+}·a; K_y = B^b_F/m_y = B^{b,+}/m_y^+ (a perfectoid field); θ_y: B^b_F → K_y, with |·|_y normalised by |θ_y([x])|_y = |x|, so that K_y^♭|F is isometric.
items.locator: Définition 3.1.13, p. 139, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Degree-one points planned via RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts; general degree not planned.

items.name: Remarques 3.1.14–3.1.15: surjectivity of θ_y and points of the form ([a] − π)
items.statement: θ_y: A_F → O_{K_y} is surjective only if deg(y) = 1. Unlike the algebraically closed case, a degree-1 point y ∈ |Y_F| need not be of the form ([a] − π); it is iff there is ϖ ∈ K_y^♭ with ϖ^{(0)} = π.
items.locator: Remarques 3.1.14 and 3.1.15, p. 139, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.2.1: almost purity for perfectoid fields
items.statement: Let K|E be perfectoid with tilt K^♭. Every finite extension of K is perfectoid, and (−)^♭ induces an equivalence between finite étale K-algebras and finite étale K^♭-algebras.
items.locator: Théorème 3.2.1, p. 140, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (i)–(ii) (contained in [56]; FF give a different proof via Cor. 3.1.10).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.2: m_K ⊂ tr_{L/K}(O_L) for perfectoid K
items.statement: Let K|E be perfectoid and L|K a finite extension. Then m_K ⊂ tr_{L/K}(O_L).
items.locator: Proposition 3.2.2, pp. 140–141, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Implied by, but not stated in, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iv) (L°a almost finite étale over K°a); the trace inclusion is stated only in characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (v)) and for Z_p-towers (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-trace-almost-surjective).

items.name: Théorème 3.3.1 (1)(a)–(c): the map β and the residue fields
items.statement: There is β: |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F−fin} → |Y_F| inducing a bijection |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F−fin}/G_F ⥲ |Y_F|. If z ∈ |Y_{F̂̄}| maps to y = β(z) then (a) C_z is algebraically closed and K_y is perfectoid; (b) [K_y^♭ : F] = |G_F·z| = |β^{−1}(y)| = deg(y); (c) C_z = K̂̄_y (completed algebraic closure of K_y).
items.locator: Théorème 3.3.1 (1), p. 141, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Summary of 3.1.8, 3.1.11 and the proof of 3.2.1; no atlas node for non-algebraically-closed F.

items.name: Théorème 3.3.1 (1)(d): Gal(K̄_y|K_y) ≅ Gal(F̄|K_y^♭)
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y_F|, Gal(K̄_y|K_y) ⥲ Gal(F̄|K_y^♭).
items.locator: Théorème 3.3.1 (1)(d), p. 141, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger.

items.name: Théorème 3.3.1 (2): degree-d points ↔ perfectoid fields with tilt of degree d over F
items.statement: Let E_d = {(K, ι)}/∼ where K|E is perfectoid and ι: F ↪ K^♭ makes K^♭ an extension of degree d of F (ι must be continuous/isometric; see source issues). Then there is a bijection E_d ⥲ |Y_F|_{deg=d}.
items.locator: Théorème 3.3.1 (2), p. 141, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Degree 1 corresponds to PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals; degree d > 1 not planned (cf. FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F4).

items.name: Définition 3.4.1: ‖y‖ = |a_0|^{1/d} and |Y_{F,I}|
items.statement: ‖·‖: |Y_F| → ]0,1[ sends the class of a primitive irreducible a = Σ_{i≥0}[a_i]π^i of degree d to |a_0|^{1/d}; for an interval I of [0,1], |Y_{F,I}| = {y ∈ |Y_F| : ‖y‖ ∈ I}.
items.locator: Définition 3.4.1, p. 142, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: By Lemme 3.4.2(1) ‖y‖ = |π|_y, which is the radius function of RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli up to normalisation; FF's formula |a_0|^{1/d} is not planned.

items.name: Lemme 3.4.2: ‖y‖ = |π|_y and the Newton polygon of an irreducible primitive element
items.statement: (1) For y ∈ |Y_F|, ‖y‖ = |π|_y. (2) If y = (a) with a ∈ Prim^{irred}_{F,deg(y)}, the Newton polygon of a is +∞ on ]−∞,0[, 0 on [deg(y),+∞[ and a straight line of slope −log_q‖y‖ on [0, deg(y)]. Consequently ‖β(·)‖ = ‖·‖.
items.locator: Lemme 3.4.2, p. 142, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 3.4.3 and sequel: |θ_y(f)|_y ≤ |f|_{‖y‖}; extension to B_I and kernels
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y_F| and f ∈ B^b, |θ_y(f)|_y ≤ |f|_{‖y‖}. Hence for y ∈ |Y_I|, θ_y extends continuously to θ_y: B_I → K_y, and ker(θ_y: B_I → K_y) = B_I·m_y, ker(θ_y: B_I^+ → K_y) = B_I^+·m_y^+.
items.locator: Lemme 3.4.3, pp. 142–143, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Degree-one analogue planned in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate.

items.name: §3.4.1: B^+_{dR,y} and ord_y for y ∈ |Y_F|
items.statement: For y ∈ |Y_F|, B^+_{dR,y} is the m_y-adic completion of B; it is a discrete valuation ring, with valuation ord_y: B^+_{dR,y} → N ∪ {+∞}.
items.locator: §3.4.1, p. 143, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only partly planned: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-divisors/completed-rings-B-plus-and-B constructs the completion B^+_{Div^d} along a degree-d divisor, and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration asserts the complete-DVR property only 'at a geometric untilt' (d = 1, C algebraically closed). That B^+_{dR,y} is a discrete valuation ring for a closed point y of degree d of Y_F, F perfect not algebraically closed, is not planned.

items.name: Théorème 3.4.4: slopes and zeros over a perfect F
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0,1] and f ∈ B_{F,I} non-zero. The non-zero slopes of Newt_I(f) are {−log_q‖y‖ : y ∈ |Y_{F,I}|, f(y) = 0} (printed '{‖y‖ : …}'), each counted with multiplicity deg(y)·ord_y(f): the multiplicity of λ is Σ_{‖y‖ = q^{−λ}, f(y)=0} ord_y(f)·deg(y).
items.locator: Théorème 3.4.4, p. 143, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Lemme 3.4.5: normalised generators a_i/π^{deg y_i} → 1
items.statement: Let (y_i)_{i≥0} be a sequence of |Y_F| with lim ‖y_i‖ = 0. Then there are primitive a_i ∈ A_F with y_i = (a_i) and lim_{i→+∞} a_i/π^{deg y_i} = 1 in B_F^+.
items.locator: Lemme 3.4.5, pp. 143–144, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The proof's estimates contain an exponent error (see source issues); the statement holds. No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.6: divisors near 0 are principal in B^+
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ ]0,1[. For every D ∈ Div^+(Y_{]0,ρ]}) there is f ∈ B^+ with div(f) = D.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.6, p. 144, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.7: divisors near the outer boundary are dominated by principal ones
items.statement: For ρ ∈ ]0,1[ and D ∈ Div^+(Y_{[ρ,1[}) there is a non-zero f ∈ B with div(f) ≥ D.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.7, p. 145, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.5.1 (1): B_I a complete valued field (perfect F)
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1[ be compact. If I = {0}, or I = {ρ} with ρ ∉ |F|^{1/∞}, then B_I is a complete valued field.
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.1 (1), p. 145, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.5.1 (2): B_I is a PID (perfect F)
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1[ be compact, not as in (1). Then B_I is a principal ideal domain and |Y_{F,I∖{0}}| (= |Y_{F,I}|) ⥲ Spm(B_I) (printed '|Y_{F,I}| ⥲ Spm(B_{I∖{0}})', false when 0 ∈ I; see source issues).
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.1 (2), p. 145, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned only for F algebraically closed (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains) and, in Kedlaya's setting, for discretely valued ℓ (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid).

items.name: Théorème 3.5.1 (3): holomorphic functions at 0 form a PID
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1[ be compact with 0 ∈ I and I ≠ {0}. Then {x ∈ B_I : v_π(x) ≥ 0} is a principal ideal domain whose maximal ideals are in bijection with |Y_{F,I}| ∪ {(π)}.
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.1 (3), p. 145, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: §3.5.2: Div^+(Y_I) and the closed ideals a_{−D}
items.statement: For I an interval of ]0,1[, Div^+(Y_I) = lim_J Div^+(Y_J) over compact J ⊂ I (Div^+(Y_J) the free abelian monoid on Spm(B_J), i.e. the non-zero ideals of B_J), i.e. {D = Σ m(y)[y] : supp(D) ∩ |Y_J| finite for all compact J ⊂ I}. For D ∈ Div^+(Y_I), a_{−D} = {f ∈ B_I : div(f) ≥ D}, a closed ideal of B_I.
items.locator: §3.5.2, p. 146, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.2: closed ideals of B_I ↔ positive divisors
items.statement: For I an interval of ]0,1[, D ↦ a_{−D} identifies Div^+(Y_I) with the non-zero closed ideals of B_I.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.2, p. 146, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Kedlaya-setting analogue for discretely valued ℓ: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (closed ideals of Γ_an,r are principal).

items.name: Corollaire 3.5.3: |Y_I| ↔ closed maximal ideals of B_I
items.statement: For I an interval of ]0,1[, |Y_I| is identified with the set of closed maximal ideals of B_I.
items.locator: Corollaire 3.5.3, p. 146, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.5.5: divisors and ideals (perfect F)
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0,1] not reduced to {0} or {1}, and f, g ∈ B_I non-zero. (1) div(f) ≥ div(g) iff f ∈ B_I·g. (2) div(f) = div(g) iff f ∈ B_I^×·g. (3) div induces an injection (B_I∖{0})/B_I^× ↪ Div^+(Y_I) whose image corresponds, via Prop. 3.5.2, to the principal ideals of B_I.
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.5, p. 146, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.6: B_I f + B_I g principal iff inf(div f, div g) principal
items.statement: Let I be an interval of ]0,1[ and f, g ∈ B_I. The ideal B_I f + B_I g is principal iff the divisor inf{div(f), div(g)} is principal.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.6, p. 147, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses R^1 lim B_J = 0 ([31] 0_III 13.2.4). No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.5.7 (Kedlaya [42] 2.9.6): B_{]0,ρ]} is Bézout
items.statement: For ρ ∈ ]0,1[, B_{]0,ρ]} is a Bézout ring, and its closed ideals are exactly its principal ideals.
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.7, p. 147, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
