items.note: Planned only in Kedlaya's setting for discretely valued ℓ (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout) and for F the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring); not for a general perfect F.

items.name: Corollaire 3.5.8: the Robba ring R_F is Bézout
items.statement: The Robba ring R_F (Déf. 1.8.1) is a Bézout ring.
items.locator: Corollaire 3.5.8, p. 147, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Same partial coverage as Théorème 3.5.7 (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring for ℓ^alg only).

items.name: Définition 3.5.9: meromorphic functions M(Y)
items.statement: M(Y) = lim_I Frac(B_I), I running over the compact intervals of ]0,1[.
items.locator: Définition 3.5.9, p. 147, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.10: M(Y) = Frac(B)
items.statement: M(Y) = Frac(B): every meromorphic function on Y is a quotient of two holomorphic ones.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.10, p. 148, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Prop. 3.4.7. No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.5.11: divisors of meromorphic functions
items.statement: div: M(Y)^× → Div(Y), f ↦ Σ_{y∈|Y|} ord_y(f)[y] (with div(0) = +∞, so B = {f ∈ M(Y) : div(f) ≥ 0}) induces an injection M(Y)^×/B^× ↪ Div(Y) such that, for f, g ∈ M(Y)^×, div(f) ≥ div(g) ⟺ f ∈ B·g.
items.locator: Théorème 3.5.11, p. 148, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node.

items.name: Théorème 3.6.1: Galois invariants B_{F̂̄}^{G_F} = B_F and (B^+_{F̂̄})^{G_F} = B^+_F
items.statement: For F perfect with completed algebraic closure F̂̄ and G_F = Gal(F̄|F): B_{F̂̄}^{G_F} = B_F and (B^+_{F̂̄})^{G_F} = B^+_F.
items.locator: Théorème 3.6.1, pp. 148–149, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the B case is proved in the text (generalised to all B_I in §11.2.4, Remarque 3.6.2). No atlas node.

items.name: External: Weierstrass preparation for O_F[[π]] (case E = F_q((π)))
items.statement: For E = F_q((π)) and A = O_F[[π]]: every primitive series Σ x_nπ^n (0 < |x_0| < 1, some x_d a unit) is, up to A^×, a unique monic polynomial (distinguished polynomial) in O_F[π]; irreducible primitive series correspond to irreducible monic polynomials P with |P(0)|^{1/deg P} < 1.
items.locator: Introduction p. 98; Exemple 2.2.2, p. 104, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the libraries. Mathlib's Weierstrass preparation (mathlib:PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassFactorization) assumes the coefficient ring complete for its maximal ideal, and O_F is not: its maximal ideal is idempotent, so the m-adic topology is not the valuation topology. The ideal-adic variant (IsWeierstrassDivisorAt) would need the primitive series to be distinguished at a pseudo-uniformizer ideal, which Mathlib does not provide. Used in Chapter 2 for the case E = F_q((π)).

items.name: External: field of norms (Wintenberger [61])
items.statement: For Ê the completion of an algebraic closure of E and π^♭ ∈ O^♭_{Ê} with π^{♭(0)} = π, the field of norms of the arithmetically profinite extension ∪_{n≥0}E(π^{(n)}) shows that O^♭_{Ê} is the completion of the ring of integers of an algebraic closure of F_q((π^♭)).
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.15 (first proof), p. 109, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned as such; the related Fontaine–Wintenberger isomorphism is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger.

items.name: External: θ: W_{O_E}(O^♭_{Ê})/([π^♭] − π) ⥲ O_{Ê}
items.statement: For Ê the completion of an algebraic closure of E, θ induces an isomorphism W_{O_E}(O^♭_{Ê})/([π^♭] − π) ⥲ O_{Ê}.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.15 (first proof), p. 110, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: E = Q_p, C_p: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta (ker θ = ([p♭] − p)); surjectivity mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta. General E: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence (ramified untilts ↔ primitive degree-one ideals of W_{O_E}(R^+)) and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate (generator of the form π − a[ϖ]); [π^♭] − π is such an element with a = 1.

items.name: External: Lubin–Tate formal groups over O_E
items.statement: The Lubin–Tate formal group law LT over O_E with logarithm log_LT = Σ_{n≥0} T^{q^n}/π^n (resp. with [π]_LT = Q for Q ≡ X^q mod π, Q ≡ πX mod X²), its formal group G, and the fact that the π-power torsion of LT in an algebraic closure of E is generated as described (used via θ([η]_Q)).
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.15 (second proof), p. 110; §2.3.2, pp. 116–117, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Used as input (not constructed) in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover; no Lubin–Tate formal group in Mathlib or TauCeti. The accepted Part II route LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts (from PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 route 2 and PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 route 8; not yet a roadmap with stages) plans 'For arbitrary finite E/Qp construct the OE-action, LT group' and 'the formal O-action, logarithm, torsion'; this item should be routed there (source) rather than re-planned in another Part II.

items.name: External: Kummer theory
items.statement: If a field K of characteristic 0 contains the ℓ-th roots of unity, every cyclic extension of degree ℓ of K is K(a^{1/ℓ}) for some a ∈ K.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2.19, p. 112, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: External: Newton polygon of a split polynomial
items.statement: For a polynomial P = Σ_{i=0}^d x_iT^i over O_F (F algebraically closed, x_d a unit), the valuations of the roots of P, with multiplicity, are the slopes of the Newton polygon of P.
items.locator: Théorème 2.4.1 (proof), pp. 122–123, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.3/newton-slopes-of-a-split-polynomial (with ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.3/dumas-theorem).

items.name: External: value of a Laurent series at a point off the slopes
items.statement: For Q = Σ q_iT^i a Laurent series over a complete valued field converging at π, if λ = v(π) is not a slope of Newt(Q) then v(Q(π)) = min_i(v(q_i) + iλ).
items.locator: Lemme 2.4.4 (proof, 'résultat classique'), p. 124, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations/newton-polygon-breaks (c)/(e) (classical Laurent series on annuli).

items.name: External: Ax's theorem in characteristic p
items.statement: For F a perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̂̄^{Gal(F̄|F)} = F.
items.locator: Chapitre 3, §3.1, p. 133, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Characteristic-0 (C_p) version planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants.

items.name: External: Tate's method for continuous Galois cohomology ([60])
items.statement: Tate's argument deducing vanishing of continuous H^1 from almost surjectivity of traces (m_F ⊂ tr(O_L)).
items.locator: Corollaire 3.1.2, p. 134, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Cyclotomic characteristic-0 form planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem.

items.name: External: vanishing of R^1 lim for dense transition maps ([31] 0_III 13.2.4)
items.statement: For an inverse system of complete metrisable topological groups (here the Fréchet/Banach rings B_J) with dense transition maps, R^1 lim = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.6, p. 147, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only special cases are planned: the algebraic Mittag-Leffler lemma (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness) and the application to Y_S, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity ('R^1 lim_I Γ(Y_{(R,R^+),I}, F) = 0', whose hypotheses say 'the vanishing of R^1 lim is quoted from EGA 0_III 13.2.4'). The general statement for complete metrisable groups with dense transition maps is not planned.

items.name: Standing notation of Ch. 4: F_{q^h} and E_h
items.statement: F is a perfect (complete, rank-one valued) field of characteristic p, not necessarily algebraically closed, E|Q_p is a finite extension with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, and the algebraic closure F̄_q of F_q in F is algebraically closed. For every h ≥ 1 put F_{q^h} = F^{Frob_{q^h} = Id} and E_h = W_{O_E}(F_{q^h}) (more precisely its fraction field W_{O_E}(F_{q^h})[1/π]), the unramified extension of E of degree h.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1 (before 4.1.1), p. 152, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra uses E_h (degree-h unramified extension of E) and cites exactly this passage (FF p. 152) as the anchor of the notation. The printed formula names the ring of integers W_{O_E}(F_{q^h}) rather than the field; the same abuse recurs in 8.2.2.

items.name: Newton polygon Newt(x) of x ∈ B (as used in Ch. 4)
items.statement: For x ∈ B = B_{]0,1[} non-zero, Newt(x) := Newt^0_{]0,1[}(x) is the inverse Legendre transform of the function r ↦ v_r(x) on ]0,+∞[; it is Newt_{]0,1[}(x) to which one possibly adds a slope 0 to the right of its domain of definition, and which is possibly +∞ to the left of its domain.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.1, p. 152, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Recalled from Ch. 1 (1.6.3). No atlas stage or node defines Newton polygons of elements of the Fargues–Fontaine ring B; nearest is PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring (Newton polygons of elements of Kedlaya's rings Γ_I), a different ring and convention. Not in Mathlib.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.1: B^{φ=Id} = E
items.statement: With the standing hypotheses (F perfect, not necessarily algebraically closed), B^{φ=Id} = E, where φ is the Frobenius of B = B_{]0,1[}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.1, p. 152, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(ii)): E → BC(O) is an isomorphism of pro-étale sheaves; for S = Spa F this gives H^0(X_F,O) = B^{φ=1} = E. The atlas statement is relative (perfectoid S) and in diamond language; FF prove it via Newton polygons (Props. 1.9.1) and ℰ^{φ=Id} = E.

items.name: The spaces B^{φ^h=π^d}
items.statement: For d, h ∈ Z, B^{φ^h=π^d} := {x ∈ B | φ^h(x) = π^d x}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.1, p. 152, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists. These are H^0(X, O_X(d/h)) (rank-h version) in the FS/atlas language: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition defines BC(E)(T) = H^0(X_T, E) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists treats BC(O(λ)). The atlas does not give the explicit description as a Frobenius eigenspace of B for general (d,h) (only H^0(X_S,O(1)) = H^0(Y_S,O)^{φ=π} in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2: B^{φ^h=π^d} = 0 for d < 0
items.statement: For d ∈ Z_{<0} and h ∈ N_{≥1}, B^{φ^h=π^d} = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.2, p. 152, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(i)): H^0(X_S, O(λ)) = 0 for λ < 0 and all S; FF's statement is the S = Spa F case (also for non-coprime d,h). FF's proof is by Newton polygons.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.3: B^{φ^h=π^d} = (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d} for d ≥ 0
items.statement: For d ∈ N and h ∈ N_{≥1}, B^{φ^h=π^d} = (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.3, p. 153, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node states that Frobenius eigenvectors of non-negative slope on Y extend to B^+ (to ρ = 1). Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (d = h = 1, relative, where the explicit series already lies in the B^+ part) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists. Proof uses Props. 1.9.2 and 1.10.7 of Ch. 1.

items.name: Closedness of B^{φ^h=π^d} in B
items.statement: For d, h ∈ N_{≥1}, since φ acts continuously on B, B^{φ^h=π^d} is a closed sub-E_h-vector space of B, hence a sub-Fréchet space of B.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.2, p. 153, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof (immediate). The atlas treats these spaces as v-sheaves/diamonds (VB1, VB3), not as Fréchet/Banach spaces.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.4: all Gauss norms induce the same topology on B^{φ^h=π^d}
items.statement: Let d, h ∈ N_{≥1}. For ρ, ρ' ∈ ]0,1[, the topology induced by |.|_ρ on B^{φ^h=π^d} coincides with the one induced by |.|_{ρ'}. (Key identity: for x ∈ B^{φ^h=π^d}, |x|^{q^h}_{ρ^{1/q^h}} = ρ^d |x|_ρ.)
items.locator: Lemme 4.1.4, p. 153, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Banach topology on Banach–Colmez spaces is not an atlas target (atlas uses diamonds).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.5: B^{φ^h=π^d} is an E_h-Banach space
items.statement: For d, h ≥ 1, B^{φ^h=π^d} is an E_h-Banach space whose topology is defined by any Gauss norm |.|_ρ, ρ ∈ ]0,1[.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.5, p. 154, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas: VB3:general-BC only mentions the locally profinite E-vector-space behaviour of degree-0 pieces; no Banach-space structure on positive-slope H^0 is planned.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.6: (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d} ≅ B̄^{φ^h=π^d}
items.statement: Let d, h ∈ N_{≥1} and let B̄ = B^{b,+}/{v_0 > 0} = B^+/{v_0 > 0} be the quotient ring of 1.10.4. The projection B^+ ↠ B̄ induces an isomorphism (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d} ⥲ B̄^{φ^h=π^d}, with inverse x mod {v_0>0} ↦ lim_{k→+∞} π^{-kd} φ^{kh}(x).
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.6, p. 154, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The ring B̄ (Ch. 1, 1.10.4) and this comparison do not appear in the atlas.

items.name: Existence of u with u^{φ^h−1} = π'/π (Lang-type surjectivity)
items.statement: Let π' be another uniformizer of E and F̄_q the algebraic closure of F_q in F. There exists u ∈ W_{O_E}(F̄_q)^× such that u^{φ^h − 1} = φ^h(u)/u = π'/π.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.4, p. 154, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External black box (Lang's theorem for the unit group of W_{O_E}(F̄_q)); stated without proof. Atlas mentions Lang's theorem only inside PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/rank-one-filtered-modules (for W(k)^×, E = Q_p); RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 plans uniformizer-change comparisons for W_{O_E} but not this statement.

items.name: 4.1.4: change of uniformizer isomorphism B^{φ^h=π^d} ≅ B^{φ^h=π'^d}
items.statement: Let π' be another uniformizer of E. A choice of u ∈ W_{O_E}(F̄_q)^× with u^{φ^h−1} = π'/π induces an isomorphism of E_h-Banach spaces B^{φ^h=π^d} ⥲ B^{φ^h=π'^d}, x ↦ u^d x. Intrinsically, with the 1-dimensional E_h-space L_{π,π'} = {u ∈ W_{O_E}(F̄_q) | φ^h(u) π = u π'} (rationally), there is a canonical isomorphism B^{φ^h=π^d} ⊗_{E_h} L_{π,π'}^{⊗d} ⥲ B^{φ^h=π'^d}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.4, p. 154, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 plans change-of-uniformizer comparisons only for W_{O_E}(R); VB0 pins a π-normalisation but no comparison of eigenspaces.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.7: unramified change of E
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, E_n = W_{O_E}(F̄_q)_Q^{φ^n = Id} the unramified extension of degree n, with π_{E_n} = π_E, so that B_E = B_{E_n} and φ_{E_n} = φ_E^n (1.6.2). The natural morphism B_E^{φ_E^h = π_E^d} ⊗_{E_h} E_{nh} → B_{E_n}^{φ_{E_n}^h = π_{E_n}^{nd}} is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.7, p. 155, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction plans the E'|E adjunction on isocrystals and its match with π^*, π_* on the curve, but not this statement on global sections. The proof uses Galois descent (Hilbert 90) for a semilinear Gal(E_{nh}|E_h)-action on an infinite-dimensional space.

items.name: 4.1.5: the map x ↦ u^d x for a general finite extension E'|E
items.statement: Let E'|E be finite with residue field F_{q'} ⊂ F, residue degree f_{E'/E}, uniformizers π_{E'}, π_E. Since π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E^{f_{E'/E}} is a unit of O_{E'}, there exists u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)^× with u^{φ_{E'}^h − 1} = π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E^{f_{E'/E}}; consider (B_E)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d} → (B_{E'})^{φ_{E'}^h = π_{E'}^{[E':E]d}}, x ↦ u^d x.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.1.5, p. 155, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (see VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction for the isocrystal-side adjunction only).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.8: general change of E
items.statement: With the notation of 4.1.5 (E'|E finite with residue field in F), the map x ↦ u^d x induces an isomorphism (B_E)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d} ⊗_{E_h} E'_h ⥲ (B_{E'})^{φ_{E'}^h = π_{E'}^{[E':E]d}}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.8, p. 155, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof: reduce by 4.1.7 to E'|E totally ramified, where B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_E E' with φ_{E'} = φ_E ⊗ Id; "le résultat est alors aisé". Not in the atlas (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction is the nearest).

items.name: Galois descent for semilinear actions (Hilbert 90) — external
items.statement: Let L|K be a finite Galois extension and V an L-vector space (here infinite-dimensional: B_{E_n}^{φ^h=π^{nd}} over E_{nh}, with G = Gal(E_{nh}|E_h) acting through (π_E^{-d}φ_E^h)^{Z/nZ}) with a semilinear G-action. Then V^G ⊗_K L → V is an isomorphism.
items.locator: used in proof of Proposition 4.1.7, p. 155, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box ("le théorème de Hilbert 90"). PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/semilinear-galois-descent plans it only for finite-dimensional D; Mathlib has only the multiplicative form (mathlib:groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units, H^1(Gal, L^×) = 1), not descent for (infinite-dimensional) vector spaces.

items.name: Covectors CW_O, formal covectors ĈW_O and bivectors BW_O (after Fontaine [24])
items.statement: For an O_E-algebra R, CW_O(R) is the group of O_E-typical Witt covectors [x_i]_{i≤0}; ĈW_O is the formal-covector subfunctor; BW_O(R) = lim_{←, n∈N} CW_O(R) with transition maps V_π (bivectors), so that 0 → W_O(O_F) → BW_O(O_F) → CW_O(O_F) → 0 is exact and BW_O(O_F) ⊂ B^+. For O_F: CW_O(O_F) = lim_{s>0} CW(O_F/a_s) = {[x_i]_{i≤0} | x_i ∈ O_F, liminf_{i→−∞} v(x_i) > 0}, ĈW_O(O_F) = {[x_i]_{i≤0} | x_i ∈ m_F, liminf_{i→−∞} v(x_i) > 0}.
items.locator: used in 4.2, 4.3.1, 4.4 (Remarque 4.4.3), pp. 155–168, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External objects from Fontaine [24] (Ch. II), used as black boxes. No atlas node defines Witt covectors/bivectors (search for covector/bivector found nothing relevant); Mathlib has WittVector (p-typical) only.

items.name: Fontaine [24] Ch. II Prop. 1.1: summability in covectors — external
items.statement: For s > 0 and a_s = {x ∈ O_F | v(x) ≥ s}, for a sequence (T^k(y))_k in BW_{O_E}(O_F) with v_0(y) > 0 (T = π^{-d}φ^h, d = h), the infinite sum Σ_{k≥0} (T^k(y) mod BW_{O_E}(a_s)) makes sense in BW_{O_E}(O_F/a_s): writing the partial sums Σ_{k≤l} Σ_i V_π^i[y_{i,k}] = Σ_i V_π^i[z_{i,l}], for each i the sequence (z_{i,l})_l is eventually constant.
items.locator: used in proof of Proposition 4.2.1 (case d = h), p. 157, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Quoted from [24] Ch. II Prop. 1.1 "au moins lorsque E = Q_p, la preuve étant identique pour E quelconque" — the general-E version is asserted, not proved. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.1(1): (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d} lives in the bivectors
items.statement: Suppose 1 ≤ d ≤ h. The natural inclusion BW_{O_E}(O_F) ⊂ B_E^+ induces an equality BW_{O_E}(O_F)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d} = (B_E^+)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.2.1(1), p. 155, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. Proof: via Prop. 4.1.6, for x ∈ B^{b,+} with image in B̄^{φ^h=π^d} build a correction z ∈ BW(O_F) with v_0(z) > 0 by summing T^k(y) (d < h: finite sums mod a_s; d = h: Fontaine [24] II Prop. 1.1).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.1(2): explicit bijection L_{d,h}: m_F^d ≅ (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d}
items.statement: Suppose 1 ≤ d ≤ h. There is a bijection L_{d,h}: m_F^d ⥲ (B_E^+)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d}, (x_0, …, x_{d−1}) ↦ Σ_i Σ_{n∈Z} [x_i^{q^{−nh}}] π_E^{nd+i}, the sum over i running over d consecutive indices (printed Σ_{i=0}^{d}; see sourceIssues). Via L_{d,h}, m_F^d inherits a Banach-space structure (to be interpreted geometrically in 4.4).
items.locator: Proposition 4.2.1(2), p. 156; Banach structure p. 157, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequence of (1) (points of bivectors fixed by V_π^{−d}F^{h−d}). Atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover gives exactly the case d = h = 1 (X ↦ Σ_i π^i[X^{q^{−i}}], relative S); VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (iv) gives an abstract identification BC(O(λ)) = Spd k[[x_1^{1/p^∞},…,x_r^{1/p^∞}]] for 0 < λ = r/s ≤ [E:Q_p] (so m_F^d ≅ H^0 for coprime d ≤ h) without the formula. The explicit L_{d,h} for general d ≤ h is not planned.

items.name: Remarque 4.2.2: reduction to h = 1 and its limits
items.statement: Let h ≥ 1, d ≥ 0. Putting π_{E_h} = π_E, (B_E^+)^{φ_E^h = π_E^d} = (B_{E_h}^+)^{φ_{E_h} = π_{E_h}^d}. However for d ≤ h the former has an interpretation via π-divisible O_E-modules and lies in BW_{O_E}(O_F), whereas (B_{E_h}^+)^{φ_{E_h} = π_{E_h}^d} has no interpretation in terms of π-divisible O_{E_h}-modules and is not contained in BW_{O_{E_h}}(O_F) when d > 1.
items.locator: Remarque 4.2.2, p. 157, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas (FS/VB1 reduce to integral λ by unramified base change, cf. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists proof step 1).

items.name: π-divisible O-module and O-height
items.statement: Let S be an O_E-scheme on which π is nilpotent (resp. a formal scheme over Spf(O_E)). A π-divisible O-module over S is a p-divisible group H over S with an action of O_E such that the induced action on the O_S-module Lie H is the one deduced from the structure morphism S → Spec(O_E) (resp. S → Spf(O_E)). Its O-height is ht_O(H) = ht(H)/[E:Q_p].
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.1, pp. 157–158, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/p-divisible-group defines p-divisible groups (E = Q_p case); strict O_E-actions appear only in passing (EndoscopicTransfer ET.6a, ES7 special formal O_D-modules).

items.name: Height of a π-divisible O-module is divisible by [E:Q_p]
items.statement: The height of a π-divisible O-module is a multiple of [E:Q_p].
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.1, p. 158, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: The O-Dieudonné module D_O(H) = D(H)_can with F_E and V_π
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field extension of F_q and H a π-divisible O-module over k, with contravariant Dieudonné module D(H) (a W(k)-module with O_E-action commuting with F, V). Then D(H) = ⊕_{τ: F_q ↪ k} D(H)_τ, O_{E_0} = W(F_q) acting on D(H)_τ through W(τ); F: D(H)_τ → D(H)_{στ}, V: D(H)_τ → D(H)_{σ^{−1}τ}. Put D_O(H) = D(H)_can (can: F_q ↪ k the canonical embedding); it is a free W_{O_E}(k)-module of rank ht_O(H), W_{O_E}(k) = W(k) ⊗_{O_{E_0}} O_E. With σ_E = σ^f ⊗ Id (q = p^f), F_E := F^f is σ_E-linear (printed σ_E^{−1}; see sourceIssues); since O_E acts on Lie H through can, V D(H)_{στ} = p D(H)_τ for τ ≠ can and πD(H) ⊂ F_E D(H); put V_π = π F_E^{−1}, so F_E V_π = V_π F_E = π.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.1, p. 158, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. R07.2 (dieudonne-ring, dieudonne-p-divisible) plans Dieudonné theory for p-divisible groups (E = Q_p); the O_E-refinement (τ-decomposition, V_π) is not stated.

items.name: Dieudonné classification of π-divisible O-modules over a perfect field — external
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field containing F_q. H ↦ (D_O(H), F, V_π) induces an (anti-)equivalence of categories between π-divisible O-modules over k and triples (D, F, V_π) with D a free W_{O_E}(k)-module of finite rank, F: D → D σ_E-linear, V_π: D → D σ_E^{−1}-linear, F V_π = V_π F = π.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.1, p. 158, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box (deduced from classical contravariant Dieudonné theory; covariant Cartier theory of O-modules refers to [15], [35], [38], [37], [36] ch. V.29; crystalline to [16], [18] App. B). Atlas plans only the E = Q_p case: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2/dieudonne-p-divisible (and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2/dieudonne-ring). Mathlib has no Dieudonné modules.

items.name: Contravariant O-Dieudonné theory via Witt covectors — external
items.statement: For H a π-divisible O-module over a perfect k ⊃ F_q, D_O(H) ≅ Hom_O(H, CW_O); F on D_O(H) is induced by F: H → H^{(q)}, the f-th power of the Frobenius of H; there is an isogeny V_π: H^{(q)} → H inducing V_π on D_O(H); and H = Hom_{W_{O_E}(k)[F,V_π]}(D_O(H), CW_O) (as functors). When H is formal one may replace CW_O by the formal covectors ĈW_O.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.1, p. 159, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On peut montrer" — generalisation of Fontaine [24] asserted without proof. Not in the atlas (R07.2 constructs Dieudonné modules via Witt group schemes, not covectors, and only for E = Q_p).

items.name: The formal π-divisible O-module G_{d,h}
items.statement: Let 1 ≤ d ≤ h. G_{d,h} := ker(F^{h−d} − V_π^d : CW_O → CW_O).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, p. 159, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Structure of G_{d,h}: dimension, height, coordinates, Dieudonné module
items.statement: Let 1 ≤ d ≤ h. G_{d,h} is a formal π-divisible O-module over F_q of dimension d and O-height h. A system of formal coordinates is (x_0, …, x_{d−1}) with G_{d,h} = {[x_{b(i)}^{q^{a(i)(h−d)}}]_{i≤0}} ⊂ CW_O, where −i = a(i)d + b(i) is the Euclidean division of −i by d. If e ∈ Hom_O(G_{d,h}, CW_O) is the canonical embedding, D_O(G_{d,h}) = Hom(G_{d,h}, CW_O) has O-basis e, Fe, …, F^{h−d}e, V_π e, …, V_π^{d−1} e.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, p. 159, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof (verification that F^{h−d}y = V_π^d y for these coordinates is immediate). Not in the atlas.

items.name: The formal group law F_{d,h} over F_q
items.statement: The coordinates (x_0, …, x_{d−1}) of G_{d,h} define a d-dimensional formal group law F_{d,h} = (F^{(0)}_{d,h}, …, F^{(d−1)}_{d,h}) ∈ F_q[[x_0,…,x_{d−1},y_0,…,y_{d−1}]]^d, characterised by [x_{b(i)}^{q^{a(i)(h−d)}}]_{i≤0} + [y_{b(i)}^{q^{a(i)(h−d)}}]_{i≤0} = [(…, F^{(d−1)}_{d,h}, …, F^{(0)}_{d,h})] in CW_O(F_q[[x,y]]).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, p. 159, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has only 1-dimensional formal group laws (mathlib:FormalGroup, Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean); FiniteFlat FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/formal-lie-group plans commutative formal Lie groups over complete noetherian local rings, not this law.

items.name: Cartier module of G_{d,h}: basis, V-basis, structural equations and presentation
items.statement: The covariant Cartier module M = Hom(Ŵ_O, G_{d,h}) is a module over the Cartier ring E_{O,F_q} = End(Ŵ_O)^{opp}, the V-completion of W_O(F_q)[F_π, V] ({Σ_{n,m≥0} V^n[a_{n,m}]F_π^m : a_{n,m} ∈ F_q, ∀n a_{n,m} = 0 for almost all m}). The map ε: Ŵ_O → CW_O, x ↦ Σ_{n≥0} V_π^{−nd}F^{n(h−d)}x mod W_O lies in M; M = ⟨ε, Vε, …, V^{h−d}ε, F_π ε, …, F_π^{d−1}ε⟩ as W_O(F_q)-module (basis); (ε_0,…,ε_{d−1}), ε_i = F_π^i ε, is a V-basis with structural equations F_π ε_i = ε_{i+1} (0 ≤ i < d−1), F_π ε_{d−1} = V^{h−d}ε_0; hence a presentation 0 → E_{O,F_q}^d →^u E_{O,F_q}^d → M → 0 with u(x_0,…,x_{d−1}) = (x_{d−1}F_π − x_0 V^{h−d}, x_0 F_π − x_1, …, x_{d−2}F_π − x_{d−1}). The map M → G_{d,h}(F_q[[T]]), u ↦ u([T]) identifies M with the π-typical curves, and γ = Σ_i ε_i([x_i]) defines an isomorphism Spf(F_q[[x_0,…,x_{d−1}]]) ⥲ G_{d,h} recovering the coordinates used for F_{d,h}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, pp. 159–161, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Relies on Cartier theory of formal O-modules (Drinfeld [15], Hazewinkel [35]–[38]). Not in the atlas.

items.name: The lift G̃_{d,h} over O_E
items.statement: Let M̃ be the Cartier module over O_E with V_π-basis (ε̃_0,…,ε̃_{d−1}) and structural equations F_π ε̃_i = ε̃_{i+1} (0 ≤ i < d−1), F_π ε̃_{d−1} = V^{h−d} ε̃_0 (same presentation with E_{O,O_E}). Let G̃_{d,h} = Ŵ_O ⊗_{E_{O,O_E}} M̃, a π-divisible O-module over O_E with G̃_{d,h} ⊗ F_q = G_{d,h} and a resolution on Spf(O_E) 0 → Ŵ_O^d → Ŵ_O^d →^v G̃_{d,h} → 0, v(y_0,…,y_{d−1}) = (V_π y_{d−1} − F^{h−d}y_0, V_π y_0 − y_1, …, V_π y_{d−2} − y_{d−1}). With α_i: O_E[[T]] → O_E[[x_0,…,x_{d−1}]], T ↦ x_i, γ̃ = Σ_i α_{i*} ε̃_i([T]) = Σ_i ε̃_i([x_i]) defines an isomorphism Spf(O_E[[x_0,…,x_{d−1}]]) ⥲ G̃_{d,h} (formal coordinates) lifting those of G_{d,h}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, p. 161, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Logarithm of G̃_{d,h} and the curves g_{i,j}
items.statement: There is a unique isomorphism of formal O-modules over E, log: G̃_{d,h} ⊗̂ E ⥲ Ĝ_a^d, whose tangent map sends the basis of Lie G̃_{d,h} deduced from the V-basis (ε̃_i) to the canonical basis of Lie Ĝ_a^d = E^d. It is given by f = (f_0,…,f_{d−1}) ∈ E[[x_0,…,x_{d−1}]]^d with f = Σ_i g_i(x_i), where g_i = (g_{i,0},…,g_{i,d−1}) = log ε̃_i([T]) ∈ Ĝ_a^d(E[[T]]); each g_{i,j} is a π-typical curve Σ_{n≥0} a_n T^{q^n} of Ĝ_a characterised by (1) F_π.g_{i,j} = g_{i+1,j} for 0 ≤ i < d−1, (2) F_π.g_{d−1,j} = V^{h−d}.g_{0,j}, (3) g_{i,j} ≡ 0 mod T^2 if i ≠ j and g_{i,i} ≡ T mod T^2 (V: g(T) ↦ g(T^q), F_π: Σa_nT^{q^n} ↦ πΣa_{n+1}T^{q^n}); explicitly g_{i,j} = Σ_{n≥0} T^{q^{nh+j−i}}/π^{nd+j−i} if j ≥ i, and Σ_{n≥1} T^{q^{nh+j−i}}/π^{nd+j−i} if j < i.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.2, pp. 161–162, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Checked: the displayed g_{i,j} satisfy (1)–(3) with V (T ↦ T^q) in (2); the text prints V_π^{h−d} there (see sourceIssues). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.1: logarithms of the formal O-module law F̃_{d,h}
items.statement: For 0 ≤ j ≤ d−1 let f_j = Σ_{0≤i≤j} Σ_{n≥0} x_i^{q^{nh+j−i}}/π^{nd+j−i} + Σ_{j<i≤d−1} Σ_{n≥1} x_i^{q^{nh+j−i}}/π^{nd+j−i} ∈ E[[x_0,…,x_{d−1}]]. Then (f_0,…,f_{d−1}) are the logarithms of a unique law of formal O-module of dimension d over O_E, F̃_{d,h}, lifting the law of formal O-module F_{d,h} over F_q.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.1, p. 162, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas; Mathlib has no logarithms of formal groups or formal O-modules.

items.name: Exemple 4.3.2: G̃_{1,h} is a Lubin–Tate group for E_h
items.statement: If d = 1, G̃_{1,h} is a Lubin–Tate group associated with the unramified extension E_h of E; an associated formal group law has logarithm f(T) = Σ_{n≥0} T^{q^{nh}}/π^n, i.e. F̃_{1,h} = f^{−1}(f(X) + f(Y)) ∈ O_E[[X,Y]].
items.locator: Exemple 4.3.2, p. 163, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Lubin–Tate theory is not planned as such (tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 8 explicitly excludes it); VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover uses the height-1 Lubin–Tate O_E-module (h = 1) without constructing it. The accepted Part II route LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts (from PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21 route 2 and PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 route 8; not yet a roadmap with stages) plans 'For arbitrary finite E/Qp construct the OE-action, LT group' and 'the formal O-action, logarithm, torsion'; this item should be routed there (source) rather than re-planned in another Part II.

items.name: Définition 4.3.3: quasi-logarithms Quasilog(G) and Quasilog(G)/∼
items.statement: Let K|E be a complete field for a rank-one valuation extending the π-adic valuation of E, G a formal π-divisible O-module over O_K, G = Spf(R), R ≅ O_K[[x_1,…,x_d]], d = dim G, and R̂[1/π] ≅ K[[x_1,…,x_d]] the completion of R[1/π] along its augmentation ideal (so G ⊗̂ K = Spf(R̂[1/π]) is the generic-fibre formal group). Quasilog(G) is the set of f in the maximal ideal of R̂[1/π] such that Δ(f) − f ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ f ∈ (R ⊗̂ R)[1/π] and, for all a ∈ O_E, f ∘ [a]_G − a f ∈ R[1/π]. It contains the augmentation ideal of R[1/π]; Quasilog(G)/∼ denotes the quotient by it.
items.locator: Définition 4.3.3, p. 163, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (no node on quasi-logarithms). FF note this definition agrees with that of [24] Ch. IV and [41] Ch. V, "définition qui est donc trop forte".

items.name: Lemme 4.3.4: derivatives of quasi-logarithms are integral up to π
items.statement: Fix coordinates R ≅ O_K[[x_1,…,x_d]]. If f ∈ K[[x_1,…,x_d]] is a quasi-logarithm, then ∂f/∂x_i ∈ O_K[[x_1,…,x_d]][1/π] for 1 ≤ i ≤ d. (Equivalently f^*dT ∈ Ω̂^1_{G/O_K}[1/π].)
items.locator: Lemme 4.3.4, p. 163, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Logarithms and the Hodge filtration on quasi-logarithms
items.statement: There is an isomorphism Hom_O(G ⊗̂ K, Ĝ_a) ⥲ (Lie G[1/π])^* = ω_G[1/π], f ↦ f^*dT. Hence ω_G[1/π] embeds into Quasilog(G)/∼; its image is the space of logarithms (f ∈ R̂[1/π] with Δ(f) = f ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ f), and the induced filtration on quasi-logarithms is the Hodge filtration.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.3, p. 164, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas; Mathlib has no logarithm of a formal group.

items.name: Définition 4.3.5: rigid quasi-morphisms QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig)
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be the generic fibre of G as a K-rigid-analytic group (an open ball of dimension dim G). QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig) is the set of morphisms of rigid spaces f: 𝒢 → G_a^rig with f(0) = 0, ‖f(x+y) − f(x) − f(y)‖_∞ < +∞ (as a function on 𝒢 × 𝒢) and ‖f(ax) − af(x)‖_∞ < +∞ for all a ∈ O_E. QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig)/∼ is the quotient by the subgroup of f with ‖f‖_∞ < +∞.
items.locator: Définition 4.3.5, p. 165, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig) ≅ Quasilog(G)
items.statement: Using that G ⊗̂ K = Spf(Ô_{𝒢,0}) (germs of rigid functions at the unit), the natural map QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig) → Quasilog(G) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.3, p. 165, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie en utilisant le lemme 4.3.4" — proof only indicated. Not in the atlas.

items.name: The map w: CW_O(R) → R̂[1/π] ([24] II.5)
items.statement: With I = (π, x_1, …, x_d) an ideal of definition of R, CW_O(R) = lim_n CW_O(R/I^n) = {[y_i]_{i≤0} | y_i ∈ R, ∃N, ∃k, (Σ_{i≤N} R y_i)^k ⊂ I}; there is an O_E-linear morphism w: CW_O(R) → R̂[1/π], [y_n]_{n≤0} ↦ Σ_{n≥0} π^{−n} y_{−n}^{q^n}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.3, p. 165, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From [24] II.5 (E = Q_p there). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Fontaine's comparison D ⊗ K ≅ Quasilog(G)/∼ — external ([24] Ch. IV)
items.statement: Let a ⊂ m_K be an ideal with π ∈ a, G_a = G ⊗ O_K/a. Then Hom_O(G_a, CW_O) = {[y_n] ∈ CW_O(R/aR) | [Δ(y_n)] = [y_n ⊗ 1] + [1 ⊗ y_n] in CW_O(R_a ⊗̂ R_a)} and x ↦ w(x̂) (x̂ any lift to CW_O(R)) is an O_E-linear map Hom_O(G_a, CW_O) → Quasilog(G)/∼. Suppose the residue field k_K is perfect, fix a section of O_K/πO_K → k_K, and suppose the identity of G_{k_K} lifts to a (necessarily unique) quasi-isogeny ρ: G_{k_K} ⊗_{k_K} O_K/πO_K → G ⊗_{O_K} O_K/πO_K. Then, with D = Hom_O(G_{k_K}, CW_O) the Dieudonné module of the special fibre, ρ and the above map induce an isomorphism D ⊗_{W_{O_E}(k_K)} K ⥲ Quasilog(G)/∼.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.3, pp. 165–166, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box from Fontaine [24] Ch. IV (E = Q_p there; asserted for general E). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Rigidity of quasi-isogenies — external
items.statement: If the valuation of K is discrete (k_K perfect, section of O_K/πO_K → k_K given by Teichmüller), the identity of G_{k_K} automatically lifts to a unique quasi-isogeny ρ: G_{k_K} ⊗ O_K/πO_K → G ⊗ O_K/πO_K ("par rigidité des quasi-isogénies"). More generally, quasi-isogenies of p-divisible groups lift uniquely along nilpotent thickenings.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.3.3, p. 166; also 4.5.3, p. 177, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box (Drinfeld rigidity). Not stated in the atlas: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 and PELModuli:M1 mention quasi-isogenies but no rigidity statement; R07.6 covers Grothendieck–Messing only as an input.

items.name: Exemple 4.3.6: quasi-logarithms of G̃_{1,h}
items.statement: For the formal O-module G̃_{1,h} over O_E of Exemple 4.3.2, the series Σ_{n≥0} T^{q^{nh+i}}/π^n, 0 ≤ i ≤ h−1, form a basis of its quasi-logarithms (modulo ∼).
items.locator: Exemple 4.3.6, p. 166, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.1: Banach structure on G(O_F)
items.statement: Let G be a formal π-divisible O-module over F̄_q, G(O_F) = Hom_{Spec F̄_q}(Spf O_F, G), and for s > 0, a_s = {x ∈ O_F | v(x) ≥ s}, G_s(O_F) = ker(G(O_F) → G(O_F/a_s)). Then G(O_F) is an E-vector space; for every s > 0, G_s(O_F) is a π-adically complete sub-O_E-module of G(O_F) which is the unit ball of a Banach norm on G(O_F); the resulting Banach topology does not depend on s.
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.1, p. 166, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie aisément". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Rigid generic fibre of G over F and its affinoid subgroups
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = (G ⊗̂ O_F)^rig be the generic fibre of the Spf(O_F)-formal scheme G ⊗̂ O_F, a rigid-analytic group over F with G(O_F) = 𝒢(F). For s > 0 with s ∈ v(F^×) there is an affinoid subgroup 𝒢_s ⊂ 𝒢 with G_s(O_F) = 𝒢_s(F). After fixing formal coordinates Spf(k[[x_1,…,x_d]]) ⥲ G, 𝒢 ≅ B̊^d (open unit ball of dimension d = dim G over F) and 𝒢_s ≅ B^d(0, q^{−s}); for every s > 0, ∪_{n≥1} π^{−n}𝒢_s = 𝒢 is an admissible covering, and for s > t > 0 there is n ∈ N with π^n 𝒢_s ⊂ 𝒢_t. The functor G ↦ G(O_F) from formal π-divisible O-modules over F̄_q to E-Banach spaces factors through the isogeny category.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.4, p. 167, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: G(O_F) ≅ Hom_{[F,V_π]}(D, CW_O(O_F))
items.statement: With D = Hom_O(G, CW_O) the contravariant Dieudonné module of G (Frobenius F, Verschiebung V_π), there is a natural isomorphism G(O_F) ⥲ Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F,V_π]}(D, CW_O(O_F)), where G(O_F) = lim_{s>0} G(O_F/a_s) and CW_O(O_F) = lim_{s>0} CW(O_F/a_s); since G is formal one may use ĈW_O(O_F) instead.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.4, p. 167, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequence of the covector Dieudonné theory (black box above). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.2: lifting from covectors to bivectors
items.statement: The reduction map BW_O(O_F) → CW_O(O_F) induces an isomorphism of O_E-modules Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F,V_π]}(D, BW_O(O_F)) ⥲ Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F,V_π]}(D, CW_O(O_F)).
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.2, p. 168, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof uses topological nilpotence of F on D (G formal) and bijectivity of F on W_O(O_F), BW_O(O_F), CW_O(O_F). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 4.4.3: explicit lift to bivectors
items.statement: BW_O(O_F) = lim_{n∈N} CW_O(O_F) with transition maps V_π. Let N ≫ 0 with F^N D ⊂ V_π D and γ = V_π^{−1}F^N ∈ End(D). If u: D → CW_O(O_F) commutes with F and V_π, the unique lift given by Prop. 4.4.2 is (F^{−Nk} ∘ u ∘ γ^k)_{k≥0}: D → lim CW_O(O_F).
items.locator: Remarque 4.4.3, p. 168, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed formula (F^{−n} ∘ u ∘ γ^n)_{n≥0} reuses the fixed exponent n as running index (see sourceIssues). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 4.4.4: G(O_F) ≅ Hom_F(D[1/π], B^+)
items.statement: For G a formal π-divisible O-module over F̄_q with rational contravariant Dieudonné module D[1/π], there is an isomorphism of E-vector spaces G(O_F) ⥲ Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F,V_π]}(D[1/π], BW_O(O_F)) = Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F]}(D[1/π], B^+).
items.locator: Corollaire 4.4.4, p. 169, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Prop. 4.4.2, the Dieudonné–Manin theorem and Prop. 4.2.1(1). Not in the atlas (closest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover for the height-1 Lubin–Tate case in the relative setting).

items.name: Coordinates on G_{d,h}(O_F) and evaluation at e
items.statement: For 1 ≤ d ≤ h, the formal coordinates (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) of G_{d,h} (composed with e: G_{d,h} ↪ CW_O equal to [x_{b(i)}^{q^{a(i)(h−d)}}]_{i≤0} = [… , x_0^{q^{h−d}}, x_{d−1}, …, x_0]) induce a bijection m_F^d ⥲ G_{d,h}(O_F); moreover Hom_{W_O(F̄_q)[F,V_π]}(D, B^+) ⥲ (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d}, u ↦ u(e).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.4, p. 169, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.5: explicit formula for m_F^d ≅ (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d}
items.statement: Let 1 ≤ d ≤ h and F_{d,h} the formal group law of G_{d,h} for the above coordinates. Via these choices the E-vector-space isomorphism (m_F^d, +_{F_{d,h}}) ⥲ (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d} is given by (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) ↦ π^{−d} L_{d,h}(x_{d−1}^{q^{d−1}}, …, x_1^{q}, x_0), where L_{d,h} is the map of Prop. 4.2.1 (with arguments indexed so that the i-th argument carries π^{nd+i}, i = 1,…,d; see sourceIssues). Equivalently, (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) ↦ Σ_{i=0}^{d−1} Σ_{n∈Z} [x_i^{q^{−nh+i}}] π^{nd−i}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.5, p. 169, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Checked: the last formula is the one proved (V_π^{nd−i}[x_i^{q^{−n(h−d)}}] = [x_i^{q^{−nh+i}}]π^{nd−i}). Atlas: only d = h = 1 (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover, FS II.2.2).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.6: G_{d,h}(O_F) ≅ B^{φ^h=π^d} is a homeomorphism
items.statement: For 1 ≤ d ≤ h, the isomorphism G_{d,h}(O_F) ⥲ B^{φ^h=π^d} is a homeomorphism of Banach spaces (Banach structure on G_{d,h}(O_F) from Prop. 4.4.1, on B^{φ^h=π^d} from 4.1.2).
items.locator: Proposition 4.4.6, p. 170, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie facilement". Not in the atlas (no Banach topology on BC spaces).

items.name: Exemple 4.4.7(a): E = Q_p, d = h = 1
items.statement: Let E = Q_p, d = h = 1, F̃ the formal group law over Z_p with logarithm Σ_{n≥0} T^{p^n}/p^n and F its reduction over F_p. Then L: (m_F, +_F) ⥲ (B^+)^{φ=p}, x ↦ Σ_{n∈Z} [x^{p^{−n}}] p^n, is an isomorphism of E-Banach spaces.
items.locator: Exemple 4.4.7, p. 170, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the algebraic isomorphism is planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2: X ↦ Σ_i π^i[X^{q^{−i}}] is a natural isomorphism G̃(R^{♯+}) = R^{∘∘} → H^0(Y_S,O)^{φ=π}; for E = Q_p, the height-1 Lubin–Tate group with this logarithm and S = Spa F it is L). The E-Banach structure on (B^+)^{φ=p} (Prop. 4.1.5, missing) and the claim that L is an isomorphism of Banach spaces are not planned.

items.name: Exemple 4.4.7(b): the Artin–Hasse exponential and log[·]
items.statement: The Artin–Hasse exponential E(T) = exp(Σ_{n≥0} T^{p^n}/p^n) ∈ Z_p[[T]] induces an isomorphism of formal group laws E: F ⥲ Ĝ_m, and there is a commutative triangle of isomorphisms of Banach spaces (m_F, +_F) →^L (B^+)^{φ=p}, (m_F, +_F) →^E (1+m_F, ×), (1+m_F, ×) →^{log([−])} (B^+)^{φ=p}.
items.locator: Exemple 4.4.7, p. 170, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses integrality of the Artin–Hasse exponential (black box). Not in the atlas; Mathlib has 1-dimensional formal group laws incl. mathlib:FormalGroup.𝔾ₘ but no Artin–Hasse exponential.

items.name: Définition 4.5.1: the universal cover X(G)(B)
items.statement: Let A be a π-adic O_E-algebra and G a formal π-divisible O-module over A. For B an A-algebra that is adic for an ideal containing π, with G(B) := Hom_{Spf(A)}(Spf(B), G), put X(G)(B) = {(x_n)_{n∈Z} | x_n ∈ G(B), π x_{n+1} = x_n}. It is an E-vector space depending only on the isogeny class of G.
items.locator: Définition 4.5.1, p. 171, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The "universal cover" G̃ of Scholze–Weinstein [57]. Atlas: only the height-1 Lubin–Tate case, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (G̃(R^{♯+}) = R^{∘∘}); no general definition.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.2: X(G) is insensitive to closed nil-thickenings
items.statement: Let B be a J-adic A-algebra with (π) ⊂ J, and I ⊂ J an ideal of B closed for the J-adic topology; give B the J-adic and B/I the J/I-adic topology. Reduction modulo I induces an isomorphism of E-vector spaces X(G)(B) ⥲ X(G)(B/I).
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.2, p. 171, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof given (dévissage along I^l/I^{l+1}, killed by π^k). Corresponds to Scholze–Weinstein [57] Prop. 3.1.3(ii); not stated in the atlas (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists only quotes [SW13] as an input).

items.name: X(G)(W_{O_E}(O_F)) ≅ X(G_{F̄_q})(O_F) ≅ G_{F̄_q}(O_F)
items.statement: Let G be a formal π-divisible O-module over W_{O_E}(F̄_q), G_{F̄_q} its reduction, and give W_O(O_F) the weak topology. Reduction mod π induces a bijection X(G)(W_{O_E}(O_F)) ⥲ X(G_{F̄_q})(O_F), and (x_n)_{n∈Z} ↦ x_0 is a bijection X(G_{F̄_q})(O_F) ⥲ G_{F̄_q}(O_F); hence an isomorphism of E-vector spaces X(G)(W_{O_E}(O_F)) ⥲ G_{F̄_q}(O_F).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.2, p. 172, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From Prop. 4.5.2 (weak topology is (π,[ϖ])-adic). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 4.5.3: evaluation of rigid functions at W_O(O_F)-points
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = G^rig be the generic fibre of G as a W_O(F̄_q)_Q-rigid group, Γ(𝒢,O_𝒢) = Hom(𝒢, G_a^rig) with the topology of uniform convergence on affinoids (an E-Fréchet space in which the bounded functions Hom(G, Ĝ_a)[1/π] are dense). For x ∈ G(W_O(O_F)), the evaluation map Hom(G, Ĝ_a)[1/π] → B^{b,+}, f ↦ f(x), extends uniquely to a continuous map of Fréchet spaces Hom(𝒢, G_a^rig) → B^+, f ↦ f(x); indeed v_r(f(x)) ≥ w_{v_r(x)}(f), w_r the Gauss valuation on the ball of radius q^{−r}.
items.locator: Lemme 4.5.3, p. 173, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 4.5.4: uniform bound for quasi-morphisms
items.statement: If f: 𝒢 → G_a^rig is a quasi-morphism, there exists A ∈ R such that for all m ∈ N, ‖π^m f − f ∘ π^m‖_∞ ≤ A (one can take A = ‖πf − f∘π‖_∞).
items.locator: Lemme 4.5.4, p. 173, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 4.5.5: the limits lim π^n f(x_n)
items.statement: Let (x_n)_{n∈Z} ∈ X(G)(W_O(O_F)) and f ∈ QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig). (1) The sequence (π^n f(x_n))_n converges in B^+ (as n → +∞). (2) If f is bounded, lim_{n→+∞} π^n f(x_n) = 0. (3) If y ∈ X(G)(W_O(O_F)), lim π^n f(x_n + y_n) = lim π^n f(x_n) + lim π^n f(y_n).
items.locator: Lemme 4.5.5, p. 173, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Period morphism via quasi-logarithms G_{F̄_q}(O_F) → Hom_E(D[1/π], B^+)
items.statement: Lemma 4.5.5 gives an E-linear map X(G)(W_O(O_F)) → Hom(QuasiHom(𝒢,G_a^rig)/∼, B^+), (x_n) ↦ (f ↦ lim_{n→+∞} π^n f(x_n)). Composing with D[1/π] ≅ Quasilog(G)/∼ (D = Hom_O(G_{F̄_q}, CW_O)) and X(G)(W_O(O_F)) ≅ G_{F̄_q}(O_F) gives a morphism G_{F̄_q}(O_F) → Hom_E(D[1/π], B^+).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.2, p. 174, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.6: the quasi-logarithm period map equals that of Cor. 4.4.4
items.statement: The morphism G_{F̄_q}(O_F) → Hom_E(D[1/π], B^+) constructed via the quasi-logarithms of G coincides with the morphism of Corollaire 4.4.4.
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.6, p. 174, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof given (Frobenius compatibility, then difference lies in W_O(O_F), which forces equality since F is π-adically topologically nilpotent on D). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 4.5.7: period map defined by a logarithm
items.statement: Let (T_0,…,T_{d−1}) be formal coordinates on G, F the formal group law, and f ∈ E[[T_0,…,T_{d−1}]] a logarithm. For (y_n) ∈ X(G)(W_O(O_F)), π^n f(y_n) = f(y_0); hence the morphism (m_F^d, +_F) → B^+ defined by f is (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) ↦ f(lim_{n→+∞} [π^n]_F([x_0^{(n)}],…,[x_{d−1}^{(n)}])) = lim_{n→+∞} π^n f([x_0^{(n)}],…,[x_{d−1}^{(n)}]), where [π^n]_F(x_0^{(n)},…,x_{d−1}^{(n)}) = (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) in m_F^d.
items.locator: Exemple 4.5.7, p. 176, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover states the evaluation map equals the Lubin–Tate logarithm in the height-1 case only.

items.name: Exemple 4.5.8: the Lubin–Tate case G̃_{1,h}
items.statement: For F̃_{1,h} (Exemple 4.3.2) with logarithm f(T) = Σ_{k≥0} T^{q^{kh}}/π^k and [π]_{F_{1,h}} = T^{q^h}, the associated isomorphism (m_F, +_{F_{1,h}}) ⥲ (B^+)^{φ^h=π} is x ↦ lim_{n→+∞} π^n f([x^{q^{−nh}}]) = Σ_{k∈Z} [x^{q^{kh}}]/π^k, recovering Prop. 4.4.5 for d = 1 (and, via the formulas of Prop. 4.3.1, for all d).
items.locator: Exemple 4.5.8, pp. 176–177, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Statement given with the h's restored (the printed formulas are those of h = 1; see sourceIssues). Atlas: h = 1 case in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover only.

items.name: Hypothesis on ρ in 4.5.3 and its equivalent forms
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, C|E complete algebraically closed with C^♭ = F (i.e. C = C_y, y ∈ |Y_F|), G a formal π-divisible O-module over O_C, G_k its reduction to the residue field k, and fix a section of O_C/pO_C → k (giving k ⊂ O_C/pO_C and k ⊂ O_F). Existence of a quasi-isogeny ρ: G_k ⊗_k O_C/pO_C → G ⊗_{O_C} O_C/pO_C lifting the identity of G_k (then unique) is equivalent to the existence of an ideal a ⊂ m_C containing pO_C and an isomorphism ρ_a: G_k ⊗_k O_C/a ⥲ G ⊗_{O_C} O_C/a deforming the identity. It holds e.g. if G comes by base change from a p-divisible group over O_K for a complete discretely valued subfield K ⊂ C.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 177, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses rigidity of quasi-isogenies (black box). Not in the atlas.

items.name: X(G)(O_C) = X(𝒢)(C) depends only on the rigid group
items.statement: With G over O_C as above and 𝒢 = G^rig ≅ B̊^d its generic fibre, X(G)(O_C) is the projective limit of the C-points of … ←^{×π} 𝒢 ←^{×π} 𝒢 ← …; hence X(G)(O_C) = X(𝒢)(C) := {(x_n)_{n∈Z} | x_n ∈ 𝒢(C), πx_{n+1} = x_n} depends only on the rigid-analytic group 𝒢.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, pp. 177–178, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.9: Banach structure on X(G)(C)
items.statement: For r ∈ ]0,+∞[ put a_r = {y ∈ O_C | v(y) ≥ r} and X(G)_r(O_C) = {(x_n) ∈ X(G)(O_C) | x_0 ∈ ker(G(O_C) → G(O_C/a_r))}. It is a π-adically complete sub-O_E-module of the E-vector space X(G)(C) defining a Banach-space structure on X(G)(C); this Banach topology does not depend on r.
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.9, p. 178, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: ×π on 𝒢 and the lattice X(G)_r(O_C) as a projective limit of affinoids
items.statement: Let 𝒢_r ⊂ 𝒢 be the affinoid subgroup with 𝒢_r(O_C) = ker(G(O_C) → G(O_C/a_r)) (a closed ball of radius q^{−r} in coordinates). ×π: 𝒢 → 𝒢 is finite étale, a Galois covering with group G[π](O_C). For n ∈ Z let π^n𝒢_r be the preimage of 𝒢_r under ×π^{−n} (n ≤ 0), resp. its image under ×π^n (n ≥ 0), an affinoid subgroup. Then X(G)_r(O_C) is the projective limit of the C-points of … ←^{×π} π^{n+1}𝒢_r ←^{×π} π^n𝒢_r ←^{×π} π^{n−1}𝒢_r ← …, whose transition maps are Galois coverings with group G[π](O_C).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 178, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: The rigid logarithm of 𝒢 as an étale covering
items.statement: The logarithm log: 𝒢 → Lie G ⊗ G_a^rig is an étale covering in the sense of de Jong [39], Galois with group the discrete group G[π^∞](O_C). Its restriction log|_{𝒢_r}: 𝒢_r → log(𝒢_r) is a finite étale Galois covering with group 𝒢_r ∩ G[π^∞](C). If r_0 = inf{r | 𝒢_r ∩ G[π] = {0}} (printed "= ∅"), then on the open ball ∪_{r>r_0} 𝒢_r, log is an isomorphism onto its image, with inverse the exponential of the formal group, whose largest domain of convergence is ∪_{r>r_0} log(𝒢_r).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 178, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof; uses de Jong [39]. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exact sequence 0 → V_π(G) → X(G)(C) → Lie G → 0
items.statement: The logarithm defines an E-linear map log: X(G)(C) → Lie G = Lie 𝒢[1/p], (x_n) ↦ log(x_0), with kernel the rational Tate module V_π(G) = {(x_n) | x_n ∈ G(O_C), πx_{n+1} = x_n, x_n = 0 for n ≪ 0}; one gets an exact sequence of Banach spaces 0 → V_π(G) → X(G)(C) → Lie G → 0 with V_π(G) a finite-dimensional E-vector space and Lie G a finite-dimensional C-vector space. It depends only on the rigid group 𝒢.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, pp. 178–179, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3) gives 0 → O → O(1) → O_{S^♯} → 0, i.e. this sequence for the height-1 Lubin–Tate group only.

items.name: X(G)(O_C) ≅ X(G_k)(O_C/a)
items.statement: For every non-zero ideal a ⊂ m_C, reduction X(G)(O_C) → X(G)(O_C/a) is an isomorphism of E-vector spaces with inverse (y_n)_n ↦ (lim_{k→+∞} π^k ŷ_{n+k})_n (ŷ_n ∈ G(O_C) any lift). Choosing a with πO_C ⊂ a and ρ_a an isomorphism, composing with ρ_a^{−1} gives a canonical isomorphism X(G)(O_C) ⥲ X(G_k)(O_C/a).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 179, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From Prop. 4.5.2. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 4.5.10: ×π-limit versus Frobenius-limit
items.statement: The morphism of projective systems (G_k, ×π)_n → (G_k^{(q^{−n})}, F)_n given by V_π^n induces an isomorphism of E-vector spaces lim_{←, N, ×π} G_k(O_C/a) ⥲ lim_{←, N, F} G_k^{(q^{−n})}(O_C/a) = G_k((O_C/a)^♭).
items.locator: Lemme 4.5.10, p. 179, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof: G formal, so F^n = πu with u an isogeny for n large. Not in the atlas.

items.name: The isomorphism X(G)(C) ≅ G_k(O_F)
items.statement: Using the canonical identifications O_F = O_C^♭ = (O_C/a)^♭, one obtains an isomorphism of E-vector spaces X(G)(C) = X(G)(O_C) ⥲ G_k(O_F).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses that the tilt (O_C/a)^♭ does not depend on a ∋ p; the tilt as lim_{x↦x^p} is planned in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring but this independence is not stated. Not otherwise in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.11: X(G)(O_C) ≅ G_k(O_F) is a homeomorphism
items.statement: The isomorphism of E-vector spaces X(G)(O_C) ⥲ G_k(O_F) is a homeomorphism of Banach spaces.
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.11, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie alors aisément". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Decomposition of X(G)(O_C) by slopes
items.statement: With D[1/π] the rational contravariant Dieudonné module of G_k, there are isomorphisms of Banach spaces X(G)(O_C) ≅ G_k(O_F) ≅ Hom_{W_O(k)_Q[F,V_π]}(D[1/π], B^+) ≃ ⊕_{λ ∈ Q∩[0,1], λ = d/h, (d,h)=1} (B^{φ^h=π^d})^{⊕m_λ}, m_λ the multiplicity of the slope λ in the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition of (D[1/π], F).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (it would combine VB0 Dieudonné–Manin with Cor. 4.4.4).

items.name: Fontaine's θ: W_O(O_F) → O_C and its extension θ: B^+ → C
items.statement: The identification O_C^♭ = O_F determines a morphism θ: W_O(O_F) → O_C, which extends to θ: B^+ → C.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib. RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts plans marked untilts over E and θ_i: W_{O_E}(R^+) → R^{♯+} (nodes RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:integral-divisors/product-equation-and-affineness); PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib for E = Q_p. Mathlib: mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta covers only the p-typical W(O_F) → O_C; the extension to B^+ is not in Mathlib.

items.name: Lemme 4.5.12: convergence of π^n f(x_n) in C
items.statement: If f ∈ QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig) and (x_n) ∈ X(𝒢)(C), the sequence (π^n f(x_n))_{n≥0} converges in C; this defines a morphism of E-vector spaces X(𝒢)(C) → Hom_C(QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig)/∼, C), (x_n) ↦ lim_{n→+∞} π^n f(x_n).
items.locator: Lemme 4.5.12, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Analogue of Lemme 4.5.5; no separate proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.13: geometric interpretation of the period map
items.statement: Via the identification D[1/π] ⊗ C = QuasiHom(𝒢, G_a^rig)/∼, the composite X(𝒢)(C) ⥲ G_k(O_F) ⥲ Hom_{W_O(k)_Q[F,V_π]}(D[1/π], B^+) →^{θ_*} Hom_{W_O(k)_Q}(D[1/π], C) = Hom_C(D[1/π] ⊗ C, C) coincides with the morphism (x_n) ↦ (f ↦ lim_{n→+∞} π^n f(x_n)) of Lemme 4.5.12.
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.13, p. 180, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "La démonstration est laissée au lecteur" (no proof given). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.14: isomorphism of exact sequences (period map and Hodge filtration)
items.statement: Let D_C = D ⊗_{W_O(k)} C, Fil D_C^* the Hodge filtration of the dual of D_C, and Fil Hom_{W_O(k)[F]}(D[1/π], B^+) := θ_*^{−1}(Fil D_C^*). There is an isomorphism of exact sequences of Banach spaces between 0 → V_π(G) → X(G)(C) →^{log} Lie G → 0 and 0 → Fil Hom_{W_O(k)[F]}(D[1/π], B^+) → Hom_{W_O(k)_Q[F]}(D[1/π], B^+) →^{θ} D_C^*/Fil D_C^* → 0.
items.locator: Proposition 4.5.14, p. 181, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from the preceding results (no separate proof). Atlas: only the height-1 Lubin–Tate case (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence and lubin-tate-universal-cover).

items.name: Exemple 4.5.15: the fundamental exact sequence for G̃_{1,h}
items.statement: Let G̃_{1,h} be the π-divisible O-module over O_E of Exemple 4.3.2, C = \widehat{Ē}, F = C^♭. The exact sequence 0 → V_π G̃_{1,h} → X(G̃_{1,h}) → Lie G̃_{1,h}[1/π] ⊗ C → 0 identifies with 0 → ker(θ|_{B^{φ^h=π}}) → (B^+)^{φ^h=π} →^θ C → 0. The morphisms θ, θ∘φ, …, θ∘φ^{h−1}: (B^+)^{φ^h=π} → C are given by the quasi-logarithms of G̃_{1,h}, θ corresponding to the logarithm.
items.locator: Exemple 4.5.15, p. 181, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Atlas: h = 1 case in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3) and lubin-tate-universal-cover (evaluation = log). General h not planned.

items.name: 4.6.1.1: the perfection Â^d_R = lim_α Â^d
items.statement: Let R be an O_E-algebra that is I-adic for an ideal I containing π, Â^d = Spf(R[[x_1,…,x_d]]) (I + (x_1,…,x_d)-adic topology); as an fppf sheaf on Spf(R), Â^d(U) = {(x_1,…,x_d) ∈ Γ(U,O_U)^d | each x_i nilpotent}. Let α: Â^d → Â^d, α^*x_i = x_i^p. The projective limit Â^d_R of … →^α Â^d →^α Â^d, as an fppf sheaf on Spf(R), is represented by the formal spectrum of the completion of ∪_{n≥0} R[[x_1^{p^{−n}},…,x_d^{p^{−n}}]] for the I + (x_1,…,x_d)-adic topology, which equals {Σ_{α∈N[1/p]^d} a_α x^α | ∀A > 0, ∀k ∈ N, {α | |α| ≤ A, a_α ∉ I^k} is finite}; if R is discrete these are the power series with exponents in N[1/p]^d with support locally finite in R^d_+.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.1.1, pp. 181–182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas in this generality. Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit (lim along relative Frobenius of flat t-adic formal schemes over a perfect char-p field is represented by the perfection) — char-p base only.

items.name: Définition 4.6.1: R{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}}
items.statement: For an adic ring R, R{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}} := the completion of ∪_{n≥0} R[[x_1^{p^{−n}},…,x_d^{p^{−n}}]] (for the I + (x_1,…,x_d)-adic topology).
items.locator: Définition 4.6.1, p. 182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.2: formal E-vector space of dimension d
items.statement: A formal E-vector space of dimension d over Spf(R) is a Spf(R)-formal scheme in E-vector spaces which is isomorphic, as a pointed Spf(R)-formal scheme, to Â^d_R.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.2, p. 182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (FS/atlas use perfectoid balls Spd k[[x^{1/p^∞}]] in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (iv) instead).

items.name: Définition 4.6.3: X(G) as an fppf sheaf
items.statement: For G a formal π-divisible O-module over an adic O_E-algebra R, X(G) is the fppf sheaf lim_{←, N} G with transition maps ×π: G → G.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.3, p. 182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The Scholze–Weinstein universal cover [57]; only the height-1 Lubin–Tate instance is in the atlas (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover).

items.name: Â^d_R in characteristic p
items.statement: If R is annihilated by π, Â^d_R = lim_{←, N} Â^d with transition maps the relative Frobenius of Â^d/Spf(R). If moreover R is perfect, R{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}} = (R[[x_1,…,x_d]]_perf)^∧.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.2, p. 182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit (formal-scheme part). Not stated for this ring.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.4(1): X(G) is a formal E-vector space (R perfect)
items.statement: Let R be a perfect adic ring (of characteristic p, over F_q) and G a formal π-divisible O-module over R. Then X(G) is a formal E-vector space.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.4(1), p. 182, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via Lemme 4.5.10-type comparison with lim along Frobenius. Atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (iv) (BC(O(λ)) = Spd k[[x_1^{1/p^∞},…,x_r^{1/p^∞}]], quoting [SW13]) covers G = G_{d,h} with (d,h) = 1 in diamond language; the general statement is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.4(2): X(G) ≅ G ∘ (−)^♭
items.statement: With R perfect and G as above, as functors from adic R-algebras to E-vector spaces there is a canonical isomorphism X(G) ⥲ G ∘ (−)^♭, where (−)^♭: A ↦ lim_{←, N, Frob_q} A (with the projective-limit topology). In particular X(G)(A) ≅ G(A^♭) = G(A) for A a perfect adic R-algebra.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.4(2), p. 183, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: 4.6.3: canonical lift W_O(A) of a perfect F_q-algebra
items.statement: Every perfect F_q-algebra A has a unique lift to a π-adic, π-torsion-free O_E-algebra, W_O(A). If moreover A is I-adic, W_O(A) is adic for the ideal (π) + ([a])_{a∈I}. This defines a fully faithful embedding W_O: {perfect adic F_q-algebras} ↪ {π-torsion-free adic O_E-algebras}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.3, p. 183, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property. RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0/ramified-witt-universal-property: for a perfect F_q-algebra R there is a unique π-adically complete flat O_E-algebra R̃ with R̃/π = R (realised as W_{O_E}(R)); the adic-topology and embedding-of-categories statements are part of RF0's "functoriality, reduction, topology" obligations. Mathlib has only p-typical WittVector.

items.name: Lemme 4.6.5: W_O commutes with R{{x^{p^{−∞}}}}
items.statement: Let R be a perfect adic F_q-algebra. The W_O(R)-algebra morphism ∪_{n≥0} W_O(R)[[x_1^{p^{−n}},…,x_d^{p^{−n}}]] → W_O(R{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}}), x_i^{p^{−n}} ↦ [x_i^{p^{−n}}], extends to an isomorphism of adic W_O(R)-algebras W_O(R){{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}} ⥲ W_O(R{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}}).
items.locator: Lemme 4.6.5, p. 183, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.6: canonical lift Ẽ of a formal E-vector space
items.statement: Let R be a perfect adic F_q-algebra and ℰ = Spf(A) a formal E-vector space over Spf(R). Then Spf(W_O(A)) is a formal E-vector space over Spf(W_O(R)) (by Lemme 4.6.5); it is denoted ℰ̃ and called the canonical lift of ℰ.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.6, p. 184, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.7: functor of points of the canonical lift
items.statement: Let R be a perfect adic F_q-algebra and ℰ a formal E-vector space over R. (1) As functors from adic W_O(R)-algebras to E-vector spaces, ℰ̃ ≃ ℰ ∘ (− ⊗_{W_O(R)} R). (2) As functors from adic R-algebras to E-vector spaces, ℰ ≃ ℰ̃ ∘ W_O, where W_O: adic R-algebras → adic W_O(R)-algebras. Example: for G a formal π-divisible O-module over R, X̃(G) ≃ X(G) ∘ (− ⊗_{W_O(R)} R) ≃ G ∘ (−)^♭ ∘ (− ⊗_{W_O(R)} R) ≃ G ∘ (−)^♭.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.7, p. 184, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof only cites "une version améliorée [pour des anneaux topologiques]" of the adjunction of Prop. 2.1.7, which is not stated (see sourceIssues). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.8: X(G) in unequal characteristic via a quasi-isogeny
items.statement: Let R be an adic O_E-algebra and G a formal π-divisible O-module over R. Suppose there are a perfect adic F_q-algebra A with a morphism A → R/πR, a formal π-divisible O-module H over A and a quasi-isogeny ρ: H ⊗_A R/πR → G ⊗_R R/πR. Then (1) X(G) is a formal E-vector space; (2) with W_O(A) → R the canonical lift of A → R/πR, ρ induces an isomorphism X̃(H) ⊗̂_{W_O(A)} R ⥲ X(G).
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.8, p. 185, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Scholze–Weinstein [57] Prop. 3.1.3 analogue; not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 4.6.9: X(G) depends only on the special fibre
items.statement: Let K|E be complete valued with perfect residue field k_K, G a formal π-divisible O-module over O_K with special fibre G_{k_K}; fix a section of O_K/πO_K → k_K and suppose the identity of G_{k_K} lifts to a (necessarily unique) quasi-isogeny ρ: G_{k_K} ⊗_{k_K} O_K/πO_K → G ⊗_{O_K} O_K/πO_K. Then X(G) ≃ X̃(G_{k_K}) ⊗̂_{W_O(k_K)} O_K; in particular the formal E-vector space X(G) depends only on the special fibre of G.
items.locator: Corollaire 4.6.9, p. 185, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 4.6.10: X(Ĝ_m) over Z_p in coordinates
items.statement: For Ĝ_m over Z_p and the inductive system (Z_p[[U_i]])_{i∈N} with U_i ↦ (1+U_{i+1})^p − 1, there is an isomorphism Z_p{{T^{p^{−∞}}}} → (∪_{i≥0} Z_p[[U_i]])^∧ ((p,U_0)-adic completion), T^{p^{−n}} ↦ lim_{k→+∞} U_{n+k}^{p^k}. The associated formal Q_p-vector-space law Δ: Z_p{{T^{p^{−∞}}}} → Z_p{{X^{p^{−∞}},Y^{p^{−∞}}}} is Δ(T^{p^{−n}}) = Σ_{α,β ∈ N[1/p]∩[0,1], α+β≥1} a_{α,β} X^{αp^{−n}} Y^{βp^{−n}}, with a_{α,β} = lim_{n→+∞} (p^n)!/((p^n(1−α))!(p^n(1−β))!(p^n(α+β−1))!) ∈ Z_p. By Kummer/Legendre, v_p(a_{α,β}) ≥ max(0, −v_p(1−α), −v_p(1−β), −v_p(α+β−1)) ≥ −inf{v_p(α), v_p(β), v_p(α+β)}, with equality v_p(a_{α,β}) = −v_p(α) when α + β = 1. [The book instead prints, for p ≠ 2 and α ≠ 1 or β ≠ 1, v_p(a_{α,β}) = 1 − inf{v_p(α), v_p(β), v_p(α+β)}, which is false (e.g. (α,β) = (1/p, 1−1/p): valuation 1, not 2) — see sourceIssues.]
items.locator: Exemple 4.6.10, p. 186, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Coefficient formula checked (expansion of lim (X^{p^{−m}}+Y^{p^{−m}}+X^{p^{−m}}Y^{p^{−m}})^{p^m}); the valuation claim fails. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.11: M(A), |f(x)|, ‖f‖_Ω and bounded subsets
items.statement: Let K|Q_p be complete for a real valuation extending the p-adic one, and A a topological K-algebra. (1) M(A) is the set of continuous valuations v: A → R ∪ {+∞} extending the valuation of K. (2) For x ∈ M(A), f ∈ A: v(f(x)) := x(f), |f(x)| := p^{−v(f(x))}. (3) For Ω ⊂ M(A), ‖f‖_Ω = sup{|f(x)| | x ∈ Ω}. (4) Ω ⊂ M(A) is bounded if there is a neighbourhood U of 0 in A with sup{|f(x)| | f ∈ U, x ∈ Ω} < +∞ (printed "x ∈ U").
items.locator: Définition 4.6.11, pp. 186–187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/spectrum defines M(A) for normed rings (bounded multiplicative seminorms), not for topological K-algebras with continuous valuations; boundedness of subsets is not defined there.

items.name: Basic properties of ‖·‖_Ω and bounded sets
items.statement: Continuity of the valuations in M(A) is equivalent to: for all x ∈ M(A), {x} is bounded. If Ω ⊂ M(A) is bounded, ‖f‖_Ω is finite and ‖·‖_Ω: A → R_+ is a submultiplicative seminorm with ‖f^n‖_Ω = ‖f‖_Ω^n for all n ≥ 1. A finite union of bounded sets is bounded, and a subset of a bounded set is bounded.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Printed "‖f^n‖_Ω = ‖f‖_Ω", a misprint for ‖f‖_Ω^n (see sourceIssues); stated without proof. Not in the atlas in this form (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm is for Tate rings).

items.name: Définition 4.6.12: spectral K-algebra
items.statement: A spectral K-algebra is a topological K-algebra A such that M(A) is a countable union of bounded sets, the topology of A is defined by the family of seminorms (‖·‖_Ω)_{Ω bounded}, and A is separated and complete.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.12, p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Ad hoc notion of FF (superseded by perfectoid spaces, as the introduction says). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.13: topology on M(A)
items.statement: Give each bounded subset of M(A) the weak topology of maps A → R ∪ {+∞}; the topology of M(A) is the inductive-limit topology for M(A) = ∪_{Ω bounded} Ω.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.13, p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: TB.0 gives only the Banach (bounded) case topology. Not otherwise in the atlas.

items.name: Spectral Banach algebras; M(A) compact
items.statement: The spectral algebras A with M(A) bounded are the spectral Banach algebras; for them M(A) is compact ([6] 1.2.1) and one writes ‖·‖_∞ := ‖·‖_{M(A)}. Spectral algebras are Fréchet spaces.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only one ingredient is planned: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/compact-spectrum (M(A) compact for every normed commutative ring; Hausdorff by TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/hausdorff-spectrum). FF's spectral algebras (Déf. 4.6.12, missing), the characterisation of the spectral Banach algebras among them and their Fréchet property are not in the atlas.

items.name: M(A) non-empty for a spectral Banach algebra ([6] 1.2.1) — external
items.statement: If A is a (non-zero) spectral Banach K-algebra, M(A) is non-empty.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berkovich [6] Thm 1.2.1 black box. TB.0 states compactness and Hausdorffness of M(A) but not non-emptiness.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.14(1): bounded subsets of M(A) are compact
items.statement: Let A be a topological K-algebra. Every bounded subset of M(A) is relatively compact, i.e. every closed bounded subset of M(A) is compact. [Printed: "Tout sous-ensemble borné de M(A) est compact", false for non-closed bounded subsets — see sourceIssues.]
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(1), p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie facilement" — no proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.14(2): Banach completion at a bounded set and its holomorphic hull
items.statement: Let A be a topological K-algebra and Ω ⊂ M(A) bounded. The completion (A, ‖·‖_Ω)^ is a spectral Banach algebra whose spectrum is a bounded subset Ω^c ⊂ M(A) containing Ω (the "holomorphically convex hull" of Ω); as norms on (A,‖·‖_Ω)^, ‖·‖_Ω = ‖·‖_∞, and as seminorms on A, ‖·‖_Ω = ‖·‖_{Ω^c}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(2), p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof given. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.14(3): spectral completion A^sp
items.statement: Suppose M(A) is a countable union of bounded sets. Then A^sp := lim_{←, Ω bounded} (A, ‖·‖_Ω)^ is a spectral algebra with a continuous morphism A → A^sp inducing a homeomorphism M(A^sp) ⥲ M(A); A is spectral iff A → A^sp is an isomorphism; A ↦ A^sp is adjoint to the inclusion of spectral algebras into topological K-algebras whose spectrum is a countable union of bounded sets (printed "adjoint à droite"; it is the left adjoint/reflector, see sourceIssues).
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(3), pp. 187–188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof given. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.14(4): projective limits of spectral Banach algebras
items.statement: If (A_n)_{n∈N} is a projective system of spectral Banach algebras, A = lim A_n is spectral. If moreover the transition maps A_{n+1} → A_n have dense image, then each M(A_n) ⊂ M(A) is bounded, M(A) = ∪_{n≥0} M(A_n), and (A, ‖·‖_{M(A_n)})^ ⥲ A_n.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(4), p. 188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof given. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Mittag-Leffler facts for Fréchet limits of Banach spaces
items.statement: If (V_n)_{n∈N} is a projective system of Banach spaces with transition maps of dense image and V = lim V_n, the projections V → V_i have dense image and for every Banach space W, lim_{→, n} Hom(V_n, W) ⥲ Hom(V, W).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Recalled standard fact. Not in the atlas (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-dense-restriction is a related density statement).

items.name: Proposition 4.6.15: spectral algebras as pro-systems of spectral Banach algebras
items.statement: The category of spectral K-algebras is equivalent to the pro-category of projective systems (A_n)_{n∈N} of spectral K-Banach algebras with transition maps of dense image, where Hom(lim A_n, lim B_m) = lim_{←, m} lim_{→, n} Hom(A_n, B_m).
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.15, p. 188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.16: K-spectral spaces
items.statement: The category of K-spectral spaces is the opposite of the category of spectral K-algebras; M(A) denotes the spectral space of A, and |X| the underlying topological space of a spectral space X.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.16, p. 188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Inductive limits and functor of points of spectral spaces
items.statement: Every inductive system (X_n = M(A_n))_{n≥0} of bounded spectral spaces has an inductive limit M(lim_← A_n) in spectral spaces; restricted to systems with A_{n+1} → A_n of dense image this gives an equivalence between the ind-category of such systems and spectral spaces. A spectral space X is characterised by its functor on spectral K-Banach algebras A ↦ X(A), and for X = lim_→ X_n as above X(−) = lim_→ X_n(−).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, pp. 188–189, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Points of spectral spaces
items.statement: Each x ∈ X defines a complete valued field K(x) (for X = M(A), x ↔ v with support p_x = v^{−1}(+∞), K(x) is the completion of Frac(A/p_x) for v). For L|K complete valued, M(L) is a single point, and X(L) = Hom(M(L), X) → |X|; each x ∈ |X| is the image of a canonical element of X(K(x)). In particular X(K) ⊂ |X| is a totally disconnected topological subspace equal to {x ∈ |X| | K(x) = K}. By [6] 1.3.4, |X| is a single point iff X = M(L) for some complete valued L|K.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 189, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses Berkovich [6] 1.3.4. Not in the atlas (TB.0 plans completed residue fields of the Berkovich spectrum of a Banach algebra only).

items.name: Fibre products and scalar extension of spectral spaces
items.statement: Spectral spaces have fibre products: for bounded X = M(A), Y = M(B), X × Y = M((A ⊗̂_K B)^sp), (A ⊗̂_K B)^sp being the spectral completion of A ⊗̂_K B (equivalently of the normed algebra A ⊗_K B); if X = lim_→ X_n, Y = lim_→ Y_n with X_n, Y_n bounded, X × Y = lim_→ X_n × Y_n. For L|K complete valued, X ↦ X ⊗̂_K L, M(A) ⊗̂_K L = M((A ⊗_K L)^sp), is an extension-of-scalars functor.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 189, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Reduced affinoid algebras are spectral Banach algebras ([8] 6.2.4)
items.statement: If X = Sp(A) is a reduced K-affinoid rigid space, A is a spectral K-Banach algebra ([8] 6.2.4), defining a bounded spectral space X^an. This gives a fully faithful functor {reduced K-affinoid rigid spaces} ↪ {bounded K-spectral spaces}; the topological space of X^an is the underlying space of the Berkovich analytic space.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.2, p. 190, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partly planned: BGR 6.2.4 (the supremum norm on a reduced affinoid is a norm equivalent to the residue norm) is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm, and sup over M(A) = spectral radius via AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/spectrum. The functor to FF's bounded K-spectral spaces (Déf. 4.6.16, missing) and its full faithfulness are not planned.

items.name: Quasi-Stein reduced rigid spaces
items.statement: A reduced K-rigid space X is quasi-Stein if it has an admissible affinoid covering X = ∪_{n≥0} U_n with U_n ⊂ U_{n+1} a Weierstrass domain (i.e. Γ(U_{n+1}, O_X) → Γ(U_n, O_X) of dense image).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.2, p. 190, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Best node(s): AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-space. AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-space (Kiehl: exhaustion by affinoids with dense restriction maps; Stein if Weierstrass). FF's "c'est à dire" conflates Weierstrass domain with dense image; the atlas keeps them apart.

items.name: Spectral space of a reduced quasi-Stein rigid space
items.statement: Let X be a reduced quasi-Stein K-rigid space and give Γ(X, O_X) the topology of uniform convergence on quasi-compact admissible opens. Then Γ(X, O_X) is a spectral K-algebra; X^an := M(Γ(X, O_X)) has underlying space that of the Berkovich space of X; X ↦ X^an is a fully faithful functor {reduced Stein rigid spaces} ↪ {K-spectral spaces}; the bounded subsets of |X^an| are those contained in an affinoid domain; and for X = ∪ U_n as above, X^an = lim_→ U_n^an in spectral spaces.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.2, p. 190, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (nearest AdicSpacesPartII:R3 quasi-Stein nodes: definition, Theorems A/B, dense restriction).

items.name: Exemple 4.6.17: spectral open ball
