items.statement: The spectral space associated with the open ball B̊^d of dimension d is the spectrum of the Fréchet algebra {Σ_{α∈N^d} a_α x^α | ∀ρ < 1, lim_{|α|→+∞} |a_α| ρ^{|α|} = 0} with the family of Gauss norms (‖·‖_ρ)_{ρ<1}.
items.locator: Exemple 4.6.17, p. 190, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas as a spectral space.

items.name: 4.6.5.3: étale spectral spaces
items.statement: (a) For X compact totally disconnected, C^0(X,K) with the sup norm is a spectral K-Banach algebra and X → M(C^0(X,K)) is a homeomorphism; X ↦ X^ét = sp(C^0(X,K)) is a fully faithful functor {compact totally disconnected spaces} ↪ {bounded spectral spaces}. (b) With K̄ an algebraic closure, C = \hat{K̄}, G_K = Gal(K̄|K), X compact totally disconnected with continuous G_K-action, A = C^∞(X, K̄)^{G_K} (locally constant functions, (σ.f)(x) = σ(f(σ^{−1}x))) with the sup norm: X/G_K ⥲ M(A) = M(A^sp); X^ét := M(A^sp) is functorial and X^ét ⊗̂_K C = X^ét (forgetting the G_K-action), although a priori A ⊗̂_K C ≠ C^0(X, C) in general. (c) For X locally compact totally disconnected and a countable union of compacts, C^0(X,K) with compact-open topology is spectral, X ⥲ sp(C^0(X,K)), bounded subsets = relatively compact subsets, X^ét = lim_→ Ω^ét over compact Ω ⊂ X; this extends to such X with continuous G_K-action.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.3, pp. 190–191, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: 4.6.5.4: projective limit of a tower of reduced affinoids
items.statement: Let (X_n = Sp(A_n))_{n≥0} be a projective system of reduced K-affinoid rigid spaces with finite surjective transition maps. Then (A_n, ‖·‖_∞) → (A_{n+1}, ‖·‖_∞) are isometries; give A_∞ = lim_→ A_n the norm ‖·‖_∞ making each A_n ↪ A_∞ isometric, and let Â_∞ be its completion. Then (Â_∞, ‖·‖_∞) is a spectral K-Banach algebra; the natural map M(Â_∞) → lim_← M(A_n) is a homeomorphism (printed "M(A_n) → lim M(A_n)"); and X = M(Â_∞) with the natural maps X → X_n^an is a projective limit of (X_n^an) in spectral spaces.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.4, pp. 191–192, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie alors aisément". Nearest atlas notion: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit (tilde-limits of adic spaces), a different framework.

items.name: 4.6.5.4: projective limit of a tower of reduced quasi-Stein spaces
items.statement: Let (X_n)_{n≥0} be a projective system of reduced quasi-Stein K-rigid spaces with finite surjective transition maps p_n: X_n → X_0. Write X_0 = ∪_i U_i (admissible affinoid covering, U_i ⊂ U_{i+1} Weierstrass) and U_{i,n} = p_n^{−1}(U_i). Each (U_{i,n})_n satisfies the affinoid hypotheses; with sp(B_i) := lim_{←, n} U_{i,n}, the maps B_{i+1} → B_i have dense image and lim_{→, i} lim_{←, n} U_{i,n} = sp(lim_{←, i} B_i) is a projective limit of (X_n) in spectral spaces. Equivalently, with X_n = sp(A_n), ‖·‖_{i,n} the sup seminorm on U_{i,n}, the inclusions (A_n, ‖·‖_{i,n}) ↪ (A_{n+1}, ‖·‖_{i,n+1}) are isometric and define seminorms ‖·‖_i on A_∞ = ∪_n A_n; lim_← X_n is the spectrum of the spectral completion of A_∞ for (‖·‖_i)_{i≥0}.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.4, pp. 192–193, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie alors". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 4.6.18: limits of étale rigid spaces
items.statement: Let (X_n)_{n≥0} be a projective system of étale K-rigid spaces with countably many connected components and finite surjective transition maps; each X_n is Stein, giving spectral spaces (X_n^ét)_n. With X = lim_← X_n(K̄) with its continuous G_K-action, lim_← X_n^an = (lim_← X_n(K̄))^ét.
items.locator: Exemple 4.6.18, p. 193, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 4.6.19: V_p(G)^ét as a limit
items.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over Spec(O_K) with generic fibre G_η = (G[p^n] ⊗ K)_{n≥1}. Each G_η[p^n] is a finite étale K-scheme, so Γ = lim_→ G_η[p^n]^rig is an étale K-rigid group, and lim_{←, N} Γ^an ≃ V_p(G)^ét, the transition maps being ×p: Γ^an → Γ^an.
items.locator: Exemple 4.6.19, p. 193, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: 4.6.5.5: generic fibre of formally finite type affine formal schemes
items.statement: There is a generic-fibre functor 𝔛 ↦ 𝔛^rig from affine Spf(O_K)-formal schemes formally of finite type (algebra O_K[[x_1,…,x_n]]⟨y_1,…,y_m⟩/(ideal), ideal of definition (p, x_1,…,x_n)) to quasi-Stein K-rigid spaces. If 𝔛 = Spf(A) and I is an ideal of definition of A, Γ(𝔛^rig, O_{𝔛^rig}) = lim_{←, k≥0} (A[x/π]_{x∈I^k})^∧[1/π] as a projective limit of Banach algebras (π-adic completion).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.5, p. 193, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Berthelot's construction, stated without proof. Nearest atlas: AdicSpacesPartII:R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base (Conrad's (·)^rig on locally noetherian formal schemes over a noetherian adic C); the quasi-Stein property and the displayed formula for global sections are not stated there, and FF's O_K need not be noetherian.

items.name: Définition 4.6.20: the spectral generic fibre 𝔛^an of an affine adic formal scheme
items.statement: Let 𝔛 = Spf(A) be an affine formal scheme over Spf(O_K) (printed Spf(O_C)) with A adic and I an ideal of definition. For k ≥ 0 let A_k = A[x/π]_{x∈I^k} (an O_K-algebra), Â_k its π-adic completion, Â_k[1/π] the associated Banach algebra, and B = lim_{←, k≥0} Â_k[1/π] (a K-Fréchet algebra) with spectral completion B^sp. Put 𝔛^an := sp(B^sp) as a K-spectral space.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.20, p. 194, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Compatibility of 𝔛^an with the rigid generic fibre; functor of points
items.statement: If 𝔛 is a reduced affine formal scheme formally of finite type over Spf(O_K), then (𝔛^rig)^an = 𝔛^an via the embedding of reduced quasi-Stein rigid spaces into K-spectral spaces (printed "C-espaces spectraux"). As a functor on spectral K-Banach algebras, 𝔛^an(A) = 𝔛(A^0) with A^0 = {a ∈ A | ‖a‖_∞ ≤ 1}; this characterises 𝔛^an.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.5, p. 194, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.21: generic fibre commutes with projective limits
items.statement: Let (𝔛_n)_{n≥0} be a projective system of affine Spf(O_K)-formal schemes formally of finite type whose transition maps are adic, finite, free (locally free) and surjective. There is a canonical isomorphism (lim_{←, n} 𝔛_n)^an ⥲ lim_{←, n} 𝔛_n^an, where, for 𝔛_n = Spf(A_n) and I an ideal of definition of A_0, lim_← 𝔛_n is the formal spectrum of the I-adic completion of ∪_{n≥0} A_n.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.21, p. 194, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via the functor of points on spectral Banach algebras. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.22: the K-algebra K⟨⟨x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩
items.statement: K⟨⟨x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩ = {Σ_{α∈N[1/p]^d} a_α x^α | a_α ∈ K, ∀ρ < 1, |a_α| ρ^{|α|} → 0 along the cofinite filter of N[1/p]^d (for every ε > 0 only finitely many α with |a_α|ρ^{|α|} ≥ ε)} (printed "lim_{|α|→+∞} |a_α| ρ^{|α|} = 0", which does not constrain the infinitely many α of bounded size — see sourceIssues), with, for ρ < 1, ‖f‖_ρ = sup{|a_α| ρ^{|α|} | α ∈ N[1/p]^d}.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.22, p. 195, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.23(1): K⟨⟨x^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩ is spectral
items.statement: The K-algebra K⟨⟨x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩ with the family of norms (‖·‖_ρ)_{0<ρ<1} is spectral.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.23(1), p. 195, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie alors aisément". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.23(2): generic fibre of the perfectoid formal ball
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.23(2), p. 195, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof. Not in the atlas (FS-style perfectoid open ball appears in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (iv) only as Spd).

items.name: Proposition 4.6.23(3): K⟨⟨x^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩ as a limit of open balls
items.statement: M(K⟨⟨x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩) = lim_{←, n≥0} B̊^d, B̊^d the spectral open ball of dimension d, transition maps (x_1,…,x_d) ↦ (x_1^p,…,x_d^p). Under this identification, for 0 < ρ < 1, ‖·‖_ρ is the sup norm on the compact lim_{←, n≥0} |B^d(0, ρ^{p^{−n}})| ⊂ |lim_← B̊^d|, B^d(0, ρ^{p^{−n}}) the closed spectral ball of radius ρ^{p^{−n}}.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.23(3), p. 195, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof. Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit (perfection as tilde-limit along Frobenius, adic spaces).

items.name: Définition 4.6.24: B_J^+ and B_R^+ for perfect adic R
items.statement: Let R be a perfect adic F_q-algebra. For an open ideal J of R, B_J^+ := (W_{O_E}(R)[[x]/π]_{x∈J})^∧[1/π] (π-adic completion), an E-Banach algebra; for I an ideal of definition, B_R^+ := lim_{←, k≥1} B_{I^k}^+, an E-Fréchet algebra. It does not depend on I; the Witt-vector Frobenius extends to a bijective Frobenius φ on B_R^+; and the earlier ring B^+ is B^+_{O_F}.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.24, p. 196, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Relative B^+ ring. Atlas: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y/RF0:annuli plan the rings of 𝒴_S = Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) \ V([ϖ]) and Y_S (annulus rings), not this Fréchet ring B_R^+ for general adic perfect R.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.25: B^+ of the perfect power-series ring
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of Fréchet algebras B^+_{k{{x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}}}} ≃ W_{O_E}(k)_Q⟨⟨x_1^{p^{−∞}},…,x_d^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩ (k a perfect field).
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.25, p. 196, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie aussitôt ... en utilisant le lemme 4.6.5". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 4.6.26: the spectral universal cover X(𝒢)
items.statement: Let K|E be complete valued with perfect residue field k_K, G a formal π-divisible O-module over O_K, a section k_K → O_K/πO_K fixed, and assume the identity of G_{k_K} lifts to a quasi-isogeny ρ: G_{k_K} ⊗ O_K/πO_K → G ⊗ O_K/πO_K. Let 𝒢 = (G^rig)^an = 𝔊^an be the spectral group of the generic fibre. X(𝒢) := lim_{←, N} 𝒢 in K-spectral spaces, with transition maps ×π: 𝒢 → 𝒢.
items.locator: Définition 4.6.26, p. 196, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: X(𝒢) is a spectral E-vector space and X(𝒢)(K) a Banach space
items.statement: X(𝒢) is a group, indeed an E-vector space, in spectral spaces. The embedding X(𝒢)(K) ⊂ |X(𝒢)| and the topology of |X(𝒢)| give X(𝒢)(K) the structure of an E-Banach space: if U ⊂ G^rig is an affinoid subgroup, lim_{←, n∈N} (π^{−n}U)^an ⊂ X(𝒢) (printed p^{−n}U) is a bounded compact spectral sub-O_E-module whose K-points form a lattice defining the Banach topology of X(𝒢)(K).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.6, pp. 196–197, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "dont on vérifie". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.27: X(𝒢) depends only on the special fibre
items.statement: With X̃(G_{k_K}) the canonical lift over W_O(k_K) of the formal E-vector space X(G_{k_K}), there is a canonical isomorphism of spectral E-vector spaces X̃(G_{k_K})^an ⊗̂ K ≃ X(𝒢). In particular X(𝒢) depends only on the special fibre G_{k_K}. This isomorphism induces a homeomorphism of Banach spaces X(G_{k_K})(R(O_K)) ≃ X(𝒢)(K) (R(O_K) = O_K^♭).
items.locator: Proposition 4.6.27, p. 197, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From Prop. 4.6.21 and Cor. 4.6.9. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 4.6.28: convergence of π^n f_{U,n} in A_U
items.statement: Let f: G^rig → G_a^rig be a quasi-morphism (Déf. 4.3.5), U ⊂ G^rig an affinoid sub-O_E-module, X(U) = lim_{←, N} (π^{−n}U)^an = M(A_U) (printed p^{−n}U), and f_{U,n} ∈ A_U the composite of f|_{π^{−n}U} with X(U) → (π^{−n}U)^an. The sequence (π^n f_{U,n})_{n∈N} (printed p^n f_{U,n}) converges in the spectral Banach algebra A_U; if f is bounded, it tends to 0.
items.locator: Lemme 4.6.28, p. 197, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "La démonstration est identique à celle du lemme 4.5.5". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Spectral period morphism QuasiHom/∼ → Hom(X(𝒢), G_a^an)
items.statement: Put g_U = lim_{n→+∞} π^n f_{U,n} ∈ A_U (printed lim f_{U,n}); varying U gives g ∈ lim_{←, U} A_U, and since X(𝒢) = lim_{→, U} X(U) = M(lim_{←, U} A_U), g defines a morphism X(𝒢) → G_a^an, which is a morphism of spectral E-vector spaces. This defines a morphism of K-vector spaces QuasiHom(G^rig, G_a^rig)/∼ → Hom_{spectral E-v.s.}(X(𝒢), G_a^an).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.7.1, pp. 197–198, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "dont on vérifie aisément". Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 4.6.29: the logarithm of X(Ĝ_m) in coordinates
items.statement: The isomorphism Spf(Z_p{{T^{p^{−∞}}}}) ⥲ X(Ĝ_m) of Exemple 4.6.10 induces an isomorphism of spectral spaces sp(Q_p⟨⟨T^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩) ⥲ X(Ĝ_m^rig) (a one-variable spectral group law). In these coordinates, the logarithm log: X(Ĝ_m^an) → G_a^rig is given by the series Σ_{α∈N[1/p], α>0} ε(α) T^α/α ∈ Q_p⟨⟨T^{p^{−∞}}⟩⟩, with ε(α) = −1 if p = 2 and ε(α) = (−1)^{(α mod 2)+1} if p is odd (α mod 2 ∈ {0,1} for α ∈ Z_(2)) [printed: ε(α) = 1 if p = 2 and (−1)^{α mod 2} otherwise, which gives −log — see sourceIssues].
items.locator: Exemple 4.6.29, p. 198, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: 4.6.7.2: exact sequences of rigid and spectral O-modules
items.statement: Let G be a formal π-divisible O-module over O_K as in 4.6.6. There is an exact sequence for the étale topology of rigid-analytic O-modules 0 → G^rig[π^∞] → G^rig →^{log_G} Lie G ⊗ G_a^rig → 0; it induces a sequence of spectral O-modules 0 → G^rig[π^∞]^an → G^an → Lie G ⊗ G_a^an → 0, and applying lim_{←, N} with transition maps ×π, a sequence of spectral E-vector spaces 0 → V_π(G)^ét → X̃(G_k)^an ⊗̂ K → Lie G ⊗ G_a^an → 0 (the middle term being ≃ X(𝒢) by Prop. 4.6.27). It is exact in the sense that V_π(G)^ét is the kernel of the right-hand morphism in spectral groups, and for every complete algebraically closed C|K the induced map X̃(G_k)^an(C) → Lie G ⊗ C is surjective.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.7.2, pp. 198–199, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof. Atlas: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence for the height-1 Lubin–Tate case only (as sheaves on perfectoid spaces).

items.name: Geometrisation of Banach–Colmez spaces
items.statement: If K = C is algebraically closed and A is a sympathetic C-algebra in the sense of [12], the sequence of Banach spaces 0 → V_π(G) → (X̃(G_k)^an ⊗̂ C)(A) → Lie G ⊗ A → 0 is exact; hence the preceding sequence is an exact sequence of finite-dimensional Banach spaces in Colmez's sense, now endowed with a structure sheaf: if X̃(G_k) = Spf(R) (R perfect) then X̃(G_k)^an ⊗̂ C = M(B_R^+ ⊗̂ C).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.7.2, p. 199, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: "On vérifie en fait" — no proof. Atlas geometrises Banach–Colmez spaces as diamonds (VB3, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists), not via Colmez's sympathetic algebras or FF spectral spaces.

items.name: de Jong [39]: étale coverings of rigid spaces — external
items.statement: The notion of étale covering (revêtement étale) of non-archimedean analytic spaces in the sense of de Jong [39], applied to log: 𝒢 → Lie G ⊗ G_a^rig (Galois with group G[π^∞](O_C)).
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.5.3, p. 178, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box. No atlas node on de Jong coverings.

items.name: Berkovich [6] 1.3.4: one-point spectra — external
items.statement: For a K-spectral space X, |X| is a single point iff X is of the form M(L) with L|K a complete valued extension.
items.locator: Ch. 4, 4.6.5.1, p. 189, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box from Berkovich [6] (1.3.4). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 5.1.1: curve (courbe)
items.statement: A curve is a pair consisting of a noetherian, regular, connected scheme X of dimension 1, separated over Spec(ℤ), together with, for every closed point x ∈ X, an integer deg(x) ≥ 1.
items.locator: Définition 5.1.1, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No bundled notion of a scheme with a degree function. Nearest: Tau Ceti's scheme-level divisor API is stated for an integral Noetherian scheme whose local rings at codimension-one points are DVRs (and, for O_X(D) to be invertible, coheight ≤ 1): this is exactly the scheme underlying an FF curve (regular + connected ⇒ integral). The degree function is an arbitrary weight in tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.weightedDegree. The FF-curve instance (X_C^alg connected regular noetherian of dimension 1) is planned in VB2:ampleness (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point).

items.name: Remark after Définition 5.1.1: non-empty opens of a curve are cofinite
items.statement: If X is a curve, the non-empty open subsets of X are exactly the complements of finite sets of closed points of X (equivalently, curves are the connected schemes separated over Spec ℤ obtained by gluing finitely many spectra of Dedekind rings, equipped with a degree function on their maximal ideals).
items.locator: Remark after Définition 5.1.1, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Asserted ('on vérifie'). Tau Ceti has the finiteness half for Noetherian integral schemes: SchemeWeilDivisor.finite_setOfPred_not_mem (a non-empty open misses only finitely many codimension-one points, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Scheme/Principal.lean), but not the characterization of opens.

items.name: Valuations ord_x and sections of O_X on a curve
items.statement: Let X be a curve with generic point η and field of rational functions E(X) = O_{X,η}. Every closed point x ∈ |X| defines a valuation ord_x : E(X) → ℤ ∪ {+∞}, normalized so that ord_x is surjective, and for every non-empty open U ⊂ X, Γ(U, O_X) = {f ∈ E(X) | ∀ x ∈ |U|, ord_x(f) ≥ 0}.
items.locator: §5.1 after Définition 5.1.1, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: orderAt is the order of a nonzero rational function at a codimension-one point; exists_orderAt_eq gives surjectivity onto ℤ when the local ring is a DVR; mem_sections_zero_iff says the sections of O_X(0) (rational functions with ord ≥ 0 at every codimension-one point of U) are exactly the regular functions on U, for U of dimension ≤ 1 on a locally Noetherian integral scheme with DVR codimension-one stalks. On a curve the codimension-one points are the closed points. The text writes v_x for ord_x in the display.

items.name: Définition 5.1.2: divisors Div(X) and their degree
items.statement: If X is a curve, Div(X) denotes the free abelian group on |X| (the Weil divisors). For D = Σ_{x∈|X|} m_x[x] ∈ Div(X), deg(D) = Σ_{x∈|X|} m_x·deg(x).
items.locator: Définition 5.1.2, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: SchemeWeilDivisor X is the finitely supported ℤ-valued functions on the codimension-one points (= closed points of a curve); weightedDegree w D = Σ D(x)·w(x) for an arbitrary weight w, here w = deg.

items.name: Line bundle O_X(D) of a divisor, with its rational section 1
items.statement: For D = Σ_x m_x[x] ∈ Div(X) and an open U, set D_U = Σ_{x∈U} m_x[x] ∈ Div(U). O_X(D) is the line bundle with Γ(U, O_X(D)) = {f ∈ E(X)^× | div(f|_U) + D_U ≥ 0} ∪ {0} for every open U; it carries the rational section 1 ∈ E(X) and hence defines a Cartier divisor (O_X(D), 1).
items.locator: §5.1 after Définition 5.1.2, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: SchemeWeilDivisor.sheaf D has sections {f | f = 0 or ord_x f ≥ −D(x) at every codimension-one x ∈ U} as a subsheaf of the sheaf of rational functions; toInvertibleSheaf packages it as a line bundle when X is Noetherian integral of dimension ≤ 1 with DVR codimension-one stalks. Tau Ceti's scheme-level divisor API is stated for an integral Noetherian scheme whose local rings at codimension-one points are DVRs (and, for O_X(D) to be invertible, coheight ≤ 1): this is exactly the scheme underlying an FF curve (regular + connected ⇒ integral).

items.name: Weil divisors = Cartier divisors (L, s) on a curve
items.statement: On a curve X, Div(X) is identified with the group of isomorphism classes of pairs (L, s), L a line bundle on X and s ∈ L_η ∖ {0} a generically nonzero rational section (Cartier divisors), with group law (L, s)·(L', s') = (L ⊗ L', s ⊗ s'). The map is (L, s) ↦ div(L, s) = Σ_x m_x[x], m_x the order of vanishing (or minus the order of the pole) of s at x, and D ↦ (O_X(D), 1) is its inverse.
items.locator: §5.1 after Définition 5.1.2, p. 202, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated 'comme d'habitude'. Tau Ceti has a Weil-to-Cartier homomorphism into Cartier divisors as sections of K_X^×/O_X^× (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.toCartierDivisorHom) with an order map back (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CartierDivisor.orderAt), and the sheaf O_X(D), but not the (L, s) formulation or this bijection. The JacobianChallenge Layer A stage plans 'Cartier ≃ line bundles' and 'Weil ≃ Cartier' only for smooth curves over a field (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-a-line-bundles-divisors-picard-group-degree).

items.name: Principal divisor map div : E(X)^× → Div(X)
items.statement: For f ∈ E(X)^×, div(f) = Σ_{x∈|X|} ord_x(f)[x] ∈ Div(X); this defines a group homomorphism div : E(X)^× → Div(X).
items.locator: §5.1, pp. 202–203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: OrderSystem.ofScheme X assembles the orders at codimension-one points of a Noetherian integral scheme (with the finite-support theorem); principalHom is the resulting homomorphism Additive E(X)^× →+ WeilDivisor. The text's formula 'div(f) = div(O_X.f, 1)' has a sign slip (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Divisor exact sequence 0 → Γ(X,O_X)^× → E(X)^× → Div(X) → Pic(X) → 0
items.statement: For a curve X there is the usual exact sequence 0 → Γ(X, O_X)^× → E(X)^× --div--> Div(X) → Pic(X) → 0, the last map being D ↦ [O_X(D)].
items.locator: §5.1, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Tau Ceti has pieces: the kernel of div as an abstract subgroup (WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.principalKernel, not identified with global units) and injectivity of Cl(X) → {line-bundle classes} (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.classGroupToLineBundleClass_injective); surjectivity onto Pic is explicitly not yet done. The JacobianChallenge Layer A stage plans Cl(X) ≅ Pic X for curves over a field only.

items.name: Définition 5.1.3: complete curve (courbe complète)
items.statement: A complete curve is a curve X such that deg(div(f)) = 0 for every f ∈ E(X)^×.
items.locator: Définition 5.1.3, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: IsWeightedDegreeZero w holds for an order system S when weightedDegree w (S.principalDivisor g) = 0 for all g; applied to OrderSystem.ofScheme X with w = deg it is exactly Définition 5.1.3. The underlying curve structure (Définition 5.1.1) is not bundled.

items.name: Exemple 5.1.4: smooth projective curves over a field are complete curves
items.statement: If k is a field and X a smooth projective connected curve over k in the usual sense, then setting deg(x) = [k(x) : k] for x ∈ |X| makes X a complete curve in the sense of Définition 5.1.3.
items.locator: Exemple 5.1.4, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: AlgebraicCurves Layer 3 plans the product formula deg(div f) = 0 for function fields (Stichtenoth Thm 1.4.11); Layer 12 plans the function-field/curve dictionary. Stage text only; no packet node.

items.name: Degree map deg : Pic(X) → ℤ on a complete curve
items.statement: If X is a complete curve, the degree of divisors induces a degree function deg : Pic(X) → ℤ.
items.locator: §5.1 after Exemple 5.1.4, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Tau Ceti descends the weighted degree to the divisor class group Cl(X) under IsWeightedDegreeZero (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.weightedDegreeClass), but Cl(X) → Pic(X) is only known injective, so the degree on Pic(X) itself is not available.

items.name: Lemme 5.1.5: global functions on a complete curve form an algebraically closed subfield
items.statement: If X is a complete curve, Γ(X, O_X) is a subfield of E(X), algebraically closed in E(X).
items.locator: Lemme 5.1.5, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof: f ∈ Γ(X,O_X) ⇔ div f ≥ 0 ⇔ div f = 0 for f ≠ 0, and valuations trivial on E are trivial on its algebraic closure in E(X). Not in the library; AlgebraicCurves Layer 0/3 plan the analogous constant-field statements for function fields over k only.

items.name: Définition 5.1.6: field of definition of a complete curve
items.statement: If X is a complete curve, its field of definition is the field Γ(X, O_X).
items.locator: Définition 5.1.6, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Depends on Lemme 5.1.5 for the field structure; the global-sections ring is Mathlib's Γ(X, ⊤) but the notion is not packaged.

items.name: Exemple 5.1.7: field of definition of a smooth projective curve
items.statement: In the situation of Exemple 5.1.4, the field of definition of X in the sense of Définition 5.1.6 is the algebraic closure of k in k(X).
items.locator: Exemple 5.1.7, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: AlgebraicCurves Layer 0 fixes the constant field k̃ = algebraicClosure k F; Layer 12 plans H⁰(X, O_X(D)) ≅ L(D), which with L(0) = k̃ (Layer 3) gives the statement. Stage text only.

items.name: Euclidean stathme (recalled, §5.2.1)
items.statement: A Euclidean stathme on a ring B is a function deg : B → ℕ ∪ {−∞} such that (1) deg(a) = −∞ if and only if a = 0, and (2) for a, b ∈ B ∖ {0}, deg(a) ≤ deg(ab).
items.locator: §5.2.1, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest mathlib:EuclideanDomain, which uses a well-founded relation r with r (a % b) b and ¬ r (a*b) a instead of an ℕ ∪ {−∞}-valued stathme; the notions do not coincide.

items.name: Euclidean ring (recalled, §5.2.1)
items.statement: A Euclidean ring is an integral domain B with a Euclidean stathme deg such that for all x, y ∈ B with y ≠ 0 there exist a, b ∈ B with x = ay + b and deg(b) < deg(y).
items.locator: §5.2.1, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Every such ring is a mathlib:EuclideanDomain (take r = (deg · < deg ·)), but Mathlib's class is more general (arbitrary well-founded relation), so it does not match the definition.

items.name: In a Euclidean ring, elements of degree 0 are units
items.statement: In a Euclidean ring (B, deg), every element of degree 0 is invertible.
items.locator: §5.2.1, p. 203, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated as a remark ('Remarquons').

items.name: Définition 5.2.1: almost Euclidean ring (anneau presque euclidien)
items.statement: An almost Euclidean ring is an integral domain B with a Euclidean stathme deg such that (1) every element of degree 0 in B is invertible, and (2) for all x, y ∈ B with deg(y) ≥ 1 there exist a, b ∈ B with x = ay + b and deg(b) ≤ deg(y).
items.locator: Définition 5.2.1, p. 204, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No Mathlib/Tau Ceti analogue; not in any atlas stage or node.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.2: principality criterion for almost Euclidean rings
items.statement: Let (B, deg) be an almost Euclidean ring whose stathme is multiplicative, deg(ab) = deg(a) + deg(b). Then B is principal if and only if for all x, y ∈ B ∖ {0} of the same degree there exist a, b ∈ B such that either −∞ ≠ deg(ax + by) < deg(x), or ax + by = 0 and b ∈ B^×.
items.locator: Proposition 5.2.2, p. 204, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The text notes it is not used later.

items.name: Exemple 5.2.3 (a): B_{F,E}[1/t]^{φ=Id} is a principal ideal domain
items.statement: With the notations of the preceding chapters, assume F algebraically closed. Let t ∈ B_{F,E}^{φ=π} and y ∈ |Y_F| with t(y) = 0. Then the ring B_{F,E}[1/t]^{φ=Id} ⊂ B_{dR,y} is principal (proved in Chapter 6).
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.3, p. 204; Introduction, p. 201, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Forward reference to Chapter 6. B_{F,E}[1/t]^{φ=Id} = Γ(X ∖ {∞}, O_X); planned for the FS normalization as 'X_C^alg ∖ {x} is the spectrum of a PID' in node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains.

items.name: Exemple 5.2.3 (b): B_{F,E}[1/t]^{φ=Id} with −ord_y is almost Euclidean
items.statement: In the situation of Exemple 5.2.3 (F algebraically closed, t ∈ B_{F,E}^{φ=π}, y ∈ |Y_F| with t(y) = 0), the ring B_{F,E}[1/t]^{φ=Id} ⊂ B_{dR,y} with the stathme −ord_y is almost Euclidean (proved in Chapter 6).
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.3, p. 204; Introduction, p. 201, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node or stage mentions (almost) Euclidean structure of B^{φ=1}[1/t]; the PID property is planned (previous item).

items.name: Lemme 5.2.4: DVRs meeting B in a field ↔ valuations negative on B
items.statement: Let B be an integral domain with fraction field K. The following data are equivalent: (i) a discrete valuation subring A ⊂ K such that A ∩ B is a field; (ii) a valuation ord_∞ : K → ℤ ∪ {+∞} with ord_∞(K^×) = ℤ such that ord_∞(b) ≤ 0 for all b ∈ B ∖ {0}, and ord_∞(b) = 0 implies b ∈ B^×.
items.locator: Lemme 5.2.4, p. 204, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed proof breaks off after 'Démonstration. — Si' (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Degree filtration on B attached to a valuation at infinity (§5.2.2)
items.statement: Given the data of Lemme 5.2.4, let F = B ∩ A; then B^× = F^×. Set deg = −ord_∞|_B : B → ℕ ∪ {−∞}, a Euclidean stathme, and Fil_i B = {b ∈ B | deg(b) ≤ i} (i ∈ ℤ), an increasing filtration with Fil_0 B = F and Fil_i B = 0 for i < 0. The standing hypothesis is: for every i ≥ 1 the map Fil_i B / Fil_{i−1} B → m_A^{−i}/m_A^{−i+1} is surjective, m_A being the maximal ideal of A.
items.locator: §5.2.2, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.2.5: surjectivity on graded pieces implies almost Euclidean
items.statement: Under the hypothesis of §5.2.2 (for B an integral domain with fraction field K and ord_∞ as in Lemme 5.2.4, the maps Fil_i B/Fil_{i−1} B → m_A^{−i}/m_A^{−i+1} are surjective for all i ≥ 1), the pair (B, deg) is almost Euclidean.
items.locator: Proposition 5.2.5, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The proof contains an exponent misprint (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Affine curve Spec(B) of a principal B with degree
items.statement: If moreover B is principal, X = Spec(B) with deg(x) = deg(f) for a closed point x and f ∈ B an irreducible element associated to x is a curve (to be compactified by adding the valuation v_∞ with deg(∞) = 1).
items.locator: §5.2.2 after Proposition 5.2.5, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Exemple 5.2.6 (a): degree filtration on B_e = B_cris^{φ=1} and its graded pieces
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field extension of ℚ_p with perfect residue field, K̄ an algebraic closure, C = the completion of K̄, B_cris = B_cris^+[1/t] and B_e = B_cris^{φ=Id}, with the valuation v_∞ induced by B_e ⊂ B_cris ⊂ B_dR. Then Fil_i B_e = B_e ∩ Fil^{−i} B_cris, Fil_0 B_e = ℚ_p, and for every i ≥ 1, Fil_i B_e / Fil_{i−1} B_e ≅ t^{−i}B_dR^+/t^{−i+1}B_dR^+ = C(−i).
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.6, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequence of the fundamental exact sequence, planned as node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence ((Fil^0 B_cris)^{φ=1} = ℚ_p and B_e → B_dR/B_dR^+ surjective).

items.name: Exemple 5.2.6 (b): (B_e, deg) is almost Euclidean
items.statement: In the situation of Exemple 5.2.6, the pair (B_e, deg) is almost Euclidean.
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.6, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Follows from (a) and Proposition 5.2.5; no atlas node.

items.name: Exemple 5.2.6 (c): B_e is principal, with irreducibles exactly the degree-one elements
items.statement: In the situation of Exemple 5.2.6, B_e is a principal ideal domain and its irreducible elements are the elements of degree 1 (announced; proved later).
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.6, p. 205, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Forward claim. Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) plans the PID property of X_C^alg ∖ {x} and the bijection classical points ↔ closed points; the degree-one statement for irreducibles is not stated as such.

items.name: External: Fontaine's fundamental exact sequence ([25], th. 5.3.7)
items.statement: (Used as a black box.) 0 → ℚ_p → B_cris^{φ=1} → B_dR/B_dR^+ → 0 is exact; equivalently (Fil^0 B_cris)^{φ=1} = ℚ_p and B_cris^{φ=1} → B_dR/B_dR^+ is surjective.
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.6, p. 205 (citing [25], th. 5.3.7), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence.

items.name: Théorème 5.2.7 (a): each hyperplane section is a single point
items.statement: Let P = ⊕_{i≥0} P_i be a graded integral domain with P_0 = F a field and dim_F P_1 ≥ 2, and X = Proj(P). Assume (1) the multiplicative monoid ∪_{d≥1}(P_d ∖ {0})/F^× is free on the elements of (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^×, and (2) for every t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0} there is a field extension C of F with P/Pt ≅ {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F} as graded F-algebras. Then for every t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0}, the vanishing locus V^+(t) of the hyperplane section t consists of a single point ∞_t.
items.locator: Théorème 5.2.7 (a), p. 206, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. The FF-curve instance (P = ⊕ H^0(X, O(n))) is handled differently in the atlas: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map constructs Proj P and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) proves regularity, dimension 1 and PID complements. mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj exists but nothing about this situation.

items.name: Théorème 5.2.7 (b): closed points ↔ (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^×
items.statement: Let P = ⊕_{i≥0} P_i be a graded integral domain with P_0 = F a field and dim_F P_1 ≥ 2, and X = Proj(P). Assume (1) the multiplicative monoid ∪_{d≥1}(P_d ∖ {0})/F^× is free on the elements of (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^×, and (2) for every t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0} there is a field extension C of F with P/Pt ≅ {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F} as graded F-algebras. Then t ↦ ∞_t induces a bijection (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^× ≅ |X|, |X| the set of closed points of X.
items.locator: Théorème 5.2.7 (b), p. 206, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. The FF-curve instance (P = ⊕ H^0(X, O(n))) is handled differently in the atlas: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map constructs Proj P and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) proves regularity, dimension 1 and PID complements. mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj exists but nothing about this situation. (b) is not argued separately in the proof.

items.name: Théorème 5.2.7 (c): Proj(P) with deg ≡ 1 is a complete curve
items.statement: Let P = ⊕_{i≥0} P_i be a graded integral domain with P_0 = F a field and dim_F P_1 ≥ 2, and X = Proj(P). Assume (1) the multiplicative monoid ∪_{d≥1}(P_d ∖ {0})/F^× is free on the elements of (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^×, and (2) for every t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0} there is a field extension C of F with P/Pt ≅ {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F} as graded F-algebras. Then X, with deg(x) = 1 for every closed point x, is a complete curve.
items.locator: Théorème 5.2.7 (c), p. 206, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. The FF-curve instance (P = ⊕ H^0(X, O(n))) is handled differently in the atlas: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map constructs Proj P and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) proves regularity, dimension 1 and PID complements. mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj exists but nothing about this situation. (c) is not argued separately in the proof.

items.name: Théorème 5.2.7 (d): complements of closed points are spectra of almost Euclidean PIDs
items.statement: Let P = ⊕_{i≥0} P_i be a graded integral domain with P_0 = F a field and dim_F P_1 ≥ 2, and X = Proj(P). Assume (1) the multiplicative monoid ∪_{d≥1}(P_d ∖ {0})/F^× is free on the elements of (P_1 ∖ {0})/F^×, and (2) for every t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0} there is a field extension C of F with P/Pt ≅ {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F} as graded F-algebras. Then for every closed point ∞ ∈ X, X ∖ {∞} is an affine open Spec(B) with B principal (i.e. Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0), and (B, −v_∞) is almost Euclidean.
items.locator: Théorème 5.2.7 (d), pp. 206–208, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. The FF-curve instance (P = ⊕ H^0(X, O(n))) is handled differently in the atlas: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map constructs Proj P and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9) proves regularity, dimension 1 and PID complements. mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj exists but nothing about this situation.

items.name: Lemme 5.2.8: Proj of {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F} is a point
items.statement: Let C|F be a field extension and D = {f ∈ C[T] | f(0) ∈ F}, a graded F-algebra. Then Proj(D) consists of a single point, the zero homogeneous prime ideal.
items.locator: Lemme 5.2.8, p. 208, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj provides Proj but not this computation. The proof's case split is incomplete (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Exemple 5.2.9: the graded algebra ⊕_d (B_cris^+)^{φ^h=p^d} satisfies Théorème 5.2.7
items.statement: With the notations of Exemple 5.2.6 and an integer h ≥ 1, the graded algebra ⊕_{d≥0}(B_cris^+)^{φ^h = p^d} satisfies the hypotheses of Théorème 5.2.7 (announced; proved later).
items.locator: Exemple 5.2.9, p. 208, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Forward claim. The atlas builds Proj of the graded algebra of sections (node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map) and plans its geometric properties via FS II.2.9 (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point), not via hypotheses (1)–(2) of Théorème 5.2.7.

items.name: Category Fib_X of vector bundles on a curve
items.statement: For a curve X, Fib_X is the category of locally free O_X-modules of finite rank on X (vector bundles).
items.locator: §5.3, p. 208, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned for every scheme by node KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/vector-bundle (isVectorBundle X on X.Modules via Mathlib's SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData with IsLocallyFreeData and IsFiniteType; Vect(X) its full subcategory), and on the FF curve by the VB1 stage 'Define bundles as finite locally free O_X modules on the existing curve'. Tau Ceti has only the rank-one case (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf).

items.name: Proposition 5.3.1 (i): gluing bundles from U and the local rings O_{X,x_i}
items.statement: Let X be a curve with field of rational functions K, U ⊊ X a non-empty open with X ∖ U = {x_1,…,x_r}. Let C be the category of triples (E, (M_i)_{1≤i≤r}, (u_i)_{1≤i≤r}) with E ∈ Fib_U, M_i a free O_{X,x_i}-module of finite rank and u_i : M_i ⊗_{O_{X,x_i}} K ≅ E_η. Then E ↦ (E|_U, (E_{x_i})_i, (can_i)_i) is an equivalence of categories Fib_X → C.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3.1, p. 209, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof ('ne pose pas de problème'). Not planned: the atlas plans only the formal-completion version (next item).

items.name: Proposition 5.3.1 (ii): Beauville–Laszlo gluing along the formal discs
items.statement: With X, U, x_1,…,x_r as above, let Ĉ be the category of triples (E, (M_i), (u_i)) with E ∈ Fib_U, M_i a free Ô_{X,x_i}-module of finite rank and u_i : M_i ⊗_{Ô_{X,x_i}} K̂_{x_i} ≅ E_η ⊗_K K̂_{x_i}. Then E ↦ (E|_U, (Ê_{x_i})_i, (can_i)_i) is an equivalence of categories Fib_X → Ĉ.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3.1, p. 209 (citing [3]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box [3] (Beauville–Laszlo). Planned as node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/beauville-laszlo-module-gluing (BL for modules over a ring with a nonzerodivisor f), used there along Cartier divisors of the relative curve.

items.name: Corollaire 5.3.2 (i): bundles on X as triples (M, (N_i), (u_i)) with completions
items.statement: Suppose U affine with Pic(U) trivial, and let B = Γ(U, O_X). Then the category of vector bundles on X is equivalent to that of triples (M, (N_i)_{1≤i≤r}, (u_i)_{1≤i≤r}) where M is a free B-module of finite rank, each N_i is a free Ô_{X,x_i}-module of finite rank, and u_i : M ⊗_B K̂_{x_i} ≅ N_i ⊗_{Ô_{X,x_i}} K̂_{x_i}.
items.locator: Corollaire 5.3.2, p. 209, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Printed with a single N although one module per x_i is meant (see sourceIssues). Follows from BL gluing (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/beauville-laszlo-module-gluing) plus freeness of projective modules over B when Pic(U) = 0.

items.name: Corollaire 5.3.2 (ii): the same with the local rings O_{X,x_i} and K
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollaire 5.3.2, the same equivalence holds with K̂_{x_i} replaced by K and Ô_{X,x_i} by O_{X,x_i}.
items.locator: Corollaire 5.3.2, p. 209, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Corollaire 5.3.2 (iii): rank-n bundles as a double coset space
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollaire 5.3.2, isomorphism classes of rank-n vector bundles on X are identified with GL_n(B) \ Π_{i=1}^r GL_n(K̂_{x_i}) / GL_n(Ô_{X,x_i}).
items.locator: Corollaire 5.3.2, p. 209, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor plans the related BL description of the affine Grassmannian, not this double coset.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.3: cohomology of a bundle from its gluing data
items.statement: Suppose U affine, Pic(U) = 0 and X ∖ U = {∞}. Let E be a vector bundle on X with data (M, N, u), resp. (M, N̂, û), i.e. M = Γ(U, E), N = E_∞, N̂ = Ê_∞. Then canonically H^0(X, E) = u(M) ∩ N = û(M) ∩ N̂ and H^1(X, E) = N ⊗ K/(u(M) + N) = N ⊗ K̂_∞/(û(M) + N̂). More generally RΓ(X, E) is isomorphic to the complex M ⊕ N → N ⊗ K, (x, y) ↦ u(x) − y, or to the same complex with N, K, u replaced by N̂, K̂_∞, û.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3.3, p. 209, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated as 'on vérifie aisément'.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.4: twisting by k·∞ in terms of gluing data
items.statement: For k ∈ ℤ and t_∞ a uniformizer of O_{X,∞}, if E corresponds to (M, N, u), resp. (M, N̂, û), then E(k∞) corresponds to (M, t_∞^{−k}N, u), resp. (M, t_∞^{−k}N̂, û).
items.locator: Proposition 5.3.4, p. 210, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Lemme 5.4.1: Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0 ⇔ deg : Pic(X) ≅ ℤ
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve with a point ∞ such that deg(∞) = 1 and X ∖ {∞} is affine. The following are equivalent: Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0; the degree function induces an isomorphism deg : Pic(X) ≅ ℤ.
items.locator: Lemme 5.4.1, p. 210, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated as 'on vérifie aussitôt'.

items.name: Sections of O_X(k) and the degree filtration of B (§5.4)
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve with ∞ of degree 1, X ∖ {∞} = Spec(B) affine with Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0, O_X(k) = O_X(k·∞) and deg = −ord_∞ : B → ℕ ∪ {−∞}. Multiplication by the canonical section of O_X(1) gives injections F = H^0(O_X) ⊂ H^0(O_X(1)) ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ H^0(O_X(k)) ⊂ ⋯ which correspond to the degree filtration F = B^{deg≤0} ⊂ B^{deg≤1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ B^{deg≤k} ⊂ ⋯ of B; moreover H^0(O_X(k)) = 0 for k < 0.
items.locator: §5.4, p. 210, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Abstract statement not planned; for the FF curve the VB1 stage plans 'Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology'.

items.name: Surjections H^1(O_X(k)) ↠ H^1(O_X(k+1)) and propagation of vanishing
items.statement: In the situation of §5.4, for k ∈ ℤ cup-product with the section of O_X(1) induces a surjection H^1(X, O_X(k)) ↠ H^1(X, O_X(k+1)); with A = O_{X,∞} with uniformizer t and K the function field, it is the canonical surjection K/(B + t^{−k}A) → K/(B + t^{−k−1}A). Hence if H^1(X, O_X(d)) = 0 then H^1(X, O_X(k)) = 0 for all k ≥ d.
items.locator: §5.4, p. 210, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: H^1(X, O_X) = 0 implies the surjectivity hypothesis of §5.2.2
items.statement: In the situation of §5.4, with i : {∞} ↪ X, for every k ∈ ℤ there is an exact sequence 0 → O_X(k−1) → O_X(k) → i_*(m_A^{−k}/m_A^{−k+1}) → 0; consequently, if H^1(X, O_X) = 0 then for every k ≥ 1 the map B^{deg≤k}/B^{deg≤k−1} → m_A^{−k}/m_A^{−k+1} is surjective, i.e. the condition of §5.2.2 holds.
items.locator: §5.4, pp. 210–211, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Printed with B^{deg≥k} for B^{deg≤k} (see sourceIssues).

items.name: For X = Proj(P) as in Théorème 5.2.7: P_k = H^0(X, O_X(k))
items.statement: When X = Proj(P) as in Théorème 5.2.7, t ∈ P_1 is distinguished and V^+(t) = {∞}, there are identifications for k ∈ ℕ, P_k = B^{deg≤k} = H^0(X, O_X(k)), b ↦ b/t^k; hence X = Proj(⊕_{d∈ℕ} Γ(X, O_X(d))), the inclusions above are given by multiplication by t ∈ H^0(O_X(1)), and O_X(d) ≅ P̃[d] for every d ∈ ℤ.
items.locator: §5.4, p. 211, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For the FF curve the atlas takes X^alg := Proj(⊕ H^0(X, O(n))) as the definition (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map, VB2:ampleness GAGA), not this abstract statement.

items.name: Proposition 5.4.2 (1): Euclidean ⇔ H^1(X, O_X(−1)) = 0
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} = Spec(B) is affine and Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0, and deg = −ord_∞ on B. Then (B, deg) is Euclidean if and only if H^1(X, O_X(−1)) = 0; if so, H^1(X, O_X(k)) = 0 for all k ≥ −1.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4.2 (1), p. 211, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via H^1(X, O_X(−1)) = K/(B + tA).

items.name: Proposition 5.4.2 (2): almost Euclidean ⇔ H^1(X, O_X) = 0
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} = Spec(B) is affine and Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0, and deg = −ord_∞ on B. Then (B, deg) is almost Euclidean if and only if H^1(X, O_X) = 0; if so, H^1(X, O_X(k)) = 0 for all k ≥ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4.2 (2), p. 211, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via H^1(X, O_X) = K/(B + A).

items.name: Exemple 5.4.3: the curve Proj ⊕(B_cris^+)^{φ^h=p^d} has H^1(O) = 0 but H^1(O(−1)) ≠ 0
items.statement: With the notations of Exemple 5.2.9, X = Proj(⊕_{d≥0}(B_cris^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) satisfies the hypotheses of point (2) of Proposition 5.4.2 but not those of point (1): H^1(X, O_X) = 0 (B almost Euclidean) while H^1(X, O_X(−1)) ≠ 0 (B not Euclidean) (announced; proved later).
items.locator: Exemple 5.4.3, p. 211; Introduction, p. 201, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Forward claim. The cohomology of O(n) on the FF curve is planned in the VB1 stage ('Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology') and node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5: H^1 of slope-0 and negative-slope Banach–Colmez spaces). The (almost) Euclidean reformulation is not planned.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan setting (§5.5.1): exact category with degree, rank and generic fibre
items.statement: An HN category is an exact category C with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ, defined on isomorphism classes and additive on exact sequences of C, together with an abelian category A and a functor F : C → A such that: F is exact and faithful; F induces a bijection {strict subobjects of X} ≅ {subobjects of F(X)} (strict = fitting in an exact sequence); rg = rg_A ∘ F for an additive function rg_A : A → ℕ with rg_A(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and (crucial hypothesis) if u : X → X' in C is such that F(u) is an isomorphism then deg(X) ≤ deg(X'), with equality if and only if u is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §5.5.1, p. 212 (after [19], [2]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: HN categories are quasi-abelian; kernels, images, cokernels (after André [2])
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. Then C is quasi-abelian in the sense of André: every morphism u : X → Y has a kernel and a cokernel; ker u is the unique strict subobject X' of X with F(X') = ker F(u), Im u is the unique strict subobject of Y with F(Im u) = Im F(u), and coker u = Y/Im u. The natural map X/ker u → Im u is an isomorphism after applying F, and it is an isomorphism if and only if deg(X/ker u) = deg(Im u).
items.locator: §5.5.1, pp. 212–213 (citing [2]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box [2] (André, Slope filtrations). The text prints 'sous-objet strict X'' de X' and 'coker u = X/Im(u)' (should be Y; see sourceIssues). Not stated in any atlas node.

items.name: Slope µ = deg/rg
items.statement: For X ∈ C, X ≠ 0, µ(X) = deg(X)/rg(X) ∈ ℝ.
items.locator: §5.5.1, p. 213, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: Définition 5.5.1: semistable object
items.statement: A nonzero object X of C is semistable if µ(X') ≤ µ(X) for every nonzero strict subobject X' of X.
items.locator: Définition 5.5.1, p. 213, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: Théorème 5.5.2: existence and uniqueness of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. Then every object X of C has a unique filtration in the exact category C, 0 = X_0 ⊊ X_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ X_r = X, such that X_i/X_{i−1} is semistable for 1 ≤ i ≤ r and the sequence of slopes (µ(X_i/X_{i−1}))_{1≤i≤r} is strictly decreasing.
items.locator: Théorème 5.5.2, p. 213 (citing [33], [2]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin'). Proof by the Harder–Narasimhan argument [33]; details referred to [2]. The σ-module analogue over the Robba ring is node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan polygon HN(X)
items.statement: For X ∈ C with HN filtration (X_i), HN(X) is the unique concave polygon with origin (0, 0) whose slopes are the µ(X_i/X_{i−1}), 1 ≤ i ≤ r, with respective multiplicities rg(X_i/X_{i−1}).
items.locator: §5.5.1 after Théorème 5.5.2, p. 213, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles (VB1 node degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism; polygon used in node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon). See the atlas gap 'Harder-Narasimhan sign/dominance convention is not pinned across sources' in the VB0 packet and the VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals decomposition.

items.name: Théorème 5.5.3: strict subobjects lie below the HN polygon; HN(X) is a concave envelope
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. If X' ⊂ X is a strict subobject, the point (rg(X'), deg(X')) lies below the polygon HN(X). Consequently HN(X) is the concave envelope of the points (rg(X'), deg(X')) as X' ranges over the strict subobjects of X.
items.locator: Théorème 5.5.3, p. 213, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Printed with the coordinates (deg(X'), rg(X')), which is inconsistent with the definition of HN(X) (abscissa = rank); see sourceIssues. The sentence is quoted as a source excerpt under node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism and discussed in the HN-convention gap, but no node statement contains it. The σ-module analogue ('the HN polygon lies above the polygon of any semistable filtration') is in node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration.

items.name: Subcategories C^{≤λ}, C_{≥λ} and C^ss_λ
items.statement: For λ ∈ ℝ: C^{≤λ} is the full subcategory of objects whose largest HN slope is ≤ λ (equivalently µ(Y) ≤ λ for every nonzero strict subobject Y); C_{≥λ} is the full subcategory of objects whose smallest HN slope is ≥ λ (equivalently µ(Y) ≥ λ for every strict epimorphism X ↠ Y with Y ≠ 0); C^ss_λ = C^{≤λ} ∩ C_{≥λ} is the full subcategory of semistable objects of slope λ together with 0.
items.locator: §5.5.1, p. 213, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: Théorème 5.5.4 (1): C^{≤λ} and C_{≥λ} are exact and stable under extensions
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. For every λ ∈ ℝ, the categories C^{≤λ} and C_{≥λ} are exact subcategories of C stable under extensions.
items.locator: Théorème 5.5.4 (1), p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The VB0 packet read Thm 5.5.4(1)–(3), but node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states only (2) and (3).

items.name: Théorème 5.5.4 (2): Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0 for λ > µ
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. If λ > µ then Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0; in particular, if X is semistable of slope λ, Y semistable of slope µ and λ > µ, then Hom(X, Y) = 0.
items.locator: Théorème 5.5.4 (2), p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: Théorème 5.5.4 (3): C^ss_λ is abelian and stable under extensions
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. For every λ ∈ ℝ, C^ss_λ = C^{≤λ} ∩ C_{≥λ} is an abelian category, stable under extensions in C.
items.locator: Théorème 5.5.4 (3), p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 5.5.5: stable object
items.statement: An object X ∈ C is stable if µ(X') < µ(X) for every nonzero strict subobject X' of X with X' ≠ X.
items.locator: Définition 5.5.5, p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: no layer plans the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5.1 (exact category, rank, degree, generic-fibre functor); only its instance for bundles on X_C is planned. The condition X' ≠ X is missing in the printed definition (see sourceIssues); the VB1 node states it correctly ('stable means strict inequality' for proper nonzero subbundles). Planned for bundles on X_C: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism states that 'the Harder-Narasimhan axiomatics of Fargues-Fontaine 5.5.1 apply' and lists the consequences (semistable, stable, Hom(C_{≥λ}, C^{≤µ}) = 0, C^ss_λ abelian and extension-stable, finite length, simple = stable, unique HN filtration). No abstract exact-category formalism node; nothing at the pins (the VB0 packet gap 'Nothing in the Harder-Narasimhan half of VB1 exists at either pin').

items.name: Proposition 5.5.6: C^ss_λ has finite length; its simple objects are the stable objects
items.statement: Let C be an exact category with functions deg : Ob C → ℝ and rg : Ob C → ℕ on isomorphism classes, additive on exact sequences, and an abelian category A with an exact faithful 'generic fibre' functor F : C → A inducing, for every X, a bijection between strict subobjects of X and subobjects of F(X); rg factors through an additive rg : A → ℕ with rg(Y) = 0 ⇔ Y = 0; and for every morphism u : X → X' of C with F(u) an isomorphism, deg(X) ≤ deg(X') with equality iff u is an isomorphism. Let λ ∈ ℝ. Every object of the abelian category C^ss_λ has finite length, and the simple objects of C^ss_λ are the stable objects of slope λ.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5.6, p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.1: vector bundles on a complete curve form an HN category
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve defined over F (field of definition), C the category of locally free O_X-modules of finite rank with rank and degree, A the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces over the function field, and the generic-fibre functor C → A. These satisfy the axioms of §5.5.1; in particular, if u : E → E' is an isomorphism on generic fibres then deg(E') = deg(E) + deg(E'/u(E)), where a coherent torsion sheaf F has degree deg(F) = Σ_{x∈|X|} deg(x)·length_{O_{X,x}}(F_x). Hence vector bundles on X have HN filtrations.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.1, p. 214, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary complete curve over its field of definition); only the instance X = X_C is planned. Planned for X_C: VB1 stage ('Build degree, rank, slope, saturated subbundles and semistability, including exact-sequence degree additivity and the behavior of torsion quotients') and node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism. Abstract complete curves not planned.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.2: filtered vector spaces form an HN category
items.statement: Let L|K be a field extension and VectFil_{L/K} the exact category of pairs (V, Fil^•V_L) with V a finite-dimensional K-vector space and Fil^•V_L a decreasing filtration of V ⊗_K L with Fil^iV_L = 0 for i ≫ 0 and Fil^iV_L = V_L for i ≪ 0; set rg = dim_K V and deg = Σ_{i∈ℤ} i·dim_L gr^iV_L. Then the forgetful functor to Vect_K satisfies the axioms of §5.5.1, by the formula deg = n·dim Fil^nV_L + Σ_{i>n} dim Fil^iV_L (n ≪ 0), which gives deg(V', Fil^•V'_L) = deg(V, Fil^•V_L) + Σ_{i∈ℤ} dim Fil^iV'_L/u(Fil^iV_L) when u : V ≅ V'.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.2, pp. 214–215, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 plans filtered vector spaces and t_H (nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-vector-spaces, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/hodge-number-tH) but not their HN structure. Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/hodge-number-tH does record the HN axioms in the case L = K: t_H is additive on short exact sequences, and 'if h: D' → D is a bijective morphism then t_H(D') ≤ t_H(D), with equality iff h is an isomorphism in Fil_F'.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.2 consequence: morphisms between semistable filtered spaces of equal slope are strict
items.statement: In VectFil_{L/K}, every morphism between semistable objects of the same slope is strictly compatible with the filtrations (Théorème 5.5.4 applied to Exemple 5.5.2.2).
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.2, p. 215, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest planned: strictness of morphisms of weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-modules, node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weakly-admissible-category-abelian.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.3: HN filtration of isocrystals = Dieudonné–Manin (slope) filtration
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, K_0 = W(k)[1/p] with Frobenius σ, and φ-Mod_{K_0} the abelian ℚ_p-linear category of k-isocrystals (D, φ) (D finite-dimensional over K_0, φ a σ-linear bijection). With rank ht(D, φ) = dim_{K_0} D and degree t_N(D, φ) = v_p(a) where det(D, φ) = K_0·e, φ(e) = a·e, the axioms of §5.5.1 hold; the associated HN filtration is the Dieudonné–Manin filtration and the (concave) HN polygon is obtained from the (convex) Newton polygon by reversing the order of slopes. This filtration is canonically split: the HN filtration for (ht, −t_N) is opposite to it, and the pair of opposite filtrations gives the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.3, p. 215, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing as stated (k perfect): the Dieudonné–Manin/HN nodes of RD.1 assume an algebraically closed residue field, and the HN formalism of §5.5.1 is not planned abstractly. The canonical slope decomposition over K_0 = W(k)[1/p] with k perfect is node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/slope-decomposition. Nodes PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-slopes-are-hn-slopes (over W(ℓ,O)[π^{-1}] with v_ℓ trivial the slope decomposition is canonical and gives the HN filtration) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block. Printed 'ht(D, φ) = dim_{K_0} N' (see sourceIssues).

items.name: External: Dieudonné–Manin classification of isocrystals
items.statement: (Used as a black box.) For k perfect of characteristic p, every k-isocrystal over K_0 = W(k)[1/p] has a canonical decomposition into isoclinic parts (Dieudonné–Manin decomposition), so its slope filtration is canonically split.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.3, p. 215, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib classifies only one-dimensional isocrystals over algebraically closed k (WittVector.isocrystal_classification, Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Isocrystal.lean), so the library entry is partial. The canonical isoclinic decomposition for k perfect is node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/slope-decomposition. The classification over an algebraically closed residue field is planned in VB0 (stage text) and node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical; the VB0 packet gap 'Dieudonne-Manin is quoted, never proved, in anything read' applies.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.4: filtered φ-modules; semistable of slope 0 = weakly admissible
items.statement: Let K|K_0 be a field extension and φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} the exact category of triples (D, φ, Fil^•D_K) with (D, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0} and Fil^•D_K a decreasing exhaustive separated filtration of D ⊗_{K_0} K, exact sequences being exact sequences of isocrystals strictly compatible with the filtrations. With t_H(D, φ, Fil^•) = deg(D, Fil^•D_K) (Exemple 5.5.2.2), rank ht and degree t_H − t_N, the functor forgetting the filtration is a generic-fibre functor, so HN filtrations exist, and the abelian category of semistable objects of slope 0 is the category of weakly admissible filtered φ-modules.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.4, p. 216, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing as stated: R06.2 plans weak admissibility only over a p-adic field K (K/K_0 finite) and not the HN structure of φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} for an arbitrary field extension K|K_0; the abstract HN formalism is not planned. Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility (t_H(D) = t_N(D) and t_H(D') ≤ t_N(D') for subobjects) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weakly-admissible-category-abelian; the HN-category packaging itself is not planned. The reference for weak admissibility is printed '[?]' (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.4 (bis): HN bi-filtrations for the degree (t_H − t_N, −t_N) ∈ ℤ²
items.statement: The HN formalism extends to degree functions valued in a totally ordered abelian group; for φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} with rank ht and degree (t_H − t_N, −t_N) : φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} → ℤ² (lexicographic order) one obtains the Harder–Narasimhan bi-filtrations studied in [23].
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.4, p. 216 (citing [23]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box [23].

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.5: φ-modules over a Bézout ring (Robba ring) form an HN category
items.statement: Let R be a Bézout ring (integral domain in which every finitely generated ideal is principal), E ⊂ R a subfield with a non-trivial valuation v : E → ℤ ∪ {+∞} and E^× = R^×, and σ an endomorphism of R stabilizing E with v(σ(x)) = v(x) for x ∈ E. Let C be the exact category of pairs (M, φ), M a free R-module of finite rank and φ a σ-linear endomorphism whose linearization Φ : σ^*M → M is an isomorphism. Then Pic(C) ≅ H^1(σ^ℤ, E^×) (the cocycle c_σ ↦ (R, x ↦ c_σσ(x))), deg : Pic(C) → ℤ, [c_σ] ↦ −v(c_σ), and rg(M, φ) = rank M, deg(M, φ) = deg det(M, φ) are additive, and (M, φ) ↦ (M ⊗ Frac(R), φ ⊗ 1) (the semilinear extension of φ) is a generic-fibre functor, since for any Bézout ring the free direct-summand submodules of M correspond to the Frac(R)-subspaces of M ⊗ Frac(R) via N ↦ N ⊗ Frac(R), V ↦ V ∩ M. Assuming moreover that λ ∈ R ∖ {0} with λ^{σ−1} ∈ E satisfies v(λ^{σ−1}) ≥ 0, with equality iff λ ∈ E, every generic isomorphism u : (M, φ) → (M', φ') satisfies deg(M, φ) ≤ deg(M', φ') with equality iff u is an isomorphism; hence C has HN filtrations. For R the Robba ring and E the bounded subring these are Kedlaya's filtrations [43] (with the opposite sign convention).
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.5, pp. 216–217 (citing [43]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: only the Robba-ring case is planned. Planned only over the Robba ring: nodes PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration (which records the reversed inequalities) and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists (Kedlaya). The abstract Bézout-ring version is not planned. The Bézout-domain linear algebra used in the example (saturated spans of a finite free module are free direct summands; Galois descent of saturated submodules) is node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.6 (a): Frobenius sheaves on a one-dimensional scheme form an HN category
items.statement: Let X be an irreducible noetherian scheme of dimension 1 with a finite flat morphism σ : X → X of degree deg(σ) > 1, and C the category of pairs (E, φ) with E a coherent sheaf on X without embedded components (E ↪ j_*j^*E, j : η → X the generic point) and φ : E → E σ-linear such that Φ : σ^*E → E is an isomorphism at the generic point. C is an exact category, stable under extensions in the abelian category of coherent sheaves with a σ-linear map. Set rg(E, φ) = length_{O_{X,η}}(E_η) and deg(E, φ) = −length(coker Φ) (both additive; the book prints deg = +length(coker Φ), for which the HN axiom fails, sourceIssue E109), and let A be the pairs (N, φ) with N a finitely generated O_{X,η}-module and φ σ-linear. Then (E, φ) ↦ (E_η, φ_η) is a generic-fibre functor and, for every generic isomorphism u : (E, φ) → (E', φ'), deg(E', φ') = deg(E, φ) + length(σ^*coker u) − length(coker u) ≥ deg(E, φ) (= deg(E, φ) + (deg(σ) − 1)·length(coker u) when σ induces isomorphisms on the residue fields of closed points); equality holds iff u is an isomorphism provided length(σ^*k(x)) ≥ 2 for every closed point x (true when σ induces isomorphisms on residue fields, e.g. for Breuil–Kisin modules); under these conventions C has HN filtrations.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.6, p. 218, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: As printed the degree formula has the wrong sign (length(coker u∘Φ) = length(coker Φ'∘σ^*u) gives deg(E') = deg(E) − (deg σ − 1)·length(coker u)), so the axioms hold for deg = −length(coker Φ); see sourceIssues. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 plans (torsion) Kisin modules (node FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules) but no HN theory for them.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.6 (b): Breuil–Kisin-type modules over a 2-dimensional regular local ring
items.statement: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension 2, p a height-one prime, σ : R → R a finite flat endomorphism of degree > 1 with σ(p) = p, X_n = Spec(R/p^n) and C = ∪_{n≥1} C_n (C_n the category of (a) for (X_n, σ)). By Auslander–Buchsbaum, C is the category of pairs (M, φ) with M an R-module killed by a power of p and of projective dimension 1, and φ : M → M σ-linear and an isomorphism at the generic point of Spec(R/p); for u ∈ m_R ∖ p, equivalently M is killed by a power of p, has no u-torsion, and φ ⊗ σ : M[1/u] → M[1/u] is a σ-linear isomorphism. With rg(M, φ) = length_{R[1/u]} M[1/u] and deg(M, φ) = −length_R M/R·φ(M) (the book prints +length_R M/R·φ(M), see sourceIssue E109), C is an HN category; for R = W(k)[[u]], σ(u) = u^p, σ|_W the Frobenius and p = pR these are the categories of [10] and [46].
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.6, pp. 218–219 (citing [10], [46]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Same sign problem as (a) for deg = length_R M/R·φ(M). FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 plans (torsion) Kisin modules (node FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules) but no HN theory for them.

items.name: External: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
items.statement: (Used as a black box.) For a finitely generated module M of finite projective dimension over a regular local ring R, pd(M) + depth(M) = depth(R); hence an R-module killed by a power of p (R regular local of dimension 2, p of height 1) has no embedded components iff it has projective dimension 1.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.6, p. 218, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds (decomposition). Not in Mathlib at the pin.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.7 (a): HN filtrations of finite flat group schemes ([19])
items.statement: Let K be a field complete for a non-trivial real valuation, p the residue characteristic, and C the category of commutative finite flat group schemes over O_K of p-power order with étale generic fibre, with ht(G) = log_p|G| and deg(G) = Σ_i v(a_i) if ω_G ≅ ⊕_i O_K/a_iO_K. With A the étale commutative group schemes over K and G ↦ G ⊗ K, the axioms of §5.5.1 hold, so objects of C have HN filtrations for the slope deg/ht.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.7, p. 219 (citing [19]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Black box [19]. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 plans finite flat group schemes (e.g. node FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/schematic-closure-of-generic-subgroups) but no degree function or HN filtration.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.7 (b): characteristic p, finite flat group schemes ≃ (M, φ) over W(k)[[u]]
items.statement: If K is discretely valued of characteristic p with perfect residue field k, K ≅ k((u)), then C is equivalent to the category of pairs (M, φ) with M a W(k)[[u]]-module killed by a power of p without u-torsion and φ a σ-linear endomorphism inducing a σ-linear isomorphism after inverting u (the category of Exemple 5.5.2.6); HN filtrations correspond under this equivalence, and the degree comes from a degree on height-one objects and a determinant.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.7, pp. 219–220, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Asserted ('On peut alors montrer'). Not planned.

items.name: Exemple 5.5.2.7 (c): characteristic 0, Kisin's classification ([46])
items.statement: If K is discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k, O_K ≅ W(k)[[u]]/(E(u)) with E an Eisenstein polynomial, then by [46] C is equivalent to the category of pairs (M, φ) with M a W(k)[[u]]-module killed by a power of p without u-torsion and φ σ-linear with M/W(k)[[u]]·φ(M) killed by E(u); this category is not tensorial, and the HN filtrations of C are a special case of those of Exemple 5.5.2.6 via this equivalence.
items.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.7, p. 220 (citing [46]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Kisin's classification is node FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/finite-flat-classification (p > 2) and .../dyadic-classification; the HN compatibility is not planned. The text prints 'K ≃ K_0[[u]]/(E(u))' (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Définition 5.6.1: Riemann sphere (sphère de Riemann)
items.statement: A Riemann sphere is a complete curve X having a point ∞ ∈ X of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine, Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0, and H^1(X, O_X(−∞)) = 0.
items.locator: Définition 5.6.1, p. 220, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. P^1 over a field is the model example (Grothendieck [30]).

items.name: Basic properties of a Riemann sphere
items.statement: Let X be a Riemann sphere (a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine, Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0 and H^1(X, O_X(−∞)) = 0), O_X(k) = O_X(k·∞). Then deg : Pic(X) ≅ ℤ; for k ∈ ℤ and a vector bundle E, µ(E(k)) = µ(E) + k and E is semistable iff E(k) is; H^0(X, O_X(k)) = 0 for k < 0 and H^1(X, O_X(k)) = 0 for k ≥ −1 (in particular H^1(X, O_X) = 0).
items.locator: §5.6.1 after Définition 5.6.1, p. 220, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequences of §5.4.

items.name: Sub-bundles and the image of a morphism of bundles
items.statement: A sub-bundle means a locally direct summand sub-bundle, i.e. a strict subobject in the exact category of bundles. For a morphism of bundles u : E → F, Im(u) is the image in the category of bundles, a sub-bundle of F: the scheme-theoretic closure of the generic-fibre image of u.
items.locator: §5.6.1, p. 221, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (bundles on an arbitrary curve); planned only on the FF curve. VB1 stage plans 'saturated subbundles' on the FF curve; nothing at the pins.

items.name: Théorème 5.6.2 (1): semistable bundles on a Riemann sphere are O(d)^a
