items.statement: Let X be a Riemann sphere (a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine, Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0 and H^1(X, O_X(−∞)) = 0), O_X(k) = O_X(k·∞). Then the semistable bundles on X are exactly the bundles isomorphic to O_X(d)^{⊕a} for integers d ∈ ℤ and a ≥ 0.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.2 (1), pp. 221–222 (reinterpreting [30]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Reinterpretation of Grothendieck's classification on P^1 [30], proved in the text by induction on the rank. Not planned; no P^1 splitting theorem in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Théorème 5.6.2 (2): HN filtrations on a Riemann sphere split
items.statement: Let X be a Riemann sphere (a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine, Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0 and H^1(X, O_X(−∞)) = 0), O_X(k) = O_X(k·∞). Then the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of every vector bundle on X is split.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.2 (2), p. 221, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: From (1) and Ext^1(O(d2), O(d1)) ≅ H^1(X, O(d1 − d2)) = 0 for d1 > d2.

items.name: Théorème 5.6.2 (3): classification of rank-n bundles on a Riemann sphere
items.statement: Let X be a Riemann sphere (a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine, Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0 and H^1(X, O_X(−∞)) = 0), O_X(k) = O_X(k·∞). Then for every integer n the map {(d_1,…,d_n) ∈ ℤ^n | d_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ d_n} → {rank-n bundles on X}/≅, (d_1,…,d_n) ↦ [⊕_{i=1}^n O_X(d_i)], is a bijection.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.2 (3), p. 221, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.3: three equivalent forms of the divergence from P^1 (rank 2)
items.statement: Let X be a complete curve with a point ∞ of degree 1 such that X ∖ {∞} is affine and Pic(X ∖ {∞}) = 0, and assume H^1(X, O_X) = 0. The following are equivalent: (1) there is a semistable rank-2 bundle on X that is not a direct sum of two line bundles; (2) H^1(X, O_X(−1)) ≠ 0; (3) for ∞ ∈ X a degree-1 point with X ∖ {∞} affine equal to Spec(B), the principal ring (B, −v_∞) is not Euclidean.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.3, pp. 223–224, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The proof contains an index misprint (d1 − d1 − 1 for d2 − d1 − 1; see sourceIssues).

items.name: Exemple 5.6.4: isocrystal bundles give semistable rank-2 bundles of slope 1/2 on the FF curve
items.statement: For the curve X of Exemple 5.4.3 with h = 1, one can associate to every isocrystal a vector bundle on X whose HN slopes are the Dieudonné–Manin slopes of the isocrystal (proved later). Hence there are semistable bundles of rank 2 and slope 1/2 on X, the hypotheses of Proposition 5.6.3 hold, and (B_e, deg) is not Euclidean.
items.locator: Exemple 5.6.4, p. 224; Introduction, p. 201, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block (the functor E(−) with explicit sign reversal) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (O(λ) stable). The non-Euclidean consequence is not planned.

items.name: Définition 5.6.5: finite étale morphism of curves
items.statement: A finite étale morphism of curves is a finite étale morphism f : X → Y of the underlying schemes such that deg(x) = [k(x) : k(f(x))]·deg(f(x)) for every (closed) point x ∈ X.
items.locator: Définition 5.6.5, p. 224, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has finite étale morphisms of schemes; the degree compatibility and the notion are absent.

items.name: Définition 5.6.6: push-forward and pull-back of divisors along a finite étale morphism
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism of curves f : X → Y: for D = Σ_{x∈|X|} m_x[x] ∈ Div(X), f_*D = Σ_{x∈|X|} m_x·[k(x) : k(f(x))]·[f(x)]; for D = Σ_{y∈|Y|} m_y[y] ∈ Div(Y), f^*D = Σ_{x∈|X|} m_{f(x)}[x].
items.locator: Définition 5.6.6, p. 224, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.pushforward is the unweighted formal push-forward (no residue-degree factor) and WeilDivisor.pullback only exists along injective maps, so neither matches. AlgebraicCurves Layer 6 plans the conorm Con for extensions of function fields over k (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-6-extensions-of-function-fields), not this setting.

items.name: Degree formulas for f_* and f^* on divisors
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism of curves f : X → Y (of constant degree deg(f)): f_*f^* = deg(f)·Id on Div(Y), deg(f_*D) = deg(D) for D ∈ Div(X), and deg(f^*D) = deg(f)·deg(D) for D ∈ Div(Y).
items.locator: §5.6.3.1 after Définition 5.6.6, p. 224, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The analogue deg(Con D) = [F':F]/[k':k]·deg D for function fields is planned in AlgebraicCurves Layer 6 only.

items.name: Lemme 5.6.7: compatibility of div with the norm and with pull-back
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of curves. Then div ∘ N_{F(X)/F(Y)} = f_* ∘ div : F(X)^× → Div(Y), and the diagram F(Y)^× → Div(Y) → Pic(Y) maps to F(X)^× → Div(X) → Pic(X) by inclusion, f^* and f^* commutatively.
items.locator: Lemme 5.6.7, p. 225, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof ('ne pose pas de problème').

items.name: Proposition 5.6.8: det(f_*O_X)^{⊗2} ≅ O_Y for finite étale f
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism of schemes f : X → Y there is a canonical isomorphism of line bundles det(f_*O_X)^{⊗2} ≅ O_Y.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.8, p. 225, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via the S_d-torsor Isom_Y({1,…,d}, X) and the signature; Remarque 5.6.10 gives the alternative proof by the discriminant of the trace form. The proof contains an index misprint (see sourceIssues). A special case is planned: node EllipticKTheory:E.5/class-of-the-pushed-forward-structure-sheaf ('If f is separable, det(f_*O_{E′})^{⊗2} ≅ O_E' for an isogeny f of elliptic curves). The determinant bundle of a vector bundle on a scheme is node KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5/determinant-bundle.

items.name: Remarque 5.6.9: det(f_*O_X) need not be trivial
items.statement: In general det(f_*O_X) ≇ O_Y: if 2 is invertible on Y and L is a non-trivial line bundle with L^{⊗2} ≅ O_Y, and f : X → Y is the associated µ_2-torsor, then f_*O_X = O_Y ⊕ L has non-trivial determinant.
items.locator: Remarque 5.6.9, p. 225, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: A special case is planned: node EllipticKTheory:E.5/class-of-the-pushed-forward-structure-sheaf (c) ('If char F ≠ 2 and f is separable of degree 2, then det(f_*O_{E′}) is a non-trivial 2-torsion line bundle').

items.name: Lemme 5.6.11: det(f_*O_X(D)) ≅ det(f_*O_X) ⊗ O_Y(f_*D)
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a (finite) étale morphism of curves and D ∈ Div(X). Then det(f_*O_X(D)) ≅ det(f_*O_X) ⊗ O_Y(f_*D).
items.locator: Lemme 5.6.11, pp. 225–226, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.12: Riemann–Roch–Grothendieck for finite étale maps modulo 2-torsion
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of curves and Pic(X) ≅ Div(X)/∼ the isomorphism sending [O_X(D)] to the class of D. Then the square Pic(X) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] → (Div(X)/∼) ⊗ ℤ[1/2], with det ∘ f_* : Pic(X) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] → Pic(Y) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] on the left and f_* : (Div(X)/∼) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] → (Div(Y)/∼) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] on the right, commutes.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.12, p. 226; Remarque 5.6.13, pp. 226–227, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Remarque 5.6.13: this is RRG modulo 2-torsion for finite étale maps; Remarque 5.6.9 shows it fails integrally.

items.name: Lemme 5.6.14: det(f_*E) versus det(f_* det E)
items.statement: For f : X → Y a finite locally free morphism of schemes and E a vector bundle of rank n on X, det(f_*E) ≅ det(f_* det E) ⊗ det(f_*O_X)^{⊗(n−1)} (≅ N_{X/Y}(det E) ⊗ det(f_*O_X)^{⊗n}). The book states det(f_*E) ≅ det(f_* det E), false in general (sourceIssue E114); for f finite étale the two sides differ by a 2-torsion line bundle (Proposition 5.6.8), which is all Proposition 5.6.15 uses.
items.locator: Lemme 5.6.14, p. 227 (citing [9]), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: False as stated for rank E ≥ 2; the correct formula is det(f_*E) ≅ det(f_* det E) ⊗ det(f_*O_X)^{⊗(rk E − 1)} (see sourceIssues). The discrepancy is 2-torsion for finite étale f (Prop. 5.6.8), so Prop. 5.6.15 survives.

items.name: External: det of restriction of scalars is the norm of det ([9])
items.statement: (Used as a black box.) For a finite locally free (free) extension of rings S/R and an S-linear endomorphism g of a free S-module A of finite rank, det_R(g) = N_{S/R}(det_S(g)); equivalently the diagram Res_{X/Y}GL_n → Res_{X/Y}G_m → G_m (Res det, then norm) agrees with GL(f_*O_X^n) → G_m (det).
items.locator: Proof of Lemme 5.6.14, p. 227 (citing [9], lemme 1, A.3.112), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: LinearMap.det_restrictScalars : (f.restrictScalars R).det = Algebra.norm R f.det for S free over R and A free over S (Mathlib/RingTheory/Norm/Transitivity.lean). The group-scheme/torsor form is not in the library.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.15: deg(f_*E) = deg(E) for finite étale f
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of complete curves and E a vector bundle on X. Then deg(f_*E) = deg(E).
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.15, p. 227, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Lemme 5.6.14 and Proposition 5.6.12; remains true despite the error in 5.6.14. For the FF curve, push-forward along coefficient extension is node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction, which does not state a degree formula.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.16 (a): a finite étale cover of a complete curve is complete
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of curves with Y complete. Then X is complete.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.16, p. 227, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.16 (b): rank, degree and slope of f_*E
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of curves with Y complete. For a vector bundle E on X: rg(f_*E) = deg(f)·rg(E), deg(f_*E) = deg(E), µ(f_*E) = µ(E)/deg(f).
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.16, p. 227, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.16 (c): rank, degree and slope of f^*E
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale morphism of curves with Y complete. For a vector bundle E on Y: rg(f^*E) = rg(E), deg(f^*E) = deg(f)·deg(E), µ(f^*E) = deg(f)·µ(E).
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.16, p. 227, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For coefficient extension of the FF curve the slope rescaling appears in node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/HN-filtration-base-change.

items.name: Lemme 5.6.17: Galois descent of vector bundles along finite étale Galois covers
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale Galois morphism of curves with group Γ. Then E ↦ f^*E and F ↦ (f_*F)^Γ are mutually inverse equivalences between vector bundles on Y and Γ-equivariant vector bundles on X.
items.locator: Lemme 5.6.17, p. 228, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Recalled as standard. Not planned: VB1 plans v/pro-étale descent over the base S of the relative curve, and ModularCurves 0E plans fpqc descent in specified forms, neither covering this. Tau Ceti's GaloisDescent namespace concerns group algebras, not sheaves. The affine-local statement is planned: node PerfectoidSpaces:P9/finite-galois-descent-of-modules (for a finite étale Galois ring extension A → B with group H, M ↦ B ⊗_A M is an equivalence onto B-modules with semilinear H-action, preserving finite projectivity and rank); the gluing to finite étale Galois covers of curves is not stated anywhere.

items.name: Exemple 5.6.18: f^*f_*E ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Γ} σ^*E
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemme 5.6.17, for a bundle E on X, f^*f_*E ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Γ} σ^*E; thus the bundle f_*E on Y corresponds to the induced equivariant bundle Ind_{{1}}^Γ E.
items.locator: Exemple 5.6.18, p. 228, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Lemme 5.6.19: HN filtrations commute with finite étale Galois pull-back
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a finite étale Galois morphism of complete curves and E a vector bundle on Y with HN filtration 0 = E_0 ⊊ E_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ E_r = E. Then 0 = f^*E_0 ⊊ f^*E_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ f^*E_r = f^*E is the HN filtration of f^*E. In particular E is semistable iff f^*E is.
items.locator: Lemme 5.6.19, p. 228, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality. Planned for the relevant FF-curve instance (coefficient extension X_{E'} → X_E, E'|E finite separable): node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/HN-filtration-base-change (FS II.2.13). The abstract lemma for Galois covers of complete curves is not planned.

items.name: Γ-equivariant bundle and the associated Γ-action on Aut(E)
items.statement: Let X be a scheme with an action of a group Γ. A Γ-equivariant bundle on X is a pair (E, (c_σ)_{σ∈Γ}) with E a bundle and isomorphisms c_σ : σ^*E ≅ E such that c_τ ∘ τ^*c_σ = c_{στ} for all σ, τ ∈ Γ. Γ acts on Aut(E) by f^σ = c_σ ∘ σ^*f ∘ c_σ^{−1}; for another equivariant structure (c'_σ), d_σ = c_σ ∘ c'^{−1}_σ ∈ Aut(E) is a 1-cocycle.
items.locator: §5.6.3.2, pp. 228–229, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.20: equivariant structures and H^1(Γ, Aut(E))
items.statement: Let E be a bundle with a Γ-equivariant structure and Γ → Aut(E) the associated action. (1) The Γ-equivariant structures on E are in bijection with Z^1(Γ, Aut(E)), the cocycle c giving the twisted equivariant bundle E ∧^Γ c. (2) E ∧^Γ c_1 ≅ E ∧^Γ c_2 as equivariant bundles iff c_1 and c_2 differ by a coboundary. (3) The isomorphism classes of equivariant bundles whose underlying bundle is isomorphic to E are in bijection with H^1(Γ, Aut(E)).
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.20, p. 229, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 5.6.21: generalized Riemann sphere
items.statement: A generalized Riemann sphere is a pair (X, E_∞) where X is a complete curve with field of definition E and E_∞|E is an algebraic Galois extension with group Ẑ, such that: (1) for every x ∈ |X|, E_∞|E embeds into k(x)|E; (2) there is a closed point ∞ ∈ |X| of degree 1 such that for every finite extension E'|E inside E_∞ there is a closed point of X ⊗_E E' above ∞ whose complement is the spectrum of a principal ring; (3) H^1(X, O_X) = 0.
items.locator: Définition 5.6.21, p. 229, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. For the FF curve the tower X_h = X ⊗_E E_h is coefficient extension along unramified E_h|E (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction).

items.name: The tower X_h = X ⊗_E E_h of a generalized Riemann sphere and the bundles O_{X_h}(k)
items.statement: For (X, E_∞) a generalized Riemann sphere let E_h = E_∞^{hẐ} (cyclic of degree h), X_h = X ⊗_E E_h, π_h : X_h → X and π_{h',h} : X_{h'} → X_h for h | h'. Then X_h is noetherian regular of dimension 1 and integral (E is algebraically closed in E(X), Lemme 5.1.5); π_h is totally split at every closed point (each fibre consists of h closed points with the residue field of x); with deg(x) = deg(π_h(x)), X_h is a complete curve with field of definition E_h, the π_{h',h} are finite étale in the sense of Définition 5.6.5, and (X_h, E_∞) is again a generalized Riemann sphere satisfying the hypotheses of §5.4. Fixing a compatible system (∞_h)_h ∈ lim |X_h| of degree-1 points and σ = 1̄ ∈ ℤ/hℤ = Aut(X_h/X), set O_{X_h}(k) = O_{X_h}(Σ_{i=0}^{k−1}[σ^i(∞_h)]) for k ≥ 1 and O_{X_h}(k) = O_{X_h}(−k)^{−1} for k ≤ 0.
items.locator: §5.6.4.1, pp. 229–230, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The text asserts these properties ('On vérifie'). Not planned abstractly.

items.name: Pic(X_h) ≅ ℤ via d ↦ O_{X_h}(d)
items.statement: For every h, d ↦ [O_{X_h}(d)] is an isomorphism ℤ ≅ Pic(X_h) inverse to deg; in particular O_{X_h}(d) ≅ O_{X_h}(1)^{⊗d}.
items.locator: §5.6.4.1, pp. 230–231, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The accompanying remark that the definition gives a canonical identification π_{nh,h}^*O_{X_h}(d) = O_{X_{nh}}(nd) holds only when h | d or n = 1 (e.g. always for h = 1); see sourceIssues.

items.name: Définition 5.6.22: the bundles O_X(d, h) and O_X(λ)
items.statement: For d ∈ ℤ and h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, O_X(d, h) = π_{h*}(O_{X_h}(d)) as a vector bundle on X. For λ ∈ ℚ, λ = d/h with (d, h) = 1 and h > 0, O_X(λ) = O_X(d, h). For an integer n the same notations are used for the generalized Riemann sphere (X_h)_{n|h}: O_{X_n}(d, h) = π_{nh,n*}(O_{X_{nh}}(d)).
items.locator: Définition 5.6.22, p. 231, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block (standard block and its bundle), and the push-forward description via VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (downward isocrystal functor ↔ π_{E'|E*}).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.23 (1): O_X(d, h) ≅ O_X(d/h)^{⊕δ}
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, d ∈ ℤ, h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and for λ ∈ ℚ let m(λ) be the order of λ mod ℤ in ℚ/ℤ. If δ = gcd(d, h) then O_X(d, h) ≅ O_X(d/h)^{⊕δ}.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.23 (1), pp. 231–232, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: VB2:classification stage ('stable bundles have the ranks and degrees prescribed by reduced rational slopes'). The printed proof has misprints h/δ for d/δ (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.23 (2): pull-back and push-forward of O(d, h) along π_n
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, d ∈ ℤ, h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and for λ ∈ ℚ let m(λ) be the order of λ mod ℤ in ℚ/ℤ. For n ∈ ℕ_{>0}: π_n^*O_X(d, h) ≅ O_{X_n}(nd, h) and π_{n*}O_{X_n}(d, h) ≅ O_X(d, nh); hence π_n^*O_X(λ) ≅ O_{X_n}(nλ)^{⊕ m(λ)/m(nλ)} and π_{n*}O_{X_n}(λ) ≅ O_X(λ/n)^{⊕ n·m(λ)/m(λ/n)}.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.23 (2), pp. 231–232, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (upward/downward isocrystal functors ↔ π^*, π_*). The printed proof of the non-coprime case has a gap (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.23 (3): O_X(d, h) and O_X(λ) are semistable
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, d ∈ ℤ, h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and for λ ∈ ℚ let m(λ) be the order of λ mod ℤ in ℚ/ℤ. O_X(d, h) is semistable of slope d/h; for every λ ∈ ℚ, O_X(λ) is semistable of slope λ.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.23 (3), pp. 231–232, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (the O(λ) are stable). Proof via π_h^*O_X(d, h) ≅ O_{X_h}(d)^{⊕h} and Lemme 5.6.19.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.23 (4): tensor products and duals of O(d, h)
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, d ∈ ℤ, h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and for λ ∈ ℚ let m(λ) be the order of λ mod ℤ in ℚ/ℤ. O_X(d_1, h_1) ⊗ O_X(d_2, h_2) ≅ O_X(d_1h_2 + d_2h_1, h_1h_2) and O_X(d, h)^∨ ≅ O_X(−d, h); in particular O_X(λ_1) ⊗ O_X(λ_2) ≅ O_X(λ_1 + λ_2)^{⊕ m(λ_1)m(λ_2)/m(λ_1+λ_2)} and O_X(λ)^∨ ≅ O_X(−λ).
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.23 (4), pp. 231, 233, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: VB0 stage ('Prove functoriality under coefficient extension, tensor slope addition and dual slope negation'). The printed proof has index misprints and, in the non-coprime case, a gap (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.23 (5): Hom and Ext^1 vanishing between the O(λ)
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, d ∈ ℤ, h ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and for λ ∈ ℚ let m(λ) be the order of λ mod ℤ in ℚ/ℤ. For λ > µ, Hom(O_X(λ), O_X(µ)) = 0; for λ ≤ µ, Ext^1(O_X(λ), O_X(µ)) = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.23 (5), pp. 231, 233, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (an arbitrary generalized Riemann sphere); only the FF-curve instance, recorded again in Chapter 8, is planned. Planned only for the FF curve, where O(λ) is built from isocrystals: VB2:classification stage ('Prove Hom/Ext vanishing') and node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (H^1(O(λ)) = 0 for λ ≥ 0 on affinoid bases). The printed proof cites a non-existent 'condition (4)' of Déf. 5.6.21 (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Définition 5.6.24: pure bundle
items.statement: A bundle E on X is pure if there are λ ∈ ℚ and a ∈ ℕ with E ≅ O_X(λ)^{⊕a}; similarly on X_h. By Proposition 5.6.23, E is pure iff E ≅ O_X(deg E, rg E).
items.locator: Définition 5.6.24, pp. 233–234, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No 'pure' notion in the atlas for bundles (RD.1 has isoclinic σ-modules, node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.25: purity descends along π_h
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere, E a bundle on X and h an integer ≥ 1. Then E is pure iff π_h^*E is pure.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.25, p. 234, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proof via Proposition 5.6.20 and Hilbert 90; one step misidentifies the Galois action on Aut(F) (see sourceIssues).

items.name: External: Hilbert 90 for GL_a
items.statement: (Used as a black box.) For a finite Galois extension E_h|E, H^1(Gal(E_h|E), GL_a(E_h)) = {∗}.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.6.25, p. 234, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has only the case a = 1 (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Hilbert90.lean), so the library entry is partial. GL_n version planned in node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/semilinear-galois-descent. The proof actually needs H^1(Gal(E_h|E), (A ⊗_E E_h)^×) = {∗} for a finite-dimensional E-algebra A (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Théorème 5.6.26 (1): under the extension hypothesis, semistable = pure
items.statement: Let (X_h)_{h≥1}, X = X_1, be a generalized Riemann sphere. Assume that for every h and every n ≥ 1, whenever 0 → O_{X_h}(−1/n) → E → O_{X_h}(1) → 0 is an exact sequence of bundles, H^0(X_h, E) ≠ 0. Then the semistable bundles on X are exactly the pure bundles.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.26 (1), pp. 234–237, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. For the FF curve the conclusion is node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (FS II.2.14), and the hypothesis corresponds to node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/key-extension-lemma (FS II.2.15, in the form 0 → O(−1) → E → O(1/n) → 0, after extending C). Proof 'strongly inspired by [43]'.

items.name: Théorème 5.6.26 (2): under the extension hypothesis, HN filtrations split
items.statement: Let (X_h)_{h≥1}, X = X_1, be a generalized Riemann sphere. Assume that for every h and every n ≥ 1, whenever 0 → O_{X_h}(−1/n) → E → O_{X_h}(1) → 0 is an exact sequence of bundles, H^0(X_h, E) ≠ 0. Then the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of every bundle on X is split.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.26 (2), pp. 234–235, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. For the FF curve the conclusion is node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (FS II.2.14), and the hypothesis corresponds to node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/key-extension-lemma (FS II.2.15, in the form 0 → O(−1) → E → O(1/n) → 0, after extending C). Proof 'strongly inspired by [43]'.

items.name: Théorème 5.6.26 (3): under the extension hypothesis, classification of bundles by slopes
items.statement: Let (X_h)_{h≥1}, X = X_1, be a generalized Riemann sphere. Assume that for every h and every n ≥ 1, whenever 0 → O_{X_h}(−1/n) → E → O_{X_h}(1) → 0 is an exact sequence of bundles, H^0(X_h, E) ≠ 0. Then the map {(λ_i)_{1≤i≤n} ∈ ℚ^n | n ∈ ℕ, λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_n} → {bundles on X}/≅, (λ_1,…,λ_n) ↦ ⊕_{i=1}^n O_X(λ_i), is a bijection.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.26 (3), p. 235, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The abstract theorem is not planned. For the FF curve the conclusion is node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (FS II.2.14), and the hypothesis corresponds to node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/key-extension-lemma (FS II.2.15, in the form 0 → O(−1) → E → O(1/n) → 0, after extending C). Proof 'strongly inspired by [43]'.

items.name: Remarque 5.6.27: the extension hypothesis of Théorème 5.6.26 is necessary
items.statement: If the conclusions of Théorème 5.6.26 hold, then for every exact sequence 0 → O_{X_h}(−1/n) → E → O_{X_h}(1) → 0, E (of degree 0) has a direct summand O(λ) with λ ≥ 0 and hence H^0(X_h, E) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Remarque 5.6.27, pp. 237–238, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Corollaire 5.6.28: semistable bundles of slope λ ≃ vector spaces over a division algebra
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Théorème 5.6.26, for every λ ∈ ℚ the abelian category of semistable bundles of slope λ on X is semisimple with unique simple object O_X(λ) up to isomorphism; End(O_X(λ)) is a division algebra; and E ↦ Hom(O_X(λ), E) is an equivalence between this category and finite-dimensional End(O_X(λ))^{opp}-vector spaces.
items.locator: Corollaire 5.6.28, p. 238, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Abstract statement not planned. For the FF curve, End(O(λ)) = D_λ is node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra and the semistable-of-slope-λ classification is part of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles.

items.name: Modification of a vector bundle
items.statement: A modification of a bundle E on X is a bundle E' together with an isomorphism on generic fibres E'_η ≅ E_η, i.e. an isomorphism E'|_{X∖S} ≅ E|_{X∖S} for some finite S ⊂ |X|.
items.locator: §5.6.4.2 before Théorème 5.6.29, p. 238, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality (any curve, any finite S ⊂ |X|); only modifications at a degree-one divisor of the relative FF curve are planned. Node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor (modifications at a degree-one divisor of the relative curve, meromorphic along D); the FF notion allows any finite S.

items.name: Modifications of degree 1 under the classification (i): kernels of O(1/n) → F
items.statement: Assume the conclusions of Théorème 5.6.26 hold on X (every bundle is a direct sum of O_X(λ), λ ∈ ℚ). If n ≥ 1 and 0 → E → O_X(1/n) → F → 0 is exact with F a coherent torsion sheaf of degree 1, then E ≅ O_X^n.
items.locator: §5.6.4.2 before Théorème 5.6.29, p. 238, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Modifications of degree 1 under the classification (ii): extensions of torsion by O^n
items.statement: Assume the conclusions of Théorème 5.6.26 hold on X (every bundle is a direct sum of O_X(λ), λ ∈ ℚ). If n ≥ 1 and 0 → O_X^n → E → F → 0 is exact with E a vector bundle and F coherent torsion of degree 1, then E ≅ O_X(1/m) ⊕ O_X^{n−m} for some m ∈ {1,…,n}.
items.locator: §5.6.4.2 before Théorème 5.6.29, pp. 238–239, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Théorème 5.6.29: classification criterion via degree-one modifications
items.statement: Let (X, E_∞) be a generalized Riemann sphere. Assume that for every h ≥ 1: (1) if n ≥ 1 and 0 → E → O_{X_h}(1/n) → F → 0 is exact with F torsion of degree 1, then E ≅ O_{X_h}^n; (2) if n ≥ 1 and 0 → O_{X_h}^n → E → F → 0 is exact with E a vector bundle and F torsion of degree 1, then E ≅ O_{X_h}(1/m) ⊕ O_{X_h}^{n−m} for some m ∈ {1,…,n}. Then the hypotheses, and hence the conclusions, of the classification theorem 5.6.26 hold.
items.locator: Théorème 5.6.29, p. 239 (proof p. 242), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Main original result of the chapter (Introduction, p. 201). Not planned: the atlas proves the FF-curve classification by the FS II.2.14/II.2.15 route (VB2:classification), not via modifications. The final step of the proof needs a flag of the torsion cokernel with degree-one graded pieces (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Définition 5.6.30: elementary bundle
items.statement: A bundle E on X is elementary if it is nonzero and has a presentation 0 → O_X^n → ⊕_{i∈I} O_X(1/h_i) → E → 0 with n ∈ ℕ and h_i ≥ 1 for all i.
items.locator: Définition 5.6.30, p. 239, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.31 (1): degree-one elementary bundles
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Théorème 5.6.29. Let E be an elementary bundle on X and u : E ↠ F an epimorphism with F coherent torsion of degree 1. If deg(E) = 1 then H^0(X, ker u) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.31 (1), pp. 239–240, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The proof has an index misprint O_X(1/n) for O_X(1/h) (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 5.6.31 (2): elementary sub-bundles of kernels of degree-one modifications
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Théorème 5.6.29. Let E be an elementary bundle on X and u : E ↠ F an epimorphism with F coherent torsion of degree 1. If deg(E) > 1 there exist an elementary bundle E' of degree deg(E) − 1 and a monomorphism of O_X-modules E' ↪ ker u.
items.locator: Proposition 5.6.31 (2), pp. 240–241, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: External: projection formula, base change and adjunctions for finite étale maps of curves
items.statement: (Used as black boxes.) For a finite étale morphism π of curves: projection formula π_*(F ⊗ π^*G) ≅ π_*F ⊗ G; flat base change along cartesian squares X_{h_1h_2} = X_{h_1} ×_X X_{h_2} (h_1, h_2 coprime) and the Künneth formula; and π_* is left adjoint to π^* = π^! (Hom(L, π^*E) ≅ Hom(π_*L, E)).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemme 5.6.11 (p. 226), Proposition 5.6.23 (pp. 232–233) and Théorème 5.6.26 (p. 236), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has pull-back/push-forward of sheaves of modules on schemes but not these statements for coherent sheaves (no projection formula, no π_* ⊣ π^* for finite étale π).

items.name: Définition 6.1.1: the graded algebra P_{F,E,π}
items.statement: Setting (FF §1.1): F|F_q a perfect field of characteristic p, complete for a non-trivial absolute value; E a local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π; A = W_{O_E}(O_F); B = B_{F,E} the Fréchet E-algebra of holomorphic functions of the variable π on the punctured disc Y, B^+ ⊂ B and B^b ⊂ B as in Ch. 1, ϕ the Frobenius; |Y| the set of closed points (primitive ideals of degree 1 of A), and for y ∈ |Y| its residue field C_y, θ_y : B → C_y, m_y = ker θ_y. Define the graded E-algebra P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{ϕ=π^d}, whose homogeneous elements of degree d are P_d = B^{ϕ=π^d} = {x ∈ B : ϕ(x) = π^d x}. When the dependence on E, F and π must be specified it is written P_{F,E,π}.
items.locator: Définition 6.1.1, p. 243, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF3 stage: 'Form the graded algebra of global sections for affinoid S and construct Proj'; node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map defines P = ⊕_{n≥0} H^0(X_S,O_{X_S}(n)) for S affinoid perfectoid. For S = Spa(F), H^0(X_S,O(n)) = H^0(Y_S,O)^{ϕ=π^n} (O(n) normalised in RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign; the n = 1 case is written out in VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover), i.e. FF's B^{ϕ=π^n}. No Fargues-Fontaine rings (B, B^+, B^b, P, Y, X) exist in Mathlib or Tau Ceti at the pinned commits (declarations.tsv has no perfectoid/tilt/Lubin-Tate/FF entries).

items.name: No 6.1.1: P is a subalgebra of B^+
items.statement: By Proposition 4.1.3, P = ⊕_{d≥0} (B^+)^{ϕ=π^d}, i.e. B^{ϕ=π^d} = (B^+)^{ϕ=π^d} for every d ≥ 0; the canonical map P → B^+ is injective and identifies P with a sub-E-algebra of B^+.
items.locator: no 6.1.1 (after Définition 6.1.1), pp. 243–244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (sections of O(n) on Y_S). No node states that ϕ-eigenvectors of slope d ≥ 0 extend over the boundary (lie in B^+); Proposition 4.1.3 itself is outside this range.

items.name: No 6.1.1: P_0 = E
items.statement: By Proposition 4.1.1 the homogeneous elements of degree 0 of P are P_0 = B^{ϕ=Id} = E.
items.locator: no 6.1.1, p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(ii)): E → BC(O) is an isomorphism of pro-étale sheaves, so H^0(X_S,O) = E for connected S such as Spa(F).

items.name: No 6.1.2: change of uniformizer u_{π,π'}
items.statement: Suppose F contains an algebraic closure F̄_q of F_q. Let π' be another uniformizer of E and L_{π,π'} = {u ∈ W_{O_E}(F̄_q)_Q : ϕ(u)π = uπ'}, a 1-dimensional E-vector space. There is a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras u_{π,π'} : ⊕_{d≥0} P_{π,d} ⊗_E L_{π,π'}^{⊗d} ⥲ P_{π'}, given by the recipe of §4.1.4 (x ⊗ u^{⊗d} ↦ u^d x).
items.locator: no 6.1.2, p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 stage ('uniformizer-change comparisons' for W_{O_E}) and RF3 ('the chosen pi-normalization' of O(1)); neither states a comparison of the graded algebras P_π and P_{π'}. No Fargues-Fontaine rings (B, B^+, B^b, P, Y, X) exist in Mathlib or Tau Ceti at the pinned commits (declarations.tsv has no perfectoid/tilt/Lubin-Tate/FF entries).

items.name: No 6.1.2: cocycle relation for u_{π,π'}
items.statement: If π'' is a third uniformizer of E then, via the canonical isomorphism L_{π,π'} ⊗_E L_{π',π''} ⥲ L_{π,π''}, one has u_{π,π''} = u_{π',π''} ∘ u_{π,π'}.
items.locator: no 6.1.2, p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in any atlas node (see previous item).

items.name: No 6.1.3: unramified change of E
items.statement: Suppose F contains an algebraic closure of F_q. Let E_h|E be the unramified extension of degree h (E_h = W_{O_E}(F̄_q)_Q^{ϕ^h=Id}). Then P_{E_h,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} (B_E^+)^{ϕ_E^h=π^d}, and (Proposition 4.1.7) there is a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras P_{E,π,•} ⊗_E E_h ⥲ P_{E_h,π,h•}.
items.locator: no 6.1.3, p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (change of coefficient field for isocrystals, σ_{E'} = σ_E^f, and π_{E'|E}: X_{E'} → X_E); it does not treat the graded algebra P.

items.name: No 6.1.3: totally ramified change of E
items.statement: Suppose F contains an algebraic closure F̄_q of F_q. Let E'|E be totally ramified with uniformizers π_{E'}, π_E, and L_{π_E,π_{E'}} = {u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)_Q : ϕ(u)π_E = uπ_{E'}^{[E':E]}}, a 1-dimensional E'-vector space. There is a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras ⊕_{d≥0} (P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E E') ⊗_{E'} L_{π_E,π_{E'}}^{⊗d} ⥲ P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•}, x ⊗ u^{⊗d} ↦ u^d x (corrected form, as in Proposition 4.1.8; the book prints u ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_Q, calls L an E-line and tensors over E, see E128).
items.locator: no 6.1.3, p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: As printed L is {0} unless π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E ∈ E (see sourceIssues); the correct version is Proposition 4.1.8 (p. 155), with u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)_Q and an extra ⊗_E E'. Nearest atlas: VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (isocrystals only).

items.name: No 6.2.1: free abelian monoids and factorial domains
items.statement: An abelian monoid M is free if it is isomorphic to (N^{(I)},+) for a set I. A nonzero m ∈ M is irreducible if it cannot be written m = m'+m'' with m',m'' ≠ 0; a free abelian monoid with set of irreducibles I is canonically N^{(I)} ⥲ M. For U ⊂ M^× a subgroup of the invertible elements, M/U is the quotient monoid. An integral domain A is factorial if the quotient monoid (A∖{0})/A^× is free.
items.locator: no 6.2.1, p. 245, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib's UniqueFactorizationMonoid (cancellative, well-founded strict divisibility, irreducible ⇔ prime; with IsDomain = UFD) is the standard equivalent of FF's definition (freeness of (A∖{0})/A^× on the classes of irreducibles); the literal free-monoid formulation is not a Mathlib declaration.

items.name: Théorème 6.2.1: P is graded-factorial with irreducibles of degree 1
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. Then the algebra P is graded-factorial with irreducible elements of degree 1, in the sense that the monoid ⋃_{d≥0} (P_d∖{0})/E^× is free on (P_1∖{0})/E^×.
items.locator: Théorème 6.2.1, p. 245 (proof §§6.2.2–6.2.3, pp. 245–251), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence ((BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× ≅ Div^1, the degree-1 part) and VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism (Pic(X_C) = Z); no node states the factoriality of the graded algebra P.

items.name: Théorème 6.2.1 (consequence): factorisation into degree-1 elements
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. If x ∈ B^{ϕ=π^d} with d ≥ 1, there exist t_1,…,t_d ∈ B^{ϕ=π} such that x = t_1⋯t_d.
items.locator: Théorème 6.2.1, p. 245, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: See previous item; not stated in any atlas node.

items.name: Définition 6.2.2: ϕ-invariant effective divisors Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z)
items.statement: With the notation of §2.7.2 (Div^+(Y): formal sums D = Σ_{y∈|Y|} a_y[y], a_y ∈ N, with finite support on every compact annulus |Y_J|), Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) denotes the set of D ∈ Div^+(Y) with ϕ^*D = D.
items.locator: Définition 6.2.2, p. 245, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts (effective Cartier divisors of degree d on X_S, Div^1) and RF1 (the quotient Y_S/ϕ^Z); neither introduces ϕ-invariant locally finite divisors on Y.

items.name: No 6.2.2: ϕ-orbit sums of finite divisors
items.statement: If D ∈ Div^+(Y) has finite support, the infinite sum Σ_{n∈Z} ϕ^{n*}D is a well-defined element of Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) (because ‖·‖∘ϕ = ‖·‖^q, where ‖·‖ : |Y| → ]0,1[ is the distance to the origin of the punctured disc). This defines a surjective morphism of monoids Σ_{n∈Z} ϕ^{n*} : Div^+(Y)_{finite} → Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z).
items.locator: no 6.2.2, p. 245, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (see Définition 6.2.2).

items.name: Lemme 6.2.3: Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) is free on |Y|/ϕ^Z
items.statement: Via the injection |Y|/ϕ^Z ↪ Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z), y mod ϕ^Z ↦ Σ_{n∈Z}[ϕ^n(y)], the monoid Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) is the free abelian monoid on |Y|/ϕ^Z.
items.locator: Lemme 6.2.3, p. 246, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. (The printed statement writes Div^+(Y/Z); see sourceIssues.)

items.name: Définition 6.2.4: degree of a ϕ-invariant divisor
items.statement: For D ∈ Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) written D = Σ_{i∈I} Σ_{n∈Z} [ϕ^n(y_i)] with y_i ∈ |Y|, set deg(D) = Σ_{i∈I} deg(y_i).
items.locator: Définition 6.2.4, p. 246, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF2:untilts (degree-d Cartier divisors); no degree on ϕ-invariant divisors of Y.

items.name: Lemme 6.2.5: degree computed on a fundamental domain
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ ]0,1[, so that |Y_{]ρ^q,ρ]}| ⊂ |Y| is a fundamental domain for the action of ϕ on |Y|. Then for every D ∈ Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z), deg(D) = deg(D|_{Y_{]ρ^q,ρ]}}).
items.locator: Lemme 6.2.5, p. 246, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli and RF1/frobenius-quotient-and-presentation (fundamental domains for ϕ); the divisor-degree statement is absent.

items.name: No 6.2.2: divisor map on homogeneous elements of P
items.statement: If x ∈ P_d is nonzero, the functional equation ϕ(x) = π^d x gives ϕ^* div(x) = div(ϕ(x)) = div(π^d x) = div(x) since π is a unit; hence div : B∖{0} → Div^+(Y) induces a monoid morphism div : ⋃_{d≥0} (P_d∖{0})/E^× → Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z). Both monoids carry a degree function, the degree of an element of P_d∖{0} being d.
items.locator: no 6.2.2, p. 246, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.6: the divisor map preserves degrees
items.statement: The monoid morphism div : ⋃_{d≥0}(P_d∖{0})/E^× → Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) is compatible with degrees: for nonzero x ∈ P_d, deg(div x) = d.
items.locator: Proposition 6.2.6, pp. 246–247, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the degree-1 case is implicit in VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (V(f) ∈ Div^1 for 0 ≠ f ∈ BC(O(1))). The proof uses the Newton-polygon slope relation λ_{i+kd} = q^{-k}λ_i and Théorème 3.4.4.

items.name: Théorème 6.2.7 (injectivity): divisors determine elements of P up to E^×
items.statement: The monoid morphism div : ⋃_{d≥0}(P_d∖{0})/E^× → Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) is injective.
items.locator: Théorème 6.2.7, p. 247, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Degree-1 case only: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence ((BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× ⥲ Div^1). The proof uses Théorème 3.5.5(2), Corollaire 1.9.5 (B^× = (B^b)^×) and (B^b)^{ϕ=π^k} = 0 for k ≠ 0, = E for k = 0.

items.name: Théorème 6.2.7 (surjectivity): div is an isomorphism when F is algebraically closed
items.statement: If F is algebraically closed, the monoid morphism div : ⋃_{d≥0}(P_d∖{0})/E^× → Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Théorème 6.2.7, p. 247 (surjectivity proved via Weierstrass products, pp. 247–251), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas beyond degree 1 (VB3 fundamental-exact-sequence).

items.name: No 6.2.3: the sets M_d of normalised primitive elements
items.statement: For an integer d ≥ 0, M_d = {x ∈ A∖πA : x ≡ π^d mod W_{O_E}(m_F)} ⊂ Prim_d, where Prim_d is the set of primitive elements of degree d of A = W_{O_E}(O_F).
items.locator: no 6.2.3, p. 247, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/primitive-untilt-correspondence (primitive degree-ONE ideals ↔ untilts); no normalised representatives, no degree d > 1.

items.name: No 6.2.3: M_d/M_0 = Prim_d/A^×
items.statement: Modulo A^×, every primitive element of degree d can be represented by an element of M_d: M_d/M_0 = Prim_d/A^×.
items.locator: no 6.2.3, p. 247, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: See previous item.

items.name: No 6.2.3 (example): the Lubin–Tate primitive element u_ε ∈ M_1
items.statement: Let Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q(X) ≡ X^q mod π and Q(X) ≡ πX mod X², and let ε ∈ m_F∖{0}. Then u_ε = [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/q}]_Q ∈ M_1 (with [·]_Q as in Définition 2.3.6).
items.locator: no 6.2.3, p. 248, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the cyclotomic case (E = Q_p, Q = (1+X)^p − 1, u_ε = ([ε]−1)/([ε^{1/p}]−1)) is planned: AInfCohomology:AI.0 stage (ξ = μ/ϕ^{-1}(μ)) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/frobenius-kernel-ideals-of-ainf (τ generates ker θ). The general Lubin–Tate element is absent.

items.name: No 6.2.3: the convergent half-product Π^+(b)
items.statement: For b ∈ M_d one has lim_{n→+∞} ϕ^n(b)/π^d = 1 in B^+; hence the infinite product Π^+(b) = ∏_{n≥0} ϕ^n(b)/π^d converges in B^+ and div(Π^+(b)) = Σ_{n≥0} ϕ^{n*} div(b).
items.locator: no 6.2.3, p. 248, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Exemple 6.2.8: Π^+ of π − [z]
items.locator: Exemple 6.2.8, p. 248, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.10: one-dimensionality of slope-zero Frobenius eigenspaces
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. For every b ∈ B^b with v_π(b) = 0, the E-vector space {x ∈ B^b_F : ϕ(x) = bx} has dimension 1. (The proof shows: if moreover b ∈ A∖πA, a nonzero solution x exists in A = W_{O_E}(O_F), constructed π-adically by solving X^{q−1} = b_0 and then Artin–Schreier equations.)
items.locator: Proposition 6.2.10, p. 249, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB0 (Dieudonné–Manin over L = W_{O_E}(F̄_q)[1/π]) and VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism (Pic(X_C) = Z, so degree-0 line bundles are trivial); neither states the explicit rank-one statement over B^b. See sourceIssues for a sign slip in the proof.

items.name: Définition 6.2.11: the Weierstrass products Π^+(b), Π^−(b), Π(b)
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. For b ∈ M_d set Π^+(b) = ∏_{n≥0} ϕ^n(b)/π^d, let Π^−(b) be any nonzero element of A satisfying ϕ(Π^−(b)) = bΠ^−(b) (it exists and is unique up to E^× by Proposition 6.2.10), and set Π(b) = Π^+(b)Π^−(b). Thus Π^−(b) and Π(b) are only defined up to multiplication by E^×.
items.locator: Définition 6.2.11, p. 250, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 6.2.3: Π as a monoid morphism M/M_0 → (P∖{0})/E^×
items.statement: Let M = ⋃_{d≥0} M_d, a monoid under multiplication. For b_1,b_2 ∈ M, Π(b_1b_2) = Π(b_1)Π(b_2) up to E^×; for b ∈ M_0, Π(b) ∈ E^×, and M_0 = ker(W_{O_E}(O_F)^× → W_{O_E}(k_F)^×) is a subgroup of A^×. Hence Π defines a monoid morphism Π : M/M_0 → (P∖{0})/E^×, with Π(b) ∈ P_d for b ∈ M_d.
items.locator: no 6.2.3 (after Définition 6.2.11), p. 250, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 6.2.12: divisor of the Weierstrass product Π(b)
items.statement: For b ∈ M_d, in Div^+(Y/ϕ^Z) one has div(Π(b)) = Σ_{n∈Z} ϕ^n(div b), where for D = Σ_y m(y)[y] one writes ϕ(D) = Σ_y m(y)[ϕ(y)]. More precisely div(Π^−(b)) = Σ_{n<0} ϕ^n(div b) (and div(Π^+(b)) = Σ_{n≥0} ϕ^n(div b)). Consequently div is surjective in Théorème 6.2.7, which completes the proof of Théorème 6.2.1.
items.locator: Lemme 6.2.12, pp. 250–251, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 6.2.13: Galois obstruction to descending Π(b)
items.statement: If F is not algebraically closed, Π(b) can be defined in P_{F̂̄}∖{0}; the obstruction to descending Π(b) to an element of P_F is an element of H^1(G_F, E^×), which is the group Pic^0(X_F) (Chapter 7).
items.locator: Remarque 6.2.13, p. 251, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof here; compare Proposition 7.2.4 and §7.8. No atlas node treats Pic^0 of the curve over a non-algebraically-closed F.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1: the Lubin–Tate logarithm as lim π^{-n}[π^n]
items.statement: Let Q ∈ O_E[X] with Q ≡ X^q mod π and Q ≡ πX mod X², and let LT_Q be the Lubin–Tate formal group law with [π]_{LT_Q} = Q. In the Fréchet space of rigid analytic functions on the one-dimensional open unit ball over E, the sequence [π^n]_{LT_Q}/π^n converges to the logarithm log_{LT_Q} of LT_Q.
items.locator: Proposition 6.3.1, pp. 251–252, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2), which uses log_G of a Lubin–Tate group but does not state this limit formula. Mathlib has only the bare FormalGroup structure (Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean); no Lubin–Tate groups or logarithms.

items.name: Remarque 6.3.2: Weierstrass product expansion of log_{LT_Q}
items.statement: If moreover Q is monic, then, grouping factors, log_{LT_Q} = X ∏_{n≥0} ∏_{ζ ∈ LT_Q[π^{n+1}]∖LT_Q[π^n]} (1 − X/ζ) (a convergent product, as in [49]); the ungrouped product over all nonzero ζ ∈ LT_Q[π^∞] does not converge since |ζ| → 1.
items.locator: Remarque 6.3.2, p. 252, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 6.3: the Weierstrass product of u_ε is a Lubin–Tate period
items.statement: For ε ∈ m_F∖{0} and u_ε = [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/q}]_Q ∈ M_1: Π^+(u_ε) = log_{LT_Q}([ε]_Q)·1/(π[ε^{1/q}]_Q), Π^−(u_ε) = [ε^{1/q}]_Q, and hence Π(u_ε) = log_{LT_Q}([ε]_Q) (up to E^×).
items.locator: no 6.3 (after Remarque 6.3.2), p. 253, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (the map from the Lubin–Tate universal cover to H^0(X,O(1))), which does not identify it with a Weierstrass product.

items.name: No 6.3: compatibility of |Y|/ϕ^Z, (P_1∖{0})/E^× and the Lubin–Tate parametrisation
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The diagram m_F∖{0} ↠ (m_F∖{0})/O_E^× ≅ |Y| ↠ |Y|/ϕ^Z ≅ (P_1∖{0})/E^× commutes with the vertical isomorphism L : m_F∖{0} ≅ (B^+)^{ϕ=π}∖{0} of Proposition 4.2.1, where m_F∖{0} → |Y| is ε ↦ (u_ε) and |Y| → (P_1∖{0})/E^× sends the ideal (a), a ∈ M_1, to Π(a)E^×.
items.locator: no 6.3, p. 253, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (R^{∘∘} ≅ H^0(X_S,O(1)) via the universal cover of the Lubin–Tate group) and VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence ((BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× ≅ Div^1) together state this parametrisation of degree-one points by nonzero degree-one sections modulo E^×; the Weierstrass-product description of the map is not stated.

items.name: Théorème 6.4.1: the generalised fundamental exact sequence
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. Let y_1,…,y_d ∈ |Y| with generators a_1,…,a_d ∈ M_1 such that y_i ∈ ϕ^Z(y_j) ⇒ y_i = y_j, and let t_i = Π(a_i) ∈ B^{ϕ=π} (1 ≤ i ≤ d). Then there is an exact sequence of E-Banach spaces 0 → E·∏_{i=1}^d t_i → B^{ϕ=π^d} → B/m_{y_1}⋯m_{y_d}B → 0.
items.locator: Théorème 6.4.1, pp. 253–254, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the case d = 1 is planned: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (0 → O → O(1) → O_{S♯} → 0; with H^1(X,O) = 0 this gives 0 → E·t → B^{ϕ=π} → C_y → 0). The several-point/higher-multiplicity version is not stated. See sourceIssues ('de gauche').

items.name: Exemple 6.4.2: Fontaine's fundamental exact sequence
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If E = Q_p, ε ∈ m_F∖{0}, Q(X) = (1+X)^p − 1, u_ε = ([1+ε]−1)/([(1+ε)^{1/p}]−1), y = (u_ε) and t_y = log([1+ε]), there is an exact sequence 0 → Q_p·t_y^d → (B^+)^{ϕ=p^d} → B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^d B^+_{dR,y} → 0; this recovers the fundamental exact sequence of [25].
items.locator: Exemple 6.4.2, p. 254, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence, whose variant (4) gives 0 → Q_p → (Fil^{-r}B_cris)^{ϕ=1} → Fil^{-r}B_dR/B_dR^+ → 0 and (Fil^r B_cris)^{ϕ=p^r} = Q_p t^r; after multiplying by t^r this becomes the present sequence only once (Fil^0 B_cris)^{ϕ=p^r} is identified with (B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^r} = (B^+)^{ϕ=p^r}, which no node states.

items.name: Corollaire 6.4.3: P/tP
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) Let t ∈ P_1, t ≠ 0, and y ∈ |Y| with div(t) = Σ_{n∈Z}[ϕ^n(y)]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras P/tP ⥲ {f ∈ C_y[T] : f(0) ∈ E}, induced in degree d by x ↦ θ_y(x)T^d.
items.locator: Corollaire 6.4.3, p. 254, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB3 fundamental-exact-sequence (degree 1) and RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map; the graded quotient is not described anywhere.

items.name: Théorème 6.4.4: ideals of A cut out by all Frobenius twists of points
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) Let y_1,…,y_d ∈ |Y| with generators a_1,…,a_d ∈ M_1 such that (as in Théorème 6.4.1) y_i ∈ ϕ^Z(y_j) ⇒ y_i = y_j, and let Π^−(a_1),…,Π^−(a_d) ∈ A∖πA be as in Définition 6.2.11. Then the ideal of A formed by the x ∈ A such that ϕ^n(x) ∈ y_1⋯y_d for all n ≥ 0 is the principal ideal generated by ϕ(Π^−(a_1)⋯Π^−(a_d)) = a_1⋯a_d·Π^−(a_1)⋯Π^−(a_d); equivalently Π^−(a_1)⋯Π^−(a_d) generates the ideal defined by the condition for all n ≥ 1. (Corrected form: the book prints 'engendré par Π^−(a_1)…Π^−(a_d)' and omits the orbit hypothesis, see E127 and E211. Generalises [25] Proposition 5.1.3, where the ideal is generated by [ε] − 1.)
items.locator: Théorème 6.4.4, p. 254, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: As printed the generator is off by one Frobenius: the correct generator is ϕ(Π^−(a_1)⋯Π^−(a_d)) = a_1⋯a_d·Π^−(a_1)⋯Π^−(a_d) (see sourceIssues). The classical case (E = Q_p, y_1 = … = y_d the cyclotomic point) is planned in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/frobenius-kernel-ideals-of-ainf ({a : ϕ^n(a) ∈ Fil^r for all n ≥ 0} = ([ε]−1)^r A_inf), which confirms the corrected form; the general statement is absent.

items.name: Définition 6.5.1: the fundamental curve X_{F,E}
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. X_{F,E} = Proj(P_{F,E,π}), an E-scheme, written X when there is no ambiguity about F or E.
items.locator: Définition 6.5.1, p. 254, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map: X_S^alg = Proj P for S affinoid perfectoid (here S = Spa F). The Proj construction itself exists in Mathlib (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Scheme.lean) but not the curve.

items.name: No 6.5.1: X_{F,E} is canonically independent of π
items.statement: Although P_{F,E,π} depends on the uniformizer π, by the isomorphism u_{π,π'} of §6.1.2 and [32] Prop. 3.1.8 (iii), the scheme X_{F,E} does not depend, canonically, on this choice.
items.locator: no 6.5.1, pp. 254–255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned: node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (FS II.2.7 and Remark II.2.8) states that 'X^alg is independent of the chosen O_X(1) up to canonical isomorphism' among line bundles satisfying its ampleness hypotheses, which O(1)_π and O(1)_{π'} do (VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation). FF's route through the explicit isomorphism u_{π,π'} of §6.1.2 and EGA II 3.1.8 (iii) is not planned (items 672, 770).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(1): X is a complete curve with all closed points of degree 1
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The scheme X is a complete curve (Définitions 5.1.1, 5.1.3: connected separated regular noetherian of dimension 1, with deg(div f) = 0 for f ∈ E(X)^×) with field of definition E (Γ(X,O_X) = E), all of whose closed points have degree 1.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(1), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9: X_C^alg connected regular noetherian of dimension 1, classical points ↔ closed points); VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism (Pic(X_C) = Z, so principal divisors have degree 0); VB1/cohomology-of-twists (H^0(X,O) = E). FF derive it from Théorème 5.2.7 via Théorèmes 6.2.1, 6.4.1, Corollaire 6.4.3.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(2): change of E
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If E'|E is a finite extension, there is a canonical isomorphism X_{E'} ⥲ X_E ⊗_E E'.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(2), p. 255 (proof p. 256), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction, which presupposes π_{E'|E}: X_{E'} → X_E and matches adjoint functors on isocrystals, but does not state X_{E'} ≅ X_E ⊗_E E'. Proof uses [32] 2.4.7(i) and §6.1.3 (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(3): the hyperplane section V^+(t) and its residue field
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) For every nonzero t ∈ P_1, V^+(t) = {∞_t}, the vanishing locus of the hyperplane section defined by t, consists of a single point. The residue field C_t of X at ∞_t is an algebraically closed complete valued field extension of E, and there is a canonical identification C_t^♭ = F.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(3), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (V(f) ∈ Div^1 is a single untilt S♯ for 0 ≠ f ∈ BC(O(1))); RF2:untilts ('At a geometric untilt identify the complete discrete valuation ring and its residue field'); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii) (K algebraically closed iff K♭ is).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(4a): closed points ↔ degree-one sections modulo E^×
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The map (P_1∖{0})/E^× → |X|, t·E^× ↦ ∞_t, is a bijection.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(4), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence ((BC(O(1))∖{0})/E^× ≅ Div^1) with VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (classical points of X_C ↔ closed points of X_C^alg).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(4b): |X| = |Y|/ϕ^Z
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) There is a natural bijection |Y|/ϕ^Z ⥲ |X| sending y mod ϕ^Z to the point ∞_t where t is such that div(t) = Σ_{n∈Z}[ϕ^n(y)].
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(4), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (classical points of X_C are |Y_C|^cl/ϕ^Z, in bijection with Div^1(C)) and VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(5a): local rings are discrete valuation rings
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) For every nonzero t ∈ P_1 the local ring O_{X,∞_t} is a discrete valuation ring.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(5), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (regular noetherian of dimension 1, hence DVR local rings at closed points).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(5b): completed local rings are B^+_dR
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If t ∈ P_1∖{0} and y ∈ |Y| satisfy div(t) = Σ_{n∈Z}[ϕ^n(y)], there is a canonical isomorphism Ô_{X,∞_t} ⥲ B^+_{dR,y}, and t is a uniformizer of B^+_{dR,y}.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(5), p. 255 (proof p. 256), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: B^+_dR at an untilt is planned (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration: a complete DVR with residue field the untilt), but no node identifies it with the completed local ring of the schematic curve Proj P.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(6): B^+ as the Frobenius-stable part of B^+_cris
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If E|Q_p is unramified, let B^+_cris(C_t) be the ring of crystalline periods of the residue field at ∞_t. There is a canonical identification B^+_F = ∩_{n≥0} ϕ^n(B^+_cris(C_t)).
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(6), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/crystalline-period-ring (A_cris, B^+_cris, B_cris) and P7/log-extended-period-rings (B̃^+_rig); the identity B^+ = ∩ϕ^n B^+_cris is not stated. FF's proof does not address this point explicitly (cf. §1.10.3).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(7a): the ring B_e
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) For t ∈ P_1∖{0} set B_e = B^+[1/t]^{ϕ=Id}; then B^+[1/t]^{ϕ=Id} = B[1/t]^{ϕ=Id}, and this equals B_cris(C_t)^{ϕ=Id} when E|Q_p is unramified.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(7), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence defines B_e := B_cris^{ϕ=1} (for C = C_p) but no node identifies it with B^+[1/t]^{ϕ=1} = B[1/t]^{ϕ=1}.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(7b): D^+(t) = Spec(B_e) and B_e is principal
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) D^+(t) = X∖{∞_t} = Spec(B_e), and B_e is a principal ideal domain.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(7), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point ('for any classical point x, X_C^alg∖{x} is the spectrum of a principal ideal domain'); VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(7c): B_e is almost Euclidean
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If ord_{∞_t} is the valuation on B_e induced by the embedding B_e ⊂ Frac(Ô_{X,∞_t}), the pair (B_e, −ord_{∞_t}) is almost Euclidean (Définition 5.2.1).
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(7), p. 255, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The notion of almost Euclidean ring does not occur in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(8): fibres of X_{E'} → X_E
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If E'|E is finite, then via the étale covering X_{E'} → X_E the inverse image of a closed point x ∈ |X_E| consists of [E':E] points with the same residue field as x.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(8), p. 256, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (π_{E'|E}); the fibre statement is absent.

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(9): Pic(X) = Z
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The degree map induces an isomorphism Pic(X) ⥲ Z.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(9), p. 256, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism: 'Pic(X_C) = Z via n ↦ O_{X_C}(n)' (for the adic curve; transfer to Proj P by VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence).

items.name: Théorème 6.5.2(10): H^1(X,O_X) = 0
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) H^1(X, O_X) = 0.
items.locator: Théorème 6.5.2(10), p. 256, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(ii): RΓ_proét(S,E) ≅ RΓ(X_S,O), so H^1(X_C,O) = 0 at a geometric point) with VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence for the schematic curve.

items.name: Corollaire 6.5.3: the tower (X_{E_h}) is a generalised Riemann sphere
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The tower of curves (X_{E_h})_{h≥1} is a generalised Riemann sphere in the sense of Définition 5.6.21.
items.locator: Corollaire 6.5.3, p. 256, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The notion of generalised Riemann sphere (Définition 5.6.21) does not occur in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 6.6.1: meromorphic functions on Y/ϕ^Z
items.statement: Let M(Y) be the field of meromorphic functions on Y (Définition 3.5.9). Set M(Y/ϕ^Z) = M(Y)^{ϕ=Id}.
items.locator: Définition 6.6.1, p. 256, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas node defines meromorphic functions on Y or their ϕ-invariants.

items.name: Proposition 6.6.2: E(X) = M(Y/ϕ^Z)
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The field M(Y/ϕ^Z) identifies with the field of rational functions E(X) (via E(X) = {x/y : x,y ∈ P homogeneous of the same degree, y ≠ 0} ⊂ Frac(P) ↪ Frac(B) = M(Y)).
items.locator: Proposition 6.6.2, p. 257, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (FS II.2.7, bundles/cohomology on X_S vs Proj); function fields are not compared.

items.name: No 6.6: description of X by valuations on M(Y/ϕ^Z)
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) The map |Y| → {valuations on M(Y/ϕ^Z)}, y ↦ ord_y|_{M(Y/ϕ^Z)}, induces an embedding |Y|/ϕ^Z ↪ {valuations on M(Y/ϕ^Z)}, which via E(X) ≅ M(Y/ϕ^Z) and |Y|/ϕ^Z ≅ |X| corresponds to x ↦ ord_x. The nonempty open subsets of X are the complements of finite subsets of |Y|/ϕ^Z, and for such an open U, Γ(U,O_X) = {f ∈ M(Y/ϕ^Z) : ord_y(f) ≥ 0 for all [y] ∈ U}.
items.locator: no 6.6 (after Proposition 6.6.2), p. 257, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 6.7: the ind-scheme lim_I Spec(B_I) with its ϕ-action
items.statement: Consider the ind-scheme lim→_I Spec(B_I), I running over the compact intervals of ]0,1[. It carries an action of ϕ by automorphisms via ϕ : Spec(B_I) ⥲ Spec(B_{ϕ^{-1}(I)}), where ϕ(ρ) = ρ^q for ρ ∈ ]0,1[.
items.locator: no 6.7, p. 258, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces layer 6.3 (interval rings B^I) and RF1 (adic quotient Y_S/ϕ^Z); the schematic ind-scheme is absent.

items.name: Proposition 6.7.1(1): X as categorical quotient of lim Spec(B_I) by ϕ^Z
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) There is a ϕ-invariant morphism of ind-schemes lim→_I Spec(B_I) → X which makes X a categorical quotient of lim→_I Spec(B_I) by ϕ^Z, in the sense that it is universal for ϕ-invariant morphisms from lim→_I Spec(B_I) to a scheme.
items.locator: Proposition 6.7.1(1), p. 258 (proof pp. 258–259), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (map of locally ringed spaces X_S → X_S^alg); no universal property is stated.

items.name: Proposition 6.7.1(2): flatness of Spec(B_I) → X
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) For every compact I ⊂ ]0,1[ the morphism Spec(B_I) → X is flat; it is faithfully flat if I = [ρ_1,ρ_2] with ρ_1 ≤ ρ_2^q.
items.locator: Proposition 6.7.1(2), p. 258, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 6.7.2: X is an fpqc quotient of Spec(B_I)
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) If I is sufficiently large, X is an fpqc quotient of Spec(B_I); there does not seem to be a simple description of the equivalence relation Spec(B_I) ×_X Spec(B_I) on Spec(B_I).
items.locator: Remarque 6.7.2, p. 259, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.1.1: B^+_{dR,z}, its Galois action and canonical Banach structures
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Let y ∈ |Y_F| and z ∈ |Y_{F̂̄}| with β(z) = y (Ch. 3), with residue fields K_y ⊂ C_z = K̂̄_y (Théorème 3.3.1). The complete DVRs B^+_{dR,z} (residue field C_z) and B^+_{dR,y} (residue field K_y); Gal(K̄_y|K_y) acts on B^+_{dR,z}; Fil^k B^+_{dR,z} is the k-th power of the maximal ideal. Every B^+_{dR,z}-module of finite length is canonically an E-Banach space: for k ≥ 0 the Fréchet topology of B_{F̂̄} induces via the surjection B_{F̂̄} → B^+_{dR,z}/Fil^k B^+_{dR,z} a quotient topology which is Banach, making it a successive extension of the E-Banach space C_z. A finite type B^+_{dR,z}-module W with semilinear Gal(K̄_y|K_y)-action is called continuous if the induced action on each Banach space W/Fil^k B^+_{dR,z}W (k ≥ 0) is continuous.
items.locator: no 7.1.1, pp. 261–262, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-natural-topology (natural topology and continuous G_K-action on B_dR^+ for C = C_p, K/Q_p finite) and RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration (B^+_dR at an untilt); neither treats Gal(K̄_y|K_y) for a perfectoid residue field K_y of the curve nor the Banach structure on finite-length quotients.

items.name: Proposition 7.1.1(1): Galois invariants of B^+_{dR,z}
items.statement: (Notation of no 7.1.1.) B^+_{dR,y} = (B^+_{dR,z})^{Gal(K̄_y|K_y)}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.1(1), p. 262 (no proof: 'standard' application of Proposition 3.2.2 and the Sen–Tate method), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants (C^{G_K} = K for K/Q_p finite); nothing for B^+_dR over a general perfectoid K_y.

items.name: Proposition 7.1.1(2): vanishing of H^1 for finite-length B^+_dR-modules
items.statement: (Notation of no 7.1.1.) If W is a B^+_{dR,z}-module of finite length with a continuous semilinear action of Gal(K̄_y|K_y), then H^1(Gal(K̄_y|K_y), W) = 0 (continuous cohomology).
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.1(2), p. 262 (no proof given), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-vanishing-on-hk (H^n_cont(H_K, W) = 0 for C-representations: the special case K_y = K̂_∞, length one) and PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iv) (almost étaleness, the input to Tate's method).

items.name: Proposition 7.1.1(3): Galois descent for B^+_dR-modules
items.statement: (Notation of no 7.1.1.) The functor V ↦ V ⊗_{B^+_{dR,y}} B^+_{dR,z} induces an equivalence between finite type B^+_{dR,y}-modules and finite type B^+_{dR,z}-modules equipped with a continuous semilinear action of Gal(K̄_y|K_y); a quasi-inverse is W ↦ W^{Gal(K̄_y|K_y)}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.1(3), p. 262 (no proof given), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: R06.1/tate-sen-vanishing-on-hk (W = C ⊗ W^{H_K}) and R06.1/semilinear-galois-descent; not for B^+_dR-modules over a general perfectoid field.

items.name: No 7.1.2 (proof): Tate-type vanishing for the Lubin–Tate filtration
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Let U = G(O_{F̂̄}) = (m_{F̂̄}, +_{LT}) for a Lubin–Tate group G over O_E, U_ρ = (m_{F̂̄,ρ}, +_{LT}) with m_{F̂̄,ρ} = {x ∈ m_{F̂̄} : |x| < ρ} (so πU_ρ = U_{ρ^q} and U_ρ/U_{ρ²} ≅ (m_{F̂̄,ρ}/m_{F̂̄,ρ²}, +)), and Λ a G_F-stable lattice in a continuous finite-dimensional E-representation V. Then (Lemme 3.1.1 and Tate's method) H^i(G_F, m_{F̂̄,ρ} ⊗_{F_q} Λ/πΛ) = 0 for i > 0, hence H^1(G_F, (U_{ρ^{2^n}}⊗Λ)/(U_{ρ^{2^{n+1}}}⊗Λ)) = 0; and H^0(G_F, (U_ρ⊗Λ)/(U_{ρ²}⊗Λ)) ≠ 0.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.1.2, pp. 263–264, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iv) (almost étale) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-vanishing-on-hk; no characteristic-p statement of this form. The proof's H^0 step writes V_ρ(χ) for U_ρ ⊗ Λ (a notational leftover).

items.name: Proposition 7.1.2(1): vanishing of H^1(G_F, B^{ϕ=π^d} ⊗ V)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Fix a uniformizer π of E. For every continuous representation ρ : G_F → GL(V) on a finite-dimensional E-vector space and every d > 0, H^1(G_F, B^{ϕ=π^d}_{F̂̄} ⊗_E V) = 0, the cohomology being continuous cohomology for the Banach structure of B^{ϕ=π^d}_{F̂̄} (§4.1.2).
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.2, p. 262 (proof pp. 263–264), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (VB1 v-descent of bundle cohomology concerns sheaf cohomology, not continuous Galois cohomology of Banach–Colmez spaces).

items.name: Proposition 7.1.2(2): nonvanishing of H^0(G_F, B^{ϕ=π^d} ⊗ V)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For every continuous representation G_F → GL(V) on a nonzero finite-dimensional E-vector space V and every d > 0, H^0(G_F, B^{ϕ=π^d}_{F̂̄} ⊗_E V) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.2, p. 262 (proof p. 264), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.2: the graded algebras P_{F,π}, P_{F̂̄,π} and the rings B_{F,e}, B_{F̂̄,e}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For a uniformizer π of E put P_{F,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} B_F^{ϕ=π^d} (also written P_{F,E,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} B_E^{ϕ_E=π^d}, §7.3) and P_{F̂̄,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} B_{F̂̄}^{ϕ=π^d}. For nonzero t ∈ P_{F,π,1} put B_{F,e} = B_F[1/t]^{ϕ=Id} = P_{F,π}[1/t]_0 and B_{F̂̄,e} = B_{F̂̄}[1/t]^{ϕ=Id} = P_{F̂̄,π}[1/t]_0.
items.locator: no 7.2, p. 264 (and no 7.3, p. 266), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map applies to any affinoid perfectoid S, in particular S = Spa(F) for F not algebraically closed, and uses the degree-0 localisations P[g^{-1}]_0.

items.name: No 7.2: Galois descent of P (Théorème 3.6.1)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). P_{F,π} = (P_{F̂̄,π})^{G_F}; consequently B_{F,e} = (B_{F̂̄,e})^{G_F}.
items.locator: no 7.2, p. 264 (from Théorème 3.6.1; B^{G_F}_{F̂̄,e} = B_{F,e} used in pp. 264–266, 270), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Would follow from VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology (cohomology of bundles is a v-sheaf) applied to Spa F̂̄ → Spa F, but no node states the Galois-invariants identity.

items.name: No 7.2 (proof of Proposition 7.2.1): quotients of B_{F,e} by principal ideals
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Let f ∈ B_{F,e}, f ∉ E^× ∪ {0}, written f = x/t^k with x ∈ P_{F,π,k}∖tP_{F,π,k−1}. Then B_{F,e}/B_{F,e}f = (B_{F̂̄,e}/B_{F̂̄,e}f)^{G_F} ≃ ∏_{[y]∈|Y_F|/ϕ^Z} B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^{ord_y(x)}B^+_{dR,y} (a finite product), using B_{F̂̄,e}/B_{F̂̄,e}f ≃ ∏_{[y]} ∏_{[z]∈|Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F-fin}/ϕ^Z, [β(z)]=[y]} B^+_{dR,z}/Fil^{ord_y(x)}B^+_{dR,z} and lim→_d H^1(G_F, B^{deg≤d}_{F̂̄,e}) = 0.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.2.1, pp. 264–265, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.1: B_{F,e} is a Dedekind domain
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The ring B_{F,e} is a Dedekind domain.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.1, p. 264, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the algebraically closed case is planned: VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains and VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (PID complements). The notion is Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.

items.name: Lemme 7.2.2: a criterion for Dedekind domains
items.statement: An integral domain A is a Dedekind domain if and only if for every nonzero a ∈ A, A/(a) is isomorphic to a (finite) product of discrete valuation rings each quotiented by a power of its maximal ideal.
items.locator: Lemme 7.2.2, p. 265 (no proof given), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has other criteria (isDedekindDomain_iff, isDedekindDomain_iff_isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime: noetherian with DVR localisations) but not this one; not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.3: maximal ideals and completions of B_{F,e}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). There is a bijection (|Y_F|∖V(t))/ϕ^Z → Spm(B_{F,e}), [y] ↦ {f ∈ B_{F,e} : f(y) = 0}. Moreover, if the maximal ideal m corresponds to [y], there is a canonical isomorphism from the m-adic completion (B_{F,e})^_m to B^+_{dR,y}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.3, p. 265, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Algebraically closed analogue planned in VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains (maximal ideals ↔ classical points); no completion statement, nothing for general F.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.4: Cl(B_{F,e}) ≅ Hom(G_F, E^×)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The ideal class group of the Dedekind domain B_{F,e} is Cl(B_{F,e}) ≃ Hom(G_F, E^×) (continuous characters): to a nonzero ideal I one attaches the character χ with f^σ = χ(σ)f, where B_{F̂̄,e}I = (f); moreover every ideal I satisfies I = (B_{F̂̄,e}I)^{G_F}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.4, p. 265 (proof pp. 265–266), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (the notion is Mathlib's ClassGroup; no Pic^0 of the curve over a non-closed F is planned).

items.name: No 7.3 (proof of Proposition 7.3.1): degree-one sections over F
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Let t ∈ B_F^{ϕ=π} be nonzero and y ∈ |Y_F| with div(t) = Σ_{n∈Z}[ϕ^n(y)]. There is an exact sequence 0 → E·t → B_F^{ϕ=π} → K_y (the last map θ_y); B_F^{ϕ=π} is an infinite-dimensional E-Banach space (the O_F-points of a Lubin–Tate group over F_q), so there exists s ∈ B_F^{ϕ=π} with θ_y(s) ≠ 0.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.3.1, pp. 266–267, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (0 → O → O(1) → O_{S♯} → 0 for any perfectoid S with untilt; global sections give 0 → E·t → H^0(O(1)) → K_y) and lubin-tate-universal-cover (H^0(X_S,O(1)) ≅ R^{∘∘}).

items.name: Proposition 7.3.1: P_{F,E,π} is generated in degree 1
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The graded algebra P_{F,E,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} B_E^{ϕ_E=π^d} is generated by its homogeneous elements of degree 1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.3.1, p. 266 (proof pp. 266–267), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation (sufficiently positive twists are globally generated), which is a different statement; generation of P in degree 1 is not stated.

items.name: Remarque 7.3.2: non-factorisation when F is not algebraically closed
items.statement: If F is not algebraically closed, there exist homogeneous elements of degree > 1 of the graded algebra P_F that are not products of elements of degree 1.
items.locator: Remarque 7.3.2, p. 267, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.3: the curve X_{F,E} for F perfect
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Set X_{F,E} = Proj(P_{F,E,π}). If F contains an algebraic closure of F_q, it is canonically independent of π by §6.1.2 (a π-free description for all F is given in §7.4). By Proposition 7.3.1, X_F = ⋃_{t ∈ P_{F,1}∖{0}} D^+(t).
items.locator: no 7.3, p. 267, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (X_S^alg = Proj P for any affinoid perfectoid S, including Spa F).

items.name: Théorème 7.3.3(1): X_{F,E} is a curve
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The scheme X_{F,E} is a curve (Définition 5.1.1: connected separated noetherian regular of dimension 1).
items.locator: Théorème 7.3.3(1), p. 267, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point covers only algebraically closed C; the stage text restricts to 'S a geometric perfectoid point'.

items.name: Théorème 7.3.3(2): |X_{F,E}| = |Y_{F,E}|/ϕ^Z
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). There is a bijection u : |Y_{F,E}|/ϕ^Z ⥲ |X_{F,E}| sending the class of y ∈ |Y_{F,E}| to the homogeneous ideal whose homogeneous elements of degree d are the f ∈ P_{F,E,π,d} ⊂ B_F with f(y) = 0.
items.locator: Théorème 7.3.3(2), p. 268, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the algebraically closed case is planned (VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains).

items.name: Théorème 7.3.3(3): X_{F,E} is a complete curve
