items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Setting deg(x) = deg(y) for x = u([y]) ∈ |X_F|, X_{F,E} becomes a complete curve (Définition 5.1.3) with field of definition E.
items.locator: Théorème 7.3.3(3), p. 268, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the algebraically closed case is planned (VB2:ampleness, VB1).

items.name: Théorème 7.3.3(4): completed local rings of X_F
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). If u([y]) = x, there is a canonical isomorphism Ô_{X_F,x} ⥲ B^+_{dR,y}.
items.locator: Théorème 7.3.3(4), p. 268, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (see Théorème 6.5.2(5b)).

items.name: Proposition 7.4.1: E(X) = M(Y/ϕ^Z) for F perfect
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The field of rational functions E(X_F) identifies with M(Y_F/ϕ^Z) = M(Y_F)^{ϕ=Id}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.4.1, p. 268, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.4: π-free description of X_{F,E}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). As in §6.6, X_{F,E} is described in terms of M(Y_{F,E}/ϕ^Z) and the valuations ord_y, y ∈ |Y_{F,E}|; consequently X_{F,E} does not depend, canonically, on the choice of the uniformizer π.
items.locator: no 7.4 (after Proposition 7.4.1), p. 268, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The π-free description via M(Y/ϕ^Z) is not in the atlas. The π-independence alone is covered for F ⊇ F̄_q by node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence ('X^alg is independent of the chosen O_X(1) up to canonical isomorphism').

items.name: Proposition 7.5.1: X_E ⊗_E E' = X_{E'}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For a finite extension E'|E there is a canonical identification X_E ⊗_E E' = X_{E'}; in particular E(X_E) ⊗_E E' = E'(X_{E'}).
items.locator: Proposition 7.5.1, p. 269, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (presupposes π_{E'|E}). The proof as written relies on B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_E E', valid only for E'|E totally ramified (see sourceIssues); implicitly the residue field of E' must embed in F.

items.name: Proposition 7.6.1: X_L → X_F is a finite étale Galois cover
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For a finite Galois extension L|F, the action of Gal(L|F) on X_L makes X_L a finite étale Galois covering of X_F with group Gal(L|F), and X_F = X_L/Gal(L|F). Hence there is a pro-Galois covering (X_L)_{L|F} → X_F with group G_F, L running over the finite extensions of F in F̄.
items.locator: Proposition 7.6.1, p. 270, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (tilting equivalence of finite extensions) and FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 (finite étale sites of X_F); neither states that X_L → X_F is Galois with group Gal(L|F).

items.name: Définition 7.7.1: the curve X_{F̄,E}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). X_{F̄,E} := lim←_{L|F} X_{L,E} (projective limit in the category of schemes), L running over the finite extensions of F contained in F̄.
items.locator: Définition 7.7.1, p. 270, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 7.7.2: X_{F̄} is a (noetherian) curve
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). The scheme X_{F̄} is a curve with field of definition E; in particular it is noetherian.
items.locator: Proposition 7.7.2, p. 271, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 7.7.3: colimits of Dedekind rings along inert étale extensions
items.statement: Let (B_i)_i be an inductive system of Dedekind rings such that for i ≤ j the map B_i → B_j is finite étale. Assume that for every index i and every maximal ideal p of B_i there exists j ≥ i such that every q ∈ Spm(B_j) above p is inert in B_k|B_j for all k ≥ j (i.e. B_k q is a prime ideal of B_k). Then lim→_i B_i is a Dedekind ring.
items.locator: Lemme 7.7.3, p. 271, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: No 7.7: the tower X_{F̂̄} → X_{F̄} → X_F
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). There are G_F-equivariant morphisms of curves X_{F̂̄} → X_{F̄} → X_F, where X_{F̄} → X_F is pro-Galois with group G_F and |X_F| = |X_{F̄}|/G_F = |X_{F̂̄}|^{G_F-fin}/G_F. Via X_{F̂̄} → X_{F̄}, the closed points whose G_F-orbit is infinite are sent to the generic point of X_{F̄}.
items.locator: no 7.7 (after Lemme 7.7.3), p. 271, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.8: ϕ-modules over B, Pic(ϕ-Mod_B) and degree
items.statement: ϕ-Mod_B is the category of pairs (M, ϕ) with M a finitely generated projective B-module and ϕ : M → M a ϕ-linear isomorphism (the book prints 'endomorphisme'; bijectivity is needed, cf. Ch. 11 and E135); it is a tensor category with duals, internal Homs and unit 1 = (B, ϕ); H^0(M,ϕ) = M^{ϕ=Id}. I is the class of invertible objects, i.e. the (M,ϕ) with M of rank one, and Pic(ϕ-Mod_B) = I/≃ is a group under ⊗. For F algebraically closed and M = B·e with ϕ(e) = λe, λ ∈ B^× = (B^b)^×, the integer v_π(λ) does not depend on e and deg(M,ϕ) := −v_π(λ); for general F the degree is defined after extending scalars from B_F to B_{F̂̄}. Pic^0(ϕ-Mod_B) denotes the kernel of deg : Pic(ϕ-Mod_B) → Z.
items.locator: no 7.8, pp. 271–272, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign (O(n) from isocrystals, sign convention) and VB1 (bundles vs finite projective modules on annuli with Frobenius descent); ϕ-modules over the Fréchet ring B and their Picard group are not stated.

items.name: No 7.8: Pic^0(ϕ-Mod_B) ≅ Hom(G_F, E^×)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). deg : Pic(ϕ-Mod_B) → Z is a surjective group morphism and Pic^0(ϕ-Mod_B) ⥲ Hom(G_F, E^×) (continuous characters). In detail: if F is algebraically closed every rank-one ϕ-module over B of degree 0 is isomorphic to 1; for general F and L ∈ I_F of degree 0, H^0(L ⊗_{B_F} B_{F̂̄}) is a 1-dimensional E-vector space and the G_F-action on it defines the character; the inverse sends χ to (B_{F̂̄}(χ)^{G_F}, ϕ).
items.locator: no 7.8, p. 272 (relies on Chapter 11), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.8: section algebras of positive rank-one ϕ-modules
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For L ∈ I of degree k > 0, after fixing an isomorphism L ⊗_{B_F} B_{F̂̄} ≃ (B_{F̂̄}, π^{−k}ϕ), there is a continuous character χ : G_F → E^× such that ⊕_{d≥0} H^0(L^{⊗d}) ≅ ⊕_{d≥0} (B_{F̂̄}^{ϕ=π^{kd}}(χ^d))^{G_F}.
items.locator: no 7.8, p. 272, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 7.8.1: multiplication of sections of positive ϕ-line bundles is surjective
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For L_1, L_2 ∈ I of degree > 0, the map H^0(L_1) ⊗_E H^0(L_2) → H^0(L_1 ⊗ L_2) is surjective. In particular ⊕_{d≥0} H^0(L^{⊗d}) is generated by its elements of degree 1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.8.1, p. 273, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. See sourceIssues (gap in the deduction of point (2)).

items.name: Proposition 7.8.2: X = Proj of the section algebra of any positive ϕ-line bundle
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). For L ∈ I of degree > 0 there is an identification X = Proj(⊕_{d≥0} H^0(L^{⊗d})).
items.locator: Proposition 7.8.2, p. 273 (proof pp. 273–274), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF3 (Proj of the section algebra of O(1)); independence of the ample ϕ-line bundle is not stated in this generality. Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence gives independence of X^alg from the chosen line bundle among those satisfying its global-generation and vanishing hypotheses, but those hypotheses are planned only for the O(n) (VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation), not for an arbitrary positive ϕ-line bundle over a non-algebraically-closed F.

items.name: Exemple 7.8.3: X = Proj ⊕ B^{ϕ=λ^d}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 7: F is perfect (complete valued, characteristic p), not necessarily algebraically closed; F̄ an algebraic closure, F̂̄ its completion, G_F = Gal(F̄|F). Let λ ∈ B^× = (B^b)^× with v_π(λ) > 0. Then X = Proj(⊕_{d≥0} B^{ϕ=λ^d}).
items.locator: Exemple 7.8.3, p. 274, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: No 7.9: the Lubin–Tate parametrisation L : m_F ≅ B^{ϕ=π}
items.statement: The map L : m_F → B^{ϕ=π}, x ↦ Σ_{n∈Z} [x^{q^{−n}}]π^n, is a bijection (the period isomorphism G(O_F) ≅ P_{F,1} of a Lubin–Tate group G, recalled also in the proof of Proposition 7.1.2).
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.9.1, p. 274 (also p. 263), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover: 'X ↦ Σ_{i∈Z} π^i[X^{q^{-i}}] defines a natural isomorphism G̃(R^{♯+}) = R^{∘∘} → H^0(X_S,O(1)) = H^0(Y_S,O_{Y_S})^{ϕ=π}' — the same formula.

items.name: No 7.9: local estimate for L on an annulus
items.statement: If ρ ∈ ]0,1[, x ∈ F and α ∈ ]0,1[ satisfy ρ^{q/(q−1)}α^{−2} ≤ |x| ≤ α²ρ^{1/(q−1)}, then L(x) = [x](1 + u(x)) with |u(x)|_ρ ≤ α.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 7.9.1, pp. 274–275, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 7.9.1: Runge-type density of B_e in B_I
items.statement: Let I be a compact interval of ]0,1[ with endpoints in |F^×| such that I ∩ ϕ(I) = ∅ (ϕ(ρ) = ρ^q), and t ∈ B^{ϕ=π} (nonzero) with supp(div(t)) ∩ |Y_I| = ∅. Let B_e = B[1/t]^{ϕ=Id}. Then the inclusion B_e ⊂ B_I has dense image.
items.locator: Proposition 7.9.1, p. 274 (proof pp. 274–276), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (AdicSpaces layer 6.3 constructs the interval rings B^I; RF3 maps X_S → X_S^alg but no density statement).

items.name: Corollaire 7.9.2: recovering Y/ϕ^Z from the schematic curve
items.statement: One can recover the analytic curve 'Y/ϕ^Z' from the normed ringed space (X, O_X, (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈]0,1[}).
items.locator: Corollaire 7.9.2, p. 276, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map and VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (analytic ↔ algebraic comparison in the other direction).

items.name: External ([32] EGA II Prop. 3.1.8 (iii)): Proj is unchanged by an invertible twist of the grading
items.statement: For a graded algebra S = ⊕_{d≥0} S_d over a base and an invertible module L, Proj(⊕_{d≥0} S_d ⊗ L^{⊗d}) is canonically isomorphic to Proj(S) (as used to show X_{F,E} is independent of π).
items.locator: black box used in no 6.5.1, p. 254 ('[32] prop. 3.1.8, (iii)'), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib has AlgebraicGeometry.Proj but no twist-invariance statement; not in the atlas.

items.name: External ([32] EGA II 2.4.7 (i)): Veronese invariance of Proj
items.statement: For a graded ring S and an integer e ≥ 1, Proj(S^{(e)}) ≅ Proj(S) canonically, where S^{(e)} = ⊕_{n≥0} S_{ne} (as used for P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•} in Théorème 6.5.2(2), and implicitly in Proposition 7.8.2).
items.locator: black box used in the proof of Théorème 6.5.2(2), p. 256 ('[32] 2.4.7 (i)'); also p. 273, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not found in Mathlib (no Veronese subring/Proj comparison in declarations.tsv); not in the atlas.

items.name: External ([1] SGA 1 exp. V cor. 2.4): quotients by finite groups with trivial inertia are étale
items.statement: If a finite group G acts on a scheme X (admissibly, so that X/G exists) and all inertia groups are trivial, then X → X/G is a finite étale Galois covering with group G.
items.locator: black box used in the proof of Proposition 7.6.1, p. 270, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib; the atlas has only the adic/perfectoid analogue PerfectoidSpaces:P8/free-action-quotient-is-torsor.

items.name: External: roots of polynomials over the algebraically closed field F
items.statement: Every nonconstant polynomial over the algebraically closed field F has a root; in particular every element of F^× is a (q−1)-th power and the equations X^{q−1} = b_0 and U^q − b_0U + z = 0 (b_0, z ∈ O_F, b_0 ≠ 0) have solutions (in O_F).
items.locator: black box used in the proof of Proposition 6.2.10, p. 249, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: IsAlgClosed.exists_root (p.degree ≠ 0 ⇒ ∃ root) and IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq (∃ z, z^n = x), Mathlib/FieldTheory/IsAlgClosed/Basic.lean lines 78, 81. Integrality of the roots (O_F integrally closed) is separate.

items.name: §8.1.1: the Lubin–Tate deformation space of a one-dimensional formal O_E-module
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let F̄_q be the algebraic closure of F_q in F, n ≥ 1, and 𝐇 a π-divisible formal O_E-module of dimension 1 and O_E-height n over F̄_q (unique up to non-unique isomorphism). Its covariant O-Dieudonné module D_O(𝐇), with V induced by the isogeny F_{𝐇}: 𝐇 → 𝐇^{(q)}, is D_O(𝐇) = ⟨e, Ve, …, V^{n−1}e⟩ with V^n e = πe. Let Ĕ = W_{O_E}(F̄_q)_Q and let 𝔛 be the formal Spf(O_Ĕ)-scheme of deformations of 𝐇 by isomorphisms; non-canonically 𝔛 ≅ Spf O_Ĕ⟦x_1,…,x_{n−1}⟧, and its Berkovich generic fibre 𝔛^an is an open ball of dimension n−1. For every complete valued extension K|Ĕ (real-valued valuation), 𝔛^an(K) = 𝔛(O_K) = {(H, ρ)}/≅ where H is a π-divisible O-module over O_K and ρ: 𝐇 ⊗_{F̄_q} O_K/pO_K → H ⊗_{O_K} O_K/pO_K is a height-0 quasi-isogeny.
items.locator: §8.1.1, p. 278, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Missing in the stated generality: FF take E any nonarchimedean local field (Chapter 8 standing hypotheses), while the Lubin–Tate deformation space is planned only for E/Q_p finite. ET.6a: 'Starting with the existing formal-module/p-divisible-group deformation owners, construct the Lubin–Tate tower with its GL_n(E), D× and W_E actions' — restricted to E/Q_p finite; FF allow E of characteristic p. The Lubin–Tate/Hazewinkel uniqueness and the power-series description of 𝔛 are used as black boxes by FF. Also planned for E/Q_p: 'universal formal-module deformations at finite height' in the accepted Part II LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts (PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21, route 2), and Rapoport–Zink spaces of p-divisible groups with the Lubin–Tate case as a test in the accepted Part II HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasIntegralPartII (PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20, route 4).

items.name: §8.1.1: universal vector O-extension, Hodge filtration and the Gross–Hopkins period morphism π̆: 𝔛^an → P
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let P be the Berkovich Ĕ-analytic space of the projective space of D_O(𝐇). For K|Ĕ complete and [(H,ρ)] ∈ 𝔛^an(K), the universal vector O-extension E_O(H) ([18] App. B.3) has Lie algebra Lie E_O(H), a free O_K-module of rank ht_O(H), with Hodge filtration 0 → V_O(H) → Lie E_O(H) → Lie H → 0, where V_O(H) = ω_{H^D}/I·ω_{H^D} (H^D the Cartier dual, I = ker(O_K ⊗_{Z_p} O_E → O_K)); D_O(𝐇) is the value of the Lie-algebra crystal of E_O, and ρ induces ρ_*: D_O(𝐇)[1/π] ⊗_Ĕ K ≅ Lie E_O(H)[1/π]. The period morphism π̆: 𝔛^an → P (Gross–Hopkins [29], Rapoport–Zink [54] ch. 5) sends [(H,ρ)] to the point of P(K) defined through ρ_* by the Hodge filtration.
items.locator: §8.1.1, pp. 278–279, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No stage or node constructs the de Rham (Gross–Hopkins / Rapoport–Zink) period morphism on the Lubin–Tate space or the universal vector O-extension. ET.6a names 'period morphisms' only for the Drinfeld tower; HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 builds the Hodge–Tate map; FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2 is Dieudonné theory over perfect fields.

items.name: Théorème 8.1.1 (Laffaille [48], Gross–Hopkins [29]): surjectivity of the Lubin–Tate period morphism
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The period morphism π̆: 𝔛^an → P is surjective. Concretely: for every complete valued K|Ĕ and every y ∈ P(K) there are a finite extension L|K and x ∈ 𝔛^an(L) with π̆(x) = y.
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.1, p. 279, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External black box (proved in [48] for K discretely valued and E = Q_p, 'les arguments s'adaptent aussitôt'; also from [29] Cor. 23.15). No atlas stage states the image of the Lubin–Tate period map (admissible = weakly admissible locus).

items.name: Théorème 8.1.2 (a): p-adic Hodge-theoretic form of Gross–Hopkins — surjectivity and kernel
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let C|E be a complete algebraically closed valued field with C^♭ = F, i.e. C = C_y for some y ∈ |Y|, let n ≥ 1 and λ_0,…,λ_{n−1} ∈ C not all zero. Then the E-linear map B_{F,E}^{φ^n=π} → C, x ↦ Σ_{i=0}^{n−1} λ_i θ_y(φ^i(x)), is surjective and its kernel V is an E-vector space of dimension n.
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.2, p. 279, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated as a translation of Théorème 8.1.1, no proof. Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2, the height-one case B^{φ=π} = universal cover of the Lubin–Tate group), which does not cover height n or the λ-combinations.

items.name: Théorème 8.1.2 (b): the associated modification is injective with cokernel killed by t
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. In the situation of 8.1.2(a), let t ∈ B_{F,E} be the period of a π-divisible formal O-module of dimension 1 and height 1 over O_C (a Lubin–Tate group), so div(t) = Σ_{k∈Z}[φ^k(y)] ∈ Div^+(Y_{F,E}). Then the B_{F,E}-linear map V ⊗_E B_{F,E} → B_{F,E}^n, v ⊗ 1 ↦ (v, φ(v), …, φ^{n−1}(v)), is injective with cokernel killed by t.
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.2, p. 279, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No proof in the text; equivalent (via Prop. 8.3.2) to a modification V ⊗ O_X ↪ O_X(1/n) with cokernel of length 1 at ∞. Not in the atlas. The printed formula has a variable slip (x for v), see source issues.

items.name: §8.1.2: the division algebra D of invariant 1/n and its maximal order
items.statement: D is the central division algebra over E of invariant 1/n: D = E_n[Π], where E_n|E is the unramified extension of degree n (residue field F_{q^n}), Π is a uniformizer of D, Π^n = π and Πx = σ(x)Π for x ∈ E_n; O_D = O_{E_n}[Π] is its maximal order.
items.locator: §8.1.2, p. 279, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra gives the presentation D_λ = E_h[Π], Π^h = π^d, Πx = σ_E(x)Π, which for λ = 1/n is this D; the Brauer-invariant identification is an open obligation there. The text writes D = O_{E_n}[Π] and W_{O_E}(F_{q^n}) = E_n (ring for field), see source issues.

items.name: §8.1.2: special formal O_D-module (Drinfeld)
items.statement: Let S be an O_E-scheme on which p is (locally) nilpotent, or a formal Spf(O_E)-scheme. A special formal O_D-module over S is a π-divisible formal O-module G over S with an action of O_D such that Lie G is a locally free O_{E_n} ⊗_{O_E} O_S-module of rank 1; equivalently, étale-locally on S (it suffices to pass to S ⊗_{O_E} O_{E_n} → S), writing Lie G = ⊕_{τ: O_{E_n} ↪ O_S} (Lie G)_τ with O_{E_n} acting on (Lie G)_τ through τ, each (Lie G)_τ is a locally free O_S-module of rank 1.
items.locator: §8.1.2, p. 280, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:equal-characteristic/special-formal-modules states the definition (Hausberger 2005, Def. 3.1) for E = F_q((t)) only; ET.6a builds the Drinfeld tower for E/Q_p without stating the definition. FF cite Drinfeld [14] here; the correct reference is [15] (source issue).

items.name: §8.1.2: grading of the Dieudonné module of a special formal O_D-module; the degree-0 isocrystal is unit
items.statement: Let can: E_n ↪ W_O(F̄_q)_Q be the canonical embedding and G a special formal O_D-module over F̄_q. Its covariant O-Dieudonné module decomposes as D_O(G) = ⊕_{i∈Z/nZ} D_O(G)_i, with O_{E_n} acting on D_O(G)_i via σ^{−i}∘can, and V and Π are homogeneous of degree +1; Lie G = ⊕_{i∈Z/nZ} D_O(G)_i/V·D_O(G)_{i−1}, each graded piece a 1-dimensional F̄_q-vector space. If G has O-height n² (D_O(G)_0 free of rank n over W_O(F̄_q)), then for every lattice M ⊂ D_O(G)_0, with Λ = ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Π^i M, one has n = dim G = [Λ : VΛ] = n[V^{−1}ΠM : M] + [M : πM], hence [V^{−1}ΠM : M] = 0; there is i_0 ∈ {0,…,n−1} with Π·D_O(G)_{i_0} = V·D_O(G)_{i_0}, and Π^{−i_0}D_O(G)_{i_0} is a V^{−1}Π-stable lattice. Consequently the O-isocrystal (D_O(G)_0[1/π], V^{−1}Π) is unit, i.e. isoclinic of slope 0.
items.locator: §8.1.2, pp. 280–281, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Proved in the text by the index computation (checked). No atlas node on the Dieudonné theory of special formal O_D-modules (ES7:equal-characteristic uses Hausberger's formal-module theory, not this Dieudonné computation).

items.name: §8.1.2: special formal O_D-modules of height n² up to isogeny ↔ unit isocrystals ↔ n-dimensional E-vector spaces
items.statement: The functor G ↦ (D_O(G)_0[1/π], V^{−1}Π) induces an equivalence between special formal O_D-modules of O-height n² over F̄_q up to isogeny and unit O-isocrystals; consequently G ↦ D_O(G)_0[1/π]^{V=Π} induces an equivalence between special formal O_D-modules (of height n²) over F̄_q up to isogeny and E-vector spaces of dimension n.
items.locator: §8.1.2, pp. 280–281, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Asserted ('On montre alors'), no proof. The ES7:equal-characteristic node records only that all special formal O_D-modules of height d² over an algebraically closed extension of F_{q^d} are isogenous (equal characteristic).

items.name: §8.1.2: Drinfeld's formal scheme Ω̂ and the period morphism π̆: Ω → P(W)
items.statement: Fix a special formal O_D-module 𝐆 of height n² over F̄_q and W = D_O(𝐆)_0[1/π]^{V=Π}, an n-dimensional E-vector space. Ω̂ is the formal Spf(O_Ĕ)-scheme parametrizing deformations of 𝐆 by height-0 quasi-isogenies, Ω = Ω̂^an its Berkovich generic fibre, and P the Berkovich space of P(W)_Ĕ. For K|Ĕ complete and [(G,ρ)] ∈ Ω̂(O_K) = Ω(K) (G special over O_K, ρ: 𝐆 ⊗ O_K/pO_K → G ⊗ O_K/pO_K a height-0 quasi-isogeny), Lie E_O(G) = ⊕_{i∈Z/nZ} Lie E_O(G)_i (E_n acting via can∘σ^{−i}), the Hodge filtration is graded with Π homogeneous of degree +1, and ρ induces a graded isomorphism ρ_*: D_O(𝐆)[1/π] ⊗_Ĕ K ≅ Lie E_O(G)[1/π], whose degree-0 part is W ⊗_E K = D_O(𝐆)_0[1/π] ⊗_Ĕ K ≅ Lie E_O(G)_0[1/π]. The Hodge filtration gives a surjection W ⊗_E K ↠ (Lie G)_0[1/π], i.e. a point π̆([(G,ρ)]) ∈ P(K).
items.locator: §8.1.2, p. 281, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: ET.6a: 'Construct the Drinfeld tower and its level maps, period morphisms' (E/Q_p); ES7:equal-characteristic/special-formal-modules states representability of the moduli problem by Ω̂^d ⊗̂ Ô^nr for E = F_q((t)). Neither states the graded Hodge-filtration description of the period point.

items.name: Théorème 8.1.3 (Drinfeld): the Drinfeld period morphism is an isomorphism onto the complement of the E-rational hyperplanes
items.statement: The period morphism π̆: Ω → P induces an isomorphism between Ω and the open subspace P ∖ ⋃_{H ∈ P̌(W)(E)} H^an of P, the complement of the E-rational hyperplanes in the analytic projective space on the E-vector space W. (Remarque 8.1.4: Laffaille [47] also computes this image.)
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.3 and Remarque 8.1.4, p. 282, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: External black box. ES7:equal-characteristic/special-formal-modules gives representability by Ω̂^d in equal characteristic only and not the period-morphism identification; ET.6a constructs period morphisms but states no image theorem. FF cite [14] (Drinfeld, 'Elliptic modules'); the correct source is [15] (source issue).

items.name: Théorème 8.1.5 (a): p-adic Hodge-theoretic form of Drinfeld's theorem — surjectivity and kernel
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let C = C_y (y ∈ |Y|, C^♭ = F) and λ_0,…,λ_{n−1} ∈ C linearly independent over E. Then the map ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} B^{φ^n=π} → C^n, (x_0,…,x_{n−1}) ↦ (Σ_{i=0}^{n−1} λ_i θ_y(φ^j(x_i)))_{0≤j≤n−1}, is surjective with kernel an E-vector space of dimension n².
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.5, p. 282, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated as a translation of 8.1.3, no proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 8.1.5 (b): the kernel is a one-dimensional D-vector space
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Give ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} B^{φ^n=π} the D-vector-space structure Π·(x_0,…,x_{n−1}) = (φ(x_0),…,φ(x_{n−1})) and a·(x_0,…,x_{n−1}) = (a x_0,…,a x_{n−1}) for a ∈ E_n = B^{φ^n=Id}. Then the kernel V of 8.1.5(a) is a D-subspace of dimension 1.
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.5, p. 282, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 8.1.5 (c): the associated modification is injective with cokernel killed by t^n
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. With V as in 8.1.5(b) and t the period of a Lubin–Tate group as in 8.1.2(b), the natural map V ⊗_E B → ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} B^n, (x_0,…,x_{n−1}) ⊗ 1 ↦ ((φ^j(x_0),…,φ^j(x_{n−1})))_{0≤j≤n−1}, is injective with cokernel killed by t^n.
items.locator: Théorème 8.1.5, pp. 282–283, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. (A degree/fibre count — cokernel of length n at ∞ whose fibre has dimension ≥ n — indicates it is even killed by t; t^n is correct but not sharp. Not reported as an issue.)

items.name: Définition 8.2.1: the line bundles O_X(d) = P[d]~
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For d ∈ Z, O_X(d) is the sheaf of O_X-modules associated (EGA II 2.5.3) with the graded P-module P[d] (P shifted by d).
items.locator: Définition 8.2.1, p. 283, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF3: 'construct O(n) … Form the graded algebra of global sections … construct Proj'; nodes RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign (O(n) = ℰ(Ĕ, π^{−n}σ) by Frobenius descent) and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map; the comparison with Proj P is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence. The atlas defines O(n) by descent, not as P[d]~.

items.name: §8.2.1.1: basic properties of O_X(d)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For every d ∈ Z, O_X(d) is a line bundle and O_X(d) = O_X(1)^{⊗d}; O_X(1) depends on π (another uniformizer gives a non-canonically isomorphic bundle); P = ⊕_{d≥0} Γ(X, O_X(d)) as graded rings; for s ∈ P_d ∖ {0} with s = ∏_{i=1}^d t_i, t_i ∈ P_1, V^+(t_i) = {∞_i}, one has div(s) = Σ_{i=1}^d [∞_i] in Div(X).
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, p. 283, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RF3 (O(n), tensor comparisons, graded algebra); the factorization of elements of P_d into elements of P_1 is used in the proof of FS II.2.9 (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point).

items.name: §8.2.1.1 (recalling Corollaire 5.3.2 and Proposition 5.3.3): bundles as pairs (M, N) and their cohomology complex
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Fix t ∈ P_1 ∖ {0} with V^+(t) = {∞}, residue field C = C_y where div(t) = Σ_{n∈Z}[φ^n(y)]. Then X ∖ {∞} = Spec(B_e) with B_e = B[1/t]^{φ=Id}, and Ô_{X,∞} = B^+_dR (= B^+_{dR,y}) with uniformizer t. Vector bundles on X are equivalent to pairs (M, N) with N a free B^+_dR-module and M ⊂ N[1/t] a free B_e-submodule of the same rank generating N[1/t] (equivalently M ⊗_{B_e} B_dR ≅ N[1/t]); if ℰ ↔ (M,N), RΓ(X,ℰ) is the complex M ⊕ N → N[1/t], (m,n) ↦ m − n.
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, p. 283 (recalling Corollaire 5.3.2 and Proposition 5.3.3, p. 209), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Beauville–Laszlo gluing: node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/beauville-laszlo-module-gluing. The two-term cohomology complex is not stated in any node (VB1 constructs H^0, H^1 by other means).

items.name: §8.2.1.1: global sections of O_X(d) as the degree filtration of B_e
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. With t, ∞, B_e, B^+_dR as above: O_X(d) corresponds to the pair (B_e, t^{−d}B^+_dR). With deg = −v_∞: B_e → N ∪ {−∞}, H^0(X, O_X(d)) = B_e ∩ t^{−d}B^+_dR = B_e^{deg≤d}, via the isomorphism P_d ≅ B_e^{deg≤d}, x ↦ x/t^d; the inclusions H^0(X,O_X) →(×t) H^0(X,O_X(1)) →(×t) ⋯ →(×t) H^0(X,O_X(d)) →(×t) ⋯ identify with the filtration E = B_e^{deg≤0} ⊂ B_e^{deg≤1} ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ B_e^{deg≤d} ⊂ ⋯ of B_e.
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, pp. 283–284, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB1 stage: 'Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology with actual Frobenius maps and signs.' No node states the B_e-filtration description.

items.name: §8.2.1.1 summary (1): Pic(X) ≅ Z
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The map Z → Pic(X), d ↦ [O_X(d)], is an isomorphism, with inverse the degree deg: Pic(X) → Z.
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, point 1, p. 284, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism: 'Pic(X_C) = Z via n ↦ O_{X_C}(n)' (FS II.2.10), for the adic curve at a geometric point (C = F here).

items.name: §8.2.1.1 summary (2): H^0(X, O_X(d))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. H^0(X, O_X(d)) = P_d if d ≥ 0 and = 0 if d < 0; after the choice of a point ∞ ∈ |X| it identifies with B_e^{deg≤d}.
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, point 2, p. 284, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(i)): H^0(X_S, O(λ)) = 0 for λ < 0; VB1 stage text asks for the O(n) sections.

items.name: §8.2.1.1 summary (3): H^1(X, O_X(d))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Choose ∞ ∈ |X| with B^+_dR = Ô_{X,∞} and uniformizer t. Then H^1(X, O_X(d)) = 0 if d ≥ 0, and H^1(X, O_X(d)) = B^+_dR/(t^{−d}B^+_dR + E) if d < 0 (the text prints t^d; see source issues).
items.locator: §8.2.1.1, point 3, p. 284, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists: H^1(X_S,O(λ)) = 0 for λ > 0 (S affinoid), and (ii) H^1(X_S,O) vanishes pro-étale locally (so H^1(X_C,O) = 0); the explicit quotient for d < 0 is not stated (FS II.2.5(i) treats BC(O(λ)[1]) instead).

items.name: §8.2.1.2: behaviour of O(d) under change of coefficient field
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For a finite extension E'|E and π_{E'/E}: X_{E'} → X_E there is a non-canonical isomorphism π_{E'/E}^* O_{X_E}(d) ≃ O_{X_{E'}}([E':E]d). If E' = E_h is the unramified extension of degree h and π_E is used as uniformizer of E_h to define O_{X_{E_h}}(d), there is a canonical isomorphism π_{E_h/E}^* O_{X_E}(d) ≅ O_{X_{E_h}}(hd).
items.locator: §8.2.1.2, p. 284, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Recorded in node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (hypotheses) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/HN-filtration-base-change ('the pullback of O_{X_{C,E}}(1) is O_{X_{C,E'}}(r)', E'|E separable of degree r).

items.name: §8.2.1.3: geometric interpretation of the fundamental exact sequence
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let d ≥ 1 and s ∈ H^0(X, O_X(d)) = P_d nonzero. There is an exact sequence 0 → O_X →(×s) O_X(d) → ℱ → 0 with ℱ torsion coherent, and, since H^1(X,O_X) = 0, an exact sequence 0 → E →(×s) P_d → H^0(X,ℱ) → 0. If s = ∏_{i=1}^r t_i^{a_i} with t_i ∈ P_1, V^+(t_i) = {x_i} and x_i ≠ x_j for i ≠ j, then ℱ = ⊕_{i=1}^r i_{x_i*} O_{X,x_i}/(t_i^{a_i}) and, with B^+_{dR,i} = Ô_{X,x_i}, the sequence reads 0 → E·∏_i t_i^{a_i} → P_d → ⊕_{i=1}^r B^+_{dR,i}/(t_i^{a_i}) → 0, which is the exact sequence of Théorème 6.4.1.
items.locator: §8.2.1.3, p. 285, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3: 0 → O → O(1) → O_{S^♯} → 0, degree 1). The degree-d version with multiplicities is not stated.

items.name: Définition 8.2.2: the bundles O_{X_E}(d,h) and O_{X_E}(λ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Fix a uniformizer π of E; for h ≥ 1 let E_h be the unramified extension of E of degree h and π_h: X_{E_h} → X_E. (1) For d ∈ Z, h ≥ 1: O_{X_E}(d,h) := π_{h*}O_{X_{E_h}}(d). (2) For λ = d/h ∈ Q with gcd(d,h) = 1, h ≥ 1: O_{X_E}(λ) := O_{X_E}(d,h). Since π_h is finite étale of degree h, O_{X_E}(d,h) is a vector bundle of rank h and degree d, and μ(O_{X_E}(λ)) = λ.
items.locator: Définition 8.2.2, p. 285, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The atlas defines O(−λ) := ℰ(D_λ, φ_λ) from isocrystals (node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign); the pushforward description O(λ) = f_*O(s) appears in the proof steps of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (FS proof of II.2.14). All choices depend on π (non-canonical isomorphism under change of π).

items.name: §8.2.2: graded-module and gluing descriptions of O(d,h)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let M(d,h) = ⊕_{i∈N} B_E^{φ_E^h = π^{ih+d}}, a graded P_E = ⊕_i B_E^{φ_E=π^i}-module. Then O_{X_E}(d,h) = M(d,h)~ and M(d,h) = ⊕_{i∈N} H^0(X_E, O_{X_E}(d,h) ⊗ O_{X_E}(i)). For t ∈ P_{E,1} ∖ {0}, {∞} = V^+(t), B^+_dR = Ô_{X_E,∞}: π_h^{−1}(X_E ∖ {∞}) = Spec(B_E[1/t]^{φ_E^h=Id}), and in terms of Proposition 5.3.1 O_{X_E}(d,h) corresponds to the triple (M, N, u) with M the free B_e-module B^+[1/t]^{φ_E^h=π^d}, N = (B^+_dR)^h and u: M ⊗_{B_e} B_dR ≅ (B_dR)^h, x ⊗ 1 ↦ (x, φ_E(x), …, φ_E^{h−1}(x)).
items.locator: §8.2.2, pp. 285–286, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No node gives these descriptions; nearest RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block (standard block ↦ O(λ)). The text prints (B_dR)^r for (B_dR)^h (source issue).

items.name: Proposition 8.2.3 (1): H^0 of O(d,h)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. H^0(X_E, O_{X_E}(d,h)) = 0 if d < 0, and = B_E^{φ_E^h = π^d} if d ≥ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 8.2.3, p. 286, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(i), reduction to λ integral by passing to the unramified extension of degree s). Left to the reader in FF.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.3 (2): H^1 of O(d,h)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let t ∈ P_{E,1} ∖ {0}, {∞} = V^+(t), B^+_dR = Ô_{X_E,∞}. Then H^1(X_E, O_{X_E}(d,h)) = 0 if d ≥ 0, and = B^+_dR/(t^{−d}B^+_dR + E_h) if d < 0 (printed t^d; source issue).
items.locator: Proposition 8.2.3, p. 286, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iii) for λ > 0; the λ < 0 case is treated there via BC(O(λ)[1]), without this explicit quotient).

items.name: Définition 8.2.5: the category φ-Mod_L of isocrystals
items.statement: Let L = W_{O_E}(F̄_q)[1/π] (printed as W_{O_E}(F̄_q), source issue) with its Frobenius σ (L_E, σ_E when the dependence on E matters). φ-Mod_L is the category of isocrystals: finite-dimensional L-vector spaces D with a σ-linear isomorphism φ. It depends on E and not only on L (if E'|E is unramified then L_E = L_{E'}).
items.locator: Définition 8.2.5, p. 286, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block. Mathlib has the case E = Q_p only: mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Isocrystal.lean — a K(p,k)-module with a Frobenius-semilinear automorphism, no finite-dimensionality built in), IsocrystalHom, IsocrystalEquiv; the general-E (ramified W_{O_E}) version is absent.

items.name: §8.2.3: the graded module M(D,φ) and the standard block
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L let M(D,φ) := ⊕_{i∈N} (D ⊗_L B)^{φ=π^i}, a graded P-module. If D = ⟨e_1,…,e_h⟩ with φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < h and φ(e_h) = π^{−d}e_1, then M(D,φ) = M(d,h).
items.locator: §8.2.3, p. 287, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block states the block convention and quotes 'M(D,φ) = M(d,h)'. (Checked: (D⊗B)^{φ=π^i} ≅ B^{φ^h=π^{ih+d}} via the e_1-coordinate.)

items.name: Proposition 8.2.6 (a): the functor ℰ(−) from isocrystals to bundles and its values
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L, ℰ(D,φ) := M(D,φ)~ is a vector bundle on X isomorphic to ⊕_{λ∈Q} O_X(−λ)^{m_λ}, m_λ the multiplicity of the slope λ in the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition of (D,φ). This defines a functor ℰ(−): φ-Mod_L → Fib_X compatible with tensor products and duals.
items.locator: Proposition 8.2.6, p. 287, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block (statement copied from FF); RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign constructs the exact tensor functor by Frobenius descent.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.6 (b): gluing data of ℰ(D,φ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. In terms of the classification of Proposition 5.3.1, ℰ(D,φ) corresponds to the pair ((D ⊗_L B[1/t])^{φ=Id}, D ⊗_L B^+_dR).
items.locator: §8.2.3, after Proposition 8.2.6, p. 287, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: 'On vérifie'. Not stated in the atlas; it would follow from RF3's descent construction of ℰ(D,φ) together with RF4 gluing.

items.name: Remarque 8.2.9: ℰ(D,φ) = (Y × D)/φ^Z
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Thinking of X as 'Y/φ^Z', the bundle ℰ(D,φ) is (Y × D)/φ^Z.
items.locator: Remarque 8.2.9, p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 8.2.7: the division algebra D_λ
items.statement: For λ ∈ Q, λ = d/h with gcd(d,h) = 1, h ≥ 1, D_λ is the central division algebra over E defined by D_λ = E_h[Π] with Π^h = π^d and Πx = σ_E(x)Π for x ∈ E_h.
items.locator: Définition 8.2.7, p. 287, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra (explicit cyclic presentation). Tau Ceti has Brauer-group infrastructure (tauceti:TauCeti.BrauerGroup.*) but no cyclic algebra or local invariant.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.8: D_λ ≅ End(O_{X_E}(λ))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For λ ∈ Q there is an isomorphism D_λ ≅ End(O_{X_E}(λ)). (Proof: D_λ is the endomorphism algebra of the simple isocrystal of slope −λ, giving an embedding via 8.2.6; End(O(λ)) = H^0(X, O(λ) ⊗ O(λ)^∨) and O(λ) ⊗ O(−λ) ≃ O^{⊕h²} by 5.6.23(4), so dim_E End(O(λ)) = h².)
items.locator: Proposition 8.2.8, pp. 287–288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra (same statement and proof). (Checked: with the block φ(e_h) = π^{−d}e_1 the inverse of the cyclic shift satisfies Π^h = π^d, Πx = σ(x)Π.)

items.name: §8.2.3: change of coefficient field — adjoint functors on isocrystals match π^* and π_*
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let E'|E be finite with maximal unramified subextension E'_0|E of degree f (so σ_{E'} = σ_E^f). The functor φ-Mod_{L_E} → φ-Mod_{L_{E'}}, (D,φ) ↦ (D ⊗_{L_E} L_{E'}, φ^f ⊗ σ_{E'}), and the functor φ-Mod_{L_{E'}} → φ-Mod_{L_E}, (D,φ) ↦ (⊕_{i=0}^{f−1} D ⊗_{L_E,σ_E^i} L_E, ξ) with ξ(x_0⊗λ_0,…,x_{f−1}⊗λ_{f−1}) = (φ(x_{f−1})⊗σ_E(λ_{f−1}), x_0⊗σ_E(λ_0),…,x_{f−2}⊗σ_E(λ_{f−2})), are adjoint, and via ℰ(−) they correspond to π_{E'|E}^*: Fib_{X_E} → Fib_{X_{E'}} and π_{E'|E*}: Fib_{X_{E'}} → Fib_{X_E}.
items.locator: §8.2.3, p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction. (The text prints 'Fix_{X_E}' for Fib_{X_E}.)

items.name: §8.2.4: ℰ(−) is essentially surjective
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The functor ℰ(−): φ-Mod_L → Fib_X is essentially surjective.
items.locator: §8.2.4, p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB2:classification stage: 'The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes'.

items.name: §8.2.4: ℰ(−) is an equivalence from isoclinic isocrystals of slope −λ to semistable bundles of slope λ
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For λ ∈ Q, ℰ(−) induces an equivalence between the category of isoclinic isocrystals of slope −λ and the category of semistable bundles of slope λ on X.

items.name: Théorème 8.2.10 (1): semistable bundles of slope λ are sums of O(λ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For λ ∈ Q, the semistable vector bundles of slope λ on X are exactly the bundles isomorphic to finite direct sums of O_X(λ).
items.locator: Théorème 8.2.10 (1), p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (FS II.2.14: 'If E is semistable of slope λ, then E is isomorphic to O_{X_C}(λ)^m'); here C = F.

items.name: Théorème 8.2.10 (2a): uniqueness of the stable bundle of slope λ
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For λ ∈ Q there is, up to isomorphism, a unique stable vector bundle of slope λ on X, namely O_X(λ).
items.locator: Théorème 8.2.10 (2), p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Théorème 8.2.10 (2b): semistable bundles of slope λ ≃ finite-dimensional D_λ^op-vector spaces
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For λ ∈ Q the abelian category of semistable vector bundles of slope λ on X is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional D_λ^op-vector spaces (via V ↦ V ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ)).
items.locator: Théorème 8.2.10 (2), p. 288, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Théorème 8.2.10 (3): the Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The Harder–Narasimhan filtration of every vector bundle on X is split.

items.name: Théorème 8.2.10 (4): classification of vector bundles on X (F algebraically closed)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The map {(λ_i)_{1≤i≤n} ∈ Q^n | n ∈ N, λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_n} → {isomorphism classes of vector bundles on X}, (λ_1,…,λ_n) ↦ [⊕_{i=1}^n O_X(λ_i)], is a bijection.

items.name: §8.3.1: modifications of ℰ(D,φ) at ∞ ↔ B^+_dR-lattices; t-killed cokernels ↔ subspaces Fil D_C
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L and fix ∞ ∈ |X| with residue field C, B^+_dR = Ô_{X,∞} with uniformizer t. Since ℰ(D,φ)^_∞ = D ⊗_L B^+_dR canonically, giving a modification 0 → ℰ' → ℰ(D,φ) → ℱ → 0 with ℱ torsion coherent supported at ∞ is equivalent to giving a B^+_dR-lattice Λ ⊂ D ⊗_L B^+_dR; those with ℱ killed by t (ℱ = i_{∞*}W, W a C-vector space) correspond, via Λ ↦ Λ/tD⊗B^+_dR, to lattices tD⊗B^+_dR ⊂ Λ ⊂ D⊗B^+_dR, i.e. to C-subspaces Fil D_C ⊂ D_C = D ⊗_L C.
items.locator: §8.3.1, p. 289, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor (modifications at a degree-one divisor via Beauville–Laszlo). The lattice ↔ filtration dictionary is not stated.

items.name: Définition 8.3.1: admissible triple (D, φ, Fil D_C)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. A triple (D, φ, Fil D_C) (with ∞, C as in 8.3.1) is admissible if the modified bundle ℰ(D,φ,Fil D_C) := ker(ℰ(D,φ) → i_{∞*}(D_C/Fil D_C)) is trivial.
items.locator: Définition 8.3.1, p. 289, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas notion of admissibility of a filtered isocrystal over C via the curve. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 treats (weak) admissibility of filtered (φ,N)-modules over a p-adic field K classically.

items.name: §8.3.1: Rapoport–Zink space and the Hodge–de Rham period map π_dR: M → ℱ
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let 𝐇 be a π-divisible O_E-module over F̄_q with covariant O-Dieudonné module (D,φ), M the associated Rapoport–Zink space. An O_C-point (H,ρ) of M is a π-divisible O_E-module H over O_C with a quasi-isogeny ρ: 𝐇 ⊗_{F̄_q} O_C/πO_C → H ⊗_{O_C} O_C/πO_C. Via ρ, the Hodge filtration of Lie of the universal vector O-extension of H gives a filtration Fil D_C; this is the image of the point under the Hodge–de Rham period map π_dR: M → ℱ (ℱ the flag variety).
items.locator: §8.3.1, pp. 289–290, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Rapoport–Zink spaces and their de Rham period maps are not planned; HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS2 defines local shtuka moduli and only asks to match them with local Shimura moduli in examples. The accepted Part II HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasIntegralPartII (PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20, route 4) plans Rapoport–Zink spaces of p-divisible groups over F̄_p (E = Q_p) and their comparison with shtuka spaces, not the Hodge–de Rham period map.

items.name: Period map of a π-divisible O-module over O_C (external, used in Proposition 8.3.2)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For (H,ρ) as in 8.3.1, there is a period map V_p(H) → (D ⊗_L B)^{φ=π} (V_p(H) the rational Tate module, an E-vector space) whose image lies in Fil(D ⊗_L B)^{φ=π}, and which induces an isomorphism V_p(H) ⊗_E B[1/t] ≅ D ⊗_L B[1/t].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 8.3.2, p. 290, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Used without proof (earlier chapters/[18]). Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover (FS II.2.2 / Scholze–Weinstein Thm A, height-one Lubin–Tate case only).

items.name: Proposition 8.3.2: the de Rham periods of p-divisible groups are admissible
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The image of π_dR is contained in the admissible locus attached to (D, π^{−1}φ). More precisely, if Fil D_C is the filtration attached to (H, ρ), then ℰ(D, π^{−1}φ, Fil D_C) ≃ V_p(H) ⊗_E O_X. (Proof: the period map gives V_p(H) ⊗ O_X → ℰ(D,π^{−1}φ,Fil D_C), an isomorphism off ∞; both sides have degree 0 since deg ℰ(D,π^{−1}φ) − dim_C D_C/Fil D_C = −Σ_λ d_λ m_λ − dim H = dim H − dim H.)
items.locator: Proposition 8.3.2, p. 290, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (no Rapoport–Zink period map, no admissible locus).

items.name: §8.3.2.1: the category C of minuscule modifications of trivial bundles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. C is the category of modifications 0 → ℰ' → ℰ → ℱ → 0 with ℰ', ℰ vector bundles, ℰ' ≃ O_X^n trivial, and ℱ coherent torsion supported at ∞ and killed by t (ℱ = i_{∞*}W, W a C-vector space). Since there are no nonzero maps from such ℱ to a vector bundle, these extensions are rigid, and C is a full subcategory of the category of triples (ℰ', ℱ, ξ) with ℰ' trivial, ℱ killed by t, ξ ∈ Ext^1(ℱ, ℰ').
items.locator: §8.3.2.1, p. 291, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §8.3.2.1: Tate twists E{1}, ℋ{1}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. E{1} := E·t, the line spanned by t in H^0(X, O_X(1)) (the point ∞ determines this line, not t); for a coherent sheaf ℋ, ℋ{1} := ℋ ⊗_E E{1}; E{d} := E{1}^{⊗d} for d ∈ Z.

items.name: Lemme 8.3.3: Ext^1(i_{∞*}C, O_X) is one-dimensional
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The C-vector space Ext^1(i_{∞*}C, O_X) has dimension 1, generated by the class of the extension 0 → O_X{1} → O_X(1) → i_{∞*}C → 0.

items.name: §8.3.2.1: Hom_C(W{1}, V_C) ≅ Ext^1(i_{∞*}W, V ⊗_E O_X)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For V ∈ Vect_E and W ∈ Vect_C there is an isomorphism Hom_C(W{1}, V_C) ≅ Ext^1(i_{∞*}W, V ⊗_E O_X), sending u: W{1} → V_C to the pull-back by i_{∞*}u{−1} of 0 → V{−1} ⊗_E O_X{1} (= V ⊗_E O_X) → V{−1} ⊗_E O_X(1) → V{−1} ⊗_E i_{∞*}C (= i_{∞*}V_C{−1}) → 0.

items.name: §8.3.2.1: trivial bundles ≃ Vect_E and t-killed torsion sheaves ≃ Vect_C
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The functors ℰ' ↦ H^0(X,ℰ') and V ↦ V ⊗_E O_X are inverse equivalences between trivial vector bundles on X and Vect_E (compatibly with tensor products); ℱ ↦ H^0(X,ℱ) and W ↦ i_{∞*}W are inverse equivalences between coherent sheaves killed by t and Vect_C.

The t-killed skyscraper part is elementary and not stated.

items.name: Proposition 8.3.4: classification of minuscule modifications of trivial bundles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The category C is equivalent to the category of pairs (V, W) with V ∈ Vect_E and W{1} ⊂ V_C a C-vector subspace.

items.name: §8.3.2.1: splitting off the trivial part of a minuscule modification
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let (V,W) be as in Prop. 8.3.4, V' ⊂ V the smallest subspace with W{1} ⊂ V'_C, and V'' a complement of V' in V. Then (V,W) = (V',W) ⊕ (V'',0), and the middle term of the modification attached to (V,W) is ≃ V'' ⊗_E O_X ⊕ ℰ'' with ℰ'' the middle term attached to (V',W).
