items.name: §8.3.2.2: dual of a minuscule modification under Hom(−, O_X(1/n))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let 0 → ℰ' → ℰ → ℱ → 0 be in C. Since D_{1/n} = End(O_X(1/n)), applying ℋom_{O_X}(−, O_X(1/n)) gives an exact sequence of D_{1/n} ⊗_E O_X-modules 0 → ℋom(ℰ, O_X(1/n)) → ℋom(ℰ', O_X(1/n)) → ℰxt^1(ℱ, O_X(1/n)) → 0 with ℰxt^1(ℱ, O_X(1/n)) ≃ ℱ^∨ ⊗_L N, where (N,φ) is the simple isocrystal of slope −1/n, ℰ(N,φ) = O_X(1/n), and for ℱ = i_{∞*}W: ℱ^∨ = i_{∞*}W^∨, W^∨ = Hom_{B^+_dR}(W, B_dR/B^+_dR) = W^*{−1} (W^* the C-dual). ℰxt^1(ℱ, O_X(1/n)) = i_{∞*}M with M a C ⊗_E D_{1/n}-module that is free of rank dim_C W over C ⊗_E E_n, i.e. rk_{C⊗_E E_n} i_∞^* ℰxt^1(ℱ, O_X(1/n)) = dim_C i_∞^*ℱ; the original modification is recovered by applying ℋom_{D_{1/n}⊗O_X}(−, O_X(1/n)).
items.locator: §8.3.2.2, pp. 292–293, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. The text writes C ⊗_L D_{1/n} and C ⊗_L E_n where ⊗_E is meant (source issue).

items.name: Proposition 8.3.5: duality between minuscule modifications and D_{1/n}-modifications
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The functor ℋom(−, O_X(1/n)) induces an anti-equivalence between C and the category of modifications of bundles with D_{1/n}-action 0 → 𝒢' → 𝒢 → ℋ → 0 where 𝒢 is a D_{1/n} ⊗_E O_X-module isomorphic to a sum of copies of O_X(1/n), 𝒢' is a locally free D_{1/n} ⊗_E O_X-module and ℋ is coherent and killed by t. If 0 → ℰ' → ℰ → ℱ → 0 maps to 0 → 𝒢' → 𝒢 → ℋ → 0, then rk_{E_n⊗_E C} i_∞^*ℋ = dim_C i_∞^*ℱ; and if the first modification corresponds to (V,W) (Prop. 8.3.4), the E-linear map Hom_{D_{1/n}}(O_X(1/n), 𝒢) → Hom_{D_{1/n}}(O_X(1/n), ℋ) identifies with the composite V^* ↪ V_C^* ↠ W^∨ = W^*{−1}.
items.locator: Proposition 8.3.5, p. 293, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §8.3.2: hypothesis (1) of Théorème 5.6.29 holds (from Gross–Hopkins)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For every h ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, if 0 → ℰ → O_{X_{E_h}}(1/n) → ℱ → 0 is exact with ℱ torsion of degree 1, then ℰ is trivial (deduced from Théorème 8.1.1 for E_h and Proposition 8.3.2, since O(1/n) = ℰ(D, π^{−1}φ) for D the Dieudonné module of a one-dimensional formal O-module of height n and a degree-one quotient is a point of P(D)).
items.locator: §8.3.2, p. 291, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The dual statement ('minuscule modifications O(−1/n) → ℰ with rank-one skyscraper cokernel force ℰ ≅ O^n') is quoted in node ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:GLn-comparison/two-tower-realisation as a known consequence, not planned as a proof; the atlas proves classification by FS's route instead.

items.name: §8.3.2.3: hypothesis (2) of Théorème 5.6.29 holds (from Drinfeld)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let 0 → ℰ' → ℰ → ℱ → 0 be exact with ℰ' = V ⊗_E O_X trivial of rank n and ℱ = i_{∞*}W of degree 1 supported at ∞, and assume W{1} ⊄ V'_C for every proper subspace V' ⊊ V (equivalently V^* → W^* injective, a point of Drinfeld's space Ω ⊂ P(V^*)). Then ℰ ≃ O_X(1/n). (Proof: with (N,φ) simple of slope 1 − 1/n, ℰ(N, π^{−1}φ) = O_X(1/n), (V^* ⊗_E N, Id ⊗ φ) is the isocrystal of a special formal O_D-module; Théorème 8.1.3 and Proposition 8.3.2 give 𝒢' ≃ D_{1/n} ⊗ O_X, hence ℰ ≃ O_X(1/n).) Combined with the splitting of 8.3.2.1 this gives hypothesis (2) of 5.6.29.
items.locator: §8.3.2.3, pp. 293–294, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §8.3.3: Hodge–de Rham and Hodge–Tate periods of a rigidified minuscule modification
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L of height n and ξ: 0 → ℰ' → ℰ → ℱ → 0 a modification in C, with fixed isomorphisms η_1: O_X^n ≅ ℰ' and η_2: ℰ(D,φ) ≅ ℰ. The Hodge–de Rham period is π_dR(ξ, η_2) = (i_∞^*η_2)^{−1}(image of i_∞^*ℰ' in i_∞^*ℰ) ⊂ D_C, a point of the Grassmannian of D_C. If ξ ↔ (V,W) (Prop. 8.3.4), η_1 amounts to E^n ≅ V and the Hodge–Tate period is π_HT(ξ, η_1) = W{1} ⊂ V_C ≃ C^n.
items.locator: §8.3.3, pp. 294–295, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. (The text prints '0 → ℰ' → ℰ' → ℱ → 0' for ξ, source issue.)

items.name: §8.3.3: comparison with the de Rham and Hodge–Tate period maps of Rapoport–Zink spaces at infinite level
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let (D,φ) be the covariant Dieudonné module of 𝐇 and (H,ρ) a point of the associated Rapoport–Zink space at infinite level (with a fixed isomorphism E^n ≅ V_p(H)), ξ the modification of Prop. 8.3.2 with the rigidifications (η_1, η_2) coming from the level structure and ρ. Then π_dR(ξ, η_2) is the image of (H,ρ) under the Hodge–de Rham period map ([54] ch. V) and π_HT(ξ, η_1) its image under the Hodge–Tate period map: W{1} ⊂ V_p(H)_C is the first (injective) arrow of the Hodge–Tate exact sequence 0 → ω_H^*[1/π]{1} → V_p(H)_C →(α_H) ω_{H^∨}[1/π] → 0, i.e. W = ω_H^*[1/π] = Lie H[1/π] (the book says 'la flèche de droite'; source issue).
items.locator: §8.3.3, p. 295, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 builds the Hodge–Tate map of p-divisible groups but does not state exactness of the Hodge–Tate sequence over O_C or the comparison with modifications.

items.name: Hodge–Tate exact sequence of a π-divisible O-module over O_C (external, used in 8.3.3)
items.statement: For a π-divisible O_E-module H over O_C there is an exact sequence 0 → ω_H^*[1/π]{1} → V_p(H) ⊗_E C →(α_H) ω_{H^∨}[1/π] → 0 (α_H the Hodge–Tate map, H^∨ the dual, ω_H^* = Lie H).
items.locator: §8.3.3, p. 295, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 ('Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map … and its passage to the completed p-adic map'); exactness over O_C is not stated. Stage HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T2 ('Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site') plans only the displayed sequence 0 → Lie(A^∨)(1) → T_pA^∨ ⊗ C → ω_A → 0 for abelian varieties over C (content/campaign/HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups/README.md, 'Inputs and conventions'), not for p-divisible groups or π-divisible O_E-modules over O_C, although the accepted Part II PrismaticCohomologyPartIIPrismaticDieudonneTheory (PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20 route 1) says it imports Theorem 12.1.1 from T0/T2.

items.name: §8.3.3: in the Lubin–Tate case the two modifications correspond under the duality of Proposition 8.3.5
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For the Lubin–Tate space, via the isomorphism between the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers at infinite level ([17], [18]), the modification attached to a point of the Lubin–Tate tower and the one attached to the corresponding point of the Drinfeld tower correspond to each other under the duality of Proposition 8.3.5.
items.locator: §8.3.3, pp. 295–296, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas; the twin-towers isomorphism itself is planned in ET.6a (next item).

items.name: Isomorphism between the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers at infinite level (Faltings [17], Fargues [18]; external)
items.statement: The Lubin–Tate tower and the Drinfeld tower (for GL_n(E) and D^×, D of invariant 1/n) become isomorphic at infinite level, compatibly with the actions of GL_n(E) × D^× × W_E, exchanging the de Rham and Hodge–Tate period maps.
items.locator: Introduction of Ch. 8, p. 277, and §8.3.3, p. 295, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: ET.6a: 'Prove the infinite-level moduli description and duality isomorphism' (Scholze–Weinstein §§6–7 route), for E/Q_p only.

items.name: §8.4.1: Colmez's category BC of finite-dimensional Banach spaces (external)
items.statement: Let C|E be complete algebraically closed. Colmez ([12], [13]) constructs an abelian category BC with an exact faithful functor BC → Banach (E-Banach spaces), X ↦ X(C), and exact fully faithful functors Vect_C → BC, W ↦ W^an, and Vect_E → BC, V ↦ V^ét, with W^an(C) = W and V^ét(C) = V; every X ∈ BC is ≃ Y/V'^ét for some extension 0 → V^ét → Y → W^an → 0 and some finite-dimensional V' ⊂ Y(C). The embedding Vect_C ↪ BC extends to the finite-length B^+_dR-modules (Vect_C = those killed by t).
items.locator: §8.4.1, pp. 295–296, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The atlas's Banach–Colmez spaces are Fargues–Scholze's v-sheaves BC(ℰ)(T) = H^0(X_T, ℰ) (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/banach-colmez-space-definition); Colmez's abstract abelian category with its structure is not planned.

items.name: §8.4.1: Colmez's dimension and height
items.statement: There are unique additive functions dim: BC → N and ht: BC → Z with dim W^an = dim_C W, dim V^ét = 0, ht W^an = 0, ht V^ét = dim_E V (printed dim_{Q_p} V, source issue); moreover Vect_E = {X ∈ BC | dim X = 0}.
items.locator: §8.4.1, p. 296, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists and VB3 speak of dimensions of diamonds, not of Colmez's additive dim/ht). The accepted Part II VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 2, not yet a layer) plans heights of quasi-Banach–Colmez spaces and of almost C-representations in Colmez's framework and imports 'Banach-Colmez geometry with the Dimension formalism' from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, but no VB stage or node states Colmez's dim and ht.

items.name: §8.4.1: the Banach–Colmez spaces X(d,h) and Plût's spectral model
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For d, h ∈ N there is X(d,h) ∈ BC with X(d,h)(C) = B_E^{φ^h=π^d}, of dimension d and height h. In Plût's theory [52] (equivalent to Colmez's), for 0 < d ≤ h, X(d,h) is the E-vector-space spectral space X(G̃_{d,h})^an ⊗̂_{W_O(k)_Q} C of §4.6.6 (G_{d,h} the formal O-module of §4.3.2); a lift G̃ of G_{d,h} to O_C gives X(G̃_{d,h})^an ⊗̂ C ≃ X(G̃^rig) and a presentation 0 → V_π(G̃)^ét → X(G̃^rig) → Lie G̃ ⊗ G_a^an → 0.
items.locator: §8.4.1, p. 296, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iv): BC(O(λ)) is a perfectoid open ball for 0 < λ ≤ [E:Q_p]) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/lubin-tate-universal-cover; Colmez/Plût structures not planned.

items.name: Colmez: Hom(C^an, V^ét) = 0 and Hom(C^an, X(1,1)) = 0 (external, used in 8.4.2)
items.statement: In BC, Hom(C^an, E^ét) = 0 (hence Hom(C^an, V^ét) = 0 for V ∈ Vect_E) and Hom(C^an, X(1,1)) = 0.
items.locator: §8.4.2, p. 297, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §8.4.2: Kedlaya criterion verified with Banach–Colmez spaces
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. For every n ≥ 1, every exact sequence 0 → O_{X_E}(−1/n) → ℰ → O_{X_E}(1) → 0 has H^0(X_E, ℰ) ≠ 0. Equivalently, for ξ ∈ H^1(X_E, O(−1−1/n)) = H^1(X_{E_n}, O_{X_{E_n}}(−n−1)) its class, the composite H^0(X_E, O(1)) →(π_n^*) H^0(X_{E_n}, O(n)) →(−∪ξ) H^1(X_{E_n}, O(−1)) has nonzero kernel. Via H^0(X_E,O(1)) = (B_E^+)^{φ_E=π_E}, H^1(X_{E_n}, O(−1)) = C/E_n and H^1(X_{E_n}, O(−n−1)) = B^+_dR/(t^{n+1}B^+_dR + E_n), this composite is induced by a morphism u: X(1,1) → C^an/E_n^ét of BC; u cannot be injective (it would be an isomorphism since dim X(1,1) = dim C^an/E_n^ét = 1 and Hom(C^an, E^ét) = 0, contradicting ht X(1,1) = 1 ≠ −n = ht C/E_n). Applied to all E_h, this verifies the hypothesis of Théorème 5.6.26 and proves Théorème 8.2.10.
items.locator: §8.4.2, p. 297, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned in this form. The atlas's key lemma is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/key-extension-lemma (FS II.2.15) for the dual-shaped extension 0 → O(−1) → ℰ → O(1/n) → 0, proved with diamonds after enlarging C.

items.name: §8.5: the curve X_Ē and the line bundles O_{X_Ē}⟨λ⟩
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Let Ē be an algebraic closure of E, X_Ē := X_E ⊗_E Ē and π_{Ē/E}: X_Ē → X_E. For λ ∈ Q put O_{X_Ē}⟨λ⟩ := π_{Ē|E_h}^* O_{X_{E_h}}(hλ) for h (sufficiently divisible) with hλ ∈ Z, a line bundle on X_Ē. π_{Ē|E}^* O_{X_E}(λ) is not O_{X_Ē}⟨λ⟩ but a direct sum of copies of it.
items.locator: §8.5, p. 298, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (all atlas bundle theory is over a fixed local field E). The printed warning on p. 298 swaps the two notations ('π^*O_{X_E}⟨λ⟩ n'est pas O_{X_Ē}(λ) mais une somme directe de copies de O_{X_Ē}(λ)'); the statement above gives the intended form (source issue).

items.name: Théorème 8.5.1 (a): every vector bundle on X_Ē is a sum of line bundles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. Every vector bundle on X_Ē is a direct sum of line bundles (of the form O_{X_Ē}⟨λ⟩).
items.locator: Théorème 8.5.1, p. 298, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from 8.2.10 without written proof (descent to a finite E'|E and splitting of π^*O(λ)). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 8.5.1 (b): classification of vector bundles on X_Ē
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The map {(λ_1,…,λ_n) | n ∈ N, λ_i ∈ Q, λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_n} → Fib_{X_Ē}/≅, (λ_1,…,λ_n) ↦ [⊕_{i=1}^n O_{X_Ē}⟨λ_i⟩], is a bijection.
items.locator: Théorème 8.5.1, p. 298, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 8.5.2: Ē may be replaced by any algebraic extension containing a Ẑ-extension
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. In Théorème 8.5.1, Ē can be replaced by any algebraic extension of E containing a Ẑ-extension of E.
items.locator: Remarque 8.5.2, p. 298, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. (Consistent: pull-back along E''|E multiplies slopes by [E'':E], so any extension with subextensions of all degrees splits every O(λ).)

items.name: Théorème 8.6.1: geometric simple connectedness of the curve
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 8: F is an algebraically closed complete perfectoid field of characteristic p, E a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, B = B_{F,E}, Y = Y_{F,E}, X = X_{F,E} = Proj(P), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}. The scheme X_Ē = X_{F,E} ⊗_E Ē is simply connected: every finite étale cover Y → X_Ē is a disjoint union of copies of X_Ē. (Proof: f_*O_Y ≅ ⊕_i O⟨λ_i⟩ with Σλ_i = 0 by Prop. 5.6.8; a positive λ_i would make the n-fold multiplication vanish on O⟨λ_i⟩^{⊗n}, contradicting reducedness; so f_*O_Y = O_{X_Ē} ⊗ A with A = H^0(Y,O_Y) a finite étale Ē-algebra.)
items.locator: Théorème 8.6.1, pp. 298–299, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. The printed proof writes O_{X_Ē}(λ_i) for O_{X_Ē}⟨λ_i⟩ and O_{X_Ē}^{⊗n} for O_{X_Ē}⟨λ_i⟩^{⊗n} (source issue E148); the argument is correct with these readings. FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 compares finite étale sites of X_F and X_F^♢ but does not compute π_1.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over an algebraically closed field are split (external, used in 8.6.1)
items.statement: If K is an algebraically closed (more generally separably closed) field and A a finite étale K-algebra, then A ≅ K^r as K-algebras.
items.locator: Proof of Théorème 8.6.1, p. 299, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean: for K separably closed and A essentially of finite type and formally étale over K, A ≃ₐ[K] (PrimeSpectrum A → K); see also mathlib:Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod.

items.name: §9.1.1: the φ-invariant map u: lim_I Spec(B_I) → X
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. There is a φ-invariant morphism of ind-schemes u: lim→_I Spec(B_I) → X, I running over compact intervals of ]0,1[: for 0 ≠ t ∈ B^{φ=π}, the inclusion B[1/t]^{φ=Id} ⊂ B_I[1/t] gives Spec(B_I[1/t]) → Spec(B[1/t]^{φ=Id}) = D^+(t), and these glue as t varies (as in 6.7 for F algebraically closed).
items.locator: §9.1.1, p. 301, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (the map of locally ringed spaces from the adic curve X_S to X_S^alg = Proj P, built from P[g^{-1}]_0 → O(D(g))). FF's u starts from the ind-scheme of the Spec(B_I), not from the adic space; comparison via VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence.

items.name: §9.1.1: the analytic bundle ℰ^an = (M_I)_I attached to a coherent sheaf
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. For ℰ coherent on X, ℰ^an := u^*ℰ = (M_I)_I is a family of finitely generated B_I-modules with isomorphisms M_J ⊗_{B_J} B_I ≅ M_I (I ⊂ J) and a φ-structure M_I ⊗_{B_I,φ} B_{φ(I)} ≅ M_{φ(I)}, satisfying the evident compatibilities. If t, ∞ = V^+(t), y with div(t) = Σ_n [φ^n(y)] and B_e = B[1/t]^{φ=Id} are as usual and ℰ is a vector bundle corresponding to (M_e, M_dR), M_e = Γ(X ∖ {∞}, ℰ), M_dR = ℰ^_∞, then M_I = (M_e ⊗_{B_e} B_I[1/t]) ∩ ∏_{n∈Z, φ^n(y)∈|Y_I|} M_dR ⊗_{Ô_{X,∞}} B^+_{dR,φ^n(y)}.
items.locator: §9.1.1, pp. 301–302, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB1 stage: 'Define bundles as finite locally free O_X modules on the existing curve; compare with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent'. The intersection formula is not stated. The text prints B_e = B[1/t]^{φ=π} (source issue).

items.name: §9.1.1: profinite groups of automorphisms of F and their action on X
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. H is a profinite subgroup of Aut(F|F_q): H acts isometrically on F, trivially on F_q, and for every principal ideal 𝔞 ⊂ O_F the action of H on O_F/𝔞 is discrete (factors through an open subgroup). Such H acts naturally on X, by convention on the left (σ ∈ H acts on X through σ^{−1} on the rings defining the curve). Finitely generated modules over the noetherian Banach algebras B_I carry canonical Banach structures.
items.locator: §9.1.1, p. 302, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (RF1 records functoriality of X_S in S, not group actions with these continuity conditions).

items.name: Définition 9.1.1: H-equivariant coherent sheaves on X
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. An H-equivariant coherent sheaf on X is a coherent sheaf ℰ with isomorphisms c_σ: σ^*ℰ ≅ ℰ (σ ∈ H) satisfying c_{στ} = c_τ ∘ τ^*c_σ, such that, writing ℰ^an = (M_I)_I, for every I the semilinear action of H on the Banach B_I-module M_I is continuous. Coh^H_X denotes the category of H-equivariant coherent sheaves (Fib^H_X that of H-equivariant vector bundles).
items.locator: Définition 9.1.1, pp. 302–303, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §9.1.2.1: the topology of the function field E(X)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Give E(X) ⊂ Frac(B) the family of Gauss norms (|·|_ρ)_{ρ∈]0,1[}. Since E(X) ⊂ Frac(B)^{φ=Id} (with equality), this topology is defined by the norm sup_{ρ∈]ρ_0^q, ρ_0]} |·|_ρ, making E(X) a normed E-algebra; finite-dimensional E(X)-vector spaces get the product topology through any basis (independent of the basis).
items.locator: §9.1.2.1, p. 303, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 9.1.2: continuity can be tested at the generic point
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Let ℰ be a vector bundle on X with an action of H compatible with the action on X. The action is continuous in the sense of Définition 9.1.1 iff the semilinear action of H on the generic fibre ℰ_η is continuous.
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.2, p. 303, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §9.1.2.2: Banach topology on B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^k and Fréchet topology on B^+_{dR,y}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. For y ∈ |Y|, k ≥ 1 and compact I with y ∈ |Y_I|, the surjection B_I → B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^k B^+_{dR,y} = B_I/ξ^k B_I (y = (ξ)) gives B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^k a Banach E-algebra structure (quotient topology; B_I ξ^k is closed), independent of I by the open mapping theorem; for k = 1 it is the topology of |·|_y on the residue field K_y; B^+_{dR,y} = lim← B^+_{dR,y}/Fil^k becomes a Fréchet E-algebra.
items.locator: §9.1.2.2, pp. 303–304, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts constructs B^+_dR with its ideal filtration (node BdR-completion-and-filtration) but not this Banach/Fréchet topology.

items.name: Banach open mapping theorem (external, used in 9.1.2.2 and 9.1.3)
items.statement: A surjective continuous linear map between Banach spaces over a nontrivially normed complete field is open; in particular a continuous linear bijection between Banach spaces is a homeomorphism.
items.locator: §9.1.2.2, p. 303, and proof of Proposition 9.1.3, p. 304, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Banach.lean, stated over NontriviallyNormedField (covers E).

items.name: Proposition 9.1.3: continuity can be tested at an H-stable closed point
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Assume there is a point ∞ = V^+(t) ∈ |X|, t ∈ B^{φ=π}, stable under H. Let ℰ be a vector bundle on X with an action of H compatible with that on X. The action is continuous (defines an H-equivariant bundle in the sense of 9.1.1) iff the semilinear action of H on ℰ^_∞ (with its Fréchet topology) is continuous.
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.3, p. 304, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 9.1.3: the exact sequence 0 → E → B^{φ=π^k} ⊕ B^+_dR/Fil^{l−k} → B^+_dR/Fil^l → 0
items.statement: Let F be algebraically closed, t ∈ B^{φ=π} vanishing at y, and l > k ≥ 1 (Fil^• the t-adic filtration of B^+_dR = B^+_{dR,y}). Then 0 → E →(u) B^{φ=π^k} ⊕ B^+_dR/Fil^{l−k} →(v) B^+_dR/Fil^l → 0 with u(λ) = (λt^k, −λ), v(x, y mod Fil^{l−k}) = x + t^k y mod Fil^l, is exact; consequently the topology induced on B^{φ=π^k} by B^+_dR/Fil^l is its Banach topology (using: if W, W' are closed subspaces of a Banach space V with W ∩ W' = 0 and W ⊕ W' closed — automatic if dim W' < ∞ — then W → V/W' is strict).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 9.1.3, p. 304, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Exactness checked from the fundamental exact sequence 0 → Et^k → B^{φ=π^k} → B^+_dR/t^k → 0 (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence covers k = 1). The strictness lemma is not in Mathlib as such (only the open mapping theorem).

items.name: Proposition 9.1.4: the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of an equivariant bundle is equivariant
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. For ℰ ∈ Fib^H_X, the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of the underlying bundle is H-invariant, hence a filtration by H-equivariant sub-bundles (because μ(σ^*ℱ) = μ(ℱ) and the HN filtration is unique).
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.4, p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Uses the HN formalism of node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism (uniqueness, functoriality); equivariance is not stated anywhere.

items.name: §9.1.4: the twisted H-action on Aut(ℰ) and continuous 1-cocycles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. For an H-equivariant bundle ℰ with underlying bundle ℰ_0 and structure (c_σ)_{σ∈H}, give Aut(ℰ_0) the topology induced by Aut(ℰ_0) ⊂ GL(ℰ_{0,η}) (equal to the one from Aut(ℰ_0) ⊂ GL_{B_I}(M_I) for I with I ∩ φ(I) ≠ ∅). H acts on the left on Aut(ℰ_0) by f^σ = c_{σ^{−1}} ∘ (σ^{−1})^*f ∘ c_{σ^{−1}}^{−1}; Z^1(H, Aut(ℰ_0)) denotes the continuous 1-cocycles for this action.
items.locator: §9.1.4, p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas; Mathlib's groupCohomology is for abelian (Rep) coefficients only, no nonabelian continuous H^1. (Checked that f ↦ f^σ is a left action by the cocycle relation.)

items.name: Proposition 9.1.5 (1): equivariant structures ↔ 1-cocycles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. With ℰ, ℰ_0 as in §9.1.4, the set of H-equivariant structures on ℰ_0 is in bijection with Z^1(H, Aut(ℰ_0)).
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.5 (1), p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 9.1.5 (2): cohomologous cocycles ↔ isomorphic equivariant bundles
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Two such cocycles are cohomologous iff they define isomorphic H-equivariant bundles.
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.5 (2), p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 9.1.5 (3): forms of an equivariant bundle ↔ H^1(H, Aut(ℰ))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. The set of isomorphism classes of H-equivariant bundles whose underlying bundle is isomorphic to ℰ_0 is in bijection with H^1(H, Aut(ℰ_0)).
items.locator: Proposition 9.1.5 (3), p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 9.1.6: twist ℰ ∧ c of an equivariant bundle by a cocycle
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. For ℰ ∈ Fib^H_X with underlying bundle ℰ_0 and c = (c_σ)_{σ∈H} ∈ Z^1(H, Aut(ℰ_0)), ℰ ∧ c is the H-equivariant bundle with underlying bundle ℰ_0 obtained by twisting by c.
items.locator: Définition 9.1.6, p. 305, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: §9.2 and Définition 9.2.1: the equivariant bundles O_{X_E}(λ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Assume F algebraically closed, λ = d/h, gcd(d,h) = 1, E_h|E unramified of degree h with residue field F_{q^h} = F^{φ^h=Id}. H → Aut(F|F_q) → Aut(F_{q^h}|F_q) gives H → Gal(E_h|E); the action of H on X_E/Spec(E) extends to X_{E_h}, inducing this action on Spec(E_h), π_{E_h/E}: X_{E_h} → X_E is H-equivariant, and O_{X_{E_h}}(d) = P_{F,E_h,π}[d]~ is canonically H-equivariant. Définition 9.2.1: O_{X_E}(λ) := π_{E_h/E*} O_{X_{E_h}}(d) ∈ Fib^H_{X_E} (depending on π).
items.locator: §9.2, Définition 9.2.1, p. 306, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas (no equivariant structures on O(λ)).

items.name: §9.2: the induced H-action on D_λ = End(O_X(λ))
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. With F algebraically closed, D_λ = End(O_X(λ)), and the H-action on D_λ induced by the equivariant structure is given by H → Aut(F|F_q) → Gal(F_{q^h}|F_q) → Aut(D_λ), the Frobenius of Gal(F_{q^h}|F_q) going to the inner automorphism x ↦ ΠxΠ^{−1} of D_λ = E_h[Π].
items.locator: §9.2, p. 306, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 9.2.2: equivariant semistable bundles of slope λ ↔ semilinear D_λ^op-representations
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Assume F algebraically closed. Let Rep_{D_λ}(H) be the category of finite-dimensional D_λ^op-vector spaces (right D_λ-vector spaces) with a continuous semilinear action of H (for the H-action on D_λ above), and Fib^{H,λ}_X the category of H-equivariant semistable bundles of slope λ. Then V ↦ V ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ) is an equivalence Rep_{D_λ}(H) ≅ Fib^{H,λ}_X.
items.locator: Théorème 9.2.2, p. 306, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from 8.2.10 and 9.1.5. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 9.2.3: low-degree Hochschild–Serre sequence for equivariant extensions
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Let ℰ_1, ℰ_2 be H-equivariant bundles with underlying bundles E_1, E_2 (structures c_σ, d_σ). There is an exact sequence 0 → H^1(H, Hom(E_1,E_2)) → Ext^1(ℰ_1, ℰ_2) → H^0(H, Ext^1(E_1,E_2)), where H acts on Ext^•(E_1,E_2) by Ext^•(E_1,E_2) →(σ^*) Ext^•(σ^*E_1, σ^*E_2) →(Ext^•(c_σ^{−1}, d_σ)) Ext^•(E_1,E_2); 1-cocycles with values in Hom(E_1,E_2) are continuous if continuous at the generic point; and the class of a cocycle (a_σ)_σ ∈ Z^1(H, Hom(E_1,E_2)) maps to the extension 0 → ℰ_2 → (ℰ_2 ⊕ ℰ_1) ∧ α → ℰ_1 → 0 with α_σ = (Id_{E_2}, a_σ; 0, Id_{E_1}).
items.locator: Proposition 9.2.3, p. 307, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. Printed with α_σ appearing in its own definition and G_F for H (source issues).

items.name: Théorème 9.3.1 (a): Galois descent for vector bundles on the curve
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Pull-back along X_{F̂̄} → X_F induces an equivalence between vector bundles on X_F and G_F-equivariant vector bundles on X_{F̂̄} (continuity as in Définition 9.1.1).
items.locator: Théorème 9.3.1, p. 307 (vector-bundle case proved via Théorème 9.3.4, pp. 307–310), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB1 stage: 'Prove rational/pro-étale/v descent in the exact source scope'; node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology (FS II.2.1: S ↦ bundles on X_S is a v-stack). Applied to the pro-étale G_F-torsor Spa F̂̄ → Spa F this gives descent for the adic curve; identifying descent data with FF's continuous semilinear G_F-actions, and GAGA to the schematic curve (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence), are not stated.

items.name: Théorème 9.3.1 (b): Galois descent for coherent sheaves on the curve
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Pull-back along X_{F̂̄} → X_F induces an equivalence Coh_{X_F} ≅ Coh^{G_F}_{X_{F̂̄}}. (Torsion equivariant sheaves descend since their finite support is G_F-stable, by Prop. 7.1.1; for general ℰ, ℰ_tor and ℰ/ℰ_tor descend and the equivariant extension splits because H^1(G_F, Hom(ℰ/ℰ_tor, ℰ_tor)) = 0 by 7.1.1.)
items.locator: Théorème 9.3.1 and end of its proof, pp. 307, 310, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Coherent (torsion) sheaves are not covered by the atlas's bundle descent.

items.name: §9.3: gluing descriptions of Fib_{X_F} and Fib^{G_F}_{X_{F̂̄}}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Fix ∞ = V^+(t) ∈ |X_F|, 0 ≠ t ∈ B_F^{φ=π}, and the unique closed point ∞ of X_{F̂̄} above it; B_{F,e} = B_F[1/t]^{φ=Id}, B_{F̂̄,e} = B_{F̂̄}[1/t]^{φ=Id}, B^+_{F,dR} = Ô_{X_F,∞}, B^+_{F̂̄,dR} = Ô_{X_{F̂̄},∞}. Fib_{X_F} is equivalent to triples (M_e, M_dR, u) with M_e a projective B_{F,e}-module, M_dR a free B^+_{F,dR}-module and u: M_e ⊗ B_{F,dR} ≅ M_dR[1/t]; Fib^{G_F}_{X_{F̂̄}} is equivalent to triples with M_e a free B_{F̂̄,e}-module with semilinear G_F-action, M_dR a free B^+_{F̂̄,dR}-module with continuous semilinear G_F-action, and u G_F-equivariant.
items.locator: Proof of Théorème 9.3.1, pp. 307–308, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Non-equivariant gluing is RF4:vector-bundles (Beauville–Laszlo); the equivariant version (continuity imposed only on M_dR, via Prop. 9.1.3) is not in the atlas. The text prints B_{F,e} = B_F[1/π]^{φ=Id} (source issue).

items.name: Définition 9.3.2: B_{F̂̄,e}-representations of G_F
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. A B_{F̂̄,e}-representation of G_F is a free B_{F̂̄,e}-module M with a semilinear G_F-action such that there is a G_F-stable B^+_dR-lattice W ⊂ M ⊗_{B_{F̂̄,e}} B_{F̂̄,dR} on which the action is continuous; Rep_{B_{F̂̄,e}}(G_F) is their category — equivalently, the B_{F̂̄,e}-modules with semilinear G_F-action of the form Γ(X_{F̂̄} ∖ {∞}, ℰ) for some ℰ ∈ Fib^{G_F}_{X_{F̂̄}}.
items.locator: Définition 9.3.2, p. 308, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 9.3.3: continuity is automatic on every stable lattice
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. In Définition 9.3.2, if W' ⊂ M ⊗ B_{F̂̄,dR} is another G_F-stable B^+_dR-lattice, the action on W' is automatically continuous.
items.locator: Remarque 9.3.3, pp. 308–309, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Théorème 9.3.4: Galois descent for B_e-modules
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. Extension of scalars − ⊗_{B_{F,e}} B_{F̂̄,e}: Proj_{B_{F,e}} → Rep_{B_{F̂̄,e}}(G_F) (Proj_{B_{F,e}} = finitely generated projective B_{F,e}-modules) is an equivalence of categories, with inverse M ↦ M^{G_F}.
items.locator: Théorème 9.3.4, pp. 309–310, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Corollaire 9.3.5: H^1(X, O_X) = Hom(G_F, E)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. There is an identification H^1(X_F, O_{X_F}) = Hom(G_F, E) (continuous homomorphisms).
items.locator: Corollaire 9.3.5, p. 311, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(ii)): 'RΓ_proet(S, E) → RΓ(X_S, O_{X_S}) is an isomorphism', which at S = Spa F gives H^1(X_F, O) = H^1_cont(G_F, E) = Hom(G_F, E) (for the adic curve; GAGA via VB2:ampleness).

items.name: Corollaire 9.3.6: Narasimhan–Seshadri-type equivalence
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. The category of semistable vector bundles of slope 0 on X_F is equivalent to the category of étale E-local systems on Spec(F) (continuous representations of G_F on finite-dimensional E-vector spaces).
items.locator: Corollaire 9.3.6, p. 311, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/slope-zero-local-systems (FS II.2.20: pro-étale E-local systems on a perfectoid S ≅ bundles with HN polygon constant 0), at S = Spa F.

items.name: Théorème 9.4.1: the Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits for F perfect
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. The Harder–Narasimhan filtration of every vector bundle on X_F is split. (Proof: for equivariant ℰ_1, ℰ_2 semistable of slopes λ_1 < λ_2, Ext^1(E_1,E_2) = 0 over X_{F̂̄} and H^1(G_F, Hom(E_1,E_2)) = 0 by 7.1.2 and 9.2.2; conclude with 9.2.3.)
items.locator: Théorème 9.4.1, p. 311, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/relative-HN-filtration-and-proetale-splitting (FS II.2.19(ii)) only splits the HN filtration after a pro-étale cover of S, which for S = Spa F does not give a splitting over F.

items.name: Remarque 9.4.2: vanishing of H^1 for bundles with positive slopes, F perfect
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. If ℰ ∈ Fib_{X_F} has all Harder–Narasimhan slopes strictly positive, then H^1(X_F, ℰ) = 0; thus, for vanishing of cohomology, the difference between F algebraically closed or not appears only for semistable bundles of slope 0.
items.locator: Remarque 9.4.2, p. 311, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iii)) states H^1(X_S, O(λ)) = 0 for λ > 0 and S affinoid, only for the bundles O(λ), not for arbitrary positive-slope bundles over a non-closed F.

items.name: Théorème 9.4.3: classification of vector bundles on X_F for F perfect
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. There is a bijection {((λ_1,[ρ_1]),…,(λ_n,[ρ_n])) | n ∈ N, λ_i ∈ Q, ρ_i ∈ Rep_{D^op_{λ_i}}(G_F), ρ_i ≠ 0, λ_1 > ⋯ > λ_n} ≅ Fib_{X_F}/≅ ([ρ_i] isomorphism classes). The map sends ((λ_i,[ρ_i]))_i to the descent to X_F (Théorème 9.3.1) of the G_F-equivariant bundle ⊕_i ρ_i ⊗_{D_{λ_i}} O_{X_{F̂̄}}(λ_i) (Théorème 9.2.2). (The book omits ρ_i ≠ 0 and does not write the map; source issue.)
items.locator: Théorème 9.4.3, p. 311, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas. The printed statement omits the nonvanishing of the ρ_i and does not write the map (source issue).

items.name: Théorème 9.5.1: the fundamental group of X_{F,Ē}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Chapter 9: F is an arbitrary perfect complete valued field of characteristic p, F̄ an algebraic closure, G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completion of F̄, X = X_{F,E}. With X_{F,Ē} := X_{F,E} ⊗_E Ē, the Galois pro-covering (X_{L,Ē})_{L|F finite} → X_{F,Ē} is a universal pro-covering; hence π_1(X_{F,Ē}) ≃ Gal(F̄|F).
items.locator: Théorème 9.5.1, p. 312, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas; FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 compares (X_F)_fét with (X_F^♢)_fét but computes no fundamental group.

items.name: No 10.1.1: Galois action on the curve, the point ∞ and its completed local ring
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Via the injection G_K ↪ Aut(F), the curve X = X_{F,Q_p} carries an action of G_K. The kernel of θ: A_F → O_C defines a G_K-invariant point y_∞ ∈ |Y_F|; explicitly y_∞ = (u_ε) where ε is a generator of Z_p(1) over C (u_ε = ([ε]−1)/([ε^{1/p}]−1)). Via |Y|/φ^Z ≅ |X|, y_∞ determines a Galois-invariant closed point ∞ = V^+(t) ∈ |X| with t = log[ε] ∈ B^{φ=p}. The identifications Ô_{X,∞} = B^+_dR(C) = B^+_{dR,y_∞} are compatible with the G_K-actions.
items.locator: no 10.1.1, p. 314, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action). items.name: Proposition 10.1.1: G_K-orbits of closed points of X∖{∞} are infinite
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Every closed point of X ∖ {∞} has an infinite G_K-orbit; equivalently ∞ is the only closed point of X whose G_K-orbit is finite.
items.locator: Proposition 10.1.1, p. 314, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action). The proof uses Tate's vanishing of C(χ)^{G_K} and (C^♭)^{G_{K'}} = k_{K'} for K' discretely valued; see sourceIssues for a gap in the case split (unramified χ of infinite order).

items.name: Tate [60] (black box): Galois invariants and cohomology of C and B_dR
items.statement: Let K be as in Ch. 10. (a) If χ: G_K → Z_p^× is a continuous character with χ(I_K) infinite, then H^0(G_K, C(χ)) = 0 (and H^1(G_K, C(χ)) = 0). (b) C^{G_K} = K, C(i)^{G_K} = 0 and H^1(G_K, C(i)) = 0 for i ≠ 0, H^1(G_K, C) is a 1-dimensional K-space (K ≅ H^1(G_K,C), 1 ↦ −[log∘χ_cyc]). (c) B_dR^{G_K} = K, (Fil^i B_dR)^{G_K} = K for i ≤ 0 and 0 for i > 0; equivalently there is a unique G_K-equivariant section K̄ → B^+_dR of θ over K̄ ⊂ C. (d) For a > 0, θ induces H^0(G_K, B^+_dR/t^a B^+_dR) ≅ H^0(G_K, C) = K; H^1(G_K, B^+_dR) = H^1(G_K, C). (e) C^{I_K} = K̂^{nr}. Used in the form stated in Prop. 10.1.1 as “H^0(G_K, C(χ^{-1})) = 0 if χ has infinite order” (which is only correct when χ(I_K) is infinite).
items.locator: used in Prop. 10.1.1 (p. 314), no 10.2.3 (p. 320), no 10.4.1 (p. 334), proof of Prop. 10.6.16 (p. 348), no 10.6.5.4 (pp. 351–352), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (special case K/Q_p finite). PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem ('Let K/Q_p be finite …'), R06.1/period-ring-invariants and R06.2/hodge-tate-decomposition-tate state (a), (b) and (e) only for K/Q_p finite; R06.1/de-rham-invariants gives (c) for any complete discretely valued K with perfect residue field, and R06.1/algebraic-closure-in-bdr-plus the section K̄ → B^+_dR. FF use Tate's results for K with arbitrary perfect residue field, including k_K algebraically closed after the reduction of No 10.6.5.2 (H^1(G_K, C) in No 10.6.5.3), which no node plans.

items.name: Définition 10.1.2(1): B_e-representations of G_K
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A B_e-representation of G_K is a free B_e-module M of finite rank with a semilinear G_K-action such that M ⊗_{B_e} B_dR contains a G_K-stable B^+_dR-lattice on which the action is continuous. Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is the category they form; it is Q_p-linear with tensor products, duals and internal Hom.
items.locator: Définition 10.1.2(1), p. 315, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: No 10.1.2: G_K-equivariant bundles on X = B-pairs (Berger)

items.name: Proposition 10.1.3 (Berger [5]): Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is abelian
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The category Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is abelian. (Proof: the support of a G_K-equivariant torsion coherent sheaf on X∖{∞} is a finite G_K-invariant set of closed points, hence empty by Prop. 10.1.1; so Coh^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} = Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}}.)

items.name: Corollaire 10.1.4: Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is Tannakian
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. items.name: Théorème 10.1.5: descent of G_K-equivariant sheaves to an arithmetically profinite extension
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let L|K be a Galois algebraic extension contained in K̄ which is arithmetically profinite ([61]), and Γ = Gal(L|K). Then the morphism X_F → X_{L̂^♭} induces an equivalence of categories Coh^{G_K}_{X_F} ≅ Coh^Γ_{X_{L̂^♭}}. One also gets an equivalence Fib^{Γ,0}_{X_{L̂^♭}} ≃ Rep_{Q_p}(G_K) between Γ-equivariant semistable bundles of slope 0 and finite-dimensional p-adic representations of G_K.
items.locator: Théorème 10.1.5, p. 316, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Remarque 10.1.6: HN filtrations of Γ-equivariant bundles need not split equivariantly
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. With L|K APF and Γ = Gal(L|K) as in Thm 10.1.5: although the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of a bundle on X_{L̂^♭} splits (Thm 9.4.1), the HN filtration of a Γ-equivariant bundle is in general not split Γ-equivariantly: if 𝓔_1 ∈ Fib^{Γ,λ} and 𝓔_2 ∈ Fib^{Γ,μ} are semistable Γ-equivariant bundles with λ < μ, then H^1(Γ, Hom(E_1,E_2)) ≅ Ext^1(𝓔_1,𝓔_2), which is non-zero in general.
items.locator: Remarque 10.1.6, p. 316, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Théorème 10.1.7: classification of G_K-equivariant semistable bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For λ = d/h ∈ Q let D_λ = Q_{p^h}[Π] carry the unramified G_K-action through G_K → Gal(k̄_K|k_K) under which Frobenius acts by x ↦ ΠxΠ^{-1}, and let Fib^{G_K}_{X,λ} be the category of G_K-equivariant semistable bundles of slope λ. Then V ↦ 𝒱 ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ) is an equivalence Rep_{D_λ^op}(G_K) ≅ Fib^{G_K}_{X,λ}, where Rep_{D_λ^op}(G_K) is the category of finite-dimensional D_λ^op-vector spaces with continuous semilinear G_K-action and 𝒱 is the G_K-equivariant sheaf on X defined by V; a quasi-inverse is 𝓔 ↦ Hom(O_X(λ), 𝓔). In particular Rep_{Q_p}(G_K) ≅ Fib^{G_K,0}_X.
items.locator: Théorème 10.1.7, pp. 316–317, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: No 10.2.1 / Définition 10.2.1: the G_K-equivariant bundle E(D,φ) of an isocrystal
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let φ-Mod_{K_0} be the category of isocrystals over K_0. The functor E(−): φ-Mod_{K_0} → Fib_X of §8.2.3, E(D,φ) = (⊕_{d≥0} (D ⊗_{K_0} B)^{φ=p^d})^~, extends to a functor φ-Mod_{K_0} → Fib^{G_K}_X because the graded P-module ⊕_{d≥0}(D ⊗_{K_0} B)^{φ=p^d} carries a semilinear G_K-action; E(D,φ) denotes the resulting G_K-equivariant bundle. Its B-pair is ((D ⊗_{K_0} B[1/t])^{φ=Id}, D ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR).
items.locator: no 10.2.1 and Définition 10.2.1, p. 317, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: No 10.2.1: isoclinic isocrystals as semilinear D_λ-representations of Gal(k̄_K|k_K)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let L = W(k̄_K)_Q. For λ = d/h, (d,h) = 1, let 1(λ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0} have basis (e_1,…,e_h) with φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < h and φ(e_h) = p^d e_1. Using D_λ = End(1(λ) ⊗ L)^op, the functor (D,φ) ↦ Hom_{φ-Mod_L}(1(λ) ⊗ L, (D,φ) ⊗ L) is an equivalence φ-Mod^λ_{K_0} ≅ Rep_{D_λ}(Gal(k̄_K|k_K)), the category of continuous semilinear representations of Gal(k̄_K|k_K) on finite-dimensional D_λ-vector spaces. If (D,φ) is isoclinic of slope λ with associated V then E(D,φ) ≃ V ⊗_{D_λ^op} O_X(−λ).
items.locator: no 10.2.1, p. 317, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block fixes the standard block and D_λ, but only over an algebraically closed residue field; the Galois-descent description over K_0 is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 10.2.2: essential image of E: φ-Mod_{K_0} → Fib^{G_K}_X
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The essential image of E: φ-Mod_{K_0} → Fib^{G_K}_X consists of the equivariant bundles that are direct sums of semistable equivariant bundles associated (via Thm 9.2.2) to unramified semilinear representations of G_K. E induces an equivalence between isoclinic isocrystals of slope λ and these equivariant semistable bundles of slope −λ.

items.name: No 10.2.2: invariants of a G-scheme with no nontrivial invariant closed subschemes form a field
items.statement: Let Z be an integral scheme with an action of a group G such that the only G-invariant closed subschemes of Z are ∅ and Z. Then E := Γ(Z, O_Z)^G is a field (every f ∈ E∖{0} is a unit, since V(f) is G-invariant and ≠ Z).
items.locator: no 10.2.2, p. 318, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Pure commutative algebra/scheme theory with group actions; not in Mathlib or the atlas in this form.

items.name: Lemme 10.2.3: O_{Z,η}^G = E
items.statement: With Z, G, E as in no 10.2.2 and η the generic point of Z: O_{Z,η}^G = E.
items.locator: Lemme 10.2.3, p. 318, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: Lemme 10.2.4: the generic-fibre functor on G-equivariant bundles is fully faithful
items.statement: With Z, G, E as in no 10.2.2, let Fib^G_Z be the category of G-equivariant vector bundles on Z and Fib^G_η that of finite-dimensional O_{Z,η}-vector spaces with semilinear G-action. The generic-fibre functor Fib^G_Z → Fib^G_η is fully faithful; in particular for 𝓔 ∈ Fib^G_Z with underlying bundle E, H^0(Z, E)^G = E_η^G.
items.locator: Lemme 10.2.4, p. 318, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: Fontaine [26] prop. 1.6.1 (black box): injectivity of W^G ⊗ B → W
items.statement: Let B be a field with an action of a group G and E = B^G. For a finite-dimensional B-vector space W with semilinear G-action, the natural map W^G ⊗_E B → W is injective; hence dim_E W^G ≤ dim_B W < ∞. (Applied with B = O_{Z,η}.)
items.locator: used in no 10.2.2, p. 319 (also no 10.4.1, p. 334), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest planned nodes: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissibility-dimension-bound (only for B ⊗_F V with V an F-linear representation) and R06.2/serre-tate-injectivity (C-representations); the general semilinear statement is not stated.

items.name: No 10.2.2: the adjoint pair (π^*, π_*) for π: [G\Z] → Spec(E)
items.statement: With Z, G, E as in no 10.2.2, the morphism of stacks π: [G\Z] → Spec(E) gives adjoint functors π^*: Vect_E → Fib^G_Z, π^*V = V ⊗_E O_Z, and π_*: Fib^G_Z → Vect_E, π_*𝓔 = Γ(Z, 𝓔)^G (π^* left adjoint to π_*).
items.locator: no 10.2.2, p. 319, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Définition 10.2.5: flat equivariant bundles
items.statement: With Z, G, E as in no 10.2.2, 𝓔 ∈ Fib^G_Z is flat if the adjunction morphism π^*π_*𝓔 → 𝓔 is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Définition 10.2.5, p. 319, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 10.2.6: criteria for flatness
items.statement: With Z, G, E as in no 10.2.2 and 𝓔 ∈ Fib^G_Z: the adjunction morphism π^*π_*𝓔 → 𝓔 is injective and dim_E π_*𝓔 ≤ rk 𝓔. Moreover the following are equivalent: (1) 𝓔 is flat; (2) dim_E π_*𝓔 = rk 𝓔; (3) the generic fibre 𝓔_η is flat (i.e. 𝓔_η^G ⊗_E O_{Z,η} → 𝓔_η is an isomorphism).
items.locator: Proposition 10.2.6, p. 319, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 10.2.7: Frac(B_I) ⊗_{K_0} K embeds in B_dR and Frac(B_I)^{G_K} = K_0
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For every compact interval I ⊂ ]0,1[ (as printed; the proof only works when |Y_I| contains a point φ^n(y_∞) of the φ-orbit of y_∞, e.g. whenever I contains an interval [ρ, ρ^{1/p}], so that B_I → B^+_{dR,φ^n(y_∞)} ≅ B^+_dR is G_K-equivariant; see sourceIssues): Frac(B_I) ⊗_{K_0} K ↪ B_dR and Frac(B_I)^{G_K} = K_0. (The proof shows B_I ⊗_{K_0} K is a domain, using the multiplicative norms |Σ[x_n]π_K^n|_ρ = sup |x_n| ρ^{n/e} on W(O_F) ⊗_{O_{K_0}} O_K.)

items.name: Corollaire 10.2.8 (part): G_K-regularity of B_I[1/t], B^+[1/t], B[1/t]

items.name: Définition 10.2.9: equivariant bundles on Y_I∖V(t) and on Y∖V(t)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (2) Fib^{G_K}_{Y[1/t]} := 2-lim_I Fib^{G_K}_{Y_I[1/t]} is the 2-projective limit of the preceding fibred category as I varies.

items.name: No 10.2.4: flat objects of Fib^{G_K}_{Y_I[1/t]} and Fib^{G_K}_{Y[1/t]} are equivalent to Vect_{K_0}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (a) For each compact I, π_{I*}M = M^{G_K} and π_I^*V = V ⊗_{K_0} B_I[1/t] are adjoint; dim_{K_0} π_{I*}M ≤ rk M with equality iff M is flat; π_I^*π_{I*}M → M is injective (it is the largest flat subbundle of M); (π_I^*, π_{I*}) induce equivalences between flat objects of Fib^{G_K}_{Y_I[1/t]} and Vect_{K_0}. (b) For M = (M_I)_I ∈ Fib^{G_K}_{Y[1/t]}, if I ⊂ J then π_*M_J ⊂ π_*M_I, and π_*M := lim_I π_{I*}M_I = ∩_I π_{I*}M_I = π_{I*}M_I for I large; π_* has a left adjoint π^*, dim_{K_0} π_*M ≤ rk M with equality iff M is flat, and (π^*, π_*) are inverse equivalences between flat objects of Fib^{G_K}_{Y[1/t]} and Vect_{K_0}.

items.name: No 10.2.5: analytification and the functor D
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} = Rep_{B_e}(G_K). The inclusions B_e ⊂ B_I[1/t] give an analytification functor (−)^an: Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} → Fib^{G_K}_{Y[1/t]}. Since Spec(B_I[1/t]) → Spec(B_e) are φ-invariant as I varies, the composite π_*∘(−)^an: Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} → Vect_{K_0} factors through φ-Mod_{K_0}; this is the functor D.

items.name: Définition 10.2.11: the functors V and D
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. items.name: Proposition 10.2.12 (1)–(3): V ⊣ D, V fully faithful, V∘D(M) ↪ M
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) The functors D: Rep_{B_e}(G_K) → φ-Mod_{K_0} and V: φ-Mod_{K_0} → Rep_{B_e}(G_K) are adjoint, V being left adjoint to D. (2) V is fully faithful: Id ≅ D∘V. (3) For M ∈ Rep_{B_e}(G_K), V∘D(M) ↪ M, with equality iff dim_{K_0} D(M) = rk_{B_e} M.

items.name: Proposition 10.2.12 (4): V and D computed with B[1/t], B^+[1/t] or B_cris

items.name: Définition 10.2.13: crystalline B_e-representations and crystalline equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) M ∈ Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is crystalline if dim_{K_0} D(M) = rk_{B_e} M. (2) 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} is crystalline if the B_e-representation H^0(X∖{∞}, 𝓔) is crystalline. (3) 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X is crystalline if its restriction to X∖{∞} is. Thus 𝓔 on X is crystalline iff 𝓔^an[1/t] is flat as an equivariant bundle on Y∖V(t).
items.locator: Définition 10.2.13, p. 324, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: No 10.2.5: D recovers D_cris; V crystalline iff V ⊗ O_X crystalline
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The composite Rep_{Q_p}(G_K) → Fib^{G_K}_X → Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} → φ-Mod_{K_0}, V ↦ D(V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X|_{X∖{∞}}), is the usual functor D_cris. Hence a p-adic representation V is crystalline iff the equivariant bundle V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X is crystalline.
items.locator: no 10.2.5, p. 324, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: D_cris itself is planned (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/period-functors) but its interpretation via equivariant bundles on the curve is not.

items.name: Théorème 10.2.14: crystalline B_e-representations = isocrystals
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. D and V induce inverse equivalences between crystalline B_e-representations and isocrystals; this gives an embedding of Tannakian categories V: φ-Mod_{K_0} ↪ Rep_{B_e}(G_K). Every subrepresentation of a crystalline B_e-representation is crystalline, and for such M, D induces a bijection between subrepresentations of M and sub-isocrystals of D(M).

items.name: Proposition 10.2.15: crystallinity can be tested at the generic point

items.name: No 10.3.1: extension of L to O_F^× and the ring map Sym_Z O_F^× → B
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Using the canonical splitting O_F^× = k_F^× × (1+m_F) given by the Teichmüller lift k_F = k̄_K → K̂_0^{nr} ⊂ C, extend L to O_F^× by L|_{k_F^×} = 0; the group morphism L then defines a ring morphism Sym_Z O_F^× → B.

items.name: Définition 10.3.1: the ring B_log with φ, N and G_K-action
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. B_log := B ⊗_{Sym_Z O_F^×} Sym_Z F^×, with the morphism L: F^× → B_log canonically extending L: O_F^× → B. (1) φ is the unique automorphism of B_log extending φ on B with φ∘L = pL. (2) N: B_log → B_log is the unique B-derivation with N(L(x)) = 1 whenever x ∈ F^× has v(x) = 1. (3) The G_K-action on B_log is the unique extension of that on B for which L is G_K-compatible: L(x)^σ = L(x^{σ−1}) + L(x) for σ ∈ G_K, x ∈ F^× (x^{σ−1} ∈ O_F^×). A choice of x ∈ F^× with v(x) = 1 gives an isomorphism B[X] ≅ B_log, X ↦ L(x), with φ(X) = pX, N(X) = 1 and X^σ = X + L(x^{σ−1}).
items.locator: Définition 10.3.1, pp. 325–326, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/semistable-period-ring (B_st^+ = Sym_Q((C^♭)^×) ⊗ B_cris^+, built on B_cris^+, with N = −d/du, opposite sign to FF's N(L(x)) = +1). FF's B_log over B = O(Y) is not planned. The printed isomorphism reads B^+[X] ≅ B_log (misprint, see sourceIssues).

items.name: Définition 10.3.2: (φ,N)-modules over K_0
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} is the category of triples (D,φ,N) with (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0} and N: D → D K_0-linear with Nφ = pφN. Such N is necessarily nilpotent.

items.name: No 10.3.2: the isomorphism (4), the cocycle log_{x,σ} and the twisted Galois action
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Fix x ∈ F^× with v(x) = 1, so B[X] ≅ B_log. For (D,φ,N) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} and d ≥ 0 there is an isomorphism (4): (D ⊗ B)^{φ=p^d} ≅ (D ⊗ B_log)^{φ=p^d, N=0}, y ↦ Σ_{i≥0} ((−1)^i/i!) N^i(y) X^i, giving an isomorphism of graded modules ⊕_d (D ⊗_{K_0} B)^{φ=p^d} ≅ ⊕_d (D ⊗_{K_0} B_log)^{φ=p^d,N=0} over P = ⊕_d B_log^{φ=p^d,N=0}, not compatible with G_K. log_{x,σ} := L(x^{σ−1}) defines a cocycle (log_{x,σ})_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, B^{φ=p}); another y ∈ F^× with v(y) = 1 changes it by a coboundary: log_{y,σ} = log_{x,σ} + L(yx^{-1})^σ − L(yx^{-1}). Transported by (4), the G_K-action on (D ⊗ B)^{φ=p^d} is y ↦ exp(−log_{x,σ} N)(y^σ).
items.locator: no 10.3.2, pp. 326–327, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 10.3.3: the G_K-equivariant bundle E(D,φ,N)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) There is a functor E(−): (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} → Fib^{G_K}_X, (D,φ,N) ↦ (⊕_{d≥0}(D ⊗_{K_0} B_log)^{φ=p^d,N=0})^~. (2) After forgetting the G_K-action, E(D,φ,N) ≃ E(D,φ). (3) The monodromy N: (D,φ) → (D,pφ) defines a morphism N: E(D,φ) → E(D,pφ) = E(D,φ) ⊗ O_X(−1) in Fib^{G_K}_X. For x ∈ F^× with v(x) = 1 one has the 1-cocycle (log_{x,σ})_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, H^0(X, O_X(1))); (log_{x,σ} ⊗ Id ∘ N)_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, End(E(D,φ))) is a 1-cocycle of nilpotent endomorphisms, (exp(−log_{x,σ} ⊗ Id ∘ N))_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, Aut(E(D,φ))), and with the notation of Déf. 9.1.6 there is an isomorphism of G_K-equivariant bundles E(D,φ,N) ≃ E(D,φ) ∧^{G_K} (exp(−log_{x,σ} ⊗ Id ∘ N))_σ.
items.locator: Proposition 10.3.3, p. 327, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Remarque 10.3.4: the cocycle log_{x,σ} and the Tate curve
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Choose x = (x^{(n)})_n ∈ F = C^♭ with x^{(0)} ∈ K^× and |x^{(0)}| ≠ 1, and let E be the Tate elliptic curve over K with E^rig = G_m^rig/(x^{(0)})^Z, so T_p(E) = {(ȳ_n)_n : ȳ_n ∈ K̄^×/(x^{(0)})^Z, ȳ_{n+1}^p = ȳ_n, ȳ_0 the neutral element (printed ȳ_0 = 0)}. There is an exact sequence of G_K-representations 0 → Z_p(1) → T_p(E) → Z_p → 0 ((ε^{(n)})_n ↦ (ε̄^{(n)})_n, (ȳ_n)_n ↦ lim_{n→∞} p^n v(y_n)/v(x^{(0)})). Then log_{x,σ} ∈ Z_p·t ⊂ B^{φ=p} and this cocycle defines the above extension of Z_p by Z_p(1).
items.locator: Remarque 10.3.4, pp. 327–328, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/tate-curve-tate-module and R06.6/kummer-representation give the Tate-curve extension 0 → Z_p(1) → T_p(E_q) → Z_p → 0 with class the Kummer class of q, for K/Q_p finite ('Throughout: K/Q_p is finite with residue field k = F_{p^f}'); R06.1/crystalline-logarithm (3) gives log_cris[ε^a] = at. The identification of FF's cocycle log_{x,σ} ∈ Z_p·t ⊂ B^{φ=p} with this class, and K with infinite perfect residue field, are not planned.

items.name: Remarque 10.3.5: ℓ-adic analogue via Grothendieck's monodromy theorem
items.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p, π_K a uniformizer of K, t_ℓ: I_K → Z_ℓ(1), σ ↦ (σ(π_K^{1/ℓ^n})/π_K^{1/ℓ^n})_n (canonical, surjective, independent of the roots). For the Tate curve E^rig = G_m^rig/π_K^Z one has 0 → Z_ℓ(1) → T_ℓ(E) → Z_ℓ → 0; a compatible system (π_K^{1/ℓ^n})_n splits it as Z_ℓ-modules, with cocycle c_ℓ ∈ Z^1(G_K, Z_ℓ(1)), c_ℓ(σ) = σ(π_K^{1/ℓ^n})/π_K^{1/ℓ^n}, and c_ℓ|_{I_K} = t_ℓ. For an ℓ-adic representation ρ: G_K → GL(V) with ρ|_{I_K} factoring through a finite quotient (printed: 'se factorise à travers un sous-groupe ouvert') and N: ρ → ρ(−1), c_ℓN ∈ Z^1(G_K, End(V)) (adjoint action), exp(c_ℓN) ∈ Z^1(G_K, GL(V)), and one forms the ℓ-adic representation ρ ∧^{G_K} exp(c_ℓN).
items.locator: Remarque 10.3.5, p. 328, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only. Stage ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2 and its decomposition node ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2/grothendieck-monodromy-and-the-weil-deligne-functor ('Let K be a non-archimedean local field with residue field k of cardinality q'; Construction 8.4.2 ρ'(F^nσ) = ρ(F^nσ)exp(−t_ℓ(σ)N)) plan Grothendieck's monodromy theorem and the Weil–Deligne functor over finite residue fields. FF's twist ρ ∧^{G_K} exp(c_ℓN) by the Tate-curve cocycle c_ℓ, for K with arbitrary perfect residue field, is not stated.

items.name: Lemme 10.3.6: the O_X-algebra 𝒜 with Γ(D^+(z), 𝒜) = B_log[1/z]^{φ=Id}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (After fixing x with v(x) = 1, for z ∈ P homogeneous of degree d > 0 one has B_log[1/z]^{φ=Id} = B[1/z]^{φ=Id}[X/w] for any nonzero w ∈ P_1 dividing z.) There is a unique quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-algebras 𝒜 such that Γ(D^+(z), 𝒜) = B_log[1/z]^{φ=Id} for every homogeneous z ∈ P; the G_K-action on O_X extends to a compatible action on 𝒜.

items.name: Définition 10.3.7: the surface X_log
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. X_log := Spec(𝒜) →π X; X_log carries a G_K-action commuting with π, and, forgetting the G_K-action, X_log → X is isomorphic to the line bundle V(O_X(1)) (geometric vector bundle whose sections are O_X(1)).

items.name: Proposition 10.3.8: X_log as a twist of V(O_X(1))
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let x ∈ F^× with v(x) = 1 and (log_{x,σ})_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, B^{φ=p}) the associated cocycle; it defines a cocycle with values in the affine automorphisms of V(O_X(1))/X given by translation by elements of B^{φ=p} = H^0(X, O_X(1)). Then, as X-schemes with G_K-action, X_log = V(O_X(1)) ∧^{G_K} (log_{x,σ})_σ. Unlike V(O_X(1)) → X, X_log → X has no G_K-invariant section.
items.locator: Proposition 10.3.8, p. 329, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Lemme 10.3.9: relative differentials of X_log/X
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. As G_K-equivariant bundles there is a canonical identification Ω^1_{X_log/X} = π^*O_X(−1). On π^{-1}(D^+(z)) the differential d: O_{X_log} → Ω^1_{X_log/X} is N: B_log[1/z]^{φ=Id} → B_log[1/z]^{φ=p^{-1}} = B_log[1/z]^{φ=Id} ⊗_{B[1/z]^{φ=Id}} B[1/z]^{φ=p^{-1}}.

items.name: Définition 10.3.10: the connection ∇_N on π^*E(D,φ)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For (D,φ,N) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} (printed: φ-Mod_{K_0}), π^*E(D,φ) has the canonical connection ∇_can = d ⊗ 1, and via Lemme 10.3.9 N induces a G_K-equivariant linear map π^*N: π^*E(D,φ) → π^*E(D,φ) ⊗ Ω^1_{X_log/X}; set ∇_N := ∇_can + π^*N, a connection on π^*E(D,φ) compatible with the G_K-action. This defines a functor from (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} to equivariant bundles with connection on X_log.

items.name: No 10.3.4: log p as a formal variable and the extended logarithm
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. log p denotes a formal variable (possibly specialised to an element of K); K[log p], B^+_dR[log p] are polynomial rings. The usual (rigid-analytic) logarithm log: 1+m_{K̄} → K̄ extends to a (locally analytic) logarithm log: K̄^× → K̄[log p].
items.locator: no 10.3.4, p. 330, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/log-extension-to-kbar (extensions log_K of log to K̄^× with a chosen value of log_K(q)); the atlas specialises log p instead of keeping it formal.

items.name: Lemme 10.3.12 (cf. [25] §4.2.1): extension of L to F^× with values in B^+_dR[log p]
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The composite O_F^× →L B^{φ=p} ↪ B^+_dR extends naturally to a G_K-compatible morphism L: F^× → B^+_dR[log p]: for x ∈ F^× with x^{(0)} = p, log([x]) := log p + Σ_{i≥1} (−1)^{i−1}([x]/p − 1)^i/i; for y ∈ F^× choose integers a ≥ 1, b with y^a/x^b ∈ O_F^× and set L(y) = (1/a)(L(y^a x^{−b}) + b·log[x]); this is independent of the choices.
items.locator: Lemme 10.3.12, pp. 330–331, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bst-embedding-into-bdr (ι(λ_st(y)) = log_dR([y]/y^♯) + log_K(y^♯)) and R06.1/crystalline-logarithm(2); stated there for a chosen value log_K(p) ∈ K_0 rather than a formal variable.

items.name: Corollaire 10.3.13: morphisms B_log → B^+_dR and trivialisation of log_{x,σ}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Each choice of an element log p ∈ K gives a morphism B_log → B^+_dR extending the inclusion B ⊂ B^+_dR, and a trivialisation in B^+_dR of the image of the cocycle (log_{x,σ})_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, B^{φ=p}) in Z^1(G_K, B^+_dR): log_{x,σ} = L(x)^σ − L(x) (printed with the opposite sign; see sourceIssues).
items.locator: Corollaire 10.3.13, p. 331, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bst-embedding-into-bdr (B_st → B_dR for B_st built on B_cris); FF's B_log over B = O(Y) is not planned.

items.name: Remarque 10.3.14: Tate modules of Tate curves are de Rham
items.statement: The Tate module of a Tate elliptic curve over K is a de Rham representation (interpretation of Cor. 10.3.13).
items.locator: Remarque 10.3.14, p. 331, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (special case K/Q_p finite): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/tate-curve-filtered-phi-n-module and R06.6/kummer-representations-semistable (V_p(E_q) semistable, hence de Rham), 'Throughout: K/Q_p is finite'. Tate curves over K with infinite perfect residue field are not planned.

items.name: Proposition 10.3.15 ([25] théo. 4.2.4): injectivity of B_log ⊗_{K_0} K → B^+_dR
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For each choice of log p ∈ K, the induced morphism B_log ⊗_{K_0} K → B^+_dR is injective. (Colmez's proof: u = log([p^♭]/p) is transcendental over Frac(B).)
items.locator: Proposition 10.3.15, pp. 331–332, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Corollaire 10.3.17: the B-pair of E(D,φ,N)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. items.name: Proposition 10.3.18: completion of E(D,φ,N) at ∞
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Specialising log p to 0 gives an isomorphism of B^+_dR-representations of G_K, Ê(D,φ,N)_∞ = (D ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR[log p])^{N=0} ≅ D ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR, with inverse y ↦ Σ_{i≥0}((−1)^i/i!) N^i(y)(log p)^i. items.name: Proposition 10.3.20: the functors D_log and V_log
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) There are two adjoint functors D_log: Rep_{B_e}(G_K) → (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0}, D_log(M) = (M ⊗_{B_e} B_log[1/t])^{G_K}, and V_log: (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} → Rep_{B_e}(G_K), V_log(D,φ,N) = (D ⊗_{K_0} B_log[1/t])^{φ=Id,N=0}. (2) The adjunction Id → D_log∘V_log is an isomorphism and V_log is an embedding of the Tannakian category (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} into the Tannakian category Rep_{B_e}(G_K). (3) For M ∈ Rep_{B_e}(G_K), dim_{K_0} D_log(M) ≤ rk(M) and V_log∘D_log(M) ↪ M, which is an isomorphism iff dim_{K_0} D_log(M) = rk(M). (B_log is G_K-regular by Prop. 10.3.15.)
