items.name: Définition 10.3.21: log-crystalline B_e-representations and equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) M ∈ Rep_{B_e}(G_K) is log-crystalline if dim_{K_0} D_log(M) = rk(M). (2) 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_{X∖{∞}} is log-crystalline if Γ(X∖{∞}, 𝓔) is. (3) 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X is log-crystalline if its restriction to X∖{∞} is. Thus 𝓔 is log-crystalline iff there is (D,φ,N) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} with 𝓔|_{X∖{∞}} ≃ E(D,φ,N)|_{X∖{∞}}, and then (D,φ,N) is determined canonically by D_log.
items.locator: Définition 10.3.21, p. 333, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: No 10.4.1: B_dR-representations and the adjunction with Vect_K
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Rep_{B_dR}(G_K) is the category of continuous semilinear G_K-representations on finite-dimensional B_dR-vector spaces (continuity: some G_K-invariant B^+_dR-lattice has continuous action, and then every invariant lattice does). (−)^{G_K}: Rep_{B_dR}(G_K) → Vect_K and − ⊗_K B_dR are adjoint; for W ∈ Rep_{B_dR}(G_K) the adjunction W^{G_K} ⊗_K B_dR → W is injective, dim_K W^{G_K} ≤ dim_{B_dR} W, with equality iff it is an isomorphism; the essential image of − ⊗_K B_dR is {W : dim_K W^{G_K} = dim_{B_dR} W}.
items.locator: no 10.4.1, p. 334, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned for general semilinear B_dR-representations; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 only treats B_dR ⊗ V (D_dR).

items.name: Définition 10.4.1: flat and generically flat representations
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (1) A B_dR-representation W is flat if dim_K W^{G_K} = dim_{B_dR} W. (2) A B^+_dR-representation W is generically flat if the B_dR-representation W[1/t] is flat. Hence − ⊗_K B_dR: Vect_K ≅ Rep^{flat}_{B_dR}(G_K).
items.locator: Définition 10.4.1, p. 334, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Remarque 10.4.2 ([28]): flatness and regular connections
items.statement: Let K_∞|K be the cyclotomic extension. Fontaine ([28]) associates to a B_dR-representation a module with connection over K_∞((t)) and shows that the B_dR-representation is flat iff this module with connection is generated by its horizontal sections (i.e. is regular).
items.locator: Remarque 10.4.2, p. 334, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/de-rham-iff-dif-connection-trivial (V de Rham iff ∇_V trivial on D_dif(V), for Q_p-representations V only).

items.name: No 10.4.1: filtration on V ⊗_K B_dR attached to a filtration of V
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A filtration of a finite-dimensional K-vector space V is a decreasing filtration Fil^•V with Fil^iV = V for i ≪ 0 and Fil^iV = 0 for i ≫ 0. Set Fil^n(V ⊗_K B_dR) := Σ_{i+j=n} Fil^iV ⊗_K Fil^jB_dR; these are G_K-invariant B^+_dR-lattices and Fil^n(V ⊗_K B_dR) = t^n Fil^0(V ⊗_K B_dR).
items.locator: no 10.4.1, pp. 334–335, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (the atlas has the filtration on D_dR(V) only, PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-vector-spaces).

items.name: Proposition 10.4.3: filtrations of V ↔ G_K-stable B^+_dR-lattices in V ⊗_K B_dR
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space. Fil^•V ↦ Fil^0(V ⊗_K B_dR) is a bijection between filtrations of V and G_K-stable B^+_dR-lattices in V ⊗_K B_dR; the inverse sends a lattice W to Fil^nV = (t^nW)^{G_K}, n ∈ Z. (Proof uses ker(H^1(G_K, Fil^kB_dR) → H^1(G_K, B_dR)) = 0 for all k ∈ Z.)
items.locator: Proposition 10.4.3, p. 335, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 10.4.4(1): filtered K-vector spaces ≃ generically flat B^+_dR-representations
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The functors (V, Fil^•V) ↦ Fil^0(V ⊗_K B_dR) and W ↦ (W[1/t]^{G_K}, (t^•W)^{G_K}) are inverse equivalences between finite-dimensional filtered K-vector spaces and generically flat B^+_dR-representations of G_K.
items.locator: Proposition 10.4.4(1), p. 336, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 10.4.4(2): structure of generically flat B^+_dR-representations
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A B^+_dR-representation W of rank n is generically flat iff there are (a_1,…,a_n) ∈ Z^n with W ≃ ⊕_{i=1}^n t^{a_i}B^+_dR.
items.locator: Proposition 10.4.4(2), p. 336, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: No 10.4.1: G_K-fixed points of the B_dR-affine Grassmannian (analogy with Gr^{G_m})
items.statement: For V ∈ Vect_K, G = GL(V), T a maximal torus and μ ∈ X_*(T)^+ with associated parabolic P_μ: (GL(V ⊗_K B_dR)/GL(V ⊗_K B^+_dR))^{G_K} = ⊔_{μ∈X_*(T)^+} G(K)/P_μ(K) (reformulation of Prop. 10.4.3/10.4.4, by analogy with Gr = ⊔ Gr_μ over C, π_μ: Gr_μ → G/P_μ Zariski-locally trivial with affine-space fibres, π_μ: Gr_μ^{G_m} ≅ G/P_μ and Gr^{G_m} = ⊔_μ G/P_μ).
items.locator: no 10.4.1, pp. 336–337, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor and GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0 loop-group nodes (B^+_dR-affine Grassmannian Gr_G without Galois fixed points).

items.name: Définition 10.4.5: de Rham equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X is de Rham if the B^+_dR-representation 𝓔̂_∞ is generically flat, i.e. 𝓔̂_∞[1/t] is generated by its G_K-invariants (geometrically: the pull-back of 𝓔 to the 'punctured formal disc' Spec(B_dR) is trivial).
items.locator: Définition 10.4.5, p. 337 (restated no 10.6.3, p. 342), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Exemple 10.4.6: log-crystalline bundles are de Rham
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Every log-crystalline 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X is de Rham (by Prop. 10.3.16 and Cor. 10.3.17).
items.locator: Exemple 10.4.6, p. 337, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Exemple 10.4.7: V de Rham iff V ⊗ O_X de Rham
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. V ∈ Rep_{Q_p}(G_K) is de Rham iff the equivariant bundle V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X is de Rham.
items.locator: Exemple 10.4.7, p. 337, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The notion 'de Rham representation' is planned (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissible-representations) but its bundle reformulation is not.

items.name: Proposition 10.4.8: de Rham equivariant bundles as triples
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The category of de Rham equivariant bundles on X is equivalent to the category of triples (M, Fil^•V, ι) with M ∈ Rep_{B_e}(G_K), Fil^•V a filtration of some V ∈ Vect_K and ι: M ⊗_{B_e} B_dR ≅ V ⊗_K B_dR a G_K-equivariant isomorphism.
items.locator: Proposition 10.4.8, p. 337, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: No 10.5.1: VectFil_K, the Hodge polygon and t_H
items.statement: VectFil_K is the exact category of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces with a finite decreasing filtration (as in no 10.4.1). The Hodge polygon of Fil^•V is the convex polygon with origin (0,0) and slopes i ∈ Z of multiplicity dim_K gr^iV; its endpoint has ordinate t_H(Fil^•V) = Σ_{i∈Z} i·dim_K gr^iV, an additive function t_H: VectFil_K → Z.
items.locator: no 10.5.1, p. 337, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nodes PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-vector-spaces and R06.2/hodge-number-tH.

items.name: No 10.5.1: t_N and ht on φ-Mod_{K_0}
items.statement: For (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0}, t_N(D,φ) is the endpoint (ordinate) of its Newton polygon and ht(D,φ) = dim_{K_0} D; these are additive functions t_N, ht: φ-Mod_{K_0} → Z on the abelian category φ-Mod_{K_0} (printed t_H for t_N; see sourceIssues).
items.locator: no 10.5.1, p. 338, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/newton-number-tN.

items.name: Définition 10.5.1(1): filtered φ-modules φ-ModFil_{K/K_0}
items.statement: φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} is the category of filtered φ-modules (D, φ, Fil^•D_K) with (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0} and Fil^•D_K ∈ VectFil_K, D_K = D ⊗_{K_0} K.
items.locator: Définition 10.5.1(1), p. 338, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules (MF^φ_K), stated for K/Q_p finite.

items.name: Définition 10.5.1(2): degree, rank, slope and HN filtrations of filtered φ-modules
items.statement: On φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} set deg(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) = t_H(Fil^•D_K) − t_N(D,φ) and rg(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) = ht(D,φ), additive functions to Z and N; μ = deg/rg. The formalism of §5.5.1 applies (the 'generic fibre' functor being the forgetful functor to φ-Mod_{K_0}, as in §5.5.2.4; the text names (D,φ,Fil^•D_K) ↦ D_K ∈ Vect_K, which does not satisfy the axioms, see sourceIssues), so every filtered φ-module has a Harder–Narasimhan filtration.
items.locator: Définition 10.5.1(2), p. 338, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The HN formalism is planned only for bundles (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism) and σ-modules over the Robba ring (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1); HN filtrations of filtered φ-modules are not planned. The printed generic-fibre functor to Vect_K is wrong (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Définition 10.5.2: weak admissibility = semistable of slope 0 (Faltings)
items.statement: A filtered φ-module is weakly admissible if it is semistable of slope 0 (for μ = (t_H − t_N)/ht); this is Faltings' reinterpretation of Fontaine's original definition ([26]).
items.locator: Définition 10.5.2, p. 338, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility (Fontaine's definition t_H(D) = t_N(D), t_H(D') ≤ t_N(D')); the equivalence with 'semistable of slope 0' is immediate but not stated.

items.name: No 10.5.2: completion at ∞ of E(D,φ)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For (D,φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{K_0}, Ê(D,φ)_∞ = D_K ⊗_K B^+_dR.
items.locator: no 10.5.2, p. 338, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Proposition 10.5.3: filtered φ-modules ≃ crystalline equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. There is an equivalence of exact categories φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} ≅ Fib^{G_K,cris}_X, (D,φ,Fil^•D_K) ↦ E(D,φ,Fil^•D_K), where E(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) is the G_K-equivariant modification of E(D,φ) at ∞ with Ê(D,φ,Fil^•D_K)_∞ = Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR). A quasi-inverse sends a crystalline 𝓔 to the isocrystal D(𝓔|_{X∖{∞}}) with the filtration (t^•𝓔̂_∞)^{G_K}.
items.locator: Proposition 10.5.3, p. 339, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Lemme 10.5.4: Hodge polygon of a lattice
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let Fil^•V ∈ VectFil_K and W = Fil^0(V ⊗_K B_dR). If V ⊗ B^+_dR = ⟨e_1,…,e_n⟩ and Fil^0(V ⊗_K B_dR) = ⟨t^{−a_1}e_1,…,t^{−a_n}e_n⟩ with a_1 ≤ … ≤ a_n, then the Hodge polygon of Fil^•V has slopes (a_1,…,a_n).
items.locator: Lemme 10.5.4, p. 339, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Lemme 10.5.5: deg E(D,φ,Fil) = deg(D,φ,Fil)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. deg E(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) = deg(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) = t_H − t_N; it follows from deg E(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) = deg E(D,φ) − [D ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR : Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR)] (generalised index of lattices).
items.locator: Lemme 10.5.5, p. 339, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Degree of a modification: nearest RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor (modifications, without degree formula); not planned in this form.

items.name: Proposition 10.5.6: HN filtrations of A and of E(A) correspond
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let A = (D,φ,Fil^•D_K) ∈ φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} with HN filtration 0 = A_0 ⊊ A_1 ⊊ … ⊊ A_r = A. Then the HN filtration of the bundle E(A) is 0 = E(A_0) ⊊ E(A_1) ⊊ … ⊊ E(A_r) = E(A). In particular A is weakly admissible iff E(A) is semistable of slope 0.
items.locator: Proposition 10.5.6, pp. 339–340, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action). Uses Prop. 9.1.4 (Galois invariance of the HN filtration).

items.name: No 10.5.3: H^0(X, E(A)) = V_cris(A); definition of admissibility
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For A ∈ φ-ModFil_{K/K_0}, H^0(X, E(A)) = V_cris(A). A is called admissible if dim_{Q_p} V_cris(A) = rg(A).
items.locator: no 10.5.3, p. 340, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: V_cris and admissibility are planned (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion, R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem) but the identification with global sections of E(A) is not.

items.name: Théorème 10.5.7: weakly admissible ⇔ admissible
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A filtered φ-module A ∈ φ-ModFil_{K/K_0} is weakly admissible iff it is admissible (proof: classification of vector bundles on X together with Prop. 10.5.6).
items.locator: Théorème 10.5.7, p. 340, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (special case K/Q_p finite): stage PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 ('Prove weak admissibility versus admissibility') and node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/colmez-fontaine-theorem ('For K/Q_p finite, ColmezFontaine(K) is the proposition: every weakly admissible D ∈ MF^{φ,N}_K is admissible'), proved in R06.3 by Berger's (φ,Γ)-module route. FF's theorem for K with arbitrary perfect residue field, and their proof via the classification of bundles on the curve, are not planned.

items.name: Théorème 10.5.7(1)–(2): dimension of V_cris(A)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For A ∈ φ-ModFil_{K/K_0}: (1) if t_H(A) > t_N(A) then dim_{Q_p} V_cris(A) = +∞; (2) if t_H(A) = t_N(A), A is admissible iff dim_{Q_p} V_cris(A) < +∞. (Because dim H^0(X, O_X(λ)) is 0 for λ < 0, 1 for λ = 0 and +∞ for λ > 0.)
items.locator: Théorème 10.5.7(1)–(2), p. 340, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest planned: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/vst-rank-one (rank one only) and R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion (finite-dimensionality for weakly admissible D).

items.name: Remarque 10.5.8: weakly admissible ⇔ admissible for filtered (φ,N)-modules
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The same proof shows that a filtered (φ,N)-module is admissible iff it is weakly admissible.

items.name: Définition 10.6.1: filtered (φ,N)-modules
items.statement: (φ,N)-ModFil_{K/K_0} is the category of quadruples (D,φ,N,Fil^•D_K) with (D,φ,N) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} and Fil^•D_K ∈ VectFil_K.

items.name: Proposition 10.6.2: filtered (φ,N)-modules ≃ log-crystalline equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Using the identification Ê(D,φ,N)_∞ = D ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR (log p = 0, Prop. 10.3.18), there is an equivalence (φ,N)-ModFil_{K/K_0} ≅ Fib^{G_K,log-cris}_X, (D,φ,N,Fil^•D_K) ↦ E(D,φ,N,Fil^•D_K), the equivariant modification of E(D,φ,N) with Ê(D,φ,N,Fil^•D_K)_∞ = Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR).
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.2, p. 340, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: No 10.6.2: restriction R_{L/K} and conjugate equivariant bundles 𝓔^{(σ)}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X and L|K finite in K̄, R_{L/K}𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_L}_X is obtained by restricting the action. For L|K Galois and 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_L}_X with underlying E and action u_τ: τ^*E ≅ E (τ ∈ G_L), and σ ∈ G_K, 𝓔^{(σ)} ∈ Fib^{G_L}_X has underlying bundle σ^*E and τ-action τ^*(σ^*E) = σ^*((στσ^{−1})^*E) →^{σ^*u_{στσ^{−1}}} σ^*E. Then (𝓔^{(σ_1)})^{(σ_2)} = 𝓔^{(σ_1σ_2)}; a morphism f induces f^{(σ)} = σ^*f; for σ ∈ G_L there is a canonical isomorphism can_σ: 𝓔^{(σ)} ≅ 𝓔 given by u_σ.
items.locator: no 10.6.2, p. 341, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Définition 10.6.3: descent data from L to K
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For L|K Galois and 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_L}_X, a descent datum from L to K on 𝓔 is a family of isomorphisms f_σ: 𝓔^{(σ)} ≅ 𝓔 in Fib^{G_L}_X (σ ∈ G_K) with f_{σ_1σ_2} = f_{σ_2} ∘ (f_{σ_1})^{(σ_2)} for σ_1,σ_2 ∈ G_K and f_σ = can_σ for σ ∈ G_L. For 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X, R_{L/K}𝓔 carries the canonical descent datum f_σ = u_σ.
items.locator: Définition 10.6.3, p. 341, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Proposition 10.6.4: Galois descent for equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For L|K finite Galois, 𝓔 ↦ (R_{L/K}𝓔 with its descent datum) is an equivalence between Fib^{G_K}_X and the category of G_L-equivariant bundles with a descent datum from L to K.
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.4, p. 341, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 10.6.5: potentially log-crystalline equivariant bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A G_K-equivariant bundle 𝓔 on X is potentially log-crystalline if there is a finite extension L of K in K̄ such that R_{L/K}𝓔 is a log-crystalline G_L-equivariant bundle.
items.locator: Définition 10.6.5, p. 341, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 10.6.6: filtered (φ,N,G_{L/K})-modules and (φ,N,G)-modules
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For L|K finite Galois (so L_0|K_0 is Galois, with restriction Gal(L|K) → Gal(L_0|K_0)): (1) a filtered (φ,N,G_{L/K})-module is (D,φ,N,Fil^•D_L) ∈ (φ,N)-ModFil_{L/L_0} with a semilinear (via Gal(L|K) → Gal(L_0|K_0)) action of Gal(L|K) on D commuting with φ and N and preserving the filtration Fil^•D_L of D ⊗_{L_0} L; category (φ,N,G_{L/K})-ModFil_{L/L_0}. (2) (φ,N,G)-ModFil := ∪_{L/K} (φ,N,G_{L/K})-ModFil_{L/L_0} over finite Galois L|K in K̄, using that for L'|L|K finite Galois the scalar-extension functor (φ,N,G_{L/K})-ModFil_{L/L_0} → (φ,N,G_{L'/K})-ModFil_{L'/L'_0} is fully faithful.
items.locator: Définition 10.6.6, p. 342, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules-with-descent-data (including the colimit over L giving filtered (φ,N,G_K)-modules); K/Q_p finite there.

items.name: Proposition 10.6.7: filtered (φ,N,G)-modules ≃ potentially log-crystalline bundles
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. The category of filtered (φ,N,G)-modules is equivalent to that of potentially log-crystalline G_K-equivariant bundles. (For A = (D,φ,N,Fil^•D_L) and σ ∈ Gal(L|K), E(A)^{(σ)} = E(A^{(σ)}) with A^{(σ)} = (D ⊗_{L_0,σ|L_0} L_0, φ⊗φ, N⊗Id, Fil^•D_L ⊗_{L,σ} L); then apply Prop. 10.6.4.)
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.7, p. 342, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action). The representation-theoretic analogue (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/potentially-semistable-descent-equivalence) is planned for representations only.

items.name: Lemme 10.6.8: potentially de Rham ⇒ de Rham
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Every potentially de Rham G_K-equivariant bundle is de Rham; equivalently, every potentially flat B_dR-representation is flat: if L|K is finite Galois and W ∈ Rep_{B_dR}(G_K), W^{G_L} is a finite-dimensional L = B_dR^{G_L}-vector space with semilinear Gal(L|K)-action and dim_L W^{G_L} = dim_K W^{G_K} (Hilbert 90).
items.locator: Lemme 10.6.8, p. 342, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/de-rham-base-change (descent of D_dR for representations).

items.name: Hilbert 90 (black box): semilinear Galois descent
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L|K and a finite-dimensional L-vector space W with a semilinear Gal(L|K)-action, W^{Gal(L|K)} ⊗_K L ≅ W.
items.locator: used in Lemme 10.6.8, p. 342, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/semilinear-galois-descent. Mathlib has only the rank-one form (groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units: H^1(Gal(L/K), L^×) = 1), not the GL_n/semilinear descent form.

items.name: Proposition 10.6.9: potentially log-crystalline ⇒ de Rham
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Every potentially log-crystalline G_K-equivariant bundle is de Rham.
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.9, p. 343, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For representations ('every potentially semistable representation is de Rham') see PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3/p-adic-monodromy-theorem; the bundle statement is not planned.

items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Every de Rham G_K-equivariant bundle on X is potentially log-crystalline.

items.name: Corollary of Théorème 10.6.10: the p-adic monodromy theorem
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (Theorem 10.6.10 applied to semistable equivariant bundles of slope 0.) Every de Rham p-adic representation of G_K is potentially log-crystalline (= potentially semistable).

FF deduce the theorem for K with arbitrary perfect residue field from Théorème 10.6.10; that generality is not planned.

items.name: No 10.6.3: reduction of Thm 10.6.10 to the flat case
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. A de Rham equivariant bundle 𝓔 can be modified at ∞ into a de Rham equivariant bundle 𝓔' with 𝓔̂'_∞ = (𝓔̂_∞[1/t])^{G_K} ⊗_K B^+_dR (a flat B^+_dR-representation); since potential log-crystallinity only depends on 𝓔|_{X∖{∞}}, Theorem 10.6.10 reduces to Theorem 10.6.11.

items.name: Théorème 10.6.11: bundles with flat completion at ∞ are potentially log-crystalline
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let 𝓔 ∈ Fib^{G_K}_X be such that 𝓔̂_∞ is a flat B^+_dR-representation of G_K (i.e. 𝓔̂_∞ ≅ (𝓔̂_∞)^{G_K} ⊗_K B^+_dR). Then 𝓔 is potentially log-crystalline.

items.name: No 10.6.4: Theorem 10.6.11 for semistable 𝓔
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let 𝓔 be as in Thm 10.6.11 and semistable of slope λ = d/h, (d,h) = 1. After a finite unramified extension (so that k_K ⊃ F_{p^h}), Thm 10.1.7 gives 𝓔 ≃ V ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ) with ρ: G_K → GL_{D_λ^op}(V) continuous; as C-representations O_X(λ)_∞ ⊗ k(∞) = C^h, D_λ ⊗_{Q_p} C ≃ M_h(C), and (via Morita) V_C := V ⊗_{Q_p} C ≃ (V_C ⊗_{M_h(C)} C^h) ⊗_C C^h, so V_C is Hodge–Tate of weight 0; by Sen, ρ(I_K) is finite, so after a finite extension L|K, R_{L/K}𝓔 ≃ (R_{L/K}V) ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ) with R_{L/K}V unramified, hence R_{L/K}𝓔 is crystalline.
items.locator: no 10.6.4, pp. 343–344, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Sen [58] 3.2 (black box): C-admissible representations have finite inertia image
items.statement: If ρ: G_K → GL(V) is a p-adic representation with V ⊗_{Q_p} C Hodge–Tate of weight 0 (i.e. V ⊗ C ≅ C^{dim V} as semilinear representations), then ρ(I_K) is finite.
items.locator: used in no 10.6.4, p. 344, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest planned: PadicHodgeTheory:P7/sen-module (Sen's operator Θ_V; V Hodge–Tate iff Θ_V semisimple with integer eigenvalues) and R06.2/hodge-tate-decomposition-tate(2) (converse direction only). The implication 'C-admissible ⇒ inertia finite' is not stated.

items.name: Morita equivalence M_h(C) ~ C (black box)
items.statement: For a field C and h ≥ 1, the category of (right) M_h(C)-modules is equivalent to that of C-vector spaces, via M ↦ M ⊗_{M_h(C)} C^h with inverse W ↦ W ⊗_C C^h (A ∈ M_h(C) acting by Id ⊗ ^tA).
items.locator: used in no 10.6.4, p. 344, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: mathlib:moritaEquivalenceMatrix gives the Morita equivalence ModuleCat R ≌ ModuleCat (Matrix ι ι R) for left modules (via ModuleCat.matrixEquivalence); the right-module form and the G_K-equivariance used by FF are not formalised.

items.name: No 10.6.5.1: the map α_{A_1,A_2} on extensions and the identification of the Ext groups
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For A_1 = (D_1,φ_1,N_1), A_2 = (D_2,φ_2,N_2) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0}, the functor A ↦ E(A) induces α_{A_1,A_2}: Ext^1_{(φ,N)-Mod_{K_0}}(A_1,A_2) → ker(Ext^1_{Fib^{G_K}_X}(E(A_1),E(A_2)) → Ext^1_{Rep_{B^+_dR}(G_K)}(Ê(A_1)_∞, Ê(A_2)_∞)); the target consists of the classes of extensions of E(A_1) by E(A_2) that are de Rham. Moreover Ext^1(A_1,A_2) = Ext^1(1, A_1^∨ ⊗ A_2), Ext^1_{Fib}(E(A_1),E(A_2)) = Ext^1(O_X, E(A_1^∨ ⊗ A_2)), and Ext^1_{Rep_{B^+_dR}}(Ê(A_1)_∞,Ê(A_2)_∞) = H^1(G_K, D_1^∨ ⊗ D_2 ⊗_{K_0} B^+_dR) = D_1^∨ ⊗ D_2 ⊗_{K_0} H^1(G_K, B^+_dR) = D_1^∨ ⊗ D_2 ⊗_{K_0} H^1(G_K, C).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.1, p. 344, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Lemme 10.6.12: extensions of (φ,N)-modules without common slopes
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For (D_1,φ_1,N_1), (D_2,φ_2,N_2) ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0} having no Dieudonné–Manin slope in common, there is an isomorphism Hom(D_1,D_2)^{φ=p^{−1}} ≅ Ext^1_{(φ,N)-Mod_{K_0}}((D_1,φ_1,N_1),(D_2,φ_2,N_2)) (f ↦ the extension D_1 ⊕ D_2 with N = (N_1 0; f N_2); here φ acts on Hom by f ↦ φ_2 f φ_1^{−1}).
items.locator: Lemme 10.6.12, p. 345, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (no Ext computations for (φ,N)-modules in the atlas).

items.name: No 10.6.5.1: α identifies with β_{D,φ,N}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Assume the slopes of (D_1,φ_1) are strictly larger than those of (D_2,φ_2), and let (D,φ,N) = (D_1,φ_1,N_1)^∨ ⊗ (D_2,φ_2,N_2). Then (Prop. 9.2.3) Ext^1_{Fib^{G_K}_X}(E(A_1),E(A_2)) = H^1(G_K, Hom(E(A_1),E(A_2))) = H^1(G_K, (D ⊗_{K_0} B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}), and α_{A_1,A_2} identifies with β_{D,φ,N}: D^{φ=p^{−1}} → ker(H^1(G_K, (D ⊗_{K_0} B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) → H^1(G_K, D ⊗_{K_0} C)), defined for any (φ,N)-module (D,φ,N) with strictly negative slopes as β_{D,φ,N} = α_{1,(D,φ,N)}, 1 = (K_0,φ,0).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.1, p. 345, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Lemme 10.6.13: β for N = 0
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let (D,φ) be a φ-module with strictly negative slopes, viewed as a (φ,N)-module with N = 0. Then β_{D,φ,0}: D^{φ=p^{−1}} → H^1(G_K, (D ⊗_{K_0} B)^{φ=Id}) is a ↦ [(a ⊗ log_{x,σ})_σ], with (log_{x,σ})_σ ∈ Z^1(G_K, B^{φ=p}) the cocycle of no 10.3.2.
items.locator: Lemme 10.6.13, pp. 345–346, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: No 10.6.5.2: dévissage of Thm 10.6.11 to a Galois-cohomology statement
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let 𝓔 be G_K-equivariant with 𝓔̂_∞ flat, with HN filtration 0 = 𝓔_0 ⊊ … ⊊ 𝓔_r = 𝓔. Any B^+_dR-representation which is a subquotient of a flat one is flat, so each (𝓔_j/𝓔_i)^_∞ is flat. By induction on r (r = 1 is no 10.6.4) and after a finite extension, 𝓔/𝓔_{r−1} = E(A_1), 𝓔_{r−1} = E(A_2) with A_1, A_2 ∈ (φ,N)-Mod_{K_0}, and the class of 0 → 𝓔_{r−1} → 𝓔 → 𝓔/𝓔_{r−1} → 0 lies in ker(Ext^1_{Fib}(E(A_1),E(A_2)) → Ext^1_{Rep_{B^+_dR}}(Ê(A_1)_∞,Ê(A_2)_∞)); hence Thm 10.6.11 follows from Prop. 10.6.14.
items.locator: no 10.6.5.2, p. 346, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Proposition 10.6.14: β_{D,φ,N} is an isomorphism
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let (D,φ,N) be a (φ,N)-module over K_0 with strictly negative slopes. Then β_{D,φ,N}: D^{φ=p^{−1}} → ker(H^1(G_K, (D ⊗_{K_0} B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) → H^1(G_K, D ⊗_{K_0} C)) is an isomorphism. (Injectivity follows from full faithfulness of (φ,N)-modules → equivariant bundles.)
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.14, p. 346, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

items.name: Définition 10.6.15: H^1_g for (φ,N)-modules
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. For a (φ,N)-module M, H^1_g(G_K, (M ⊗ B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) := ker(H^1(G_K, (M ⊗ B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) → H^1(G_K, M ⊗ B^+_dR)).
items.locator: Définition 10.6.15, p. 347, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: No 10.6.5.2: reduction of Prop. 10.6.14 to N = 0 and D isoclinic
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let D = ⊕_{i=1}^m D_i be the isoclinic decomposition with slopes λ_1 > … > λ_m (all < 0). Then N|_{D_m} = 0, D' = D_m is a sub-(φ,N)-module, D'' = D/D'; there are exact sequences 0 → D'^{φ=p^{−1}} → D^{φ=p^{−1}} → D''^{φ=p^{−1}} → 0 and 0 → H^1_g(G_K,(D'⊗B)^{φ=Id}) → H^1_g(G_K,(D⊗B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) → H^1_g(G_K,(D''⊗B_log)^{φ=Id,N=0}) (using Hom_{Fib^{G_K}}(O_X, E(D'',φ,N)) = Hom(1, D'') = 0 and Prop. 9.2.3), compatible with β; so if β_{D',φ} and β_{D'',φ,N} are isomorphisms so is β_{D,φ,N}, and by induction on the number of slopes Prop. 10.6.14 reduces to Prop. 10.6.16.
items.locator: no 10.6.5.2, pp. 346–347, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: Proposition 10.6.16: H^1_g of (D ⊗ B)^{φ=Id} for isoclinic D
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Let (D,φ) be an isoclinic isocrystal of strictly negative slope. (1) If its slope is ≠ −1 then H^1_g(G_K, (D ⊗ B)^{φ=Id}) = 0. (2) If its slope is −1 then the injection β_{D,φ}: D^{φ=p^{−1}} → H^1_g(G_K, (D ⊗ B)^{φ=Id}), a ↦ [(a ⊗ log_{x,σ})_σ], is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.16, pp. 347–348, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (FarguesFontaineDiamonds F0–F5, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB4 and AdicSpaces layer 6 construct the curve, bundles, classification and modifications without any Galois action).

items.name: No 10.6.5.2: reduction of Prop. 10.6.16 to k_K algebraically closed
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. With M = (D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id} (D of nonzero slopes): (B^+)^{I_K} = W(k̄)_Q gives M^{I_K} = 0, so Res: H^1(G_K,M) ≅ H^1(I_K,M)^{Gal(k̄|k_K)}; H^i(Gal(k̄|k_K), K̂^{nr}) = 0 for i > 0 and C^{I_K} = K̂^{nr} give Res: H^1(G_K,C) ≅ H^1(I_K,C)^{Gal(k̄|k_K)}; hence Res: H^1_g(G_K,(D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id}) ≅ H^1_g(I_K,(D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id})^{Gal(k̄|k_K)}, and since D = (D ⊗_{K_0} W(k̄)_Q)^{Gal(k̄|k_K)}, β_{D,φ} is an isomorphism if β_{(D,φ)⊗W(k̄)_Q} is. Then (k_K algebraically closed) D decomposes into simple isocrystals and Prop. 10.6.16 reduces to Prop. 10.6.17.
items.locator: no 10.6.5.2, p. 348, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Ingredients planned elsewhere: inflation–restriction (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2), invariants over K̂^{ur} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/period-ring-invariants), completed unramified descent (R06.1/semilinear-galois-descent).

items.name: Inflation–restriction (black box): five-term exact sequence in continuous cohomology
items.statement: For a closed normal subgroup I_K ⊂ G_K with quotient Gal(k̄|k_K) and a topological G_K-module M: 0 → H^1(Gal(k̄|k_K), M^{I_K}) → H^1(G_K, M) → H^1(I_K, M)^{Gal(k̄|k_K)} → H^2(Gal(k̄|k_K), M^{I_K}).
items.locator: used in no 10.6.5.2, p. 348, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (discrete or finite-dimensional coefficients). ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2/compact-five-term ('T … discrete, a finitely generated Z_p-module or a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space', five terms only under finiteness hypotheses) and R02.2/five-term-transgression ('A discrete'); tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-5-exact-sequences is explicitly limited to discrete coefficients ('do not state this layer beyond discrete coefficients'). FF apply the sequence to Banach G_K-modules such as C and (D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id} (No 10.6.5.2); not planned. Mathlib has only groupCohomology.H1InfRes_exact (abstract groups, three terms, no topology).

items.name: Proposition 10.6.17 (Colmez [13] prop. 10.11, black box): H^1_g of (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. Assume k_K algebraically closed. Let d, h > 0 be coprime integers, u: (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d} → C^h, x ↦ (θ(x), θ(φ(x)), …, θ(φ^{h−1}(x))), and H^1_g(G_K, (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) := ker(H^1(G_K,(B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) →u_* H^1(G_K, C^h)). (1) If d = h = 1, H^1_g(G_K, (B^+)^{φ=p}) is a 1-dimensional Q_p-vector space generated by the class of (log_{x,σ})_σ, which is the class of the extension 0 → Q_p(1) → V_p(E) → Q_p → 0 of a Tate elliptic curve E over K via Q_p(1) = Q_p·t ⊂ (B^+)^{φ=p}. (2) If (d,h) ≠ (1,1), H^1_g(G_K, (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) = 0.
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.17, pp. 348–349, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Colmez's Banach–Colmez Galois-cohomology computation is not planned (no H^1_g of Banach–Colmez spaces in the atlas; VB3 treats BC spaces geometrically).

items.name: No 10.6.5.3: the Lubin–Tate exact sequence and the Hodge–Tate decomposition of χ^d_{LT_h}
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (Context of Prop. 10.6.17.) For d, h > 0 coprime and χ_{LT_h}: G_K → Q_{p^h}^× the Lubin–Tate character, there is an exact sequence of G_K-modules 0 → χ^d_{LT_h} → (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d} → B^+_dR/t^dB^+_dR → 0, giving 0 → K →δ H^1(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) → H^1(G_K,(B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) → H^1(G_K, B^+_dR/t^dB^+_dR) = H^1(G_K,C), with δ the Bloch–Kato exponential; hence coker(δ) = ker(H^1(G_K,(B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) →θ_* H^1(G_K,C)). The maps χ^d_{LT_h} → gr^dB^+_dR = C(d) and θ∘φ^i: χ^d_{LT_h} → C (0 < i < h) give the Hodge–Tate decomposition χ^d_{LT_h} ⊗_{Q_p} C ≅ C(d) ⊕ C^{h−1}. H^1_g(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) := ker(H^1(G_K,χ^d_{LT_h}) → H^1(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h} ⊗_{Q_p} C)) parametrises the extensions of Q_p by χ^d_{LT_h} (equivalently of Q_{p^h} by χ^d_{LT_h} as Q_{p^h}-representations) that are de Rham; it is printed as equal to ker(H^1(G_K,(B^+)^{φ^h=p^d}) → H^1(G_K,C^h)) (only its quotient by δ(K) is; see sourceIssues).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.3, pp. 349–350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (the case h = d = 1 as 0 → O → O(1) → O_{S^♯} → 0), PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 (Bloch–Kato exponential). Lubin–Tate characters of Q_{p^h} with general (d,h) are not planned.

items.name: Proposition 10.6.18(1): extensions of Q_p by Q_p(1)
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (Context of Prop. 10.6.17: k_K algebraically closed; the book does not restate this hypothesis in Prop. 10.6.18, and the second sentence is false without it, see sourceIssues.) The Bloch–Kato exponential δ: K → H^1(G_K, Q_p(1)) has cokernel a 1-dimensional Q_p-vector space. In other words, an extension V of Q_p by Q_p(1) is either crystalline, isomorphic to the Tate module of an elliptic curve with good ordinary reduction, or semistable, isomorphic to the Tate module of a Tate elliptic curve.
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.18(1), p. 350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (special case K/Q_p finite): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/kummer-representations-semistable (d) ('Every extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) is semistable, and the crystalline classes form the Q_p-hyperplane Q_p ⊗ Ô_K^× …', 'Throughout: K/Q_p is finite'), with PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 ('Work first over a finite extension of Q_p') for the Bloch–Kato exponential. FF use Prop. 10.6.18 after the reduction of No 10.6.5.2 to k_K algebraically closed, i.e. for K with infinite residue field; not planned. The elliptic-curve interpretation is only partly covered (R06.6/tate-curve-tate-module).

items.name: Proposition 10.6.18(2): de Rham extensions of Q_{p^h} by χ^d_{LT_h} are crystalline
items.statement: Setting of Ch. 10: E = Q_p; K|Q_p complete, discretely valued, with perfect residue field k_K; K_0 = W(k_K)_Q; K̄ a fixed algebraic closure, G_K = Gal(K̄|K); C = K̄^ (completion); F = C^♭; X = X_{F,Q_p}, Y = Y_F, B = O(Y), P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=p^d}. (Context of Prop. 10.6.17: k_K algebraically closed, not restated in the book.) If (d,h) ≠ (1,1), every 2-dimensional Q_{p^h}-representation which is an extension of Q_{p^h} by χ^d_{LT_h} and is de Rham as a Q_p-representation is crystalline; i.e. the Bloch–Kato exponential δ: K → H^1_g(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) is an isomorphism (printed with H^1 in place of H^1_g, which is false for h ≥ 2; see sourceIssues).
items.locator: Proposition 10.6.18(2), p. 350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Remarque 10.6.19: Kummer theory and the Bloch–Kato exponential of Q_p(1)
items.statement: Case (1) of Prop. 10.6.18 follows from Kummer theory ([51]): with K̂^× the p-adic completion of K^×, H^1(G_K, Q_p(1)) = K̂^× ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p; exp: K → K̂^× ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p, x ↦ exp(p^n x) ⊗ p^{−n} (n ≫ 0) identifies with the Bloch–Kato exponential; v extends to v: K̂^× → Z_p, and 0 → K →exp K̂^× ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p →v⊗Id Q_p → 0 is exact.
items.locator: Remarque 10.6.19, p. 350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only (special case K/Q_p finite): PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/kummer-representation (v) (H^1(K, Q_p(1)) ≅ Q_p ⊗ K̂^× ≅ Q_p ⊕ K) and PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 (Bloch–Kato exponential, 'Work first over a finite extension of Q_p'). FF's K has arbitrary perfect residue field (algebraically closed after No 10.6.5.2); not planned. Tau Ceti has finite-level Kummer sequences (TauCeti.kummerSequence_exact) but not this p-adic statement.

items.name: Lemme 10.6.20: admissible filtrations concentrated in non-positive degrees
items.statement: Let K|Q_p be finite and (D,φ) an isoclinic isocrystal over K_0 of strictly negative slope. There is a filtration Fil^•D_K of D_K such that (D,φ,Fil^•D_K) is admissible and Fil^iD_K = 0 for i > 0.
items.locator: Lemme 10.6.20, pp. 350–351, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: No 10.6.5.4: H^1_g((D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id}) as the cokernel of the Bloch–Kato exponential
items.statement: Let K|Q_p be finite, (D,φ) isoclinic of strictly negative slope, Fil^•D_K as in Lemme 10.6.20 and V = V_cris(D,φ,Fil^•D_K) (crystalline, non-negative Hodge–Tate weights). Then Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR) ⊂ D ⊗ B^+_dR, 0 → V → (D ⊗ B^+)^{φ=Id} → D ⊗ B^+_dR/Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR) → 0 is exact, H^0(G_K,(D⊗B^+)^{φ=Id}) = 0, D_K/Fil^0D_K ≅ H^0(G_K, D ⊗ B^+_dR/Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR)), the connecting map is exp_V: D_K/Fil^0D_K → H^1(G_K,V), and with H^1_g(G_K,V) := ker(H^1(G_K,V) → H^1(G_K, V ⊗ B_dR)), H^1_g(G_K,(D⊗B^+)^{φ=Id}) = coker(exp_V: D_K/Fil^0D_K → H^1_g(G_K,V)).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.4, p. 351, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The Bloch–Kato exponential as a connecting map is planned (PadicHodgeRegulators:L1) but this identification is not.

items.name: No 10.6.5.4: Ext^1 of filtered (φ,N)-modules and the map into H^1_g(G_K,V)
items.statement: (Setting of the preceding item.) Since (D,φ) has no slope 0, Ext^1_{(φ,N)-ModFil_{K/K_0}}(1, (D,φ,Fil^•D_K)) = D^{φ=p^{−1}} ⊕ D_K/Fil^0D_K (the first factor parametrising the monodromy, cf. Lemme 10.6.12, the second the filtration). Applying V_log-cris gives an injective map D^{φ=p^{−1}} ⊕ D_K/Fil^0D_K ↪ H^1_g(G_K,V) which is exp_V on the second factor; Prop. 10.6.16 is equivalent to this map being an isomorphism, i.e. to: every de Rham extension of Q_p by V is log-crystalline.
items.locator: no 10.6.5.4, p. 352, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: No 10.6.5.4: the dual exponential and its surjectivity
items.statement: (Setting of the preceding items.) H^1(G_K, Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR)) → H^1(G_K, D ⊗ B_dR) is injective, so H^1_g(G_K,V) = ker(H^1(G_K,V) → H^1(G_K, Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR))); Tate's K ≅ H^1(G_K,C), 1 ↦ −[log∘χ_cyc], induces Fil^0D_K ≅ H^1(G_K, Fil^0(D ⊗ B_dR)); the resulting map H^1(G_K,V) → Fil^0D_K is the dual exponential exp^*_V: for x ∈ (Fil^0D_K)^* = D_dR(V^*(1))/Fil^0 and y ∈ H^1(G_K,V), ⟨exp_{V^*(1)}(x), y⟩ = Tr_{K/Q_p}⟨x, exp^*_V(y)⟩ under the perfect Tate pairing H^1(G_K,V^*(1)) × H^1(G_K,V) → H^2(G_K,Q_p(1)) = Q_p. The text concludes that exp^*_V is surjective 'by injectivity of exp_{V^*(1)}' (which requires Fil^1(D^*)^{φ=p} = (D^*)^{φ=p}; see sourceIssues).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.4, p. 352, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stage PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 plans the exponential, dual exponential and their local duality relation (K/Q_p finite). The specific surjectivity claim fails for general admissible filtrations (sourceIssues).

items.name: Tate local duality and Euler characteristic (black box)
items.statement: For K|Q_p finite and V a finite-dimensional p-adic representation of G_K: dim H^0(G_K,V) − dim H^1(G_K,V) + dim H^2(G_K,V) = −[K:Q_p]·dim V, and the cup-product pairing H^i(G_K,V^*(1)) × H^{2−i}(G_K,V) → H^2(G_K,Q_p(1)) = Q_p is perfect; in particular dim H^2(G_K,V) = dim H^0(G_K,V^*(1)).
items.locator: used in no 10.6.5.4, pp. 352–353, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 5 plans local Tate duality and the Euler characteristic for finite coefficients; ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 plans derived local duality (node D7/derived-local-duality). The rational-coefficient Euler characteristic formula is not stated as such.

items.name: No 10.6.5.4: Hyodo's alternative proof of Prop. 10.6.16 for K|Q_p finite (dimension count)
items.statement: (Setting of the preceding items.) The sequence 0 → D^{φ=p^{−1}} ⊕ D_K/Fil^0D_K →α H^1(G_K,V) →β Fil^0D_K → 0 satisfies β∘α = 0, α injective, β surjective (as claimed), and is exact by a dimension count: V^{G_K} = 0, dim H^2(G_K,V) = dim H^0(G_K,V^*(1)) = dim Fil^1(D^*)^{φ=p}, which is claimed to equal dim (D^*)^{φ=p} by weak admissibility of D^*, and dim (D^*)^{φ=p} = dim D^{φ=p^{−1}} (both are ker(Id − u), ker(Id − ^tu) for the Frobenius u of Gal(k̄|k_K) on W = (D ⊗_{K_0} W(k̄)_Q)^{φ=p^{−1}}).
items.locator: no 10.6.5.4, pp. 352–353, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned. The step Fil^1(D^*)^{φ=p} = (D^*)^{φ=p} is false for general admissible filtrations with Fil^1D_K = 0 (sourceIssues); the argument works if Fil^•D_K is chosen with all jumps equal to −1 in the slope −1 case.

items.name: §11.1.1: the ring ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭, its maximal ideal m_ℬ and the field L
items.statement: Recall (§1.10.4): ℬ := B^{b,+}/𝔭 where 𝔭 = {x ∈ B^{b,+} | v_0(x) > 0} = {Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]πⁿ ∈ B^{b,+} | ∃ε>0, ∀n, v(x_n) ≥ ε}. Put m := ker(B_E^{b,+} → W_{O_E}(k_F)_Q) = {Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]π_Eⁿ ∈ B_E^{b,+} | ∀n, v(x_n) > 0} and m_ℬ := m/𝔭. Recalled facts: ℬ is a local ring with maximal ideal m_ℬ and residue field W_{O_E}(k_F)_Q, and the map induced by B^{b,+} ⊂ B^+, ℬ → B^+/{x ∈ B^+ | v_0(x) > 0}, is an isomorphism. In §11.1 one writes L := W_{O_E}(k_F)_Q. Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: §11.1.1, p. 356, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No atlas stage or node introduces the quotient B^{b,+}/{v_0>0} (the 'strange ring' of §1.10.4/§4.1). Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/witt-partial-valuations (partial valuations v_n on Witt vectors) and AdicSpaces layer 6.1 (A_inf = W(O_F)); neither forms this quotient or proves it local with residue field W(k_F)[1/π].

items.name: Définition 11.1.1: the categories φ-Mod_A for A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ}
items.statement: For A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ}, φ-Mod_A is the category of pairs (M, φ) where M is a free A-module of finite rank and φ : M ⥲ M is a φ_E-semilinear isomorphism (morphisms: A-linear maps commuting with φ). φ-Mod_L is the Tannakian category of k_F-isocrystals relative to E. Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Définition 11.1.1, p. 356, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the case A = L is in scope anywhere: Mathlib has mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal (for E = Q_p, over Frac W(k), k a perfect domain; read in Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Isocrystal.lean — a class on a K(p,k)-vector space, finite dimension not imposed), VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 plans isocrystals over W_{O_E}(F̄_q)[1/π] (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block) and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-module defines σ-modules over W(κ,O)[π^{-1}]. No stage treats φ-modules over B^+ or over ℬ.

items.name: §11.1.1: tensor structure, internal Hom, duals and H⁰, H¹ on φ-Mod_A
items.statement: For A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ}, φ-Mod_A is an E-linear symmetric tensor category with unit 1_A = (A, φ_E), duals and internal Hom: (M_1,φ_1) ⊗ (M_2,φ_2) = (M_1 ⊗_A M_2, φ_1 ⊗ φ_2), Hom((M_1,φ_1),(M_2,φ_2)) = (Hom_A(M_1,M_2), ψ) with ψ(f) = φ_2 ∘ f ∘ φ_1^{−1}, X̌ := Hom(X, 1_A), and X̌_1 ⊗ X_2 ⥲ Hom(X_1, X_2). For X = (M, φ): H⁰(X) := Hom(1_A, X) = M^{φ=Id}, H¹(X) := Ext¹(1_A, X) (Yoneda) = coker(Id − φ : M → M); and Hom(X_1, X_2) = H⁰(Hom(X_1, X_2)). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: §11.1.1, pp. 356–357, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The same formalism (dual, tensor, internal Hom, H⁰ = ker(F−1), H¹ = coker(F−1), Ext = H¹(M_1^∨⊗M_2)) is stated in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-module, but only for R^int, R^bd, R, O_E, E, R^alg, Γ^alg_con, W(κ,O)[π^{-1}], not for B^+ or ℬ.

items.name: §11.1.1: long exact sequence of H⁰, H¹ in φ-Mod_A
items.statement: φ-Mod_A (A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ}) is naturally an exact category, and every short exact sequence 0 → X_1 → X_2 → X_3 → 0 in it gives an exact sequence of E-vector spaces 0 → H⁰(X_1) → H⁰(X_2) → H⁰(X_3) → H¹(X_1) → H¹(X_2) → H¹(X_3) → 0.
items.locator: §11.1.1, p. 357, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Snake lemma for Id − φ; no node for these coefficient rings (RD.1/frobenius-module has H⁰, H¹ for other rings but not this sequence).

items.name: §11.1.1: Tate objects A(n) and Tate twists X(n)
items.statement: Fix a uniformizer π of E. For n ∈ Z, A(n) := (A, πⁿφ_E) ∈ φ-Mod_A, and for X = (M, φ), X(n) := X ⊗ A(n) = (M, πⁿφ). One has A(n) = A(1)^{⊗n} and A(0) = 1_A.
items.locator: §11.1.1, p. 357, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Convention: φ acts on A(n) by πⁿ, so H⁰(A(−d)) = A^{φ=π^d}. Nearest: RD.1/frobenius-module (twist M(c) multiplies F by π^c, same sign) and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign (O(n) = E(Ĕ, π^{−n}σ)); neither covers B^+ or ℬ.

items.name: §11.1.2: P_{E,π} = ⊕_d H⁰(B^+(−d)) ≅ ⊕_d H⁰(ℬ(−d))
items.statement: The graded E-algebra ⊕_{d≥0} H⁰(B^+(−d)) (multiplication H⁰(X) ⊗_E H⁰(Y) → H⁰(X ⊗ Y)) is P_{E,π} = ⊕_{d≥0}(B^+)^{φ=π^d}, and by Proposition 4.1.6 the reduction map B^+ → ℬ induces an isomorphism P_{E,π} = ⊕_{d≥0} H⁰(B^+(−d)) ⥲ ⊕_{d≥0} H⁰(ℬ(−d)). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: §11.1.2, p. 357, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The graded ring P = ⊕ H⁰(X_S, O(n)) is planned in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3 (node RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map), but its comparison with invariants in B^{b,+}/{v_0>0} (Prop. 4.1.6) is not stated anywhere.

items.name: §11.1.2: the graded P_{E,π}-module functor Γ_•
items.statement: For X = (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+}, Γ_•(X) = ⊕_{d≥0} Γ_d(X), Γ_d(X) := H⁰(X(−d)) = M^{φ=π^d}, is a graded P_{E,π}-module via H⁰(B^+(−d)) ⊗ H⁰(X(−d')) → H⁰(X(−(d+d'))); this defines a functor Γ_• : φ-Mod_{B^+} → graded P_{E,π}-modules.
items.locator: §11.1.2, p. 357, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed target of the multiplication is H⁰(X(−d+d')); see sourceIssues. Nearest: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (graded algebra only, not modules attached to φ-modules over B^+).

items.name: §11.1.3: change of coefficient field, φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E' ≃ φ-Mod_{A_{E'}}
items.statement: Let E'|E be finite, with residue fields k_E, k_{E'} embedded in O_F, f = f_{E'/E}, and A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ}. Let φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E' be the category of pairs (X, ι), X ∈ φ-Mod_{A_E}, ι : E' → End(X) a morphism of E-algebras. For (M, φ, ι) one has M = ⊕_{i∈Z/fZ} M_i with M_i = {x ∈ M | ∀a ∈ W_{O_E}(k_{E'})_Q, ι(a)x = φ_E^i(a)x}, φ : M_i ⥲ M_{i+1}, M_0 is a free A_E ⊗_{W_{O_E}(k_{E'})_Q} E' = A_{E'}-module and (M_0, φ^f) ∈ φ-Mod_{A_{E'}}; this defines φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E' → φ-Mod_{A_{E'}}. Conversely for (M', φ') ∈ φ-Mod_{A_{E'}} put M = ⊕_{i=0}^{f−1} M' ⊗_{A_{E'},φ_E^i} A_{E'} with ψ_i(m ⊗ x) = m ⊗ φ_E(x) (i < f−1), φ'(m) ⊗ φ_E(x) (i = f−1); then (M, ⊕ψ_i) ∈ φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E'. The two functors are adjoint and are inverse equivalences φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E' ⥲ φ-Mod_{A_{E'}}.
items.locator: §11.1.3, p. 358, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: For A = L this is the scalar-extension adjunction planned in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 (node VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction, with the same explicit cyclic Frobenius). The cases A = B^+ and A = ℬ are not planned.

items.name: §11.1.3: the adjoint pair π_{E'/E*}, π^*_{E'/E} on φ-modules
items.statement: Via φ-Mod_{A_E} ⊗_E E' ≃ φ-Mod_{A_{E'}} there is an adjoint pair π_{E'/E*} : φ-Mod_{A_{E'}} → φ-Mod_{A_E}, π^*_{E'/E} : φ-Mod_{A_E} → φ-Mod_{A_{E'}}, given by π_{E'/E*}(X, ι) = X and π^*_{E'/E}(Y) = Y ⊗_E E' (canonical E'-action); in terms of φ-modules, π^*_{E'/E}(M, φ) = (M ⊗_{A_E} A_{E'}, φ^{f_{E'/E}} ⊗ φ_{E'}).
items.locator: §11.1.3, pp. 358–359, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: A = L case planned: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (upward functor (D ⊗ L_{E'}, φ^f ⊗ σ_{E'}), downward induced isocrystal). Not planned for B^+ or ℬ.

items.name: Définition 11.1.2: the φ-modules A(λ)
items.statement: Let A ∈ {L, B^+, ℬ} and π a uniformizer of E. For λ ∈ Q, λ = d/h with h ≥ 1, d ∈ Z, (d,h) = 1, A(λ) := A e_0 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ A e_{h−1} with φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for 0 ≤ i < h−1 and φ(e_{h−1}) = π^d e_0. Under the scalar extensions φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_ℬ → φ-Mod_L, B^+(λ) is sent to ℬ(λ) and L(λ).
items.locator: Définition 11.1.2, p. 359, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Same sign convention as Kedlaya's M_{c,d} (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules, over R^alg, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], Γ^alg[π^{-1}], W(κ,O)[π^{-1}]); VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block uses the opposite block φ(e_h) = π^{−d}e_1. For B^+ and ℬ nothing is planned.

items.name: §11.1.4: A_E(λ) = π_{E_h/E*} A_{E_h}(d)
items.statement: Let λ = d/h as in Définition 11.1.2 and suppose k_F^{φ_E^h=Id}|F_q is an extension of degree h, i.e. F_{q^h}; let E_h|E be the corresponding unramified extension. Then A_E(λ) = π_{E_h/E*} A_{E_h}(d).
items.locator: §11.1.4, p. 359, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas; nearest VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (downward functor for isocrystals).

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin theorem (external, k_F algebraically closed)
items.statement: When k_F is algebraically closed, the abelian category φ-Mod_{L_E} (isocrystals over L = W_{O_E}(k_F)_Q) is semisimple and its simple objects are the L(λ), λ ∈ Q; consequently an isocrystal has well-defined Dieudonné–Manin slopes, and for its smallest slope λ = d/h there is a W_{O_E}(k_F)-lattice Λ with φ^hΛ ⊂ π^dΛ and Λ^{φ^h=π^d} ≠ 0.
items.locator: used in §11.1.4 (p. 359), proofs of Théorème 11.1.7 (p. 363) and Proposition 11.2.24 (p. 378, citing [62] chap. VI §2 for the lattice), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Planned in full: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 stage text ('Prove the Dieudonné–Manin classification … simple objects of rational slope, multiplicities, Hom and endomorphism division algebras'); nodes VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical; the lattice statement is PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices. Mathlib has only the rank-one case over Frac W(k), k algebraically closed, E = Q_p (mathlib:WittVector.isocrystal_classification, read: a one-dimensional isocrystal is isomorphic to StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k m for some m ∈ Z).

items.name: Slope decomposition of isocrystals over a perfect k_F (external)
items.statement: For k_F perfect (not necessarily algebraically closed) and an isocrystal (D, φ) over L = W_{O_E}(k_F)_Q with smallest Dieudonné–Manin slope λ = d/h, there is a W_{O_E}(k_F)-lattice Λ ⊂ D with φ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ, and Λ = Λ^{bij} ⊕ Λ^{nilp} canonically relative to π^{−d}φ^h, with Λ^{bij}[1/π] the slope-λ factor of the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition of D.
items.locator: used in the proof of Théorème 11.1.8, pp. 363–364, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Partial plan only. PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/slope-decomposition ('Every isocrystal D over K_0 = W(k)[1/p] (k perfect) has a unique decomposition D = ⊕ D(α)') is the case E = Q_p of the slope decomposition; PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent (a) gives it over W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] (algebraically closed residue field) and RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices gives F-stable lattices when all slopes are ≥ 0. The lattice Λ with φ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ and its canonical splitting Λ = Λ^bij ⊕ Λ^nilp relative to π^{−d}φ^h, for general E and perfect k_F, are not planned.

items.name: Proposition 11.1.3: reduction φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_ℬ is fully faithful
items.statement: The reduction functor φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_ℬ is fully faithful. Equivalently (by internal Homs and Hom(X, Y) = H⁰(Hom(X, Y))), for X ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+} with reduction X̄ = X ⊗_{B^+} ℬ, H⁰(X) ⥲ H⁰(X̄). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Proposition 11.1.3, pp. 359–361, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Generalises Proposition 4.1.6. The proof shows Id − φ is bijective on Λ = {m ∈ M | ‖m‖_0 > 0} = ker(M → M ⊗ ℬ), which also gives H¹(X) ≅ H¹(X̄) (used in Remarque 11.1.10). No stage covers φ-modules over B^+ versus B^{b,+}/{v_0>0}.

items.name: Lemme 11.1.4(1): φ-invariants of a W_{O_E}(O_F)-module equal those of its reduction to k_F
items.statement: Let M be a free W_{O_E}(O_F)-module of finite rank with a φ_E-linear endomorphism φ : M → M, and M_{k_F} := M ⊗ W_{O_E}(k_F). Then M^{φ=Id} ⥲ M_{k_F}^{φ=Id} (proof: Id − φ is bijective on W_{O_E}(m_F)^n, which is complete for the weak topology and on which φ is topologically nilpotent).
items.locator: Lemme 11.1.4, p. 361, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent (descent of F-fixed vectors for Kedlaya's Γ^alg) and RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices; neither is the reduction-to-k_F statement over W_{O_E}(O_F).

items.name: Lemme 11.1.4(2): the φ-invariants span a direct-factor sub-φ-module
items.statement: In the situation of Lemme 11.1.4(1), if k_F ↪ O_F is a section of O_F ↠ k_F, then M^{φ=Id} ⊗_{W_{O_E}(k_F)} W_{O_E}(O_F) (as printed; M^{φ=Id} is an O_E-module, so read M^{φ=Id} ⊗_{O_E} W_{O_E}(O_F)) is a sub-φ-module of M which is a direct factor (Nakayama, since ker(W_{O_E}(O_F) → W_{O_E}(k_F)) lies in the Jacobson radical).
items.locator: Lemme 11.1.4, p. 361, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: See sourceIssues for the tensor-product misprint. Not planned.

items.name: Lemme 11.1.5: Ext¹(X, Y) ≅ H¹(X̌ ⊗ Y) in φ-Mod_ℬ
items.statement: For X, Y ∈ φ-Mod_{ℬ_E}, Ext¹(X, Y) ≃ H¹(X̌ ⊗ Y). (Stated without proof.) Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Lemme 11.1.5, p. 362, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The identical formula is stated for other coefficient rings in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-module ('Ext(M_1, M_2) = H¹(M_1^∨ ⊗ M_2) is the Yoneda Ext¹'), not for ℬ.

items.name: Lemme 11.1.6(1): Ext¹(ℬ(λ), ℬ(μ)) = 0 when k_F is algebraically closed
items.statement: For λ, μ ∈ Q, Ext¹(ℬ(λ), ℬ(μ)) = 0 when k_F is algebraically closed (equivalently H¹(ℬ(ν)) = coker(Id − π^dφ^h : ℬ → ℬ) = 0 for all ν = d/h). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Lemme 11.1.6, p. 362, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Over Kedlaya's R^alg the analogous Ext groups are NONzero for c'/d' < c/d (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules (c)); the vanishing here is special to ℬ. Not planned.

items.name: Lemme 11.1.6(2): Ext¹(ℬ(λ), ℬ(μ)) = 0 for λ ≠ μ and arbitrary k_F
items.statement: The vanishing Ext¹(ℬ(λ), ℬ(μ)) = 0 still holds when k_F is arbitrary and λ ≠ μ. Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Lemme 11.1.6, p. 362, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: True, but the printed proof reduces to ℬ(μ−λ) via a decomposition that fails when k_F is not algebraically closed; see sourceIssues. The authors' own generalisation (5) in the proof of Théorème 11.1.8 is the correct form. Not planned.

items.name: Théorème 11.1.7(1)(2): φ-modules over B^+ are sums of B^+(λ) (k_F algebraically closed)
items.statement: Suppose k_F algebraically closed. (1) For every splitting k_F ↪ O_F of O_F ↠ k_F, the scalar-extension functor φ-Mod_L → φ-Mod_{B^+} is essentially surjective. (2) Every X ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+} is isomorphic to a direct sum of B^+(λ), λ ∈ Q. (By Dieudonné–Manin (1) ⇔ (2).)
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.7, pp. 362–363, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned. Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification (classification of bundles, not of φ-modules over B^+).

items.name: Théorème 11.1.7(3): φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ φ-Mod_ℬ (k_F algebraically closed)
items.statement: Suppose k_F algebraically closed. The reduction functor φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_ℬ is an equivalence of categories (the proof shows every X ∈ φ-Mod_ℬ is a direct sum of ℬ(λ), λ ∈ Q). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.7, pp. 362–363, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Théorème 11.1.8(1): φ-modules over B^+ come from isocrystals (k_F arbitrary)
items.statement: k_F not necessarily algebraically closed. For every splitting k_F ↪ O_F of O_F ↠ k_F, the scalar-extension functor φ-Mod_L → φ-Mod_{B^+} is essentially surjective.
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.8, pp. 363–365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The printed proof has a failing step when F_{q^h} ⊄ k_F (the Morita isomorphism with D_λ = End(L(−λ))); see sourceIssues. Not planned; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 explicitly says a classification after algebraic closure is not one over arbitrary bases.

items.name: Théorème 11.1.8(2): φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ φ-Mod_ℬ (k_F arbitrary)
items.statement: k_F not necessarily algebraically closed. The reduction functor φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_ℬ induces an equivalence of categories. Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.8, pp. 363–365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned; same proof issue as Théorème 11.1.8(1).

items.name: Proof of Théorème 11.1.8, (5): Ext¹ vanishing between twisted slope-0 isocrystals
items.statement: If μ_1 ≠ μ_2 and D_1, D_2 ∈ φ-Mod_L are isoclinic of slope 0, then Ext¹(D_1 ⊗_L ℬ(μ_1), D_2 ⊗ ℬ(μ_2)) = 0 ('la preuve du lemme 11.1.6 s'adapte'). Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: proof of Théorème 11.1.8, display (5), p. 364, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proof of Théorème 11.1.8: D_λ = End(ℬ(−λ)) = End(L(−λ)), the division algebra of invariant λ
items.statement: D_λ := End(ℬ(−λ)) = End(L(−λ)) is the division algebra over E of invariant λ; D_λ acts on M ⊗ ℬ(−λ), and there is a canonical isomorphism of φ-modules over ℬ, M ⥲ Hom_{D_λ⊗ℬ}(ℬ(−λ), M ⊗ ℬ(−λ)). (Stated in the proof of Théorème 11.1.8 without a hypothesis on k_F.) Notation of this item: ℬ denotes the ring written B in §11.1 of the text, ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 (not the Fréchet ring B = B_{]0,1[} of §§11.2–11.4).
items.locator: proof of Théorème 11.1.8, p. 365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Correct when k_F is algebraically closed (more precisely when F_{q^h} ⊂ k_F), false otherwise; see sourceIssues. The division-algebra part is planned for isocrystals over W(F̄_q) and for O_X(λ): VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/endomorphism-division-algebra and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules (d). The equality End(ℬ(−λ)) = End(L(−λ)) and the Morita isomorphism over ℬ are not planned.

items.name: §11.1.6: the functor E(−) : φ-Mod_{B^+_E} → Fib_{X_E}
items.statement: For (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+_E}, let Γ_•(M, φ) = ⊕_{d≥0} M^{φ_E = π_E^d}, a graded P_{E,π_E}-module, and E(M, φ) := the quasi-coherent sheaf Γ_•(M, φ)~ on X_E = Proj(P_{E,π_E}).
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the isocrystal version E(D, φ) is planned (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/isocrystal-category-and-standard-block; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign, via descent of D ⊗ O_Y). The graded-module construction from φ-modules over B^+ is not.

items.name: §11.1.6: E(D ⊗_L B^+) = E(D) and E(M, φ) is a vector bundle
items.statement: With a section k_F ↪ O_F and (D, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L, E(D ⊗_L B^+, φ ⊗ φ) = E(D, φ), the vector bundle attached to the isocrystal (D, φ). Hence, by Théorème 11.1.8, E(M, φ) is a vector bundle for every (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+}.
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (depends on Théorème 11.1.8).

items.name: Théorème 11.1.9(1): E(−) : φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ Fib_X for F algebraically closed
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. The functor E(−) : φ-Mod_{B^+_E} → Fib_{X_E} is an equivalence of tensor categories, and H⁰(X_E, E(M, φ)) = H⁰(M, φ) = M^{φ=Id}. (Deduced from Théorème 8.2.10.)
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.9, p. 366, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles plans only that the ISOCRYSTAL functor induces a bijection on isomorphism classes and explicitly does not assert full faithfulness; full faithfulness on φ-modules over B^+ is what is new here.

items.name: Théorème 11.1.9(2): E(−) commutes with π^*_{E'/E} and π_{E'/E*}
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed and E'|E finite, π_{E',E} : X_{E'} → X_E. Then E(−) intertwines π^*_{E'/E} with π^*_{E',E} and π_{E'/E*} with π_{E',E*} (commutative diagram between φ-Mod_{B^+_{E'}} → Fib_{X_{E'}} and φ-Mod_{B^+_E} → Fib_{X_E}).
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.9, p. 366, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The isocrystal-level statement is planned (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction: 'Under E(−) these correspond to π^* and π_*'), not the B^+ version.

items.name: Remarque 11.1.10: E(−) is exact, its inverse is not
items.statement: The functor E(−) : φ-Mod_{B^+_E} → Fib_{X_E} is exact, but its inverse is not, so the equivalence of Théorème 11.1.9 is not an equivalence of exact categories: by Lemme 11.1.6 and Proposition 11.1.3, Ext¹(X, Y) = 0 for all X, Y ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+_E}, whereas in general Ext¹(E(X), E(Y)) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Remarque 11.1.10, p. 366, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Remarque 11.1.11: F not algebraically closed — essential image of φ-Mod_{B^+} → Fib_X
items.statement: Théorème 11.1.9 is false when F is not algebraically closed. Via the classification theorem 9.4.3, φ-Mod_{B^+} → Fib_X is fully faithful with essential image the bundles attached to (λ_i, [ρ_i])_i with every ρ_i unramified, i.e. ρ_i factors through Gal(F̄|F) → Gal(k̄_F|k_F).
items.locator: Remarque 11.1.11, p. 366, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals only classifies at geometric points.

items.name: §11.1.6: the Q_+-graded algebra P_∞ = lim_h P_{E_h,π}
items.statement: Fix E and a uniformizer π; X := X_E, P_h := P_{E_h,π}, X_h := X_{E_h} = Proj(P_h) (E_h unramified of degree h). P_∞ := lim_{→,h≥1} P_h is a Q_+-graded E-algebra, P_∞ = ⊕_{λ∈Q_+} P_{∞,λ} with P_{∞,λ} = ∪_h (B^+)^{φ^h=π^{hλ}} = (B^+)^{φ^s=π^r} ⊗_{E_s} E_∞ for λ = r/s, (r,s) = 1, E_∞ the maximal unramified extension of E.
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 366, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: §11.1.6: the P_∞-module M_∞(E) of a bundle
items.statement: For E ∈ Fib_X and h ≥ 1, M_h(E) := ⊕_{λ∈(1/h)Z} Γ(X_h, (π_h^*E)(hλ)) (π_h : X_h → X), and M_∞(E) := lim_{→,h} M_h(E) = ⊕_{λ∈Q} ∪_h Γ(X_h, (π_h^*E)(hλ)), a Q-graded P_∞-module.
items.locator: §11.1.6, pp. 366–367, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: §11.1.6: the tower (X_h) is a pro-Galois cover of group Ẑ; the isomorphisms u_h
items.statement: The tower of curves (X_h)_{h≥1} is a Galois pro-covering of X with group Ẑ: with σ = φ ∈ Gal(E_∞|E), Gal(X_h/X) = σ^{Z/hZ}. The line bundle O_{X_h}(1) = P_h[1]~ carries an isomorphism u_h : σ^*O_{X_h}(1) ⥲ O_{X_h}(1), the one associated with the φ-linear isomorphism φ : P_h[1] ⥲ P_h[1], whose h-fold composite of σ-translates equals π ∈ Aut(O_{X_h}(1)); similarly u_h^{⊗d} : σ^*O_{X_h}(d) ⥲ O_{X_h}(d) for d ∈ Z.
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 367, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction only has pullback/pushforward along X_{E'} → X_E.
