items.name: §11.1.6: the φ-linear automorphism of M_∞(E)
items.statement: The u_h^{⊗d} define a φ-linear isomorphism of P_∞-modules φ : M_∞(E) ⥲ M_∞(E), acting on Γ(X_h, (π_h^*E)(d)) by Γ(X_h,(π_h^*E)(d)) →^{σ^*} Γ(X_h, σ^*π_h^*E ⊗ σ^*O_{X_h}(d)) →^{Id⊗u_h^{⊗d}} Γ(X_h, (σ^*π_h^*E)(d)) = Γ(X_h, (π_h^*E)(d)) (as π_h ∘ σ = π_h).
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 367, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: §11.1.6: M_∞ of E(M, φ) and of B^+(μ)
items.statement: For (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+}, M_∞(E(M, φ)) = ⊕_{λ∈Q} ∪_h M^{φ^h=π^{hλ}}. For μ = r/s, (r,s) = 1, B^+(μ) = B^+e_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ B^+e_s with φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} (i < s), φ(e_s) = π^r e_1, one has M_∞(E(B^+(μ))) = M_∞(O_X(−μ)) = P_∞[−μ]e_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ P_∞[−μ]e_s, where P_∞[−μ]_λ = P_{∞,λ−μ}, with φ acting by φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} (i < s), φ(e_s) = π^r e_1.
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 367, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: §11.1.6: M_∞(−) ⊗_{P_∞} B^+ is inverse to E(−) (F algebraically closed)
items.statement: Suppose F algebraically closed. Let φ-Mod_{P_∞} be the category of Q-graded P_∞-modules M_∞ with a φ-linear isomorphism φ : M_∞ ⥲ M_∞ such that M_∞ is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of P_∞[μ], μ ∈ Q. Then M_∞(−) : Fib_X → φ-Mod_{P_∞} is a functor, and the composite Fib_X →^{M_∞(−)} φ-Mod_{P_∞} →^{−⊗_{P_∞}B^+} φ-Mod_{B^+} is an inverse of E(−).
items.locator: §11.1.6, p. 368, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: §11.1.7: φ-modules over B^+_ρ
items.statement: Recall B^+ = ∩_{ρ>0} B^+_ρ with φ : B^+_ρ ⥲ B^+_{ρ^q} ⊂ B^+_ρ. For ρ ∈ ]0,1[, a φ-module over B^+_ρ is a pair (M, φ) with M a free B^+_ρ-module of finite rank and φ a semilinear endomorphism of M inducing an isomorphism M ⊗_{B^+_ρ,φ} B^+_ρ ⥲ M (i.e. the matrix of φ in a basis of M is invertible); category φ-Mod_{B^+_ρ}.
items.locator: §11.1.7, p. 368, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Théorème 11.1.12: classification of φ-modules over B^+_ρ
items.statement: Théorème 11.1.8 remains valid with φ-Mod_{B^+} replaced by φ-Mod_{B^+_ρ}: for every (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+_ρ} with reduction (D, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_L and every choice of section k_F ⊂ O_F there is a (non-canonical) isomorphism (M, φ) ≃ (D, φ) ⊗_L B^+_ρ.
items.locator: Théorème 11.1.12, p. 368, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.13: φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ φ-Mod_{B^+_ρ}
items.statement: The scalar-extension functor φ-Mod_{B^+} → φ-Mod_{B^+_ρ} is an equivalence of categories, with inverse (M, φ) ↦ (∩_{n≥0} φⁿ(M), φ).
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.13, p. 368, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.14: B^+_{cris,ρ} and φ-Mod_{B^+_{cris,ρ}}
items.statement: (E = Q_p.) For a ⊂ O_F a proper nonzero principal ideal and ρ = |a|, B^+_{cris,ρ} := Γ((Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p))_cris, O_{Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p)})[1/p], the ring of crystalline p-adic periods attached to O_F/a; φ-Mod_{B^+_{cris,ρ}} is the category of free B^+_{cris,ρ}-modules of finite rank with a semilinear isomorphism.
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.14, pp. 368–369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: CrystallineCohomology:CR.1 (crystalline sites and crystals) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/crystalline-period-ring (A_cris of O_C only). The ring attached to O_F/a and its comparison B^+_{ρ^p} ⊂ B^+_{cris,ρ} ⊂ B^+_ρ (Prop. 1.10.12) are not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.14(1): φ-modules over B^+_{cris,ρ} come from isocrystals
items.statement: (E = Q_p, a, ρ as above; fix a section k_F ↪ O_F.) For every (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{B^+_{cris,ρ}}, with (D, φ) = (M, φ) ⊗_{B^+_{cris,ρ}} L, there is a (non-canonical) isomorphism (M, φ) ≃ (D, φ) ⊗_L B^+_{cris,ρ}.
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.14, p. 369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.14(2): F-isocrystals on O_F/a are isotrivial
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) The global-sections functor induces an equivalence between F-isocrystals on Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p) and φ-Mod_{B^+_{cris,ρ}}. Hence every F-isocrystal on Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p) is isotrivial: it is isomorphic to the extension of scalars from k_F to O_F (via the section) of an F-isocrystal on Spec(k_F)/Spec(Z_p).
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.14, p. 369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (nearest CrystallineCohomology:CR.1). Used by Scholze–Weinstein [57] (see citations).

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.14(3): F-isocrystals on O_F/a ≃ convergent F-isocrystals on Sp(F)
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) The category of F-isocrystals on Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p) is equivalent to that of 'convergent F-isocrystals on Sp(F)', i.e. φ-modules over B^+.
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.14, p. 369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Corollaire 11.1.14(4): Fib_{X_F} ≃ F-isocrystals on O_F/a (F algebraically closed)
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) When F is algebraically closed, the category of vector bundles on X_F is equivalent to that of F-isocrystals on Spec(O_F/a)/Spec(Z_p) (not an equivalence of exact categories, cf. Remarque 11.1.10).
items.locator: Corollaire 11.1.14, p. 369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Définition 11.2.1: Proj_{B_I} and the category Fib_{Y_I}
items.statement: (1) For an interval I ⊂ [0,1[, Proj_{B_I} is the category of finitely generated projective B_I-modules. (2) Fib_{Y_I} := 2-lim_{←,J} Proj_{B_J}, the 2-projective limit over the compact intervals J ⊂ I of the categories of free B_J-modules of finite rank: collections (M_J)_{J⊂I} of such modules with isomorphisms M_J ⊗_{B_J} B_{J'} ⥲ M_{J'} for J' ⊂ J satisfying the usual compatibilities.
items.locator: Définition 11.2.1, p. 369, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free defines S-vector bundles over Γ_I (finite free Γ_J-modules with compatible isomorphisms) for Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, which for ℓ = F perfect and E of characteristic 0 are the B_I (RD.0/analytic-ring). Intervals must be bounded away from Kedlaya's r_0. Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; and the S-vector-bundle node also assumes v_ℓ discrete ('Enough r_0-units; discreteness of v_ℓ'), which excludes a perfectoid F. The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.2: global sections Fib_{Y_I} ≃ Proj_{B_I}
items.statement: For an interval I ⊂ [0,1[, (B_J)_{J⊂I compact} is a Fréchet–Stein algebra (Théorème 3.5.1; [55] §3), and the global-sections functor Γ : Fib_{Y_I} → Proj_{B_I}, (M_J)_J ↦ lim_{←,J} M_J, is an exact equivalence of categories, with Γ((M_J)_J) ⊗_{B_I} B_J ⥲ M_J.
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.2, pp. 369–370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced from Schneider–Teitelbaum [55] Cor. 3.3, 3.4. Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (only I = (0,r], free modules), RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity (R¹lim = 0 on Y_S) and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorem-a (Kiehl's Theorem A for quasi-Stein spaces locally of finite type over a field). No node states the equivalence with finite projective B_I-modules for general I (e.g. I = ]0,1[).

items.name: Proposition 11.2.3: Fib_{Y_{]0,ρ]}} ≃ free B_{]0,ρ]}-modules
items.statement: For every ρ ∈ ]0,1[, via global sections Fib_{Y_{]0,ρ]}} identifies with the category of free B_{]0,ρ]}-modules of finite rank (B_{]0,ρ]} is Bézout, 3.5.7).
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.3, p. 370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free: 'For r ∈ (0, r_0) the functor from finite free Γ_an,r-modules to vector bundles over Γ_an,r = Γ_(0,r] is an equivalence' (Kedlaya's Γ_an,r = FF's B_{]0,ρ]} for ℓ = F perfect). Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; and RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free assumes v_ℓ discrete ('discreteness of v_ℓ'), which excludes a perfectoid F. The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Définition 11.2.4: coherent sheaves Coh_{Y_I}
items.statement: For an interval I, Coh_{Y_I} := 2-lim_{←,J} Mod^{tf}_{B_J}, the 2-projective limit over the compact intervals J ⊂ I of the categories of finitely generated B_J-modules.
items.locator: Définition 11.2.4, p. 370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid (coherent sheaves on locally noetherian adic spaces; B_J is strongly noetherian by Kedlaya, cf. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve §6.3). The 2-limit category over Y_I is not defined in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.5(1): Coh_{Y_I} ≃ modules M ⊕ ∏ N_y
items.statement: The global-sections functor induces an equivalence between Coh_{Y_I} and the category of B_I-modules isomorphic to M ⊕ ∏_{y∈|Y_I|} N_y with M finitely generated projective and each N_y a finitely generated torsion B^+_{dR,y}-module, such that for every compact J ⊂ I the set of y ∈ |Y_J| with N_y ≠ 0 is finite.
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.5, p. 370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (uses [55] and the structure of modules over a PID).

items.name: Proposition 11.2.5(2): bounded-fibre coherent sheaves ≃ finitely presented B_I-modules
items.statement: The global-sections functor induces an equivalence between the coherent sheaves (M_J)_J with sup_{y∈|Y_I|} length_{k(y)}(M_J ⊗ k(y)) < +∞ (J any interval with y ∈ |Y_J|) and the finitely presented B_I-modules.
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.5, p. 370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned. Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (closed submodules of free Γ_an,r-modules are free).

items.name: Lemme 11.2.6: B_I = B_{I^+} + B_{I^-}
items.statement: Let I be an interval of [0,1], I^+ the convex hull of I ∪ {1} and I^− that of I ∪ {0}. Then B_I = B_{I^+} + B_{I^−}. (Proof: for x = Σ_{n≫−∞}[x_n]πⁿ ∈ B^b put x^+ = Σ_{n≥0}[x_n]πⁿ, x^− = Σ_{n<0}[x_n]πⁿ; for ρ ≤ ρ', |x^+|_ρ ≤ |x^+|_{ρ'} and |x^−|_ρ ≥ |x^−|_{ρ'}; for f = Σ_k f_k convergent in B_I with f_k ∈ B^b, Σ f_k^+ ∈ B_{I^−} and Σ f_k^− ∈ B_{I^+}.)
items.locator: Lemme 11.2.6, pp. 370–371, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections (d)–(e) (Mayer–Vietoris splitting x = y + z for closed overlapping intervals, approximation by Γ_r); Kedlaya's intervals are bounded away from r_0, so the ring B_{I^+} with 1 ∈ I^+ is outside the node's range.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.7: Mayer–Vietoris for I ↦ B_I
items.statement: Let I, J ⊂ [0,1] be intervals with I ∩ J ≠ ∅. Then 0 → B_{I∪J} → B_I ⊕ B_J → B_{I∩J} → 0 is exact; i.e. inside B_{I∩J}, B_{I∪J} = B_I ∩ B_J and B_{I∩J} = B_I + B_J.
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.7, p. 371, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections (d): for I = [a,b], J = [c,d], a ≤ c ≤ b ≤ d, Γ_I ∩ Γ_J = Γ_{I∪J} inside Γ_{I∩J}, and x ∈ Γ_{I∩J} with w_s(x) > 0 splits as y + z. Covers closed intervals away from the endpoint ρ = 1; FF also allow 1 ∈ I and non-closed intervals. The printed proof interchanges I^+ and I^−; see sourceIssues. Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; the node also covers only closed intervals away from ρ = 1. The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.8: admissible coverings of intervals
items.statement: A covering I = ∪_{α∈A} J_α of an interval I of [0,1] by subintervals is admissible if for every compact K ⊂ I there is a finite A' ⊂ A with K ⊂ ∪_{α∈A'} J_α; the category of intervals of [0,1] is given the Grothendieck topology whose coverings are the admissible coverings.
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.8, p. 371, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Elementary; not stated in the atlas.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.8: O : I ↦ B_I is a sheaf with H¹(I, O) = 0
items.statement: O : I ↦ B_I is a sheaf for the admissible topology on intervals of [0,1], and H¹(I, O) = 0 for every interval I (consequence of Proposition 11.2.7).
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.8, p. 371, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections (Mayer–Vietoris) and RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity (H^i(Y_{S,I}, F) = 0, R¹lim = 0, H^i(Y_S, F) = 0 for vector bundles) together give this for closed intervals away from ρ = 1.

items.name: Lemme 11.2.10: approximation lemma XZYZ^{-1}
items.statement: Let B_1, B_2, A be E-Banach algebras with morphisms B_1 → A, B_2 → A such that B_1 ⊕ B_2 → A is surjective, and let Z ∈ GL_n(A) be such that the tangent map M_n(B_1) ⊕ M_n(B_2) → M_n(A), (U, V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, is surjective (hypothesis missing in print; without it the statement is false, see sourceIssues). Then there is a neighbourhood of the identity in GL_n(A) every element of which can be written XZYZ^{−1} with X ∈ GL_n(B_1), Y ∈ GL_n(B_2).
items.locator: Lemme 11.2.10, p. 372, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: False as stated for general Z (counterexample in sourceIssues); true when (U, V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, M_n(B_1) ⊕ M_n(B_2) → M_n(A), is surjective, e.g. Z = 1. The Z = 1 case over Kedlaya's rings is PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/matrix-approximation-and-factorization (b).

items.name: Lemme 11.2.11: local surjectivity of holomorphic maps with surjective tangent map
items.statement: Let C_1, …, C_n, D_1, …, D_m be E-Banach algebras with morphisms u_ij : C_j → D_i. For i = 1..m let f_i = Σ_α a_α T^α ∈ D_i[[T_1, …, T_n]] be holomorphic near 0 (∃ρ > 0, sup_α ‖a_α‖ρ^{|α|} < +∞), defining g : U_1 × ⋯ × U_n → D_1 × ⋯ × D_m, (x_1,…,x_n) ↦ (f_i(u_i1(x_1), …, u_in(x_n)))_i on small neighbourhoods U_j of 0. If f_i(0) = 0 for all i and the tangent map C_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ C_n → D_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ D_m, (x_j) ↦ (Σ_j ∂f_i/∂T_j(0) u_ij(x_j))_i, is surjective, then the image of g contains a neighbourhood of 0 (for any choice of sufficiently small U_j).
items.locator: Lemme 11.2.11, pp. 372–373, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Read Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/FDeriv.lean: for complete normed spaces over a nontrivially normed field, HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a with f' surjective gives map f (𝓝 a) = 𝓝 (f a) — exactly the conclusion (for every neighbourhood). A convergent power series map is analytic, hence strictly differentiable with the stated tangent map (mathlib:AnalyticAt.hasStrictFDerivAt / HasFPowerSeriesAt.hasStrictFDerivAt). Mathlib uses a nonlinear bounded right inverse, so it does not need FF's continuous linear section. The translation from D_i[[T]] with substitutions u_ij to an analytic map between Banach spaces is routine but not in the library.

items.name: Banach open mapping theorem and continuous linear sections over a discretely valued field (external)
items.statement: By the Banach open mapping theorem and since E is discretely valued, every continuous surjective E-linear map of E-Banach spaces D_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ D_m ← C_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ C_n (the tangent map) admits a continuous E-linear section s; Newton iteration u_0 = s(y), u_{n+1} = u_n − s(g(u_n) − y) then converges to a solution of g(x) = y for small y.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemme 11.2.11, p. 373, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Open mapping is in Mathlib (mathlib:ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap) with a bounded NONlinear right inverse (mathlib:ContinuousLinearMap.exists_nonlinearRightInverse_of_surjective); the existence of a continuous LINEAR section over a discretely valued field (via orthogonal bases of p-adic Banach spaces) is not in Mathlib, Tau Ceti or the atlas. Not needed for Lemme 11.2.11's conclusion, see that item.

items.name: §11.2.3.2: restriction functors Fib_{Y_I} → Fib_{Y_{I'}}
items.statement: For intervals I' ⊂ I ⊂ [0,1[ there is a restriction functor Fib_{Y_I} → Fib_{Y_{I'}}, E ↦ E|_{Y_{I'}}.
items.locator: §11.2.3.2, p. 373, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Part of the S-vector-bundle formalism of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free. Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; and the S-vector-bundle node assumes v_ℓ discrete, which excludes a perfectoid F. The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.12: gluing of bundles on Y_{I_1} and Y_{I_2}
items.statement: Let I_1, I_2 be intervals of [0,1[ with I_1 ∩ I_2 ≠ ∅. Then Fib_{Y_{I_1∪I_2}} identifies with the category of triples (E_1, E_2, ι) with E_i ∈ Fib_{Y_{I_i}} and ι : E_1|_{Y_{I_1∩I_2}} ⥲ E_2|_{Y_{I_1∩I_2}}. (For compact I_1, I_2: GL_n(B_{I_1})\GL_n(B_{I_1∩I_2})/GL_n(B_{I_2}) is trivial.)
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.12, pp. 373–374, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free ('the category does not depend on S (Kiehl–Tate type gluing)') with RD.0/matrix-approximation-and-factorization; also AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing (Kiehl gluing of finite projective modules on a sheafy Tate affinoid, applicable to Spa(B_{I_1∪I_2}) covered by two rational subsets; sheafiness of the interval rings is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve §6.3). The printed statement has E_2|_{Y_{I_2}} and the printed proof has a quantifier gap; see sourceIssues.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.13: Fib_{Y_I} ≃ locally free O-modules
items.statement: With the notation of Remarque 11.2.8, Fib_{Y_I} identifies with the category of locally free O-modules (for the admissible topology on subintervals of I).
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.13, p. 374, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Independence of the covering in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free. Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; and the S-vector-bundle node assumes v_ℓ discrete, which excludes a perfectoid F. The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.14: gluing extends to Coh_{Y_I}
items.statement: By the structure of finitely generated modules over a PID, Proposition 11.2.12 extends to Coh_{Y_I}.
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.14, p. 374, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.15(1): B_{L,I}|B_{F,I} is finite étale (Galois) of degree [L:F]
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1[ be a compact interval with endpoints in |F| ∩ [0,1[ and L|F a finite extension. Then B_{L,I} is a finite étale B_{F,I}-algebra of degree [L:F]; if L|F is Galois, B_{L,I}|B_{F,I} is Galois with group Gal(L|F) ⥲ Aut_{B_{F,I}}(B_{L,I}). (The proof shows B_{L,I} = ⊕_{i<d} B_{F,I}[α^{i/p^k}] for k ≫ 0, where L = F[α].)
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.15, pp. 374–376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings (Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con) — the Robba-type rings, not the compact-interval rings Γ_I.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.15(2): B°_{L,I}|B°_{F,I} is almost étale
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) The B°_{F,I}-algebra B°_{L,I} is almost étale: for every ε ∈ m_F, [ε]B°_{F,I} ⊂ tr_{L/F}(B°_{L,I}) ⊂ B°_{F,I}.
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.15, pp. 374–376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned (PerfectoidSpaces:P0 almost étale nodes concern perfectoid algebras, not these rings).

items.name: Remarque 11.2.16: new proof of Corollaire 1.8.3 (E^†_L|E^†_F finite of degree [L:F])
items.statement: Proposition 11.2.15 gives as a special case a proof of Corollaire 1.8.3: if L|F is finite then E^†_L|E^†_F is finite of degree [L:F].
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.16, p. 376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings: Γ^L_con ≅ Γ^ℓ_con[x]/(P(x)), P the minimal polynomial of a lift of a generator of L|ℓ (for ℓ = F perfect, Γ_con[π^{-1}] = E^†). Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.17: failure for B_{]0,1]}; no Galois descent for φ-modules over B^+
items.statement: When 1 ∈ I the argument of Proposition 11.2.15 fails, and the result is false for B_{]0,1]} = B^+[1/[ϖ_F]]. Consequently φ-modules over B^+ do not satisfy Galois descent, unlike those over B (cf. 11.1.11).
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.17, p. 376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Stated without proof; not planned.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.18(1): B_{F̂̄,I}^{G_F} = B_{F,I} (Sen's method)
items.statement: Let I ⊂ [0,1[ be a compact interval with endpoints in |F| ∩ [0,1[. Then B_{F̂̄,I}^{G_F} = B_{F,I} (G_F = Gal(F̄|F), F̂̄ the completed algebraic closure).
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.18, p. 376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Deduced 'de la méthode de Sen' ([58], not cited by number). Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology (T ↦ H⁰(Y_T, E|_{Y_T}) is a v-sheaf — global Y, not Y_I) and PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem (for C).

items.name: Proposition 11.2.18(2): Galois descent for free B_{F̂̄,I}-modules
items.statement: (Same hypotheses.) Scalar extension − ⊗_{B_{F,I}} B_{F̂̄,I} induces an equivalence between free B_{F,I}-modules of finite rank and free B_{F̂̄,I}-modules of finite rank with a continuous semilinear action of Gal(F̄|F).
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.18, p. 376, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology (bundles on X_S form a v-stack) — stated for X_S, not for the interval rings with continuous cocycles.

items.name: §11.2.4: Fib_{Y_{F,I}} ≃ G_F-equivariant bundles on Y_{F̂̄,I}
items.statement: For every interval I ⊂ [0,1[, Fib_{Y_{F,I}} identifies with the bundles E ∈ Fib_{Y_{F̂̄,I}} equipped with a semilinear action (c_σ)_{σ∈G_F}, c_σ : σ^*E ⥲ E, continuous in the sense that for every compact J ⊂ I the induced action on the Banach space Γ(Y_J, E) is continuous.
items.locator: §11.2.4, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology (v-stack of bundles on X_S).

items.name: §11.2.5: Frobenius pullback φ^*E of a bundle on Y_I
items.statement: For E = (M_J)_{J⊂I} a bundle on Y_I, φ^*E is the bundle (M_{φ^{−1}(J)} ⊗_{B_{φ^{−1}(J)},φ} B_J)_{J⊂φ(I)} on Y_{φ(I)}.
items.locator: §11.2.5, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 stage text: 'compare with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent'.

items.name: Définition 11.2.19(1): φ-equivariant bundles Fib_{Y/φ^Z}
items.statement: Fib_{Y/φ^Z} is the category of bundles E on Y = Y_{]0,1[} equipped with an isomorphism φ^*E ⥲ E.
items.locator: Définition 11.2.19, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Frobenius descent of bundles from Y_S to X_S = Y_S/φ^Z: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1 (quotient and descent) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 (annuli and Frobenius descent); no node spells out the category.

items.name: Définition 11.2.19(2): φ-equivariant bundles Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z}
items.statement: Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} is the category of bundles E on Y_{[0,1[} equipped with an isomorphism φ^*E ⥲ E.
items.locator: Définition 11.2.19, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The extension of Y across the π-adic end ρ = 0 is not planned (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y keeps the characteristic-p fibre of 𝒴_S, a different boundary).

items.name: §11.2.5: Fib_{Y/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_B (projective modules over the Fréchet ring B)
items.statement: By Proposition 11.2.2, Fib_{Y/φ^Z} identifies with the category φ-Mod_B of pairs (M, φ) with M a finitely generated projective B-module (B = B_{]0,1[}) and φ : M ⥲ M a semilinear isomorphism.
items.locator: §11.2.5, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 stage text (compare bundles on the curve with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent) — compact annuli, not global sections over all of Y; relies on Proposition 11.2.2, which is not planned.

items.name: §11.2.5: Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_{B_{[0,1[}}
items.statement: Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} identifies with φ-Mod_{B_{[0,1[}}.
items.locator: §11.2.5, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.20(1): φ-bundles on Y from a fundamental annulus
items.statement: Let I be an interval of ]0,1[ with φ(I) ∩ I ≠ ∅. Restriction to Y_I induces an equivalence between Fib_{Y/φ^Z} and the category of pairs (E, u) with E ∈ Fib_{Y_I} and u : (φ^*E)|_{Y_{φ(I)∩I}} ⥲ E|_{φ(I)∩I}. (Proof: ∪_{n∈Z} φⁿ(I) = ]0,1[ and Proposition 11.2.12.)
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.20, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 stage text (finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent); the window charts of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve §6.2–6.4 give the corresponding presentation of the structure sheaf. No node.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.20(2): the same for Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z}
items.statement: The same holds for Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} when I is an interval of [0,1[ containing 0 (then ∪_n φⁿ(I) = [0,1[).
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.20, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Exemple 11.2.21: iso classes of rank-n φ-bundles as a Frobenius-twisted quotient
items.statement: Fix ρ ∈ ]0,1[. Isomorphism classes of rank-n bundles on Y/φ^Z identify with the quotient GL_n(B_{[ρ^q,ρ]})\GL_n(B_{ρ^q}), where X ∈ GL_n(B_{[ρ^q,ρ]}) acts on A ∈ GL_n(B_{ρ^q}) by X·A = XAφ(X)^{−1}.
items.locator: Exemple 11.2.21, p. 377, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Consequence of Proposition 11.2.20 and Théorème 3.5.1; not stated in the atlas (nearest VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1).

items.name: Corollaire 11.2.22(1): Fib_{Y/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_R
items.statement: Let φ-Mod_R be the category of free modules of finite rank over the Robba ring R = lim_{ρ→0} B_{]0,ρ]} with a semilinear isomorphism. There is an equivalence Fib_{Y/φ^Z} ⥲ φ-Mod_R.
items.locator: Corollaire 11.2.22, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not stated in the atlas. Ingredients planned: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free (bundles over Γ_an,r free) and RD.1/frobenius-module (σ-modules over Γ_an,con = R_F for ℓ = F); the comparison of σ-modules over R_F with φ-equivariant bundles on all of Y is not.

items.name: Corollaire 11.2.22(2): Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_{E^†}
items.statement: Let φ-Mod_{E^†} be the category of finite-dimensional E^†-vector spaces (E^† = lim_{ρ→0} B_{[0,ρ]}) with a semilinear isomorphism. There is an equivalence Fib_{Y∪{0}/φ^Z} ⥲ φ-Mod_{E^†}.
items.locator: Corollaire 11.2.22, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Remarque 11.2.23: φ-equivariant coherent sheaves ≃ finitely generated R-modules with φ
items.statement: If E ∈ Coh_Y carries a φ-equivariant structure then condition (2) of Proposition 11.2.5 holds; hence Coh_{Y/φ^Z} identifies with pairs (M, φ), M a finitely generated R-module and φ a semilinear isomorphism.
items.locator: Remarque 11.2.23, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Proposition 11.2.24 (Kedlaya [45] prop. 5.11, coro. 5.12): φ-Mod_{E^†} ≃ φ-Mod_ℰ
items.statement: (The 'easy case of Kedlaya's theorem'.) The completion functor φ-Mod_{E^†} → φ-Mod_ℰ (ℰ = π-adic completion of E^†) is an equivalence of categories; hence the Dieudonné–Manin classification applies to φ-Mod_{E^†} (as printed; false in general, see sourceIssues E218 — correct form after Kedlaya [45] Prop. 5.11: every object of φ-Mod_{E^†} has a unique filtration by saturated sub-φ-modules whose graded pieces are isoclinic of strictly decreasing Dieudonné–Manin slopes, each a direct sum of E^†(λ) when F is algebraically closed; completion is essentially surjective and an equivalence on isoclinic objects, but not fully faithful). (Proof: reduce by Galois descent to F algebraically closed and show every (V, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_{E^†} is a direct sum of E^†(λ), λ ∈ Q.)
items.locator: Proposition 11.2.24, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (b) (base change of isoclinic σ-modules Γ_con[π^{-1}] → Γ[π^{-1}] fully faithful), RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent and RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent (for Γ^alg). The equivalence E^† → ℰ with a Dieudonné–Manin decomposition over E^† is not stated. The printed proof reverses the slope ordering; see sourceIssues. Beyond that the proposition is false as stated (a non-split extension of E^†(0) by E^†(1) exists since coker(Id − πφ on E^†) ∋ [ϖ^{−1}] ≠ 0) and the cited Kedlaya [45] Prop. 5.11/Cor. 5.12 give only a descending slope filtration and the isoclinic case; see E218.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 11.2.24: coker(Id − π^{−d}φ^h : E^† → E^†) = 0 for d > 0
items.statement: For d > 0 and h ≥ 1 the cokernel of Id − π^{−d}φ^h : E^† → E^† is zero (equivalently H¹ of an isoclinic E^†-isocrystal of negative slope −d/h vanishes).
items.locator: proof of Proposition 11.2.24, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules (c): 'if n < 0 and ℓ is perfect, H¹(Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)) = H¹(Γ_an,con(n)) = 0' (F = π^nσ), i.e. the case h = 1; the case h > 1 follows via restriction of Frobenius (RD.1/frobenius-restriction-and-pullback). Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: Lemme 11.2.25: φ-invariants of an O_{E^†}-lattice equal those of its completion
items.statement: Let Λ be a free O_{E^†}-module of finite rank with a semilinear endomorphism φ whose matrix lies in GL_n(O_{E^†}) (the printed statement has only 'endomorphisme', and is then false, see E219). Then Λ^{φ=Id} ⥲ Λ̂^{φ=Id} (Λ̂ the π-adic completion) is a bijection.
items.locator: Lemme 11.2.25, p. 379, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: False for non-bijective φ (E219); the printed proof writes the fixed-point equation as φ(X) = AX whereas for the matrix of φ it is X = Aφ(X), so it only covers A ∈ GL_n(O_{E^†}) (apply it to A^{−1}). Nearest: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent (F-fixed vectors of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] lie in M for M over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] with nonpositive generic slopes) — only for ℓ^alg = completed algebraic closure of k((t)) and with a slope hypothesis rather than an integral lattice; FF's statement is for arbitrary perfect F.

items.name: §11.3: the analytification functor (−)^an : Coh_X → Coh_{Y/φ^Z}
items.statement: The φ-invariant morphism of ind-schemes lim_{→, I⊂]0,1[} Spec(B_I) → X induces an analytification functor (−)^an : Coh_X → Coh_{Y/φ^Z}.
items.locator: §11.3, p. 379, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (the map of locally ringed spaces X_S → X_S^alg = Proj P) and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness (compare bundles on X_S and the Proj curve).

items.name: Théorème 11.3.1 (Kedlaya–Liu [44] théo. 8.7.8): GAGA for the curve
items.statement: The analytification functor (−)^an : Coh_X → Coh_{Y/φ^Z} is an equivalence of categories.
items.locator: Théorème 11.3.1, pp. 380–381, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (FS II.2.7: vector bundles on X^alg = Proj P ≃ vector bundles on X, with cohomology comparison) — vector bundles only; the torsion part (B^+_{dR,y} ≅ Ô_{X,x}) is not stated there, and bundles on the adic X_S vs φ-bundles on Y_S is Frobenius descent (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF1).

items.name: Proof of Théorème 11.3.1: H⁰(X, E) = Γ(Y, E^an)^{φ=Id}
items.statement: For E ∈ Fib_X, H⁰(X, E) = H⁰(Y/φ^Z, E^an) = Γ(Y, E^an)^{φ=Id}; in particular (lim_{←,I⊂]0,1[} B_I[1/t_i])^{φ=Id} = B_{e,i} := B[1/t_i]^{φ=Id} for t_i ∈ P homogeneous nonzero (using B = {f ∈ M(Y) | div(f) ≥ 0}); hence (−)^an is fully faithful on bundles.
items.locator: proof of Théorème 11.3.1, pp. 380–381, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence gives H^i(X^alg, E^alg) ≅ H^i(X, E).

items.name: Proof of Théorème 11.3.1: φ-equivariant modifications ↔ lattices ↔ modifications on X
items.statement: For E ∈ Fib_{Y/φ^Z} of rank n, a φ-equivariant monomorphism u : O^n_{Y/φ^Z} ↪ E is a modification (its cokernel is torsion) and giving one is equivalent to giving lattices (Λ_y)_{y∈|Y|}, (B^+_{dR,y})^n ⊂ Λ_y, with φ(Λ_y) = Λ_{φ(y)} and Λ_y = (B^+_{dR,y})^n for almost all y mod φ^Z; equivalently lattices (N_x)_{x∈|X|}, Ô^n_{X,x} ⊂ N_x, with equality for almost all x; equivalently a modification O_X^n ↪ F with F ∈ Fib_X, and then F^an = E.
items.locator: proof of Théorème 11.3.1, p. 381, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles (Beauville–Laszlo gluing along Cartier divisors, 'several disjoint divisors'; nodes RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/beauville-laszlo-module-gluing and …/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor).

items.name: §11.3: O_{Y/φ^Z}(d) = O_X(d)^an ↔ (B, π^{−d}φ)
items.statement: For d ∈ Z, O_{Y/φ^Z}(d) := O_X(d)^an, which corresponds to the φ-module (B, π^{−d}φ) ∈ φ-Mod_B.
items.locator: §11.3, p. 381, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign: O_{X_S}(n) = E(Ĕ, π^{−n}σ), same sign.

items.name: Théorème 11.3.2 (Kedlaya): enough global sections of E(d)
items.statement: Let E ∈ Fib_{Y/φ^Z} have rank n. For d ≫ 0 there is a monomorphism O^n_{Y/φ^Z} ↪ E(d), which is therefore a modification. (Proof not given; for E = F_q((π)) see [34] théo. 4.3, after Kedlaya [45]; also [44] prop. 6.2.2, théo. 6.3.9.)
items.locator: Théorème 11.3.2, pp. 381–382, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation (FS II.2.6 after KL15 6.2.4): for S affinoid perfectoid and E on X_S, E(n) is globally generated with H¹ = 0 for n ≫ 0; n generically independent global sections give the monomorphism (standard).

items.name: Remarque 11.3.4: Kedlaya's classification of φ-modules over R_F (external)
items.statement: (F algebraically closed.) Kedlaya's theorem classifying φ-modules over R_F (every one is a direct sum of standard modules) can be reproved by adapting the proof of Chapter 8 using periods of p-divisible groups; but to have Harder–Narasimhan filtrations for bundles on Y/φ^Z one needs that they are successive extensions of line bundles, and the only known method is Théorème 11.3.2.
items.locator: Remarque 11.3.4, p. 382, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring plans Kedlaya's Dieudonné–Manin decomposition over R^alg, i.e. only for F = the completed algebraic closure of k((t)); not for an arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid F.

items.name: §11.4: φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ φ-Mod_B for F algebraically closed (Fréchet B)
items.statement: When F is algebraically closed, scalar extension along B^+ ⊂ B = B_{]0,1[} gives an equivalence φ-Mod_{B^+} ⥲ φ-Mod_B; geometrically every φ-equivariant bundle on Y extends canonically to a φ-equivariant bundle on Y ∪ {|·|_1 = 1}; this canonical extension functor is not exact (Remarque 11.1.10). Together with GAGA and global sections this gives Fib_X ≃ Fib_{Y/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_B ≃ φ-Mod_R.
items.locator: §11.4, pp. 382–383, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The chain Fib_X ≃ Fib_{Y/φ^Z} is planned via VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness and VB1 (see Théorème 11.3.1 item); the comparison with φ-modules over B^+ is not planned.

items.name: Remarque 11.4.1: φ-modules over B are free when F is algebraically closed
items.statement: If (M, φ) ∈ φ-Mod_B with F algebraically closed, the projective module M is a free B-module (by the classification of bundles). There is no reason for this for arbitrary perfect F; and in general projective B-modules are not free (not every bundle on Y is trivial) even when F is algebraically closed, though this is probably the case when F is spherically complete.
items.locator: Remarque 11.4.1, p. 383, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Derivable from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification plus GAGA, but not stated. The printed parenthesis lacks a negation; see sourceIssues.

items.name: §11.4: φ-Mod_{E^†} → φ-Mod_R is essentially surjective, not fully faithful
items.statement: For arbitrary (perfect) F, the functor φ-Mod_{E^†} → φ-Mod_R is essentially surjective (the Harder–Narasimhan filtration is split (9.4.1), classification 9.4.3, and Proposition 11.2.24), but it is not an equivalence (not fully faithful): every φ-equivariant bundle on Y extends non-canonically to a φ-equivariant bundle on Y ∪ {0}.
items.locator: §11.4, p. 383, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned; RD.2's slope filtration theorem (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement) gives a filtration, not a splitting or descent of the whole module.

items.name: §11.4: isoclinic E^†-isocrystals of slope −λ ≃ semistable φ-modules over R of slope λ
items.statement: For λ ∈ Q, φ-Mod^{isoc,−λ}_{E^†} ⥲ φ-Mod^{ss,λ}_R is an equivalence, where the left side consists of isoclinic isocrystals of Dieudonné–Manin slope −λ and the right side of semistable φ-modules (bundles) of Harder–Narasimhan slope λ.
items.locator: §11.4, p. 383, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (c) (base change of isoclinic σ-modules of slope s from Γ_con[π^{-1}] to Γ_an,con is an equivalence) and RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement (d) (semistable ⇔ isoclinic), for Kedlaya's Γ^ℓ with ℓ complete with enough units (includes ℓ = F perfect, E of characteristic 0). Sign dictionary: DM slope −λ ↔ HN slope λ. Status corrected by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18): the cited nodes are Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ over a Cohen ring, so they cover only E of characteristic 0, while Chapter 11 allows any local field E; The node stays the partial plan, and the item is missing.

items.name: §11.5: field of norms and K̂_∞^♭ (external, [61])
items.statement: Let K|Q_p be a local field with perfect residue field, K̄ an algebraic closure, K_∞ = K(ζ_{p^∞}), Γ = Gal(K_∞|K) (an open subgroup of Z_p^×), and K̃_∞ the (non-perfect) field of norms of [61], a local field of characteristic p. Then K̂_∞^♭ = (K̃_∞^{1/p^∞})^ (completion of the perfection).
items.locator: §11.5, p. 383, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.0 stage text: 'Include field-of-norms Galois equivalence and the descent/lifting statements'; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field computes the tilt of Q_p^cycl. No node states K̂_∞^♭ = completed perfection of the field of norms for general K.

items.name: §11.5: (φ, Γ)-modules over the classical Robba ring R_{K̃_∞}
items.statement: (φ, Γ)-mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} is the category of (φ, Γ)-modules over the 'classical' Robba ring R_{K̃_∞} of the field of norms.
items.locator: §11.5, p. 384, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:P7/robba-ring-of-p-adic-field (Berger's B^†_{rig,K}); PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.2 stage text refers to 'the larger category of all Robba (φ,Γ)-modules', separate from the étale ones.

items.name: §11.5: decompletion (φ, Γ)-mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} ≃ (φ, Γ)-mod over K̂_∞^♭ ([11])
items.statement: By the main theorem of [11] (decompletion of the completion of K̃_∞^{1/p^∞} using the Γ-action and Tate-type traces) there is an equivalence (φ, Γ)-mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} ⥲ (φ, Γ)-mod_{K̂_∞^♭} (as printed; in context the target is (φ, Γ)-modules over the Robba ring R_{K̂_∞^♭} of the perfectoid field K̂_∞^♭, which Théorème 11.5.1 then identifies via GAGA with Γ-equivariant bundles on X_{K̂_∞^♭}).
items.locator: §11.5, p. 384, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Only the étale case (Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence) is planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.2; Berger's decompletion operators R_k are PadicHodgeTheory:P7/decompletion-operators. The equivalence for all (not necessarily étale) (φ, Γ)-modules is not planned.

items.name: Théorème 11.5.1 (Berger [5]): (φ, Γ)-modules ≃ Γ-equivariant bundles on X_{K̂_∞^♭}
items.statement: There is an equivalence of categories between (φ, Γ)-mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} and Γ-equivariant vector bundles on X_{K̂_∞^♭} (deduced from the decompletion equivalence and GAGA; in [5] expressed via B-pairs).
items.locator: Théorème 11.5.1, p. 384, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: B-pairs and Berger's equivalence are absent from the atlas (no hit for 'B-pair' in any stage or node).

items.name: §11.5: Γ is essential — φ-Mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} → Fib_{X_{K̂_∞^♭}} is not essentially surjective
items.statement: Since there exist p-adic representations of Gal(K̄|K_∞) that are not overconvergent, the Γ-action is essential in Théorème 11.5.1: the functor φ-Mod_{R_{K̃_∞}} → Fib_{X_{K̂_∞^♭}} is not essentially surjective.
items.locator: §11.5, p. 384, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Not planned.

items.name: Fréchet–Stein algebras: coherent sheaves ≃ coadmissible modules (external, [55] §3, Cor. 3.3, 3.4)
items.statement: For a Fréchet–Stein algebra A = lim_← A_n (in the sense of [55] §3), the functor (M_n)_n ↦ lim_← M_n from coherent sheaves (compatible finitely generated A_n-modules) to A-modules is exact and fully faithful onto the coadmissible modules, with (lim_← M_n) ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n.
items.locator: used for Propositions 11.2.2 and 11.2.5, pp. 369–370, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: No stage or node mentions Fréchet–Stein algebras or coadmissible modules. Nearest: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorem-a and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b (Kiehl's Theorems A and B for quasi-Stein spaces locally of finite type over a field), RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity (R¹lim = 0 for vector bundles on Y_S). Among accepted routes (not yet layers), the Part II NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 route 18, PAPER-FU-24 route 2) plans 'Fréchet–Stein/coadmissible modules' for the distribution algebras D(G) and is to supply 'the algebra and coadmissible-module foundations ONCE'; the general Schneider–Teitelbaum §3 statement used here would belong with it.

items.name: Préface Théorème 3.16 (Fargues [19, th. 2.1]): Y_E^ad(I) is an adic space
items.statement: (Black box, Fargues, 'Quelques résultats et conjectures concernant la courbe', th. 2.1.) If I = [r_1, r_2] with r_1, r_2 ∈ Q, then Y_E^ad(I) = Spa(B_E(I), B_E(I)^+) is an adic space, i.e. its structure presheaf is a sheaf. Consequently Y_E^ad = lim_→ Y_E^ad([r_1, r_2]) and Y_E^ad(I) (I ⊂ ]0, +∞[) are adic spaces with O(Y_E^ad) = B_E, O(Y_E^ad(I)) = B_E(I), and (Théorème 3.9) |Y_E(I)| is the set of classical points of Y_E^ad(I).
items.locator: Préface Théorème 3.16 and following paragraph, p. 37, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The print cites '[FF, th. 2.1]' (source issue E23): the result is Fargues [19] (the chapters' [20], cited in Remarque 11.2.9, p. 372). The chapters never state it as a numbered result, so the Préface statement is not a restatement. Stage RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli asks for complete separated sheafiness of the relative annulus rings, which contains this case (S = Spa C^♭). Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18).

items.name: Remarque 1.4.4 and §1.4.1: restriction of the Gauss norms to E, and their homogeneity
items.statement: For ρ ∈ ]0,1[ the restriction of |·|_ρ to E is ρ^{v_π(·)} and induces the usual non-archimedean topology of E; by contrast |·|_1 restricted to E is the trivial absolute value and induces the discrete topology. For every ρ ∈ ]0,1], a ∈ F, n ∈ ℤ and x ∈ B^b: |[a]x|_ρ = |a|·|x|_ρ and |π^n x|_ρ = ρ^n |x|_ρ; the Gauss norms are entirely determined by their restriction to A and these two properties.
items.locator: §1.4.1 (after Lemme 1.4.2) and Remarque 1.4.4, p. 62, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: The review searched the stage texts and packets of RF0, RF0:annuli, RD.0 and P7:annulus-foundations: they define Gauss norms on their own rings but do not state this for B^b with ρ = 1. Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18).

items.name: Exemples 2.3.7 and 2.3.10: the parametrisation of |Y|_{deg=1} by 1 + m_F for E = Q_p
items.statement: Let E = Q_p, F algebraically closed, Q(X) = (1 + X)^p − 1 (so [x]_Q = [1 + x] − 1 and the Lubin–Tate group is Ĝ_m). For ε ∈ m_F∖{0} put α = 1 + ε; then u_ε = [ε]_Q/[ε^{1/p}]_Q = 1 + [α^{1/p}] + [α^{2/p}] + ⋯ + [α^{(p−1)/p}] (printed with an extra term [α]; see source issues) is primitive of degree 1, and α ↦ y_ε induces a bijection (1 + m_F∖{1})/Z_p^× ⥲ |Y|_{deg=1}, where a ∈ Z_p^× acts on 1 + m_F by (1 + x)^a = Σ_{k≥0} binom(a,k) x^k.
items.locator: Exemple 2.3.7, p. 117, and Exemple 2.3.10, p. 118, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
items.note: Special case of Lemme 2.3.5 and Prop. 2.3.9 with Q = (1 + X)^p − 1. For C = C_p the fact that 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + ⋯ + [ε^{1/p}]^{p−1} generates ker θ is part of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/frobenius-kernel-ideals-of-ainf; the bijection itself is not planned. Added by the independent review (REV-PAPER-FARGUES-FONTAINE-18).

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, Espaces de Banach de dimension finie, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002), no. 3, 331–439
prerequisites.why: The category of finite-dimensional Banach spaces with its Dimension (dim, ht) and the 'lemme fondamental': the Préface's §§2.2–2.3 and the second proof of the classification (§8.4) use them as a black box.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, Espaces vectoriels de dimension finie et représentations de de Rham, Astérisque 319 (2008), 117–186
prerequisites.link: no DOI: Astérisque 319, Société Mathématique de France (2008)
prerequisites.why: Proposition 10.11 there computes H^1_g of (B^+)^{φ^h=p^d} and is Proposition 10.6.17 of the book, the key input to de Rham implies potentially semistable (§10.6.5).

prerequisites.citation: J.-M. Fontaine, Groupes p-divisibles sur les corps locaux, Astérisque 47–48 (1977)
prerequisites.link: no DOI: Astérisque 47–48, Société Mathématique de France (1977)
prerequisites.why: Witt covectors, bivectors and the Dieudonné theory of p-divisible groups over perfect rings, on which Chapter 4 builds the periods of π-divisible O-modules.

prerequisites.citation: B. H. Gross and M. J. Hopkins, Equivariant vector bundles on the Lubin–Tate moduli space, in Topology and representation theory (Evanston, 1992), Contemp. Math. 158 (1994), 23–88
prerequisites.why: Surjectivity of the Lubin–Tate period morphism (Théorème 8.1.1), one of the two inputs of the first proof of the classification.

prerequisites.citation: V. G. Drinfeld, Coverings of p-adic symmetric domains, Funct. Anal. Appl. 10 (1976), 107–115
prerequisites.why: Drinfeld's description of the period morphism of special formal O_D-modules (Théorème 8.1.3), the other input of the first proof of the classification.

prerequisites.citation: M. Lazard, Les zéros des fonctions analytiques d'une variable sur un corps valué complet, Publ. Math. IHÉS 14 (1962), 47–75
prerequisites.why: The model for Chapters 1–3: Newton polygons, Weierstrass factorisation and divisors of analytic functions on annuli, and the closed ideals of these rings (Préface Théorème 2.30).

prerequisites.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Doc. Math. 10 (2005), 447–525
prerequisites.why: The Bézout property of B_{]0,ρ]} (Théorème 3.5.7) and the slope theory of φ-modules over the Robba ring used in Chapter 11.

prerequisites.citation: L. Berger, Construction de (φ,Γ)-modules : représentations p-adiques et B-paires, Algebra Number Theory 2 (2008), no. 1, 91–120
prerequisites.why: B-pairs, which Chapter 10 identifies with G_K-equivariant bundles, and the equivalence with (φ,Γ)-modules behind Théorème 11.5.1.

prerequisites.citation: L. Fargues, La filtration de Harder–Narasimhan des schémas en groupes finis et plats, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), 1–39
prerequisites.why: Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of finite flat group schemes, the example of the §5.5 formalism in Exemple 5.5.2.7.

prerequisites.citation: Y. André, Slope filtrations, Confluentes Math. 1 (2009), 1–85
prerequisites.why: The quasi-abelian framework for slope filtrations that §5.5 follows.

prerequisites.citation: U. Hartl and R. Pink, Vector bundles with a Frobenius structure on the punctured unit disc, Compos. Math. 140 (2004), 689–716
prerequisites.why: Théorème 5.6.26, the dévissage of the classification, follows Hartl–Pink and Kedlaya; their Theorem 4.3 is the global-sections argument behind the GAGA statement of §11.3 when E = F_q((π)).

routes.reason: RF0 is the layer that constructs the ramified Witt vectors W_OE(R) with Teichmüller representatives, Frobenius, the π-adically complete flat universal property and the uniformizer-change comparisons ('A general E is not obtained by renaming p in a formula'). §1.2 of the book is that construction done for every O_E-algebra: ramified Witt polynomials and Dwork's criterion (Lemme 1.2.1), F and V_π, the comparison W_{O_E}(A) → W_{O_E'}(A) and the base change W_{O_E}(A) ⊗ O_E' ≅ W_{O_E'}(A) for perfect A, the Q-twisted functor W_{O_E,Q,π} ≅ W_{O_E,π} (Prop. 1.2.4) and the Lubin–Tate Teichmüller lifts [x]_Q, [x]_LT (Prop. 1.2.7, Lemme 1.2.9, Cor. 1.2.10) that Chapter 2 uses to write down primitive elements and the points y_ε of Y. RF0's perfect case is a specialisation, and the twisted lifts are what its later divisor and untilt layers need for general E; so these items belong inside RF0 rather than in a new layer; RF0's blueprint must state them for arbitrary π-adic O_E-algebras, not only perfect ones. The Préface's diamond reading of |Y_E| (Remarque 3.19, first bullet) belongs with RF1, which constructs 'the diamond formulas over Perf_Fq with the chosen coefficient-field embedding' ((Y_S)^◇ = S × Spd E).

routes.title: Relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and period geometry, Part II: holomorphic functions of the variable π and the schematic curve over a perfect field
routes.brief: Extend Relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and period geometry (RelativeFarguesFontaine) by the function theory on which Fargues and Fontaine build the absolute curve, Astérisque 406 (2018), Chapters 1–3, 6, 7 and §§11.2.1–11.2.4, read in the authors' copy of 16 April 2017 (statement numbers below are that copy's). The parent constructs the relative adic objects Y_S, X_S, untilts, B_dR^+ and the graded algebra of RF3 by the Fargues–Scholze route; nothing in the atlas proves the classical theory of zeros of holomorphic functions of the variable π on Y, and none of it gives the schematic curve over a perfect field that is not algebraically closed. Final theorems, as the book states them (E a local field with residue field F_q and uniformizer π, F a perfectoid field of characteristic p over F_q, A = W_{O_E}(O_F), B^b = A[1/π, 1/[ϖ]], B_I its completions for the Gauss norms |·|_ρ, ρ ∈ I, B = B_{]0,1[}, P = ⊕_{d≥0} B^{φ=π^d}): (1) Théorème 2.4.1: if F is algebraically closed, every primitive element of A of degree d ≥ 1 is a product of d primitive elements of degree 1; Corollaire 2.4.11 and Théorème 3.4.4: the non-zero slopes of Newt_I(f) are the −log_q‖y‖ of the zeros y of f in |Y_I|, with multiplicity deg(y)·ord_y(f) (with the correction recorded in sourceIssues). (2) Théorèmes 2.5.1 and 3.5.1: for F perfect and I ⊂ [0,1[ compact, B_I is a complete valued field when I = {0} or I = {ρ} with ρ ∉ |F^×| for F algebraically closed (Théorème 2.5.1), ρ ∉ |F^×|^{1/∞} for F perfect (Théorème 3.5.1), and otherwise a principal ideal domain whose closed maximal ideals are the points of |Y_I|; Théorèmes 2.7.4, 3.5.5, Proposition 3.5.2: f ∈ B_I·g iff div(f) ≥ div(g), and closed ideals correspond to positive divisors; Théorème 3.5.7 (Kedlaya): B_{]0,ρ]} is Bézout; Proposition 3.5.10: M(Y) = Frac(B). (3) Théorème 3.1.8: |Y_F| = |Y_{F̂̄}|^{G_F-fin}/G_F with deg(y) the size of the fibre; Théorème 3.3.1: degree-d points of |Y_F| correspond to perfectoid K|E with a continuous ι: F ↪ K^♭ of degree d; Théorème 3.6.1: B_{F̂̄}^{G_F} = B_F and (B^+_{F̂̄})^{G_F} = B^+_F. (4) Théorème 6.2.1: if F is algebraically closed, P is graded-factorial with irreducible elements of degree 1; Théorème 6.2.7: div: ∪_d (P_d∖{0})/E^× → Div^+(Y/φ^Z) is injective, and an isomorphism if F is algebraically closed; Théorème 6.4.1: for F algebraically closed and y_1,…,y_d ∈ |Y| in distinct Frobenius orbits and t_i = Π(a_i), there is an exact sequence of E-Banach spaces 0 → E·∏t_i → B^{φ=π^d} → B/m_{y_1}⋯m_{y_d}B → 0; Théorème 6.4.4 as corrected. (5) Théorèmes 6.5.2 and 7.3.3: for F perfect, X_{F,E} = Proj(P) is a complete curve (Déf. 5.1.3) with field of definition E, |X_F| = |Y_F|/φ^Z, and Ô_{X_F,x} ≅ B^+_{dR,y}; Propositions 7.2.1 and 7.2.4: X∖{∞} = Spec(B_{F,e}) with B_{F,e} a Dedekind domain and Cl(B_{F,e}) ≅ Hom(G_F, E^×); Propositions 7.5.1 and 7.6.1: X_E ⊗_E E' = X_{E'}, and X_L → X_F is a finite étale Galois cover with group Gal(L|F); Proposition 7.8.2: X = Proj(⊕_d H^0(L^{⊗d})) for any positive φ-line bundle L; Corollaire 7.9.2: Y/φ^Z is recovered from (X, O_X, (|·|_ρ)_ρ). Cover, in order: (a) Chapter 1, §§1.3–1.10: B^b and B^{b,+}, Gauss norms and their limit formulas, the weak topology and completeness of A, Legendre transforms and Newton polygons, the Fréchet algebras B_I and their change of E, the cases F = k((π_F^{1/p^∞})) and F maximally complete, E^† and the Robba ring, extension to the boundary radii, B^+, B^+_ρ, bivectors and A_cris,ρ. (b) Chapter 2 (F algebraically closed): the functor (−)^{♭,Q}, primitive elements and Weierstrass division, roots and Teichmüller values in A/(a), the metric space |Y|_{deg=1} and its Lubin–Tate parametrisation, Weierstrass factorisation, principality of B_I, divisors. (c) Chapter 3 (F perfect): Galois descent of points and of primitive ideals, the residue fields of |Y_F|, zeros and divisors, Galois invariants of B. (d) Chapter 6: P, graded factoriality, Weierstrass products Π^±(b), the Lubin–Tate logarithm as a product, the fundamental exact sequence, the curve for F algebraically closed, its meromorphic functions and its presentation as a quotient of lim Spec(B_I). (e) Chapter 7: Galois cohomology of B^+_dR and B^{φ=π^d} (Propositions 7.1.1–7.1.2), B_e Dedekind, the curve for F perfect, change of E and of F, X_{F̄}, ample φ-line bundles and Proj, Runge density of B_e in B_I. (f) §§11.2.1–11.2.4: bundles and coherent sheaves on Y_I as modules over B_I, Mayer–Vietoris and gluing, the finite étale extension B_{L,I}|B_{F,I}, Galois descent for B_I-modules, and the Fréchet–Stein input of Schneider–Teitelbaum. (g) From Colmez's Préface: the degree on B_e and why Bézout gives principal, the Kedlaya–Temkin answer to Fontaine's first question, the closed prime ideals of A_E, and |X| ≅ Aut(C^♭)/(Aut(C) × φ^Z) for maximally complete C. at S = Spa F these are the book's rings and must be identified with them); Foundations of adic spaces (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces) Layer 6, the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve (existing Tau Ceti work: A_inf, 𝒴, the windows, Kedlaya's interval rings B^I for E = Q_p and any perfect F, the quotient X; P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) P7:annulus-foundations (Gauss norms, Newton polygons, Weierstrass preparation on circles and zeros of Laurent series on annuli over any complete field K, which is the equal-characteristic case B_I = O_F(I) of Proposition 1.7.4); routes.title: Isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces, Part II: quasi-Banach-Colmez spaces, almost C-representations and the Hom-vanishing toolkit
routes.brief: Augment the VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII proposal (Colmez–Nizioł's quasi-Banach–Colmez spaces and almost C-representations, PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25) with the bundle theory of Fargues and Fontaine, Astérisque 406 (2018), Chapters 5, 8 (§§8.2, 8.4–8.6), 9 and 11 (§§11.1, 11.2.5, 11.4), and with Colmez's Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie and Fontaine's almost C-representations as the book's Préface presents them; statement numbers are those of the authors' copy of 16 April 2017. The parent classifies bundles at geometric points by Fargues–Scholze's route (VB2:classification) and treats Banach–Colmez spaces as diamonds (VB3); it has no abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism, no classification over a perfect field that is not algebraically closed, no φ-module description over B^+, and not Colmez's original Dimension theory. Final theorems, as the book states them: (1) §5.5: in an exact category with additive deg and rg and a faithful exact 'generic fibre' functor satisfying the axioms of §5.5.1, every object has a unique Harder–Narasimhan filtration (Théorème 5.5.2), strict subobjects lie below the polygon, which is the concave envelope of their points (rg(X'), deg(X')) (Théorème 5.5.3, with the coordinates corrected), and C^{≤λ}, C_{≥λ} are exact and stable under extensions (Théorème 5.5.4); examples: filtered vector spaces, filtered φ-modules with degree t_H − t_N, Frobenius sheaves on a one-dimensional scheme (Exemple 5.5.2.6, with the sign corrected). (2) §5.6: Théorème 5.6.2 (Grothendieck: on a Riemann sphere every bundle is ⊕O(d_i)); Théorème 5.6.26: on a generalised Riemann sphere (X_h)_h such that H^0(X_h, E) ≠ 0 for every extension 0 → O_{X_h}(−1/n) → E → O_{X_h}(1) → 0, semistable bundles are the pure ones, Harder–Narasimhan filtrations split, and (λ_1 ≥ … ≥ λ_n) ↦ ⊕O_X(λ_i) is a bijection onto isomorphism classes; Corollaire 5.6.28 (semistable bundles of slope λ ≃ finite-dimensional End(O_X(λ))^{opp}-vector spaces); Théorème 5.6.29 (the criterion by degree-one modifications); finite étale maps of curves with Propositions 5.6.12 and 5.6.15 (deg f_*E = deg E), with Lemme 5.6.14 corrected. (3) For F algebraically closed: the proof of the classification (Théorème 8.2.10, planned in VB2:classification) through Banach–Colmez spaces (§8.4); Théorème 8.5.1: every bundle on X_Ē is a sum of line bundles O⟨λ⟩, classified by decreasing slope sequences; Théorème 8.6.1: X_Ē is simply connected. (4) For F perfect: Théorème 9.2.2 (F algebraically closed, H a profinite group acting on F: H-equivariant semistable bundles of slope λ ≃ semilinear D_λ^op-representations); Théorème 9.3.1 (Coh_{X_F} ≃ Coh^{G_F}_{X_{F̂̄}}); Théorème 9.3.4 (Galois descent for B_e-modules); Théorème 9.4.1 (the Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits); Théorème 9.4.3 (bundles on X_F ↔ sequences ((λ_i, [ρ_i])) with λ_1 > … > λ_n and ρ_i non-zero in Rep_{D_{λ_i}^op}(G_F)); Théorème 9.5.1 (π_1(X_{F,Ē}) ≅ Gal(F̄|F)). (5) φ-modules: Théorèmes 11.1.7 and 11.1.8 (φ-modules over B^+ come from isocrystals, with the correction for k_F not containing F_{q^h}), Théorème 11.1.9 (E(−): φ-Mod_{B^+} ≃ Fib_X for F algebraically closed), Théorème 11.1.12 and Corollaire 11.1.14 (φ-modules over B^+_ρ and B^+_cris,ρ; Fib_X ≃ F-isocrystals on O_F/a), and the equivalences Fib_{Y/φ^Z} ≃ φ-Mod_B ≃ φ-Mod_R (§11.2.5, Corollaire 11.2.22(1)). (6) Préface §§2.2–2.4: Colmez's skew field 𝒞 and the 'lemme fondamental' (Théorèmes 2.5, 2.6, 2.8); Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie with Dim = (dim, ht) well defined and additive on kernels, images and cokernels (Théorème 2.12); Théorèmes 2.16–2.21; Fontaine's almost C-representations, abelian with additive Dim (Théorème 2.22), with their Ext groups and duality (Proposition 2.28, with the sign corrected); the Euler–Poincaré characteristic of a bundle in Dimensions (Remarques 4.4 and 4.6). Import, never rebuild: Isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals) VB0–VB4, including VB3's Dimension and height of Banach–Colmez spaces and the abelian category BC (routed there by PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 3 and this paper's route 10), with which Colmez's original Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie are compared rather than re-dimensioned (isocrystals and Dieudonné–Manin, bundles on the adic curve, the geometric classification, Banach–Colmez spaces as diamonds; the schematic objects here are identified with the parent's through VB2:ampleness's GAGA comparison); Relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and period geometry, Part II: holomorphic functions of the variable π and the schematic curve over a perfect field (RelativeFarguesFontainePartIIHolomorphicFunctionsAndSchematicCurve) (the schematic curve X_{F,E} for perfect F, B_e, and Propositions 7.1.1–7.1.2); P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) R06.1 (Tate–Sen theory and semilinear Galois descent); Tau Ceti's divisors on schemes (SchemeWeilDivisor, OrderSystem, which already cover §5.1) and Mathlib's rank-one Dieudonné–Manin. Plan the almost C-representations once, merged with the Colmez–Nizioł proposal. Tests: P^1 over a field as the first generalised Riemann sphere; O(1/2) on X_{F,Q_p}, whose endomorphisms are the quaternion algebra D_{1/2} (the example showing the Galois action in Proposition 5.6.25 is not the standard one); F = F_q((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with a non-trivial character of G_F, which gives a degree-0 line bundle not isomorphic to O_X; k_F = F_q with λ = 1/2 (the counterexample to the proof of Lemme 11.1.6); X(1,1) = B^{φ=π} of Dimension (1,1); and Colmez's B_2 = B^+_dR/t² of Dimension (2,0).
routes.reason: The parent roadmap plans isocrystals (VB0), bundles on the adic curve and their cohomology (VB1), ampleness and the classification at geometric points (VB2), Banach–Colmez spaces as diamonds (VB3) and families (VB4), all by Fargues–Scholze's route. The book reaches the same objects schematically and goes further in three directions that no layer plans: an abstract Harder–Narasimhan and classification theory for curves (Chapter 5), which the book applies to the curve through generalised Riemann spheres; the classification of bundles and the fundamental group over any perfect field (Chapter 9), which VB0 says explicitly it does not give ('a classification after algebraic closure is not a classification of all descent forms over an arbitrary perfectoid field'); and the description of bundles by φ-modules over B^+, B^+_ρ, B and the Robba ring (Chapter 11). Colmez's own Espaces de Banach de Dimension finie and Fontaine's almost C-representations, which the Préface surveys and §8.4 uses, extend what the Colmez–Nizioł proposal asks this Part II to supply (almost C-representations); the Dimension (dim, ht) of Banach–Colmez spaces and the category BC stay with VB3, where PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 3 routed them. All three are in the direction of this roadmap, so they are one Part II, merged with the existing proposal. The independent review joined the accepted VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII of PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 with its byte-identical title, moved Colmez's Dimension and the category BC (items 27, 28, 837, 838) to VB3 (route 8), and brought in the abstract Harder–Narasimhan formalism of §5.5 and the Riemann-sphere statements of §5.6 that were marked planned in VB1 or VB2 although those layers plan them only for the Fargues–Fontaine curve (items 590–603, 606, 608, 610, 619, 641, 647–652, 661), the φ-module statements 1019 and 1100, FF's bundle dictionary (1085, 1086, 1099, from route 6) and Weinstein's π_1 computations (96, 97, from route 8), which are the diamond form of Théorèmes 8.6.1 and 9.5.1.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: π-divisible O-modules over perfect rings, universal covers and period maps
routes.brief: Extend Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory), starting where R07.2 (Dieudonné theory over perfect fields) stops, with the periods of π-divisible O-modules as Fargues and Fontaine develop them in Astérisque 406 (2018), Chapter 4, §8.1 and §8.3 (authors' copy of 16 April 2017). Final theorems, as the book states them: (1) Corollaire 4.4.4 and Proposition 4.4.6: for G a formal π-divisible O-module over F̄_q with contravariant Dieudonné module D, G(O_F) ≅ Hom_{W_O(F_q)[F]}(D[1/π], B^+) as E-vector spaces, and for 1 ≤ d ≤ h the isomorphism G_{d,h}(O_F) ≅ B^{φ^h=π^d} is a homeomorphism of Banach spaces; Proposition 4.2.1(2) (with its indexing corrected): L_{d,h}: m_F^d ≅ (B^+)^{φ^h=π^d}. (2) The universal cover: X(G)(O_C) ≅ G_k(O_F) is a homeomorphism (Proposition 4.5.11); the period map defined by quasi-logarithms agrees with that of Corollaire 4.4.4 (Propositions 4.5.6, 4.5.13); the exact sequence 0 → V_π(G) → X(G)(C) → Lie G → 0 is isomorphic to 0 → Fil Hom → Hom_{W_O(k)_Q[F]}(D[1/π], B^+) → D_C^*/Fil D_C^* → 0 (Proposition 4.5.14); X(G) is a formal E-vector space for G over a perfect adic ring, and in general depends only on the special fibre up to quasi-isogeny (Propositions 4.6.4, 4.6.8, Corollaire 4.6.9); its spectral generic fibre (Définitions 4.6.20–4.6.26, with Définition 4.6.22 corrected) depends only on the special fibre (Proposition 4.6.27). (3) Period maps: Théorème 8.1.1 (Laffaille, Gross–Hopkins: the period morphism π̆ from the Lubin–Tate space to P^{n−1} is surjective) and Théorème 8.1.3 (Drinfeld: π̆ identifies Ω with the complement of the E-rational hyperplanes), with their forms on the curve, Théorèmes 8.1.2 and 8.1.5; Proposition 8.3.2: the de Rham periods of p-divisible groups are admissible, ℰ(D, π^{−1}φ, Fil D_C) ≅ V_p(H) ⊗ O_X; Propositions 8.3.4–8.3.5: minuscule modifications of trivial bundles are the pairs (V, W{1} ⊂ V_C), and Hom(−, O_X(1/n)) makes them anti-equivalent to modifications of D_{1/n}-bundles; and the second proof of the classification theorem (Théorème 8.2.10) by verifying the two hypotheses of Théorème 5.6.29 from Gross–Hopkins and Drinfeld (§8.3.2). (4) Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of finite flat group schemes (Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010); Exemple 5.5.2.7) as an instance of the book's §5.5 formalism, and their (M, φ) description over W(k)[[u]] in characteristic p. Cover also: π-divisible O-modules and O-height, the O-Dieudonné module via Fontaine's covectors and bivectors (Groupes p-divisibles sur les corps locaux), the modules G_{d,h}, the laws F_{d,h} and their lifts G̃_{d,h} with logarithms, quasi-logarithms and rigid quasi-morphisms, the Banach structure on G(O_F), and the spectral-space framework of §4.6 (M(A), spectral algebras, K-spectral spaces) or its replacement by diamonds with the comparison stated; Galois descent for semilinear actions on infinite-dimensional spaces (Hilbert 90 as used in Proposition 4.1.7). Import, never rebuild: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1–R07.2; the function theory of B^{φ^h=π^d} (Chapter 4.1) from Relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and period geometry, Part II: holomorphic functions of the variable π and the schematic curve over a perfect field (RelativeFarguesFontainePartIIHolomorphicFunctionsAndSchematicCurve); the Lubin–Tate Part II already proposed for this parent (LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts) for Lubin–Tate formal O_E-modules and their logarithms, which Chapters 1–2 of the book also use; Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic Dieudonné theory (PrismaticCohomologyPartIIPrismaticDieudonneTheory), which plans Scholze–Weinstein's Theorems A and B over O_C and O_C/p: the universal cover X(G) (Définition 4.5.1, Propositions 4.5.2, 4.6.4, 4.6.8) is constructed once, here, for π-divisible O-modules over any ring in which π is nilpotent, and that Part II imports it for G̃ and proves its G̃_C(R, R⁺) = (M ⊗ B_crys⁺)^{φ=1} agrees with Corollaire 4.4.4 and Proposition 4.5.11; Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6a, whose infinite-level duality imports Théorèmes 8.1.1 and 8.1.3 from here, and which plans the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers and their period morphisms (prove Théorèmes 8.1.1 and 8.1.3 here and export them); Isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals) VB0–VB3 (VB3:positive-basic-examples owns the Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculation of FS II.2.1–II.2.2) and its Part II (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII); Siegel and PEL moduli problems, Part II: unitary Rapoport–Zink spaces, RSZ integral models and p-adic uniformization (UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels) is a consumer of the Rapoport–Zink space and de Rham period map of §8.3.1 planned here (isocrystals, bundles, Théorème 5.6.29). Tests: μ_{p^∞} (d = h = 1, G(O_F) = 1 + m_F ≅ B^{φ=p}); the p-divisible group of a supersingular elliptic curve (d = 1, h = 2); the Lubin–Tate group G̃_{1,h} (Exemple 4.3.2) and its period map; Drinfeld's upper half plane (n = 2); and the logarithm of X(Ĝ_m) in the coordinates of Exemple 4.6.10, with the sign of Exemple 4.6.29 corrected.
routes.reason: R07.2 stops at Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields and the deformation results of p-divisible groups; no layer plans the periods of p-divisible groups over O_F or O_C, the universal cover X(G) and its structure as a formal E-vector space, the Gross–Hopkins and Drinfeld period maps with their surjectivity and image, or Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of finite flat group schemes. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a plans the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers and their period morphisms but not these theorems, and the prismatic Dieudonné Part II classifies p-divisible groups over O_C/p without Fontaine's covector description.
