routes.title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: G_K-equivariant bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve and the curve proofs of 'weakly admissible implies admissible' and of the p-adic monodromy theorem
routes.brief: Extend P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory), starting from R06.1–R06.3, with Chapter 10 of Fargues and Fontaine, Astérisque 406 (2018), and §11.5 (authors' copy of 16 April 2017): p-adic Hodge theory read on G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the curve X = X_{C^♭,Q_p}, for K|Q_p complete and discretely valued with perfect residue field. Final theorems, as the book states them: (1) no 10.1.2 and Théorème 10.1.7: G_K-equivariant bundles on X are Berger's B-pairs, and for λ ∈ Q, V ↦ 𝒱 ⊗_{D_λ} O_X(λ) is an equivalence between finite-dimensional D_λ^op-vector spaces with continuous semilinear G_K-action and G_K-equivariant semistable bundles of slope λ; in particular Rep_{Q_p}(G_K) ≃ Fib^{G_K,0}_X. (2) Théorème 10.2.14: D and V are inverse equivalences between crystalline B_e-representations and isocrystals; Proposition 10.5.3: filtered φ-modules are equivalent to crystalline equivariant bundles; Théorème 10.5.7: if t_H(A) > t_N(A) then dim V_cris(A) = ∞, and if t_H(A) = t_N(A) then A is admissible iff dim V_cris(A) < ∞, which with Proposition 10.5.6 gives 'faiblement admissible implique admissible'. (3) Propositions 10.6.2 and 10.6.7: filtered (φ,N)- and (φ,N,Gal(L|K))-modules are equivalent to log-crystalline and potentially log-crystalline equivariant bundles; Théorème 10.6.10: every de Rham G_K-equivariant bundle is potentially log-crystalline, through Théorème 10.6.11 (a bundle whose completion at ∞ is a flat B^+_dR-representation is potentially log-crystalline); hence de Rham representations are potentially semistable. (4) Théorème 11.5.1 (Berger): (φ,Γ)-modules over R_{K̃_∞} are equivalent to Γ-equivariant bundles on X_{K̂_∞^♭}. Cover, in order: the Galois action on X and its point ∞ (Proposition 10.1.1, proof corrected for unramified characters of infinite order); B_e- and B^+_dR-representations, B-pairs and their Tannakian category (Proposition 10.1.3, Corollaire 10.1.4); descent of equivariant sheaves to an arithmetically profinite extension (Théorème 10.1.5); flat equivariant bundles and the functors V and D (Propositions 10.2.6–10.2.15, with the range of Proposition 10.2.7 corrected); B_log, the surface X_log and the bundles E(D,φ,N) (§10.3); de Rham bundles and G_K-stable B^+_dR-lattices (Propositions 10.4.3–10.4.8); Harder–Narasimhan filtrations of filtered φ-modules and their match with bundles (Lemme 10.5.5, Proposition 10.5.6); Galois descent of equivariant bundles (Proposition 10.6.4); the reduction of Théorème 10.6.11 to H^1_g computations (Propositions 10.6.14–10.6.18, with 10.6.18(2) read for H^1_g and the error in Hyodo's argument recorded); and, from the Préface, Berger's pairs M(V), M(D), M(∆), the perfectoidness of Lie-type extensions (§5.4) and the categories descended to K_∞^♭. Import, never rebuild: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) R06.1–R06.3 (period rings, period functors, admissibility and the monodromy theorem as planned by the Colmez–Fontaine and Berger route; this Part II gives the curve's proofs and proves they agree with R06.2 and R06.3); Isocrystals, vector bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals) VB0–VB2 and its Part II (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII) (classification at geometric points, equivariant bundles and Galois descent from Chapter 9, the Harder–Narasimhan formalism of Chapter 5); Relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and period geometry, Part II: holomorphic functions of the variable π and the schematic curve over a perfect field (RelativeFarguesFontainePartIIHolomorphicFunctionsAndSchematicCurve) (the schematic curve, B_e and Propositions 7.1.1–7.1.2); (φ,Γ)-modules, Herr complexes and local Iwasawa cohomology (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology) PG.0–PG.2 ((φ,Γ)-modules and Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence for étale objects; the decompletion of all (φ,Γ)-modules over R_{K̃_∞} used in §11.5 is planned here); export B-pairs and their Tannakian category to The trianguline variety and its local model (TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel), which currently expects them from P7; agree with Admissible pairs, p-adic Hodge structures and the bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem (AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures) on a single owner of 'filtrations versus B_dR^+-lattices' (Propositions 10.4.3–10.4.4 here, its Theorems 3.2.1/3.2.6) and of the G_K-fixed points of the B_dR-affine Grassmannian; ArithmeticGaloisDuality (Tate local duality and inflation–restriction); PadicHodgeRegulators L1 (the Bloch–Kato exponential); PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.2 (local monodromy with Frobenius, for the comparison of routes). Tests: Q_p(1) and a non-split Kummer extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) (crystalline, t_H = t_N); V_p of a Tate curve (semistable, N ≠ 0); a character of G_K that is finite on inertia (potentially crystalline); and the weakly admissible module over K = Q_p(√p) of slope −1 that breaks Hyodo's step.
routes.reason: PadicHodgeTheory plans the period rings (R06.1), the period functors with 'weakly admissible versus admissible' (R06.2) and the p-adic monodromy theorem (R06.3), by the Colmez–Fontaine and Berger routes; no layer plans G_K-equivariant vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve, B-pairs, the surface X_log, the classification of equivariant semistable bundles, or the book's proofs of both theorems through the curve. Chapter 10 is that alternative foundation of p-adic Hodge theory and continues this roadmap's direction, so it is a Part II of it; the statements it reproves stay planned in R06.2 and R06.3. The independent review added the Chapter 10 items that the atlas plans only for K/Q_p finite (Tate's theorems, B_cris regular, the Tate-curve remarks, Théorème 10.5.7 and Remarque 10.5.8, the monodromy theorem, inflation–restriction with Banach coefficients, Proposition 10.6.18(1) and Remarque 10.6.19), since Chapter 10 works over any complete discretely valued K with perfect residue field, and the decompletion of all (φ,Γ)-modules (1103, from route 9).

RD.0 builds bounded and full Robba rings with their radius-indexed norms and RD.1 the Frobenius slope filtrations over them (Kedlaya's route). The items routed here are statements about those rings that the book and its Préface use: Lazard's theorem on closed ideals of rings of analytic functions on annuli and its extension to general complete fields (Préface Théorème 2.30(ii), Remarque 2.31(ii)); that the Robba ring has no closed ideals but 0 and R (§2.5.1); Lazard's Bézout theorem for rings of analytic functions on open annuli and discs (Préface Théorème 2.30(i), which RD.0's nodes state only for closed and half-open intervals); and Kedlaya's comparisons of φ-modules over E^† and ℰ — φ-Mod_{E^†} → φ-Mod_ℰ (Proposition 11.2.24, false as printed: the completion functor is not fully faithful, see the sourceIssues, and the item carries Kedlaya's correct statement), the invariants of an O_{E^†}-lattice for a bijective φ (Lemme 11.2.25, also corrected), the vanishing of coker(Id − π^{−d}φ^h) on E^† (proof of 11.2.24), and the classification of φ-modules over R_F (Remarque 11.3.4). They belong inside those two layers; RD.0 and RD.1 must state them for E of equal characteristic too. (The review moved Corollaire 11.2.22(2), Remarque 11.2.23 and §11.4, items 1085, 1086 and 1099, to route 3 with FF's other bundle statements.)

These are the classical proof ingredients the Préface surveys for statements these layers already own. Sen's theorem that a representation which is Hodge–Tate of weight 0 has finite inertia image (Préface Théorème 2.4; book [58] 3.2, used in §10.6.4) belongs with R06.1's Tate–Sen theory. Colmez and Fontaine's proof of 'weakly admissible implies admissible' by neighbouring representations (Préface Proposition 2.9, Remarque 2.10, §2.2.3) and Berger's proof through the (φ,Γ)-module ∆(D), which is étale exactly when D is weakly admissible (Théorème 2.42, Remarque 2.43), are the two proof routes of R06.2's admissibility theorem. Berger's monodromy theorem for non-étale (φ,Γ)-modules (Remarque 2.45) is an input to R06.3's p-adic monodromy theorem.

VB3 builds Banach–Colmez geometry, and VB3:general-BC asks: 'For the positive-slope range prove dimension and cohomological smoothness'. The accepted PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25 route 3 already routed 'Proposition 3.2: Dimension is well defined and additive; BC is abelian' to VB0–VB3, and that paper's accepted Part II imports 'Banach-Colmez geometry with the Dimension formalism' from the parent. Colmez's category BC with its exact functors (§8.4.1), its additive dim and ht (§8.4.1), and the well-definedness and additivity of Dim = (dim, ht) (Préface Théorème 2.12(i)(ii)) are the same statements, so they have this one owner. (This slot held the extraction's source route to FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1 and F3, which the independent review rejected: F1 is 'α_F : Y_F^◇ ≅ S × Spd(Q_p)' for E = Q_p only, and F3 compares étale sites without computing π_1. Its item 94 went to route 1 with RF1, and items 96 and 97 to route 3.)

PG.0 includes 'field-of-norms Galois equivalence and the descent/lifting statements required in Fontaine's construction' and PG.2 the overconvergence and Robba realisation of Cherbonnier and Colmez. The book uses the field of norms of the Kummer tower E(π^{1/p^n}) to see O^♭_Ê as the completed integral closure of F_q((π^♭)) (first proof of Proposition 2.2.15); it belongs inside PG.0, stated for arithmetically profinite towers. PG.2 ('the larger category of all Robba (φ,Γ)-modules') takes the tilde-ring clauses of Préface Théorème 2.41(i) and (iii) (items 78 and 80), which the review found planned there only over B_rig,K. The decompletion of §11.5 (item 1103) concerns all (φ,Γ)-modules, not only étale ones, and moved to route 5.

sourceIssues.reason: With the Préface's own convention (semistable means µ(D′) ≤ µ(D) for strict subobjects, slopes of the HN filtration decreasing), 'weakly admissible = semistable of slope 0' would require t_N(D′) ≤ t_H(D′) for subobjects, the opposite of Fontaine's t_H(D′) ≤ t_N(D′). Check: for a non-split crystalline extension 0 → Q_p(1) → V → Q_p → 0 (Kummer class of a unit), D = D_cris(V) is admissible, but its φ-stable line D″ of slope 0 has t_N(D″) = 0 and t_H(D″) = −1 (Fil^0 D_K is not K·D″ since V is non-split), so deg(D″) = t_N − t_H = 1 > 0 = µ(D) and D would not be 'faiblement admissible'. Likewise deg E(D) = t_H(D) − t_N(D) (E(D, φ) has slopes minus the Frobenius slopes, Remarque 4.8, and the modification by Fil adds t_H), so Proposition 5.6(i) 'deg(E(D)) = deg(D)' and Théorème 5.7(i) 'Si µ(D) > 0, alors dim V_st(D) = +∞' are false as printed: for D = K_0e, φ = 1, weight −1 (Fil^{−1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0) one has µ(D) = t_N − t_H = 1 > 0, but E(D) = O(−1) and V_st(D) = 0. Internal check: the Préface's own proof of Proposition 5.6(i) derives the degree for the trivial filtration from Remarque 4.8 (O(λ) ↔ Ĕ(−λ)), which gives deg E(D) = −t_N(D), whereas §2.1.2 gives deg(D) = t_N(D) for the trivial filtration. Proposition 2.15 (hypothesis t_H = t_N) is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Préface Exemple 2.23(ii), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that V = Qp t ⊕ Qp a, where a = log[1 + p^♭], is a two-dimensional sub-Qp-representation of U.
sourceIssues.correction: Take a = log[(1+p)^♭] (a compatible system of p-power roots of the principal unit 1 + p, or of any u ∈ 1 + m_K with log u ≠ 0); then σ(a) = a + c(σ)t with c the Kummer cocycle, V is G_K-stable, θ(a) = log(1 + p) ≠ 0 and U ⊗ V → B_2 is surjective.
sourceIssues.reason: x ↦ log[x] is a G_K-equivariant Z_p-linear isomorphism from (1 + m_{C^♭}, ×) onto a lattice of U (Théorème 3.11(ii) for E = Q_p), so V is G_K-stable iff σ(1 + p^♭) lies in the Q_p-saturation W of ε^{Z_p}(1 + p^♭)^{Z_p} for all σ. Write ℓ(u) = v_{C^♭}(u − 1). For u ∈ W, ℓ(u) ∈ {p^m} ∪ {p^m/(p−1)} (m ∈ Z) when p is odd (ℓ((1+p^♭)^{p^kα_0}) = p^k, ℓ(ε^{p^jβ_0}) = p^{j+1}/(p−1), these never coincide for p odd, and ℓ(u^{p^n}) = p^nℓ(u)). Take σ ∈ G_{K(μ_{p^∞})} with σ(p^♭) = ε^{p^s}p^♭ (s ≥ 0, possible by Kummer theory); then w = σ(1 + p^♭)/(1 + p^♭) = 1 + (ε^{p^s} − 1)p^♭/(1 + p^♭) has ℓ(w) = p^{s+1}/(p−1) + 1 = (p^{s+1} + p − 1)/(p−1), which is neither of the form p^m nor p^m/(p−1) (m ∈ Z): p^{s+1} + p − 1 ≡ −1 (mod p) cannot equal (p−1)p^m or p^m for m ≥ 1, and is too large for m ≤ 0. Hence w ∉ W and V is not G_K-stable (p odd).

sourceIssues.locator: Préface Remarque 2.38(i), p. 26, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The source calls the increasing filtration by Mµ = ⊕λ≥µ B̃rig (λ)^mλ canonical.
sourceIssues.correction: M_µ = ⊕_{λ≤µ} B̃_rig(λ)^{m_λ} (increasing in µ; its first step has the smallest Frobenius slope, as in Théorème 2.39 where λ_1 < λ_2 < ⋯).
sourceIssues.reason: Hom(B̃_rig(a), B̃_rig(b)) = (B̃_rig)^{φ=p^{a−b}} (rank one, φ(e) = p^a e ↦ g e′ with φ(g) = p^{a−b}g) is nonzero iff a ≥ b (t ∈ (B̃^+_rig)^{φ=p}; (B̃_rig)^{φ=p^{−m}} = H^0(X, O(−m)) = 0 for m > 0). So morphisms go from higher to lower Frobenius slope: in B̃_rig(0) ⊕ B̃_rig(1) the automorphism id + (multiplication by t : B̃_rig(1) → B̃_rig(0)) moves the summand B̃_rig(1) = M_1, while ⊕_{λ≤µ} is stable under all endomorphisms. sourceIssues.locator: Préface §3.1.1–3.1.4, Théorème 3.1(ii) and Théorème 3.8(ii), pp. 32–35, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: In (ii), the source asserts that a slope λ of NPx with multiplicity d admits a1 , . . . , ad ∈ OC^♭ with vC^♭(ai ) = −λvp (π) and a factorization x = (π − [a1 ]) · · · (π − [ad ])y with y ∈ AE.
sourceIssues.correction: With NP_x defined at the integer abscissae k (§3.1.1) the factor π − [a] has slope −v_{C^♭}(a), so the condition should be v_{C^♭}(a_i) = −λ; alternatively define NP_x with abscissae k·v_p(π) (the Legendre dual of v_r). The two agree only when v_p(π) = 1, i.e. E/Q_p unramified. Similarly v_r = inf_k(v(x_k) + k r v_p(π)) has slopes in v_p(π)·N, not 'pentes entières'; and in §3.1.4 the multiplicity of λ ∈ −I should be ∂_g v_{−λ}(x) − ∂_d v_{−λ}(x).
sourceIssues.reason: Example: E = Q_p(p^{1/2}), π = p^{1/2}, v_p(π) = 1/2, x = π − [π^♭] (a generator of Ker θ_E). NP_x joins (0, v(π^♭)) = (0, 1/2) to (1, 0): slope λ = −1/2 of multiplicity 1. The theorem would give a_1 with v(a_1) = −λ·v_p(π) = 1/4; but any factorisation x = (π − [a_1])y with y ∈ A_E forces y to be a unit (NP_y is constant) and θ_E(π − [a_1]) = 0, i.e. a_1^♯ = π, so v(a_1) = v_p(π) = 1/2. Also v_r(x) = min(1/2, r/2) has slope 1/2 ∉ N.

sourceIssues.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The source calls the function concave and claims that, for convex ϕ, the inverse Legendre transform recovers it by ϕ(x) = sup{L (ϕ)(λ) − λx | λ ∈ R}.
sourceIssues.correction: The inversion formula holds for ϕ convex and lower semicontinuous (in general sup_λ{L(ϕ)(λ) − λx} is the lower semicontinuous hull of ϕ).
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: ϕ(0) = 1, ϕ = 0 on ]0, 1], ϕ = +∞ elsewhere, is convex and not identically +∞; L(ϕ)(λ) = min(0, λ) and sup_λ{min(0, λ) − λ·0} = 0 ≠ 1 = ϕ(0). The polygons to which the formula is applied (Newton polygons, which take a finite value at their left endpoint and are +∞ before it) are lower semicontinuous, so nothing later is affected.

sourceIssues.reason: A continuous f: A → B with B spectral pulls bounded sets back to bounded sets, so ‖f(a)‖_{Ω'} = ‖a‖_{f^*Ω'} and f extends uniquely to A^sp → B: this is left adjointness. It asserts a canonical isomorphism ⊕_{d≥0} P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E L^{⊗d}_{π_E,π_{E'}} ⥲ P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•}.
sourceIssues.correction: Take L = {u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)_Q : ϕ(u)π_E = uπ_{E'}^{[E':E]}}, a 1-dimensional E'-vector space, and the isomorphism ⊕_{d≥0} (P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E E') ⊗_{E'} L^{⊗d} ⥲ P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•}, x ⊗ u^{⊗d} ↦ u^d x — as in Proposition 4.1.8 (p. 155), which takes u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)^×. (Also: the set is written with x but the condition with u, and the subscripts of L are swapped between the two displays.)
sourceIssues.reason: For u ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_Q = Ĕ one has ϕ(u)/u ∈ Ĕ, while π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E ∈ O_{E'}^×; since E'|E is totally ramified, Ĕ ∩ E' = E inside W_{O_{E'}}(k)_Q, so the printed set is {0} unless π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E ∈ E, which fails for general choices (e.g. replacing π_{E'} by π_{E'}(1 + π_{E'})). Moreover the left side of the displayed isomorphism is only an E-vector space tensored over E, while the right side is an E'-vector space containing P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E E'. The later use (proof of Théorème 6.5.2(2)) only needs the corrected form.

sourceIssues.correction: B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_{E'_0} E' with E'_0 the maximal unramified subextension (§1.6.2), so B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_E E' only for E'|E totally ramified. For the unramified part (which needs F_{q'} ⊂ F) B_{E'} = B_E with ϕ_{E'} = ϕ_E^{[E'_0:E]}, and M(Y_{E'}/ϕ^Z) = M(Y_E)^{ϕ^f = Id} = M(Y_E/ϕ^Z) ⊗_E E'_0 must be obtained by Galois descent (Hilbert 90 as in Proposition 4.1.7), not from a tensor identity for B.
sourceIssues.reason: By the paper's own §1.6.2 (pp. 70–71): 'lorsque E'|E est non-ramifiée, B_{E,I} = B_{E',I} mais ϕ_{E'} = ϕ_E^{[E':E]}'. The final identity for ϕ-invariants and Proposition 7.5.1 remain true, but the step (and the equality B_{E'}/(ξ) = B_E/(ξ) ⊗_E E' used next in the proof) needs this reduction.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 10.1.1, proof, p. 314, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The source places θ(t') in H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) and invokes Tate ([60]) for its vanishing when χ has infinite order. It then concludes t' ∈ ker θ, so t' is a Q_p-multiple of t and x = ∞. It next assumes, for a contradiction, that χ has finite order.
sourceIssues.correction: Split according to whether χ(I_K) is infinite or finite. If χ(I_K) is infinite, Tate gives H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) = 0 and the argument goes through. If χ(I_K) is finite, choose K'|K finite with χ|_{I_{K'}} = 1 and run the second argument with G_{K'} replaced by the inertia group I_{K'} = Gal(K̄|K'^{nr}): ε' ∈ (1+m_F)^{I_{K'}} ⊂ F^{I_{K'}} = (K̂'^{nr})^♭ = k̄_K, contradicting 0 < |1−ε'| < 1 (K̂'^{nr} is still discretely valued).
sourceIssues.reason: Tate's vanishing C(χ)^{G_K} = 0 requires χ(I_K) infinite (so stated in the atlas node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem), not merely χ of infinite order. When k_K is finite, an unramified χ with χ(Frob) = u ∈ Z_p^× of infinite order has H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) ⊇ {c ∈ K̂^{nr} : Frob(c) = uc} ≠ 0 (Lang's theorem on O_{K̂^{nr}}^×), so the first case does not conclude, and such χ is not of finite order, so the second case does not apply. The statement of Prop. 10.1.1 is unaffected (it follows from the corrected case split).

sourceIssues.locator: no 10.6.5.4, pp. 352–353, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof deduces surjectivity of exp^*_V from the perfect pairings and injectivity of exp_{V^*(1)}. It also claims that weak admissibility of (D^*, ϕ, Fil^•D^*_K), applied to the sub-isocrystal (D^*)^{ϕ=p} ⊗_{Q_p} K_0 of D^*, gives Fil^1(D^*)^{ϕ=p} = (D^*)^{ϕ=p}.
sourceIssues.correction: The equality Fil^1(D^*)^{ϕ=p} = (D^*)^{ϕ=p} (equivalently injectivity of exp_{V^*(1)}, surjectivity of exp^*_V and dim H^2(G_K,V) = dim D^{ϕ=p^{−1}}) does not follow from weak admissibility and fails for some filtrations allowed by 'Soit donc Fil^•D_K une telle filtration'. It holds if, when the slope is −1, one chooses Fil^•D_K with all jumps equal to −1 (Fil^{−1}D_K = D_K, Fil^0D_K = 0; weakly admissible since t_H = t_N for every sub-isocrystal), so that Fil^1D^*_K = (Fil^0D_K)^⊥ = D^*_K; for slope ≠ −1 both sides are 0.
sourceIssues.reason: Weak admissibility only gives t_H(D'_K) ≤ t_N(D') for sub-isocrystals D' (an upper bound), whereas Fil^1D'_K = D'_K needs all jumps of D'_K to be ≥ 1. Counterexample: K = Q_p(√p) (K_0 = Q_p), D = Q_p^2 with ϕ = p^{−1}·Id (isoclinic of slope −1), Fil^{−2}D_K = D_K ⊋ Fil^{−1} = Fil^0 = K·(1, √p) ⊋ Fil^1 = 0. Every sub-isocrystal is a line ℓ = Q_p·w, ℓ_K ∩ Fil^0 = 0, so t_H(ℓ) = −2 ≤ −1 = t_N(ℓ) and t_H(D) = −2 = t_N(D): weakly admissible, with Fil^iD_K = 0 for i > 0. But (D^*)^{ϕ=p} = Q_p^2 and Fil^1D^*_K = (Fil^0D_K)^⊥ = K·(√p, −1) meets Q_p^2 only in 0. Accordingly H^2(G_K,V) = H^0(G_K,V^*(1))^∨ = 0 while dim D^{ϕ=p^{−1}} = 2; dim H^1(G_K,V) = [K:Q_p]·2 = 4 = dim(D^{ϕ=p^{−1}} ⊕ D_K/Fil^0D_K), so α is an isomorphism, β = exp^*_V = 0 is not surjective onto Fil^0D_K ≅ K, and exp_{V^*(1)} is not injective. Prop. 10.6.16 itself is proved independently via Prop. 10.6.17.

sourceIssues.printed: The proof uses B(λ)^∨ = B(−λ) and claims that B(−λ) ⊗ B(µ) decomposes into ϕ-modules each isomorphic to B(µ − λ). It therefore reduces the task to H^1(B(ν)) = 0 for every ν ∈ Q.
sourceIssues.correction: For arbitrary k_F, B(−λ) ⊗ B(µ) is only isoclinic of slope µ − λ (a twisted form of a sum of B(µ−λ)); one should prove H^1 = 0 for every ϕ-module of the form D ⊗_L B(ν) with D isoclinic of slope 0 and ν ≠ 0 — which the d > 0 and d < 0 arguments give verbatim, and which is exactly the generalisation (5) the authors state in the proof of Théorème 11.1.8.
sourceIssues.reason: Take k_F = F_q (so L = E and φ_E is the identity on E), λ = −1/2, µ = 1/2. On L(1/2) ⊗ L(1/2) = E^4 the E-linear φ is M ⊗ M with M = [[0,π],[1,0]]; (M⊗M)^2 = π^2 and tr(M⊗M) = (tr M)^2 = 0, so L(1/2) ⊗ L(1/2) ≅ (E, π)^2 ⊕ (E, −π)^2 and ℬ(1/2) ⊗ ℬ(1/2) ≅ ℬ(1)^2 ⊕ (ℬ, −πφ)^2. But (ℬ, −πφ) ≇ ℬ(1) = (ℬ, πφ): reducing an isomorphism to the residue field L = E would give u ∈ E^× with −πu = πφ(u) = πu. So the asserted decomposition fails; the conclusion of the lemma is still true.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Théorème 11.1.8 (k_F not necessarily algebraically closed), p. 365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The source identifies D_λ = End(B(−λ)) = End(L(−λ)) as the division algebra over E with invariant λ. It then asserts the canonical isomorphism of ϕ-modules over B given by M ⥲ Hom_{D_λ⊗B}(B(−λ), M ⊗ B(−λ)).
sourceIssues.correction: Both claims need F_{q^h} ⊂ k_F (in particular they hold for k_F algebraically closed, where D_λ ⊗_E L ≅ M_h(L) and Morita theory applies). For general k_F the Morita step must be replaced, e.g. by first extending scalars to a field containing F_{q^h} and descending, or by working with the isoclinic slope-λ part directly.
sourceIssues.reason: Let k_F = F_q, λ = d/h with h ≥ 2 (e.g. λ = 1/2). Then L = E, φ_E is trivial on E, and L(−λ) = E^h with E-linear φ the companion matrix C of x^h − π^{−d}; End(L(−λ)) = E[C] ≅ E[x]/(x^h − π^{−d}), a commutative field of degree h (totally ramified since (d,h) = 1), not the central division algebra of invariant λ (dimension h^2). Moreover ℬ(−λ) is free of rank one over D_λ ⊗_E ℬ = ℬ[C], so Hom_{D_λ⊗ℬ}(ℬ(−λ), M ⊗ ℬ(−λ)) ≅ M ⊗_ℬ ℬ(−λ) has ℬ-rank nh ≠ n = rank M; the claimed isomorphism with M is false. The theorem itself (every φ-module over B^+ comes from an isocrystal) is not contradicted.

sourceIssues.reason: Hom(U_i ⊗ B, U_j ⊗ B) = H^0(U_i^∨ ⊗ U_j ⊗ B) is H^0 of a module isoclinic of slope µ_j − µ_i. Here B is the ring ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 of §11.1. With the chapter's convention A(n) = (A, π^nφ), H^0(ℬ(n)) = ℬ^{φ=π^{−n}}: it vanishes for n > 0 (H^0(ℬ(n)) = H^0(B^+(n)) by Proposition 11.1.3, and (B^+)^{φ=π^{−n}} = 0) but H^0(ℬ(−1)) = ℬ^{φ=π} ≅ P_1 ≠ 0 (§11.1.2). So Hom(ℬ(1), ℬ(0)) ≠ 0, i.e. nonzero maps go from larger to smaller slopes, and for µ_i > µ_j (i > j) the Hom need not vanish. The argument only needs some D_λ-stable filtration with graded pieces U_i ⊗ B, which the corrected filtration provides.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemme 11.2.10, statement and proof, p. 372, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The lemma takes Banach E-algebras B_1, B_2, A with maps B_1 → A and B_2 → A inducing a surjection B_1 ⊕ B_2 → A. For Z ∈ GL_n(A), it asserts that some identity neighbourhood in GL_n(A) consists of matrices XZYZ^{−1}, where X ∈ GL_n(B_1) and Y ∈ GL_n(B_2).
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that the tangent map M_n(B_1) ⊕ M_n(B_2) → M_n(A), (U, V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, is surjective (true for Z = 1, and in the application of Proposition 11.2.12 because Z = Z'DZ'' with Z', Z'' ∈ GL_n(B_{I_1∪I_2}) and every ratio of diagonal entries of D is a unit of B_{I_1∩I_2} factoring as w_1w_2, w_i ∈ B_{I_i}^×, so B_1 + (d_i/d_j)B_2 = w_1(B_1 + B_2) = A). The proof's appeal to Lemme 11.2.11 silently uses this surjectivity.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: A = E⟨T, T^{−1}⟩, B_1 = E⟨T⟩, B_2 = E⟨T^{−1}⟩ (B_1 ⊕ B_2 → A surjective), Z = diag(T, T^{−1}). For ε ∈ E^×, Z_ε = [[T, 0],[ε, T^{−1}]] satisfies L Z_ε R = [[0, −1/ε],[ε, 0]] with L = [[1, −T/ε],[0, 1]] ∈ GL_2(B_1), R = [[1, −T^{−1}/ε],[0, 1]] ∈ GL_2(B_2), so Z_ε ∈ GL_2(B_1)GL_2(B_2). But Z ∉ GL_2(B_1)GL_2(B_2): if X^{−1}Z = Y with X^{−1} = [[a,b],[c,d]] over B_1, then aT, cT ∈ B_2 ∩ T·B_1 = 0 forces a = c = 0, contradicting invertibility. Hence Z_εZ^{−1} → 1 as ε → 0 but Z_εZ^{−1} ∉ GL_2(B_1)·Z·GL_2(B_2)·Z^{−1}. (Tangent map: the (2,1)-entry of its image is B_1 + T^{−2}B_2, which misses T^{−1}.)

sourceIssues.printed: The proof invokes density of B_{I_1∪I_2} in B_{I_1∩I_2} to choose Z ∈ M_n(B_{I_1∪I_2}) ∩ GL_n(B_{I_1∩I_2}), making UZ^{−1} arbitrarily near the identity of GL_n(B_{I_1∩I_2}). sourceIssues.correction: One needs a neighbourhood in Lemme 11.2.10 that is uniform for all Z close to U (or a different route, e.g. Kedlaya's: approximate U on one side by a matrix invertible over the bounded ring so that the remaining factor is close to 1, then use the Z = 1 factorisation; cf. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/matrix-approximation-and-factorization). The proposition itself is true (Kiehl-type gluing).
sourceIssues.reason: The neighbourhood produced by Lemme 11.2.10 depends on Z (through ‖Z‖, ‖Z^{−1}‖ and the norm of a section of (U,V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, which here depends on the factorisation of the units d_i/d_j of the Smith form of Z), while Z is chosen after, and depending on, how close UZ^{−1} must be to 1. No bound uniform in Z is given, so 'aussi proche que l’on veut' does not ensure that UZ^{−1} lies in the neighbourhood attached to Z; uniformity would follow from surjectivity of the tangent map at U itself, which is equivalent to what is being proved.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 11.2.24, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof takes λ = d/h, (d, h) = 1, as the largest Dieudonné-Manin slope of (V̂, ϕ), and claims a lattice Λ ⊂ V exists with ϕ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ. It makes (V, ϕ) an extension of ⊕_i E^†(µ_i) by E^†(λ)^r, r ≥ 1, with µ_i < λ for every i. It reduces Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = 0 for λ > µ to vanishing of the cokernel of Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h : E^† → E^† when d > 0 and h ≥ 1.
sourceIssues.correction: λ must be the SMALLEST slope; then µ_i > λ for all i, and one needs Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = 0 for µ > λ, which reduces to coker(Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h) = 0 with d/h = µ − λ > 0 (as displayed). Even so corrected the argument does not close: the step through Lemme 11.2.25 fails for non-bijective φ, and Proposition 11.2.24 itself is false as stated (see the separate issues on Lemme 11.2.25 and Proposition 11.2.24).
sourceIssues.reason: (i) A lattice with ϕ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ forces every slope to be ≥ d/h, so λ is the smallest slope (as in the parallel proofs of Théorèmes 11.1.7 and 11.1.8). (ii) With the chapter's convention (E^†(n) = (E^†, π^nϕ)), Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = H^1(E^†(λ−µ)) = coker(Id − π^{d'}ϕ^{h'}) with λ − µ = d'/h'; the displayed map Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h is the case λ − µ < 0. (iii) The printed claim is false: for F algebraically closed, 0 < |ϖ| < 1, Ext^1(E^†(0), E^†(1)) = coker(Id − πϕ on E^†) ∋ [ϖ^{−1}] is nonzero, since the unique solution in ℰ of y − πϕ(y) = [ϖ^{−1}] is y = Σ_{k≥0} π^k[ϖ^{−q^k}], and sup_k |ϖ|^{−q^k}ρ^k = ∞ for every ρ > 0, so y ∉ E^†.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 10.6.18(1), p. 350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: For d = h = 1, the source says the cokernel of the Bloch-Kato exponential δ : K → H^1(G_K, Q_p(1)) has Q_p-dimension 1. It restates this by claiming that every extension V of Q_p by Q_p(1) is either crystalline and isomorphic to the Tate module of an elliptic curve with good ordinary reduction, or semistable and isomorphic to the Tate module of a Tate elliptic curve.
sourceIssues.correction: State the hypothesis k_K algebraically closed of Prop. 10.6.17 (of which 10.6.18 is announced as the translation) in Prop. 10.6.18; the first sentence of (1) holds for all K, but the 'en d'autres termes' description of crystalline extensions needs k_K algebraically closed (Serre–Tate).
sourceIssues.reason: The review classes this as a misprint that affects a stated result: the paragraph before Proposition 10.6.18 calls it 'la traduction de la proposition 10.6.17', which assumes k_K algebraically closed, so the intended hypothesis can be read from the context, but the statement as printed (for the K of Chapter 10, any perfect residue field) is false. Neither no 10.6.5.3 nor Prop. 10.6.18 restates 'k_K algébriquement clos'. For K = Q_p (finite residue field) and E/Q_p with good ordinary reduction, 0 → Q_p(1)(ψ^{−1}) → V_p(E) → Q_p(ψ) → 0 with ψ unramified, ψ(Frob) = the unit root α of X^2 − a_pX + p, and |α|_∞ = √p ≠ 1, so Q_p(ψ) ≇ Q_p; the semisimplification of V_p(E) is Q_p(ψ) ⊕ Q_p(1)(ψ^{−1}) ≠ Q_p ⊕ Q_p(1). Hence a crystalline extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) over Q_p (e.g. the Kummer class of 1+p) is not V_p of such a curve (nor of a Tate curve, which is not crystalline). With k_K algebraically closed the unramified characters are trivial and the description is right.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 11.2.24, statement, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts that completion ϕ-Mod_{E†} −→ ϕ-Mod_ℰ is an equivalence of categories, and therefore applies Dieudonné-Manin classification to ϕ-Mod_{E†}.
sourceIssues.correction: Only a filtration descends (Kedlaya [45] Prop. 5.11): every (V, ϕ) ∈ ϕ-Mod_{E†} has a unique filtration by saturated sub-ϕ-modules with isoclinic graded pieces of strictly decreasing Dieudonné–Manin slopes (each a direct sum of E†(λ) when F is algebraically closed). The completion functor is essentially surjective and an equivalence on isoclinic objects, but not fully faithful, and ϕ-modules over E† are not in general direct sums of E†(λ).
sourceIssues.reason: Let c ∈ F with |c| > 1 (any F, e.g. algebraically closed) and V = E†e_1 ⊕ E†e_2 with ϕ(e_1) = e_1 + [c]e_2, ϕ(e_2) = πe_2 (matrix of determinant π, so V ∈ ϕ-Mod_{E†}). A fixed vector xe_1 + ye_2 needs ϕ(x) = x, so x ∈ E, and y − πϕ(y) = [c]x. In ℰ, Id − πϕ is injective (π-adic valuation) and the solution for x = 1 is ŷ = Σ_{k≥0} π^k[c^{q^k}]. Since |c^{q^k}|ρ^k → ∞ for every ρ > 0, ŷ ∉ E† (Prop. 1.6.23). So V^{ϕ=Id} = 0, whereas V̂ = ℰ(e_1 + ŷe_2) ⊕ ℰe_2 ≅ ℰ(0) ⊕ ℰ(1) has a fixed vector. Hence Hom(E†(0), V) = 0 → Hom(ℰ(0), V̂) ≅ E is not surjective (completion is not full), and V ≇ E†(0) ⊕ E†(1), the only candidate sum of standard objects with those slopes, which would have fixed vectors. Equivalently, the class of [c] in Ext^1(E†(0), E†(1)) = coker(Id − πϕ on E†) is nonzero (cf. E183 (iii)). Kedlaya [45], §5.3 (arXiv math/0110124), says explicitly that the Dieudonné–Manin classification 'does not descend to Γ_con in general'; his Prop. 5.11 is the descending filtration and Cor. 5.12 the isoclinic case. The later uses in §11.4 (essential surjectivity of ϕ-Mod_{E†} → ϕ-Mod_ℛ, isoclinic equivalence) survive with the corrected form.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemme 11.2.25, statement and proof (equation (7)), p. 379, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: The source takes a finite-rank free O_{E†}-module Λ with a semilinear endomorphism ϕ and asserts a bijection Λ^{ϕ=Id} ⥲ Λ̂^{ϕ=Id}. It subsequently chooses X ∈ O_ℰ^n satisfying (7) ϕ(X) = AX.
sourceIssues.correction: Assume ϕ bijective on Λ (matrix A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†})). Then a fixed vector satisfies X = Aϕ(X), i.e. ϕ(X) = A^{−1}X, and the printed argument applies to A^{−1} (after rescaling the basis so that A^{−1} mod π ∈ M_n(O_F)).
sourceIssues.reason: With A the matrix of ϕ (ϕ(e_j) = Σ_i a_ij e_i, as on p. 360), ϕ(Σx_je_j) = Σ_j x_je_j means Aϕ(X) = X, not (7); with the correct equation the estimate becomes ‖X‖_{k,ρ_0^q} ≤ ‖X‖_{k,ρ_0}^q, which bounds nothing. The statement is false: Λ = O_{E†}e_1 ⊕ O_{E†}e_2, ϕ(e_1) = e_1 + [c]e_2, ϕ(e_2) = πe_2, c ∈ F with |c| > 1. In Λ̂, e_1 + (Σ_{k≥0} π^k[c^{q^k}])e_2 is ϕ-fixed. In Λ, a fixed vector xe_1 + ye_2 has x ∈ O_E and y = [c]x + πϕ(y), whose only solution in O_ℰ is x·Σπ^k[c^{q^k}], not in O_{E†} unless x = 0, and then y = πϕ(y) forces y = 0. So Λ^{ϕ=Id} = 0 ≠ Λ̂^{ϕ=Id} ≅ O_E. Here ϕ is injective but not bijective (det A = π). The lemma is applied in Proposition 11.2.24 to π^{−d}ϕ^h, which is not bijective in general, and this is where that proof breaks (the same V is a counterexample to the proposition).
